author: pushparaj9749
body:
## v2.9.0 — App Lock + "Naya version aaya hai" banner

### App Lock (fingerprint / PIN)
- Settings → Privacy & Data → **App Lock**: 4-digit PIN, plus fingerprint / face unlock when the phone has it.
- Locks on launch and on return, with a choice of Turant / 1 min / 5 min. A cover hides story text in the recent-apps preview.
- `AppLockGate` keeps the app mounted under the lock, so unlocking is instant and nothing is lost.
- The PIN is never stored. Only a salted, stretched SHA-256 hash is kept in expo-secure-store. Wrong PINs give a persisted cool-down: 5 tries → 30 s, doubling up to 15 min.
- "PIN bhool gaye?" resets the PIN through the phone's own screen lock.
- If no PIN is stored (for example, a backup restored on another phone), the lock switches itself off instead of trapping the user.
- The backup share sheet, backup import and image picker are wrapped in `withAppLockPaused`.

### Update banner
- `lib/updateCheck.ts` makes an anonymous GET to the public `releases/latest` endpoint only.
- It parses the tag and the github.com `.apk` link, and compares versions numerically.
- Successful results are cached for 6 h. Failures are never cached.
- Home banner with **Download** and **Baad mein**; dismissal is per version.
- About has an **Update check karo** card and a banner switch. The privacy policy is updated.
- The security test now allows exactly this one URL, only in `updateCheck.ts`.

### Tests
- New: `appLock`, `appLockGate`, `updateCheck`.
- Full run: 57 suites / 1060 tests pass; tsc is clean. Checked by hand in the web preview.

## Summary Fixes the failing CocoaPods Lint CI job and bumps the library version to **2.0.4**. ## Root Cause `TFYSwiftNestedHorizontalPan` (an `enum` with nested scroll-view gesture helpers) was defined in `TFYSwiftBase/TFYSwiftCollectionView.swift` but **referenced** by `TFYSwiftTool/TFYSwiftListContainerView.swift` (lines 540 and 550). In the podspec, `TFYSwiftTool` is the **foundation** subspec with **no dependencies**, while `TFYSwiftBase` depends on `TFYSwiftTool`. When CocoaPods lints each subspec in isolation, `TFYSwiftTool` cannot see symbols from `TFYSwiftBase`, causing: ``` error: cannot find 'TFYSwiftNestedHorizontalPan' in scope ``` ## Fix - **Moved** `TFYSwiftNestedHorizontalPan` out of `TFYSwiftBase/TFYSwiftCollectionView.swift` into its own file: `TFYSwiftTool/TFYSwiftNestedHorizontalPan.swift`. - `TFYSwiftBase` depends on `TFYSwiftTool`, so it still has access to the enum. - Added the new file to `project.pbxproj` (file reference, build phase, group). ## Version Bump (2.0.4) - `TFYSwiftSegmentedKit.podspec` — `s.version = "2.0.4"` - `README.md` — all CocoaPods/SPM install snippets and "latest version" mentions - `CHANGELOG.md` — new `[2.0.4]` entry describing the CI fix

author: bthall
body:
💡 What:
Optimized `visibleWidth` and `truncate` string layout helper functions in `internal/cli/table.go`.

🎯 Why:
- `visibleWidth` previously executed `ansiRE.ReplaceAllString` on any string containing `\x1b`, which incurred regular expression matching overhead and string heap allocations on every call during table rendering.
- `truncate` previously converted strings to `[]rune` slices via `[]rune(s)`, allocating memory on the heap and running full-string rune counting passes even when strings required truncation.

📊 Impact:
- `visibleWidth` (ANSI strings): ~6.8x speedup (663.6 ns/op -> 97.5 ns/op), reduced heap allocations by 100% (80 B/op -> 0 B/op).
- `truncate`: Eliminated intermediate `[]rune` heap slice allocations.

🔬 Measurement:
Run `TMUX= go test -bench=BenchmarkVisibleWidth_ANSI -benchmem ./internal/cli` and `TMUX= go test -bench=BenchmarkTruncate -benchmem ./internal/cli`.

author: fgarofalo56
body:
## Problem
526 `asa-loom-<id8>` Stream Analytics jobs, all state Created, never deleted (493 admin RG, 33 DLZ RG).

## Cause (measured)
- Name is already deterministic: `asa-loom-` + first 8 chars of the eventstream item id (`eventstream-standup.ts`). One job per item, so the count equals the number of eventstream items ever created.
- Nightly `loom-uat-full-suite` (cron 07:23 UTC, runs land ~12-15Z) installs use-case apps; creation clusters of 4-8 jobs per hour at 14-15Z line up with each run (e.g. 2026-10-06 run 14:17Z -> 7 jobs 14-15Z).
- Its cleanup (`e2e/_lib/uat.ts cleanupWorkspaces`) POSTed bulk-delete WITHOUT `cascade:true`, which is catalog-only by design, so Cosmos docs went and backends stayed.
- `DELETE /api/items/eventstream/[id]` deleted only the Cosmos doc (generic `/api/items/[type]/[id]` DELETE does the same for every type; not changed here).
- The auto-bind seed path discards the stand-up result, so `state.asaJobName` is never recorded and even a cascade delete would find nothing.

## Fix
- `lib/azure/asa-job-name.ts`: one `asaJobNameForItem(id)` used by stand-up and teardown.
- `resource-teardown.ts`: eventstream teardown derives the job from `item.id` when no ref is recorded (only if ASA is configured; 404 is already idempotent).
- Eventstream DELETE tears down first, deletes the doc anyway, and returns `teardown` plus a `warning` naming anything left behind.
- UAT cleanup sends `cascade:true`.

## Verification
Vitest: 25 tests across the eventstream areas pass. Mutations run in place with hash-identical restore: remove the derive fallback (2 RED), remove the ASA-configured guard (1 RED), remove the route teardown call (2 RED). Not run: live Azure, Snyk (tool unavailable in this session), full `make validate`. tsc errors in the tree are pre-existing duplicate-identifier noise in unrelated test files; none in touched files. file-size, route-inventory (regenerated), security-graph --check pass.

Merged is not deployed; existing 513 leftover jobs are NOT deleted by this PR (selection rule in the PR comment / report).

author: doodesch
body:
More NPCs Forked 1.1.0 (Nexus 2590, report by LoganaterGames) dropped the game to 2-11 FPS with freezes of up to 6 s. With this branch the same save runs at 54-60 FPS after load.

## What changed

- **0.4.7 port of the deep tier**: pause and resume through a speed control (`siesta_pause`), agent and collider back through `OnVisibilityChange`.
- **More NPCs scan compat**: `GameDealerFinder.GetRootTransforms` (160-370 ms per call) reads the NPC registry instead (0.6-0.9 ms). `ReOfficeWhiteboardDisplay.FindPropertyListingTransform` (about 1.2 s per name, about 6 s for the first board sync) uses `GameObject.Find` plus one cached sweep (1.3 s once for all four boards). The original and the replacement return the same objects (`siesta mnf`).
- **Movement throttle** (`ThrottleFarMovement`, on by default, host only): `NPCMovement.FixedUpdate` of far NPCs, and of near NPCs that stand still on an unreachable destination, runs 5 times a second. A stuck NPC re-plans its whole path in each call.
- **Stay-in-building repath**: `NPCEvent_StayInBuilding.OnActiveTick` is skipped while the path to the same door is pending. In the late load phase this cuts the tick cost from about 880 ms to 30-110 ms per 15 s.
- The version in the init log comes from the build.

## Measured (profile main = D: mods, Save 5, Snitch)

| Run | FPS |
|---|---|
| D: without More NPCs, without Siesta | 55-69 |
| D: + Siesta | 61-80 |
| D: + More NPCs | 0.6-3, freezes up to 20 s and 5.7 s |
| D: + More NPCs + this branch | 4-8 for about 40-60 s after load, then 54-60 |

Saving restores all NPCs and re-culls afterwards (G1/G2 runs). No wake failures, throws or exceptions in nine runs.

## Open

The 40-60 s at 4-8 FPS right after loading with More NPCs. It is not in any NPC component (bisection of Animator, NavMeshAgent+NPCMovement, VisionCone+NPCAwareness, NPCScheduleManager+NPCBehaviour, Avatar types), not in the path queue (`pathfindingIterationsPerFrame` 2000 empties it without FPS gain), and not in the Deep count or physics steps.

## Changelog

- Fixed: with More NPCs Forked the game froze for seconds whenever that mod looked for dealers or office boards, and its extra NPCs kept the FPS in single digits. Right after loading a save it can still be slow for up to a minute.

author: pcbeingused333
body:
A non-streaming Mistral `/audio/speech` call answers with a JSON object, `{"audio_data": "<base64>"}` ([API reference](https://docs.mistral.ai/api/endpoint/audio/speech)). `AudioEndpoint.CreateSpeech` handed that body to the caller as `SpeechTtsResult.AudioStream`, so `SaveAndDispose` wrote JSON text to the `.mp3` file.

For Mistral, the response body is now read and `audio_data` is base64-decoded into the returned stream. A body that does not start with that JSON envelope is returned unchanged. The decoding lives in `VendorMistralSpeechResult`.

Tests (`MistralSpeechResultTests.cs`): the helper decodes the envelope and leaves raw audio alone, and `CreateSpeech` against a stubbed Mistral `HttpClient` returns the decoded bytes. The endpoint test fails on `master` (it gets the 25 bytes of JSON) and passes with this change.

This change was made with Claude Code.

Les textes côté client utilisent désormais la voix de Jessie à la première personne, en français et en anglais, sur l’accueil, l’accès, l’aide, la conversation et l’export. Les deux passages demandés dans l’aide sont corrigés ; deux e-mails d’accès adaptent leur objet, texte et signature.

L’espacement des messages passe de 18 à 6 px. Date, reçu et actions apparaissent pour un seul message sélectionné par appui ou commande clavier native. Photos, copie de texte, confirmations de suppression, erreurs et reprise d’envoi restent accessibles. Les accusés de lecture de l’administration restent privés. Aucun changement d’API, de dépendance ou de schéma SQL.

Validation : 151/151 tests d’interaction, 57/57 tests éditoriaux, 23/23 tests mail et 9/9 tests de réinitialisation, sans omission ; syntaxe et build de 583 sources. [CI PR](https://github.com/fredbuhr/jessiemessage/actions/runs/39527675066) et [CI du commit de fusion](https://github.com/fredbuhr/jessiemessage/actions/runs/39528364838) réussies 5/5 : général : 3 190 réussis/36 ignorés, Chrome : 173/173, HTTPS : 3/3 et MariaDB 10.11/11.4 479/479 chacune. La CI main a nécessité la relance unique de verify après l’échec d’un test de continuité ; il passe inchangé, les quatre résultats natifs sont conservés. L’échec initial et l’hypothèse de course de fixture restent dans les [preuves](https://github.com/fredbuhr/jessiemessage/blob/main/docs/verification-proofs/jm132-verification.json).

La [release v1.3.2](https://github.com/fredbuhr/jessiemessage/releases/tag/v1.3.2) vise le commit `194557719780aed4c2d56dac2c9ec91e0f2886a9` qualifié. L’activation hébergée reste distincte et suivie dans [REPRISE](https://github.com/fredbuhr/jessiemessage/blob/main/docs/REPRISE.md).

author: pjerra
body: Plan format: a hold can carry a value (written as param with flags 8 and no encounter flag) and a wait_for can carry a hold, which plan-export writes in place of the wait; the agent's own driver still runs the wait as written. zulfarrak.json: the Weegli wait holds the stairs top until instance data 1 reads 3 (90 s), the Nekrum wait until it reads 7 (600 s); Velratha pull groups 4 and 5 get approach stands on the lower floor (>= 24 yd from every pack member, spawn and patrol data; the lone Shadowhunter 81610 is 12.9 yd from the group 4 stand but is pulled at the earlier hop). Plan reader refuses a hold value of 0 and a value on a pull or boss hold. Exporter accepts hold params above 4 when the encounter flag is off. The exported plan goes from 86 to 122 steps (14 legs). Compatibility: an agent binary built before this change refuses this zulfarrak.json (unknown fields hold and value). Reviews: Opus cold review two rounds (FIX FIRST on the approach points, then SHIP); Codex not run. Tests: 11 mutations fail a test, go test ./... with the map 209 navmeshes green. Not verified: no run under the run leader yet (module side: TortoiseBots feat/zf-plan-extended); the first run tests legs 0-8 of a changed route (71 steps, not the proven 86).

author: paramcodes
body:
## What

This pull request renders the IDE shell of Arrow and closes every hole an adversarial audit and a
second audit found on the way.

The shell:

- The activity bar, the sidebar, the editor area, the bottom panel and the status bar render
  together, and the facts of the layout live in one Zustand store that survives a reload.
- Every panel resizes by dragging its handle, and the handles resize with the arrow keys and report
  their size with `aria-valuenow`, `aria-valuemin` and `aria-valuemax`.
- The content padding of the shell is eight pixels, the density ADR-0003 records.

The fixes:

- Tailwind scans every package that ships utility classes again. The source discovery moved to
  `apps/desktop/tailwind.config.js`, and `apps/desktop/src/app.css` loads it with `@config`. The
  ten vendored primitives in `packages/ui` render styled, and the resize handles have a box to
  grab.
- The cross-tier lint rule no longer flags a computed import in a file that owns no state tier. It
  still refuses a computed import that could reach a second tier.
- The prover takes an exclusive lock on the tree before it touches it, so two overlapping runs can
  no longer fight over the same probe files.
- The alias of the workspace packages moved under `resolve` in the Vite configuration, where Vite
  reads it. The app resolves the source of the packages instead of their built output.
- The layout store test sets up the state it needs and leaves none behind, so it passes in any
  order and passes when a single case runs on its own.
- The merge gate runs the end to end suite, so a drag that stops working fails the pull request
  instead of waiting for the next session.
- `AGENTS.md` names the Tailwind source rule, and the rule names a guardrail that runs.

## Why

The audit measured the resize handles at zero pixels on their thin axis: `w-1` and `h-1` were
missing from the bundle because Tailwind v4 collects its sources from the directory of the CSS
entry point, and `packages/ui` is not that directory. A drag changed nothing, so the binding
acceptance of the shell did not hold, and every later session would have consumed unstyled
primitives.

The cross-tier rule reported every computed import, even in a file that owns no tier, so a file
that only splits its code with a variable was blocked by a rule that had nothing to say about it.

The prover shared one journal and one probe file per path between concurrent runs, and the loser
left a probe file in the tree, which then failed `pnpm verify`.

The Vite alias sat at the top level of the configuration, where Vite does not read it, so the app
bundled the built output of the packages. The comment in the file claimed the opposite.

The layout store test read the defaults of a store that an earlier case had already changed, so
the file passed only in the order it was written. A test that passes only in one order is not a
test.

The shell used twelve pixel content padding where ADR-0003 records eight pixels, so the frame of
the editor read as a consumer app instead of an editor.

The drag and keyboard resize proof lived in the end to end suite and only ran on a laptop, so a
drag that stopped working waited for the next session instead of failing the merge gate.

The Tailwind source discovery is load bearing, and a rule in `AGENTS.md` that no path enforces is
a rule that a later session can break without knowing it broke anything.

## How

- `apps/desktop/src/components/layout/**`: the five regions of the shell, the layout store, the
  keyboard shortcuts, and a guardrail that reads the components and fails when one of them asks
  for twelve pixels.
- `apps/desktop/src/stores/layout.ts` and `apps/desktop/src/stores/layout.test.ts`: a reset
  function, a hook that calls it before every case, and a case that reads the test files of the
  store and fails when one of them does not reset the store.
- `apps/desktop/tailwind.config.js` (new) and `apps/desktop/src/app.css`: the source discovery.
- `packages/ui/src/tailwind-source.test.ts` (new): the guardrail that reads the source list and
  fails when a package that ships utility classes is not scanned.
- `packages/ui/src/components/resizable.tsx`: the keyboard resize and the ARIA values of the
  handle.
- `apps/desktop/vite.config.ts`: the alias under `resolve`.
- `eslint-rules/index.mjs`: the cross-tier rule holds the unknown sources until the end of the file
  and reports them only when the file owns a tier.
- `scripts/prove-guardrails.mjs`: the lock of the tree, the ownership of the journal, the tree of a
  run taken from the script that owns it, and `${PROOF_COUNT}` so a proof payload can never carry a
  stale size of the proof set.
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: a third job that installs the Playwright browser from a cache and
  runs `pnpm test:e2e`.
- `apps/desktop/e2e/layout.spec.ts` (new): a real browser proves that the handles have a box,
  that a drag resizes both panels, and that the arrow keys resize them.
- `harness.config.json` and `scripts/prove-guardrails.mjs`: six new proof cases, the registry
  entries of the new rules, the requirement that the workflow runs the end to end suite, and
  `minimumProofs` raised from 36 to 42 in the same commits.
- `docs/mistake-log.md`: nineteen rows, one for each defect, each naming its guardrail. Three of them are new in this unit.

The gates: `pnpm verify` exits 0, `pnpm harness` scores 10/10, `pnpm prove` reports 42 caught and
0 missed, `cargo test` passes in `apps/desktop/src-tauri`, and `pnpm test:e2e` passes 5 of 5. CI
runs all of it, including the end to end suite, at
https://github.com/paramcodes/arrow/actions/runs/39535804879

## Scope and current source

Continue #307/#189 after #329's source-only integration. The initial increment bounded the pole-subtracted logarithmic derivative. The continuation constructs its analytic extension at the actual simple zero and derives an exact small-circle integral. All concrete results retain the ORIGINAL open `ConcreteNewtonPacket.SourceAcceptance`.

**SOURCE_ONLY / NOT_RUN / NOT_KERNEL_AUDITED / SOURCE_ACCEPTANCE_OPEN.** Proof scripts are unelaborated candidates and may need repair. No actual zero, source acceptance or global mathematical target is newly certified.

- Original inspected base: `b9d346f547d71d0f902cbfc4e0a9b2e020adf4d6`, tree `bcc044e4374ab1da8422fc4f918cb5af9ca6bcd8`.

- Branch: `research/307-concrete-newton-regular-part-v01`.
- Latest exact-head packet: https://github.com/grwtsk/math/pull/333#issuecomment-6305962081 .
- Initial mathematical packet and limitations remain at https://github.com/grwtsk/math/issues/307#issuecomment-6305766887 .

Cumulative scope: **four added files / 625 lines / no deletions or modified pre-existing paths**. Twenty-eight named draft theorem declarations (including the original private helper) and one definition. The latest commit adds two files / 328 lines / eighteen declarations and one definition. No source field, returned error, radius, multiplier, schedule, verifier, public-root import, dependency pin or static manifest was changed.

## Latest increment: extend before integrating

`GRWTSK/Analysis/Complex/IsolatedSimpleZeroContour.lean` (200 lines, blob `13680542936b6a0afd2edf9f96e0f6295d148634`) uses the explicit upstream divided difference g=dslope f rho. Away from rho this is f(z)/(z-rho), while g(rho)=f'(rho). The power-series shift gives analyticity at the root; ordinary analytic quotient operations handle the other points. The exact global source factorization (z-rho)*g(z)=f(z) is differentiated before any quotient cancellation.

The actual root is SIMPLE, and actual source values away from it are nonzero on the SAME closed disk. These give g!=0 including at rho. Thus H=g'/g is analytic across the root and agrees with f'/f-1/(z-rho) off the root. Its value at rho is determined by this analytic factor, not by assigning zero to a singular expression. Distinct-root uniqueness alone is not substituted for simplicity.

Boundary integrability is proved explicitly. Cauchy's theorem gives integral(H)=0. STRICT interior membership gives integral(1/(z-rho))=2*pi*i. The source draft therefore obtains

    integral_circle(f'/f) = 2*pi*i.

It also proves that two poles strictly inside the same circle have zero integrated pole difference. This does not assert their pointwise difference vanishes, allow a pole on the contour, or use a default nonintegrable integral as evidence.

`GRWTSK/NumberTheory/Zeta/Riemann/ConcreteNewtonContour.lean` (128 lines, blob `fe1dd238677c68041b5b7607125b0bfdb4cc59f9`) composes these results with the SAME original conditional source. The root is strictly inside the original radius-1/100000 disk by the already justified radius-1/250000 localization. Outer analyticity, derivative nonvanishing, exact line equality and original outer uniqueness are retained. No-other-RAW-zero is obtained from the existing actual-value separation theorem, not inferred by changing the domain of the subtype uniqueness statement.

The concrete conclusions are:

    SourceAcceptance -> analytic extension of zeta'/zeta-1/(z-rho),
    SourceAcceptance -> integral_circle(zeta'/zeta) = 2*pi*i,
    SourceAcceptance -> normalized local contour index = 1,
    SourceAcceptance -> integral_circle(zeta'/zeta-1/(z-c)) = 0.

The rational center c is not asserted to be a zero or a removable point for the last expression. The pointwise pole-location cost remains; its integral cancels because BOTH poles are strictly interior. This is an exact analytic route, not rounding of an approximate contour calculation.

## Earlier bound and obstruction retained unchanged

`ContractiveLogDerivativeRemainder.lean` (130 lines, blob `2da94a038f147362f3695a6e410002a3455d5c73`) derives a conservative quadratic numerator bound M*|z-rho|^2 from two mean-value estimates, then divides by positive scaled separation to give |f'/f-1/(z-rho)|<=|a|M/(1-q). It does not claim the sharper integral-Taylor factor 1/2. All denominator and same-disk hypotheses remain.

`ConcreteNewtonRegularPart.lean` (167 lines, blob `410f7edd3f266bcd49f654eca25f96c36b26346c`) retains M=21952, q=1/3 and |a|<=29/20, yielding the punctured-disk bound 238728/5. Replacing the actual root by the original numerical center on the boundary adds at most 200000/3, giving 1716184/15. The actual root, local line equality, simplicity, inner location and full outer uniqueness are retained.

The earlier observation R*(1716184/15)>1 remains correct: that ceiling alone cannot justify a less-than-one normalized-error rounding argument. The new extension and exact integration avoid that sufficient test; they do not improve its numerical constant or erase its pointwise pole-shift cost. The older 3,224-per-mode finite diagnostics and their limitations remain in the initial packet.

## Verification and remaining obligations

The current continuation passed 2,644 finite exact-rational algebra checks in each of normal and optimized Python with identical reports (SHA256 `749054913133264e9a92cb5be49e2522208883fdc42d745617556a1b5140207a`). Two deliberate failure runs were rejected, outside the totals. Coverage: 384 rational polynomial-point configurations, 24 pole-shift cases, repeated/additional-root controls, strict-boundary checks, zero-denominator rejection and the old rounding obstruction. This is NOT contour quadrature, a continuum analytic proof, zeta evaluation, source-verifier execution, independent full arithmetic replay or Lean evidence. Diagnostics remain outside the pure-math repository.

Both new complete files were read back at the exact commit; published blobs match prepared source. Comparison confirms one single-parent commit and only the two additions. The branch update used an expected-head lease without force. Source-text inventory/placeholder/whitespace checks are not parsing or elaboration. Relevant pinned Mathlib dslope/power-series/Cauchy/circle-integral source signatures were inspected at `db584cd6d46c92f209a44c0f1c829460d327499d`.

SourceAcceptance and every outstanding block/terminal/final equality remain OPEN. The local integral is a CONSEQUENCE of the existing conditional isolated simple zero, not an independent root-existence certificate. No complete-height count, canonical global inventory, first-zero ordering, universal simplicity, all-height RH, prime margin or Weil positivity is supplied.

No Lean/Lake/native execution, compilation, repository tests, fresh independent review, full type/import/generated/axiom/native audit, build/worker/replay request, main mutation, merge, issue closure or execution-hold release occurred. body:
## Summary

Adds a design-only proposal (status **PROPOSED**) at
`docs/plans/2026-10-20-enforcement-coverage-custom-tools-and-project-boundary.md`
for the two mutation surfaces the shipped LangChain / Agent SDK gate does not
cover, as measured on `main` by `validation/orchestrator-decision-sandbox/`
(#570, after the relative-path fix #573 `cf6bc40b`):

1. **Custom tool interception** (`unmapped_tool_literal`: `skip`, NOT_EVALUATED, handler ran).
2. **Project-boundary handling** (`write_outside_project_dir`: scoped rule UNKNOWN, `fail_open`, `[mneme] UNEVALUATED`, handler ran).

Contents: current behavior with evidence and line citations; options per gap
with trade-offs and the ADRs / frozen semantics each would touch (ADR-017/018/
019/020/023/027/030/031/033, Layer 1 freeze); recommendations; and a
regression-test proposal for `tests/integrations/` plus a separate sandbox
coverage set.

## Recommendations

- **Gap 1:** documented "propose mutation" call. A custom tool submits its
  full proposed content via the existing `MnemeLangChain.evaluate_tool_call` /
  `MnemeAgentSdk.evaluate_mutation` and honors `deny` before mutating. The tool
  map stays closed; coverage is labeled self-governed, not intercepted. Tool-map
  registration, a Mneme wrapper and Decision MCP routing are assessed and not
  recommended now.
- **Gap 2:** keep fail-open, document the boundary precisely, and leave the
  block to the orchestrator's own policy (root confinement, optional
  refuse-on-UNEVALUATED wrapper). Mneme-side fail-closed for these adapters is
  out of ADR-033 scope and deferred.

## Finding for reviewers

From code reading only, not measured by the sandbox: **unscoped** typed rules
return `APPLIED` for out-of-root paths (`mneme/path_selectors.py:229-240`), so
boundary behavior depends on whether a rule is scoped. The proposal adds a
characterization test before anything relies on this.

## Revision after design review (`92414d5c`)

Direction approved (1B; 2A + 2C; 1A/1C/2B/2D deferred). Corrections applied:

- 1B described as opt-in self-governance; unwired custom tools stay ungoverned.
- Outcome table for every gate action (deny/allow/warn/fail_open/skip); only `allow` is a PASS; no-memory and skipped operations are never presented as checked.
- Reference example returns `[mneme] DENIED` and keeps `[mneme] WARN` / `[mneme] UNEVALUATED` visible.
- Same-path, same-bytes acceptance condition for the example (canonical path, symlinks, `..`), with tests.
- Scoped vs unscoped out-of-root distinction kept, with the characterization test.
- Orchestrator refusals kept separate from Mneme violations in all metrics and evidence.
- New section 5A: CI1 (#540) alignment; Guidance -> Pre-mutation -> CI -> Evidence as separate boundaries; no second parser, resolver or evidence model; CI1 merge blocking not adopted.

## Scope

Docs only. No change to `mneme/`, `docs/adr/`, `.mneme/`, CI, the freeze
document or sandbox evidence. Synthetic examples only. Not to be merged
without owner review.

## Checks

- `mneme check --mode warn` on the new file: PASS (existing ADR freshness warnings only)
- `scripts/check_architecture_docs.py`, `check_encoding.py`, `check_install_command.py`: OK
- `scripts/check_worktree_context.py`: OK before commit

- Change author: agent
- Agent: claude-code
- Agent model: claude-opus-5-5
- Agent session: not-exposed

author: rmcdaniel
body:
## Activity lease maintenance and container logging for Server 2.11

Part of [Workflow #878](https://github.com/durable-workflow/workflow/issues/878), and incorporates #623 / refs #618. A healthy blocking activity must be able to outlive its renewable runtime lease without inventing application heartbeats or changing recorded business deadlines. Worker departure settles only that worker's original claims under the recorded retry policy.

Current exact candidate **`aefb8698e792c4cf0c5cc58ae7072e0123120a34` / whole `e5821c4e9fae5ae9fd56deccd7f8370d3f935afd`** includes current main `bedd60b4c` and logging head `cc4dba7d7`. It keeps published Core **2.10.1 / `1a5ec33f`**, Server **2.11.0 / Helm 0.3.0** and current OpenAPI **56**. Core is the only resolved package change. Native tree **`74c5ed27a00c90a22f8814021422ac4b4dd572b6`**, shared/runner fixtures and frozen actors match current main exactly.

## Implementation

- Optional worker-only activity lease renewal rechecks the original task/attempt, owner/incarnation, namespace and live session under mutation locks. Capability discovery requires the optional Core contract; custom unsupported bridges remain unsupported.
- UTC6 original run/execution deadlines and uncached server time support guarded renewal/status/terminal preflight. Core fences again after slow external resolution.
- Make documented `DW_ACTIVITY_TASK_TIMEOUT` effective as integer 1–86400, default 300. This is a runtime lease, not an authored timeout or retry-policy change.
- Settle exact activity claims atomically on either deregistration route, preserving replacement authority and rollback. Fencing does not physically stop an old user callback.
- Keep the separately qualified pinned PHP 8.3.36 base. No published tag is moved.
- Default image/Kubernetes/Helm logging to stderr, honoring explicit channels and severity. Require eight actual API/queue/scheduler logging checks on produced images before chart publication, including JSON, file override and filtering. Preserve historical immutable recovery contracts and scoped always-cleanup.
- Retain reusable normally installed PHP consumer inputs and the chart upgrade guidance. Generated metadata stays Server 2.11.0 / chart 0.3.0; #623's unpublished intermediate 0.2.4 is not published or reused.

## Evidence and remaining qualification

The prior exact `d9aac032f` passed all applicable feature, database, schema, chart, performance, CodeQL, Sonar and boundary checks. Earlier actual components include 108/956 SQLite, 73/766 MySQL, 73/2,977 PostgreSQL and the overlapping 31/2,764 route/schema selection. Published-Core departure controls also pass on all three databases. [Component evidence](https://github.com/durable-workflow/workflow/issues/878#issuecomment-6323074076).

The prepared production-image PHP SDK 3.2.0 consumer completed a genuine 360-second blocking activity under the normal 300-second lease, with one invocation/attempt, three first-attempt tasks, six events and zero application heartbeats/repairs. A separate named five-second lease owner-loss control recovered the declared second attempt under its original observer. [Exact image, failed observations and inputs](https://github.com/durable-workflow/workflow/issues/878#issuecomment-6325709459).

The combined metadata check and all 28 Helm release controls pass locally. The final test's existing-OCI output is a mock, not registry publication. Logging's parent feature/chart/performance/source checks and Sonar API review pass, with zero OPEN/CONFIRMED and three reasoned accepted serial-I/O findings. Its separate CodeQL Actions analysis was still active when combined. No earlier whole-tree result qualifies this new candidate. Fresh normal hosted checks are required before merge.

Retain failed original `386788572` / run39538649933 and the unrecovered assertion, earlier malformed fixtures, cached clock, namespace and manually late observer failures. The new functional source is not called their rescue. All previous actual source-image, consumer, compiler/dependency/database/raw phases are retired; only pushed source is held.

After exact source qualification, publish Server 2.11.0 / chart 0.3.0, verify the produced image's logging/TLS, and run normally installed PHP 3.2.0, Python 2.8.0 and Rust 4.2.0 through six-minute and killed-worker controls on the published tuple. Those SDK releases already exist; installed Server acceptance remains pending. Keep #618, Workflow #878 and shared #221 open until their own remaining acceptance is met. No native capability, image, catalog adoption or cutover follows.

author: eonsofstupid
body:
Distinct empty or identical-content projects previously received the same project, estate and instance IDs. New installations now require an explicit identity input, preserve deterministic previews, and reject applying a plan to a different initial root before managed effects. Completed estates retain their persisted identity through relocation and replay.

## Owning change brief

OBJ-07 / D-01, POAM-020; standalone qualification depends on merged PR #43. Product version stays 1.0.0 and maturity stays pre-alpha. This does not close D-01 or the broader topology/sync requirements.

- `rrd-contract/src/attunement.rs`: mandatory identity and initial-root digest in installation-plan contract v2; independent attunement/result versions stay v1. Old unbound previews fail explicitly.
- `rrd-engine/src/engine/installation.rs`: explicit OS-entropy identity allocation; deterministic planning; root binding before new/interrupted apply; persisted-authority replay after completed relocation.
- CLI `command.rs` / `installed.rs`: `install identity`, required `install plan --identity`, and version advertisement. Callers retain an identity across previews and allocate a fresh one per independent installation.
- Existing engine/contract/native process tests and SDK callers adopt the required input. The shared SDK corpus retains a fixed fixture identity and the same assertions. No alternate initializer or fallback authority.
- Documentation describes the new contract and the pinned older Connectome/engine pair's limit. Generated discovery remains mechanical. Release-only unused imports now match their existing debug-only helper conditions; helper behavior is unchanged.

## Failure oracle and replacement evidence

The initial regression failed with duplicated IDs. Acceptance requires independent fresh and identical-content estates, foreign-plan/credential rejection without project mutation, unchanged exact-preview bytes, restart/relocation/recovery, and actual staged primary-binary readback. Existing eight-stage recovery remains intact. Inspection found no new algorithm needing research or upstream adaptation; existing entropy, digest, transaction and trace boundaries remain authoritative. No performance or signed-distribution claim. Stop on lost isolation, silent identity reuse, changed recovery behavior, dirty provenance or any required CI failure.

Package journals carry exact baseline, files/symbols, read/change traceability, commands, failures and limits:
- `docs/evidence/change-journals/gate-d/d-01-independent-installation-identities.md`
- `docs/evidence/change-journals/gate-d/d-01-combined-identity-qualification.md`
- `docs/evidence/change-journals/gate-d/d-01-identity-release-qualification.md`

## Validation

author: jeongjaesoon
body:
## 왜

세션 상세(W10b)에서 승인 응답·제어·메시지 전송을 하려면 `@agent-platform/react`에 mutation hook이 있어야 하고, SSE 이벤트가 오면 관련 query가 새로 읽혀야 한다. 94S-687.

## 범위

- `useAnswer`(POST `/answers`), `useSendMessage`(POST `/messages`, `mode: "enqueue"`), `useSessionControl`(POST `/interrupt`·`/pause`·`/resume`·`/terminate`)을 더한다. 모두 기존 엔드포인트다. client에 빠진 호출은 없었다.
- 성공한 명령만 캐시를 무효화한다. 실패하면 오류를 호출자에게 넘기고 캐시는 그대로 둔다.
- Idempotency-Key는 mutate 호출마다 한 번 정해서 react-query 재시도에도 유지한다. 키는 호출마다 따로 생기는 `MutationFunctionContext`에 묶는다(onMutate에서 정하고, 시도마다 같은 키를 읽는다). 그래서 같은 변수 객체로 호출이 겹쳐도 각자 키를 지킨다. 기존 `useChangeSessionProfile`도 같은 방식으로 바꿨다.
- `useSessionEvents`가 받는 이벤트로 query를 무효화한다. `status`는 목록·상세·pending·usage, `question`은 상세·pending, `result`는 상세·usage, `error`는 상세를 무효화한다. 메시지·도구 이벤트는 아무것도 무효화하지 않는다.
- 무효화 filter는 core factory(`sessionsQuery`·`sessionQuery`·`pendingRequestsQuery`·`sessionUsageQuery`)로만 만든다. 목록과 상세 key는 다른 key의 prefix라서 `exact: true`를 준다.
- 화면(apps/web), packages/client·contracts·core는 바꾸지 않는다.

## 트레이드오프

- 이벤트 묶기: 이벤트가 오면 stale한 부분을 Set에 모으고 `setTimeout(0)` 한 번으로 flush한다. client는 한 번 읽은 chunk의 frame을 동기로 전달하고, 이미 버퍼에 있는 chunk도 microtask로 이어 읽는다. 그래서 연결 직후의 replay나 바쁜 turn이 쏟아내는 이벤트는 query마다 refetch 한 번으로 줄어든다. 테스트에서는 6개 이벤트에 무효화 4번이었다. 묶기를 빼면 이 테스트가 실패하는 것을 확인했다.
- 5초 `refetchInterval` 폴링은 그대로 둔다. 폴링을 줄이는 일은 화면을 붙일 때(W10b) 판단한다.
- 저장(dehydrate)했다가 복원한 pending mutation은 onMutate를 건너뛰어서 시도마다 새 키가 생긴다. 이 repo는 mutation을 저장하지 않으므로 다루지 않는다(Codex 3회차 Noted).
- hook 테스트는 W24(#492)가 먼저 더한 devDependencies(`@agent-platform/ui`의 setupDom, happy-dom, Testing Library)와 `/// <reference lib="dom" />`를 그대로 쓴다. base merge 뒤에는 package.json과 bun.lock이 diff에서 빠졌다.

## 영향 범위

- 기존 `useSessionEvents`는 이벤트 window·도구 이름 연결 동작을 그대로 유지한다(기존 web 세션 테스트 통과). `useChangeSessionProfile`은 키 생성 시점만 바뀐다.
- 공개 계약·DB·API는 바뀌지 않는다.

## 검증

- `bun test packages/react packages/core packages/ui apps/web`(bun 1.3.14): 통과. 전체 `bun run test`에서는 실패 5개가 나왔는데 모두 `ci-services.sh` 테스트이고, macOS에 GNU `timeout`이 없어서 생기는 로컬 환경 문제다. 판정은 CI로 한다.
- 일부러 결함을 넣어 테스트를 확인했다: `onSuccess`를 `onSettled`로 바꾸면 500 테스트가 실패하고, 이벤트마다 즉시 무효화하면 burst 테스트가 실패한다. 재시도 키 테스트는 고치기 전에 실패하고 고친 뒤 통과한다.
- 라이브(fake model, compose project `verify-ap-20261021-102321-28156`): hook과 같은 본문으로 answers(202 → pending 0 → turn 1 completed), messages(202, turn 2), interrupt(turn 2 interrupted), pause(paused), resume(resuming), terminate(stopped)를 보냈다. 이벤트 스트림에는 question·status·result가 왔다. 끝난 뒤 스택을 내렸고 남은 컨테이너는 없다.
- 검증하지 못한 것: 브라우저에서의 hook 동작. 아직 hook을 쓰는 화면이 없고 W10b에서 붙인다.

review-scope: `/code-review` 대신 Codex 독립 리뷰(2회차) / security-review 미해당(인증·암호화 변경 없음, 입력은 기존 client 경로) / blast-radius 미해당(공개 계약·마이그레이션 변경 없음, react 내부 hook 추가)

author: irvingoujatdevolution
body:
Searching every recording doesn't fit in one response, so `POST /jet/jrec/search` now returns pages.

A page ends after reading about 16 MiB of logs or after `maxHits` hits, from 1 to 1000 and 1000 by default; 0 or more than 1000 is a 400. `nextCursor` replaces `limitReached`: sending the same `query`, `recordings` and `startTime` with it as `cursor` gets the next page, until a page has no `nextCursor`.

Gateway keeps no state between pages. The cursor holds the recording, file, byte offset and line number to resume at, plus a hash of the search, so a cursor sent with another search is a 400. A cursor whose position cannot exist is a 400 too, and its file name is only matched against the recording's manifest, never joined into a path. Pages never go back, so a recording that starts behind the cursor while paging isn't searched. The paging rules are in `search.intent.md`.

author: vericommons
body:
## Contract
A completed remote signing operation remains bound to one operation ID and signing input when its HTTP response is lost. A durable result query returns the original signature after reopening the journal; an identical retry does not invoke the signing key again, and a changed input is rejected.

## Evidence
The loopback HTTP regression drops the first completed signing response after SQLite completion, compares the recovered signature with the committed result, and checks the operation ID, TBS hash, signing call count, retry, and changed-input rejection.

## Limit
The key is synthetic and the journal reopens in the same process. This does not establish external provider idempotency, process-crash recovery, hardware custody, or CSC behavior.

## Scope
Stacked draft on #47. Offline-only, non-authorizing REGISTER transaction correlation; no production TLS/Kerberos/SSPI, sign-in, network interoperability, or changes to main.

## Source → requirement → tests
- RFC 3261 (June 2002) §8.1.1.7 (Via branch magic cookie) and §17.1.3 (client transaction matching). This change applies a **deliberately restrictive fixture policy**, not a claim that RFC 3261 mandates the project's 128-byte cap or its limited character subset.
- `crates/commscraft-core/src/offline_register_branch.rs`: `FixtureRegisterBranch::new_fixture` validates the exact `z9hG4bK` cookie, a nonempty suffix, ≤128 bytes, and a restricted ASCII character set. `rejects_unbounded_injected_or_non_cookie_branches` rejects CRLF, non-ASCII, unsupported punctuation, missing suffix and 129-byte input, and accepts 128 bytes.
- `crates/commscraft-transport/src/offline_register_branch.rs` re-exports the **same core type**; `crates/commscraft-transport/src/offline_register_security_handoff.rs` uses it for REGISTER handoff; `crates/commscraft-core/src/tls_boundary.rs` uses it for fixture correlation. Existing offline correlation and security-boundary tests run in CI.

author: lucaspanjer
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"lucaspanjer"} -->
_Requested by **Lucas** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_011N5bix1hLRiX5hyS1gJx7d?thread=cmsg_011N5bix1hLRiX5hyS1gJx7dWhttHYwBCoR9JdzbseZLts)_

## Why

Questrade refresh tokens are single-use. When two processes share one, as optionator-ws and the CLI/TUI do through the same config, whichever refreshes first invalidates the token the other holds in memory, and the other fails at its next refresh. That's the "auth breaks after about a day" in optionator-web. With only a save callback, the client had no way to read back a token another process had just written.

## What

- **`TokenStore` trait** replaces `OnTokenRefresh`. It has `save` plus optional `lock` and `load`. On each refresh the manager takes the lock (on a blocking thread) and calls `load`. If another holder just fetched a valid access token, it adopts that; otherwise it uses their newer refresh token. Then it refreshes, calls `save`, and unlocks. Stores are always explicit types, and closures are not accepted.
- **`TokenManager::builder(refresh_token)`** replaces `new`/`new_with_login_url`. Its options are `.practice()`, `.login_url()`, `.store()` and `.cached()` (which accepts an `Option`), followed by `.build().await`. With no options it keeps tokens in memory.
- **Single refresh for concurrent 401s.** Retries now pass the rejected access token, so requests that all got 401 with the same token share one refresh.
- **Cancel-safe refresh.** The refresh runs on its own spawned task, so a dropped caller can't abandon it after Questrade rotated the token but before it was stored.
- New `QuestradeError::TokenStore` variant, and the library now enables tokio's `rt` feature.
- Version bumped to **0.3.0**. README, crate docs, examples and CHANGELOG are updated.

## Testing

`cargo test`, clippy (`-D warnings`), fmt and docs pass locally. CI also covers 1.88. New tests cover:
- using the refresh token from the store
- adopting a stored access token without an HTTP call
- not adopting the token that was just rejected
- five concurrent 401s causing exactly one refresh
- saving while the lock is held
- a refresh that completes after its caller timed out

The optionator side is lucaspanjer/optionator#73.

author: shenxingy
body:
## Verdict
The weekly radar cron can no longer leave unverified edits in someone's checkout. Each run edits only its own worktree. The wrapper then verifies those edits in a no-network sandbox and commits them to a local `radar/<date>` branch for review. Nothing is pushed.

## Why
The agent ran from cron's cwd (`$HOME`) and edited whichever Clade checkout was open. The 10-12 run's edits sat on `fix/warm-pace` for four days, and the 10-19 run's on `main`, where another session's Stop hook found them. The agent cannot run bash or git, so the run that wrote those edits never verified or committed them.

## How (`configs/scripts/radar-cron.sh`)
1. **Own worktree.**
   - The wrapper creates a worktree of the kit on a fresh `radar/<date>` branch from `origin/main`, placed outside `~/.claude` because the harness refuses edits there.
   - The agent runs with that worktree as its cwd. Measured on 2.1.283 with `acceptEdits`: outside its cwd the agent is refused even a Read, so no other checkout is reachable.
   - `--add-dir` grants the read-only inputs the lanes need.
2. **Verify in a sandbox.** The wrapper runs `bash -n` on every changed shell file, plus the suites that name a changed file, inside `bwrap`:
   - no network;
   - filesystem read-only except the worktree and a private `/tmp`.

   This closes the security fork the 10-12 TODO named: the run reads the open web and the private correction history, so it must not get an exfiltration path or write access to the host. Without `bwrap` (macOS), files are parse-checked only and the record says the suites were not run.
3. **Commit, never push.** The wrapper commits to the local branch with the verification in the commit message, removes the worktree, and leaves the branch. The edits came from a run that read the open web and private history, and a public repository is not where an unreviewed copy of that goes. `session-context.sh` lists `radar/*` branches when a session opens the kit.

Staged digests now go in `.radar-staged/` inside the worktree, ignored through `info/exclude`. `$HOME` staging still folds for older runs.

## Evidence
- `tests/test-radar-cron.sh` (new, registered in `shell-tests`) passes 24/24, using a stub agent. 7 mutations each turn it red: agent run from `$HOME`, worktree kept, push added, `bash -n` skipped, suites run unsandboxed, empty-run branch kept, session notice removed.
- **Live, with the real claude binary through the new wrapper**, on a throwaway clone:
  - the agent's edit landed on `radar/2099-01-01`;
  - its attempt on the main checkout did not happen (`TODO.md` hash unchanged);
  - `tests/test-hooks.sh` ran sandboxed and passed;
  - the commit message carries that record;
  - the worktree was removed.
- `ci-local.py` passed 5/5 jobs, including the new suite.

## What changes
- Each merge job records the design's seven steps (**Fetch → Rebase → Push → Re-run checks → GitHub checks → Already-fixed check → Merge**) with state (pending, running, done, skipped, failed, stopped, unknown) and start/end times, inside its existing `merge_jobs` JSON record. No schema version change; records saved before this have no `steps` and show as before.
- Preparation (`PreMergeCoordinator.start`) and the guarded merge (`MergeCoordinator.merge`, `onAsking`) report steps through display-only callbacks: a failed step write is logged and never stops the job.
- **Cancel merge** (`POST /api/action {action: "cancel-merge", jobId}`) stops the job and its preparation without cancelling the task. The task keeps its status, its PR stays open, and Merge PR can be clicked again. Refused once the job's merge attempt exists (GitHub was asked), and while the task itself is being cancelled. A restart after a cancel settles the job `cancelled`.
- The review screen shows the list under the review strip, with icon + word + color per DESIGN.md, elapsed time, and the Cancel button (marked unavailable, `aria-disabled`, once the Merge step starts).
- The merge job saves its waiting checks only when they change (it starts with none), so unchanged inspections add no revision and the page's poll backs off.
- DESIGN.md: the step marks (○ Waiting, ● Running, – Skipped, ! Stopped, ! Unknown) added to the status table and decision log, approved by the user.

author: johan-de-r
body:
## Problem
DeepInfra accepts gzip request bodies on every endpoint, but inbound compression is barely used. The Request Compression page (#21) is the only place it appears, it sits under API Features, and its examples use raw `requests`/`fetch`, while the quickstart and every other page use the OpenAI SDK. So someone trying the API never runs into it, and someone already on the SDK has no recipe for it. Its raw Python/JS examples also sent the literal string `$DEEPINFRA_API_KEY` as the bearer token.

## Why it matters
Large bodies (long chat histories, embeddings batches) usually compress 4–8×, which cuts customer upload bandwidth and latency at no cost to us.

## Fix
- `request-compression.mdx`: the guide now opens with a **With the OpenAI SDK** section (a Python `event_hooks` hook and a JavaScript custom `fetch`). The existing cURL, `requests` and `fetch` examples move under **Without an SDK**, and **When it helps** no longer argues against always-on hooks.
  - Both compress every JSON body and leave file uploads alone. There is no size cutoff: gzip only grows a body under ~150 B (`"Hello!"` gains 9 B), and a one-sentence chat request already shrinks.
  - Python: needs `openai` ≥ 1.17 (`DefaultHttpxClient`). Using `type(request.stream)` keeps it working on the httpx releases and the httpx2 releases (3.x). It skips bodies that already have a `Content-Encoding`, so a redirect hop isn't compressed twice. It also skips empty bodies, because openai-python sends `Content-Type: application/json` on GET and DELETE too. The `AsyncOpenAI` variant is one line.
  - JavaScript: needs openai-node 5 or later (native `fetch`), on Node.js, Bun or Deno. It uses the web-standard `CompressionStream`, with no `node:zlib`, `Buffer` or `duplex`. The compressed body is a buffered `Blob`: it keeps a `Content-Length`, survives a 307 redirect (Node's `fetch` can't resend a detached `ArrayBuffer`), and avoids streaming-upload support, which Firefox and Safari lack. openai-node 4 isn't covered, because it passes its proxy agent to `fetch` and native `fetch` ignores it.
  - The raw Python/JS examples now read `DEEPINFRA_API_KEY` from the environment, and the raw `fetch` example also uses `CompressionStream`.
- `quickstart.mdx`: a short **Compress large requests** section after the SDK install step, with the gzip cURL call and a link to the guide.
- `chat/overview.mdx` (multi-turn) and `apis/embeddings.mdx` (batch): a tip that links to the guide.

## Validation
- I copied every snippet verbatim from the MDX, changing only the base URL, and ran it against a local server that wraps deepapi's real `GzipRequestMiddleware`. Tested on: Python `openai` 1.17.0, 1.46.0 and 3.35.1; Node `openai` 5.23.2, 6.49.0 and 7.39.0, also under Bun 1.4.3 and Deno 2.9.6; the cURL, raw `requests` and raw `fetch` examples.
  - Every JSON request, including the examples' own `"Hello!"`, arrived with `Content-Encoding: gzip`, a compressed body, a `Content-Length` and the real API key.
  - The raw `fetch` example ran on Node.js 20, Bun and Deno.
  - `files.create` arrived as plain multipart on every SDK and runtime.

## Resumen

Fix de reporte Mariano 2026-10-20: modal **Análisis de Cartera por Vendedor** mostraba 16 clientes para MAURICIO GIL vs los **58 reales**. Causa: `v_cartera_vendor` (v1283) leía solo de `client_master.vendor`, que está sparse (**425/577 docs = 73% con vendor=null**). La fuente REAL del mapping vendor↔cliente vive en `client_applications.assignedVendor` (mismo pattern que PBI usa via `assigned_vendor_app`).

## Breakdown del impacto (58 cardCodes reales de MAURICIO)

| Estado en client_master | Count |
|---|---:|
| vendor='MAURICIO GIL' ✓ (correctos v1283) | 11 |
| vendor=null / vacío ✗ | 7 |
| vendor='OTRO' ✗ (data sucia a conciliar) | 3 |
| no existe en client_master ✗ | 37 |

## Fix

`bigquery/views.sql` — reescribir CTE `cartera`:

```sql
WITH cartera AS (
  SELECT * EXCEPT (source_priority) FROM (
    -- PRIMARIA: client_applications (fuente real negocio, igual que PBI)
    SELECT ..., 1 AS source_priority FROM client_applications_raw_raw_latest
    WHERE cardCodeSap+assignedVendor seteados
    UNION ALL
    -- FALLBACK: client_master (legacy sin alta en apps)
    SELECT ..., 2 AS source_priority FROM client_master_raw_raw_latest
    WHERE sapCardCode+vendor seteados
  )
  QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY card_code ORDER BY source_priority) = 1
)
```

Mantiene canonical UPPER + alias `MARTIN BOIERO → PACHI`. Zero cambios en los demás CTEs (visitas_agg, compras_agg, deuda_agg) ni el SELECT final.

Bump a v1381 porque v1380 ya estaba tomado por PR #1107 (fix stock mergeado en paralelo).

## Deploy ejecutado antes del PR

- `python scripts/deploy_v_cartera_vendor.py` — view LIVE en BQ ✓
- `gcloud scheduler jobs run firebase-schedule-syncCarteraVendorScheduled-southamerica-east1` — snapshot `cartera_vendor/*` regenerado 01:23 UTC ✓

## Smoke post-deploy (BQ + Firestore live)

```

```

APP_VERSION v1380 → v1381. CACHE_VERSION v1380 → v1381.

## Test plan

- [ ] Idem FEDERICO 80, PACHI 60, GONZALO 65, IOANNIS 31, SANTIAGO 26.

author: joenunnelley
body:
Summary
    
    Makes the tool reliable on large organizations and enterprises. It adds HTTP retries, better rate-limit handling, a faster way to collect active committers, resumable runs, and clear reporting when a repository's committers can't be fetched.
    
    Reliability and API handling
    
    - Shared HTTP session with retries: all requests now go through one session. It retries 500/502/503/504 errors and connection failures with exponential backoff, has a 30s timeout, and logs a warning on every retry.
    - Rate-limit handling rewritten:
      - Handles both primary and secondary rate limits, using Retry-After, X-RateLimit-Reset, or the "secondary rate limit" message in a 403.
      - Retries the request after sleeping, up to 3 times, instead of just sleeping.
      - Removed the fixed 1s sleep after every request. Requests are now only slowed down when fewer than 500 calls remain, spread over the time left until the reset.
      - Gateway errors without rate-limit headers are no longer mistaken for an exhausted limit.
    - New GitHubAPIError and a graphql_query() helper: GraphQL errors, non-JSON responses and HTTP errors are all raised the same way.
    - A 401 stops the run: whether listing repositories or fetching committers, it raises immediately and cancels queued work instead of flagging every repository as failed.
    - GraphQL URL logic: the GitHub.com vs. GHES mapping now lives in one place, get_graphql_url(), and handles a trailing slash.
    - Enterprise org listing: raises a clear error when the enterprise isn't found and skips null org entries.
    
    Faster active-committer collection
    
    - Two-step fetch:
      - A lightweight query lists branch tips and the default branch, paging through all branches. Before, only the first 100 branches were checked.
      - History is then walked one branch at a time.
    - Skips needless work:
      - Branches whose latest commit is older than 90 days.
      - Branches whose tip was already reached through another branch.
      - The rest of a branch once it reaches history that was already walked. The default branch is walked first so this happens as early as possible.
    - Adapts to timeouts: if GitHub times out (502/504) on a history query, the page size is halved, down to a minimum of 10, and the same page is retried.
    - Public repositories: they are skipped before any API call because they don't use GHAS licenses.
    - Progress logging: a line every 25 requests on long-running repositories, plus elapsed time per repository.
    - Fixed a bug where committers could be assigned to the wrong repository. Results from as_completed were matched by position, so they could go to a different repository than the one fetched.
    - UTC-aware 90-day window.
    
    New CLI options
    
    - --checkpoint PATH: active committers are saved per repository to a JSONL file as they are fetched. Re-running the same command skips repositories already in the file. Repositories that failed are not saved, so they are retried on the next run.
    - --include-inactive: includes archived repositories. Behavior change: archived repositories are now excluded by default.
    
    Reporting
    
    - Failed fetches are flagged: repositories whose committers couldn't be fetched get committers_fetch_failed, are left out of the recommendations, and are listed under a new WARNING section in the text report.
    - JSON output: includes repos_with_unknown_committers and a per-repository committers_fetch_failed field.
    - Zero repositories: current_coverage_percentage no longer divides by zero.
    
    Other
    
    - Repository listing errors: HTTP errors other than 401 now log an error and continue with partial results for that org. Before, they raised an error, including a specific "not found" message for 404.
    - main.py is now executable and has a shebang.
    - .gitignore adds *.swp, .venv and output.
    - README documents the new options and how to use checkpoints.
    
    Tests
    
    - Tests now mock requests.Session.request and assert the exact GHES GraphQL URL.
    - New tests cover the GraphQL URL mapping, stopping on a 401 (repository listing and committer fetch), and per-repository flagging of non-auth errors.
    
    ---
    Two things for reviewers: the archived-by-default change, and the switch from raising to logging when an org's repositories can't be listed. You may want to keep or reword those two points depending on whether they were intended.
    
    I also noticed --include-inactive really means "include archived". The help text could say that directly.

Validate authenticated relay-trust settings before any native writer can apply them. The helper checks device/relay binding, immutable and monotonic generation identity, canonical distinct roots, content fingerprint and effective validity. Native OpenSSL verifies each root's self-signature with ambient trust/configuration excluded. Unsupported signatures, weak RSA-PSS parameters, non-signing CAs and unknown critical extensions are refused.

Verification returns a detached snapshot and removes temporary public scratch on success or failure. Receipt parsing correlates exact generation/content identity. This component sends no requests, persists no trust and does not restart or report application. Native persistence, reload/rollback, lost-receipt retry, bootstrap migration and offline recovery remain later acceptance.

Native component validation at d4ac78d, unchanged by the main/documentation integration at 74dd995:

- Actual local OpenSSL tests: 49 passed. Positive PSS fixtures explicitly select digest-length salt and matching MGF hash; negative overrides still verify rejection of weak hashes and incorrect salt lengths across OpenSSL releases.
- Actual OPNsense source/model tests: 489 passed, one Schema test skipped because jsonschema is absent from the native harness. Source, result and log artifacts were exported with hashes. Configuration and installed 0.0.6 stayed unchanged; temporary test keys were removed.
- Secure-client unsigned 0.0.12 built on OPNsense in 58.538 seconds with Go 1.26.10/frp 0.71.1, verified licenses and zero swap activity. The exported package contains the verifier and the expected rebuilt client. SHA256: e2ce9eb2789aaa1d1e3049fd76c287313ae0ece6ac2c647cf1c3db20e15fa705. Installed configuration/client/package stayed unchanged. No installation, signature or release is claimed.
- Current exact-head hosted run 39703265810 passed all six jobs; actual logs and six DCO sign-offs were inspected. Linux plugin checks passed 573 cases with seven platform skips. Mandatory issuance/delivery/renewal/account-provisioning and cleanup receipts were true; real host SQL and combined PostgreSQL/CA recovery ran before teardown. author: slepp
body:
## Why

After the 0.6.2 release tag, main needs to identify the next development cycle. Shallow builds must report clean source correctly, and release preparation must reflect the supported platforms and their actual priority.

## What

Open 0.6.3 development and fix shallow-checkout dirty detection. Retire Intel macOS from qualification, packaging and installer selection while retaining Apple silicon. Record Linux x86_64/aarch64 as primary and macOS ARM as secondary; major build/run regressions block on every supported OS, while other patch-release failures are assessed against Linux benefits and platform complexity with an owned follow-up. Standalone WASI/non-browser Wasm remains non-gating in the 0.6 series unless needed for browser compiler/VM execution. Publish existing Rust test reports before long native acceptance jobs.

## Test

Make lint, workflow validation, build-harness tests, version producer tests and installer release-order tests pass. The built compiler reports the next development version with the actual commit distance from the release tag. Existing version controls exercise released/development identities, shallow history and real source changes. Keep same-architecture Mach-O execution and generic LLVM target coverage; remove only the retired Darwin cross-architecture distribution test.

author: alpaconstrutora
body:
## O quê
Sobra S3 da casa automática (pedido de 20/10/2026, em `docs/planos/2026-10-14-casa-automatica.md`).

- No 10 × 30 de 2 dormitórios (3 pavimentos), o 2º (a suíte, maior que o programa do 1º) enchia o 1º recuado e não alinhava ao patamar; o 1º voltava à pegada do térreo (dormitório de 52,9 m²). Nenhum 1º recuado servindo, o 1º agora é o menor retângulo **em volta do 2º** alinhado em que o corredor do 1º também cai no patamar: 5,40 × 7,60 m, dormitório de 20,55 m².
- O quadro passa a exigir parede corrida em comum com os pavimentos de cima (hipótese `paredeMinimaDoQuadroMm`, 600 mm): caía no cruzamento de 200 mm com a fachada do 1º recuado, dentro da porta do térreo, e a prumada subia pela janela do 1º.

## Medido
- 8 casas de referência idênticas ao marco; 6 lotes de 3 pavimentos com 0 encontros e 0 pilares.
- Pendências do caso: 7 → 4.

## Teste (falha sem cada parte)
`blueprintCasaAutomatica.test.ts` › "10 × 30, 2 dorm.": o 1º recuado em volta do 2º; dormitório do 1º < 25 m²; nenhum trecho em vão de porta/janela.

## 변경 목적과 결과

- M1-S(`ai/m1_stage/`)가 내는 혈압 4단계 step(normal / elevated / prehtn / htn)과 생활 데이터로 A군 10개 상태를 판정하는 규칙 모듈 **`ai/m2_state/`**(독립 패키지, v0.2.0)를 추가합니다. 혈압 수치는 받지도 계산하지도 않습니다(7일 평균·밴드·가드는 M1 역할).
- 구현 4개: ELEVATED, PREHTN(위험인자 목록 포함), HTN_SUSPECT(미치료자), NOCTURNAL_SCREEN(수면 증상 분기).
- 나머지 6개(HTN_STAGE2_SCREEN, ISH, WHITE_COAT, MASKED, MORNING, RESISTANT_SUSPECT)는 지금 결정 가능한 부분(약 복용자 not_applicable, 미복용자 negative 등)만 판정하고, 혈압 조건은 M1 추가 필드가 올 때까지 `not_evaluable` + `missing_required` 에 필요한 필드명을 적습니다(`docs/m1_interface.md`).
- 원칙은 상위 `ai/` 와 같습니다. 임계값은 `thresholds.py` 한 곳, 입력 계약은 `feature_contract.yaml` 한 곳, 범위 밖은 클리핑 없이 `out_of_range` 거부, 출력은 상태 코드·숫자만(금지 표현·비ASCII 테스트).
- `ai/README.md` 모델 표와 구조 트리에 한 줄씩 추가했습니다. 기존 모델·`m1_stage/` 와 import 관계는 없습니다.

```bash
cd ai/m2_state && python3 -m pytest          # 210 passed
python3 scripts/report_tests.py              # 규칙별 결과표 → docs/test_results.md
python3 scripts/make_golden.py               # 골든 20건(초안) 재생성, 의도 상태와 불일치 0
```

- step 값별(4단계 × 상태), 필수 항목 결측, 복약 상태 ①②③, 계약 검증·변환, 출력 표현, 골든 회귀.

- [x] 기능 작업은 `feature/* → develop`입니다.
- [ ] 릴리스/핫픽스인 경우 `main`과 `develop` 양쪽 반영을 확인했습니다. (해당 없음)

author: alxnddr
body:
### Description

`mb query --help --json` inlined 25.9k chars of JSON Schema, and it could not say which fields an older server rejects. `mb schema <command>` prints the body, or the output with `--output`, as TypeScript. Every enforced rule appears as a type or a `//` note. A gated field names its feature. The note adds `this server rejects it` when the cached profile lacks the feature, and `this server ignores it` for a field that server drops. `--json` prints the JSON Schema with the same notes, never judged. No request is sent.

A unit test checks 19,040 rule breaks and fails if tsc or a note misses any of them. Each note is judged against that member's own notes, bound included. An e2e lane checks each client input against the server's OpenAPI document. A unit test makes sure every body-sending method is either checked there or listed with a reason. The lane caught `client.dashboard.create` taking `dashcards` and `tabs`, which the server ignores. `DashboardCreateInput` is now closed, so passing them fails to compile.

The renderer is hand-written. The two existing libraries cannot render the MBQL dispatch.

### How to verify

1. `bun run build`, then `node packages/cli/dist/cli.mjs schema field update` notes `needs fieldDataSensitivity (v64+)`.
2. `bun run check` and `bun run test:e2e` pass.

author: potrock
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"Potrock"} -->
_Requested by **Patrick** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01QiJZSJCRVPmEMJ8y2mnXcK?thread=cmsg_01QiJZSJCRVPmEMJ8y2mnXcK75Mm73kLFMQW4QAahJ1nsQ)_

## What this is

A fix for team mode. A team researches one tech together (`shareResearch`), and until now the last `research` order always won. When a tech finished, both people got "Choose what to research next" and both picked, so the second pick silently replaced the first. A teammate could also replace your choice at any point without you noticing.

**Research**
- The `research` order now carries `was`, the research the chooser saw. If a teammate (a person) chose something since, their choice stands and the late order fails with "Bo just chose Pottery for the team". The tree redraws with their pick, so you can still change it on purpose.
- In the tech tree, changing research that a person on your team chose now asks first ("Bo chose Pottery for the team. Research Writing instead?"). Your own picks, and picks made by a bot teammate, don't ask.
- `researchBy` is set only when a choice actually goes through. Before, it was also set on a refused order.

**Other team-mode inconsistencies found in the audit and fixed here**
- **Lost team science.** On a team, a turn with nothing being researched threw away all of the team's science. Science left over from a tech that finished with nothing queued was lost too. A civ playing alone keeps both as `spareScience`. Teams now keep both as well, and whichever teammate chooses next spends all of the team's spare science.
- **A bot teammate could sell the team's peace.** A bot on a team with people refused peace offers through `wantsPeace`, but a peace *deal* sweetened with gold went through `evaluate` instead, and that could accept it. Accepting ended the whole team's war (`endWar` pairs every member). The bot now declines any deal that includes peace when it is teamed with people.

**Found, but left alone (design calls)**
- Any one person can still make peace or declare war for the whole team without the others agreeing. That is the same "one teammate overrides the other" pattern as research, but it matches Civ V's rules.
- The spaceship (science victory) and cultural influence (culture victory) are counted per civ, not pooled across the team. Score, domination and diplomatic votes are pooled.

## Screenshot or clip

None. The tree change is a confirm dialog that uses the existing `ask()`.

## Checklist

- [ ] `npm run build` passes: not run, because the container has no wasm-pack. `tsc --noEmit` shows no errors in `src/games/blockilization` (the only errors are the missing `@engine/voxel_engine.js` build output), and `check-boundaries` passes.
- [ ] `npm run test:headless`: not run, for the same reason. The rules cases (`tests/effects.ts`) pass, 225 of 225, including 3 new ones: simultaneous picks, science kept while nothing is chosen, and a bot refusing to sell peace. The bot case fails on `main`.
- [x] No new imports outside the game
- [x] No new names or assets

author: b3hr4d
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"b3hr4d"} -->
_Requested by **Behrad** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01Xc58tH9QUGj15xWqTKYhQp?thread=cmsg_01Xc58tH9QUGj15xWqTKYhQpKLfst6Qs8HEtUBWiJVVE59)_

Before: the wallet had no accounts. `accounts`, `add_account` and `balance` did not exist, and a `Transfer` proposal was refused.

After: an owner adds ICP and ICRC accounts, every member lists them and reads their balances from the ledgers, and `Transfer` actions send tokens, at most once each. A transfer that keeps its chain's spending over the last 24 hours within the daily limit is released at once.

**Accounts.** An account is an ICRC-1 account of the wallet's own principal. Index `n` of a chain is subaccount `n` as 32 big-endian bytes, so index 0 is the plain principal and the address of index 1 ends in `.1`, as you chose on 2026-10-21 (recorded as `docs/decisions/0002-subaccounts.md`). Adding one needs no approval, since it moves nothing, and a wallet has at most 64. The wallet reaches the ICP ledger through its ICRC-1 interface, and an `Icrc` chain may not name it, so ICP tokens have one daily limit. Bitcoin and EVM accounts are refused for now.

**At most once.** Each `execute` of a transfer makes one bounded-wait `icrc1_transfer`, and a second `execute` while it is in flight is refused. The call carries a `created_at_time`. When the wallet cannot tell whether a call ran (it timed out, its answer does not decode, or the wallet's code after it trapped, which a drop guard records), the next `execute` reuses that time, so the ledger answers with the earlier block; `Duplicate` counts as sent. Ledgers find a repeated transfer for 24 hours, so such an action stays open that long and cannot be rejected. Only a reject by the IC before the ledger ran the call (`SysFatal`, `SysTransient`, `DestinationInvalid`) counts as not run; a reject from the ledger itself, a stopped ledger's included, may follow a committed transfer, so it counts as unknown (Codex's finding). A refusal (too little in the account, a wrong fee) ends the action `Failed`, unless an earlier call may have run: a ledger checks the fee before it looks for a repeat, so then the action stays ready (Codex's finding).

**Daily limit.** A chain's spending is what it sent in the last 24 hours plus what its open transfers under the limit may still send, so several small proposals cannot pass the limit together. `execute` checks the limit again, so a lowered limit stops a transfer proposed under the old one. Under a Transfer rule of one approval and no timelock, as in the default policy, the limit changes nothing.

How: `accounts.rs` (accounts and their addresses), `transfers.rs` (checks, the ledger argument, reading the answer) and the attempt state in `actions.rs` are pure; `ledger.rs` makes the calls; `lib.rs` adds `accounts`, `add_account`, `balance` and the transfer branch of `execute`. Sent transfers go to memory 6, which the daily limit reads; accounts to memory 3, both as `docs/design.md` planned. Memory 11 is a transfer clock: every fresh ledger call gets a `created_at_time` no other call has, so two identical transfers executed in one round are both sent (Codex's finding).

**Worth your review**
- Interface: `AuditEvent` gains `AccountAdded : AccountId`, one entry per `add_account`. `Pending.expires_at_ns` can now be later than its window, for a transfer whose call may have run.
- New dependency: `icrc-ledger-types` 0.2.0, DFINITY's, for the ICRC-1 account text form and the ledger's transfer types.
- Stored format: `StoredPending` gains two optional fields; actions stored by step 7 decode with both absent, and the upgrade test now carries an open action across the upgrade.
- ICP's 64-character hex account identifiers are not accepted as a `to` yet; only ICRC-1 account text is.
- `history` is not exported yet: memory 6 holds only what the wallet sent, and incoming transfers need the ledgers' index canisters.
- The Wasm is 3.10 MB, or 715 KB gzipped (step 7: 2.74 MB and 656 KB), mostly Candid decoding of the ledger types.

**Tests.** The PocketIC tests install the ICRC-1 ledger Wasm from the dfinity/ic release `ledger-suite-icrc-2025-09-01` (CI pins the checksum its `SHA256SUMS` lists) at the ICP ledger's mainnet id on the NNS subnet, and as a token on the wallet's subnet. They check addresses against the mapping written out in the test; balances; a transfer with a memo and fee to the wallet's own subaccount and on from it; a stopped ledger, then started, sending once; two `execute` calls at once; two identical actions executed together; insufficient funds and a wrong fee; the checks at `propose`; the daily limit with open transfers and its 24-hour window; and the check again at `execute`. A property test drives the attempt state against a model ledger that sends, loses the answer, traps the callback, stalls or refuses, and checks that the tokens are sent at most once, that a transfer ends `Executed` only if they were, and that one sent unheard stays open while the ledger can find it.

**Faults.** Injected one at a time, each made at least one test fail: little-endian subaccounts; every transfer sent from the default subaccount; no in-flight lock; open transfers not counted against the daily limit; no limit check at `execute`; sent transfers not recorded; a call that did not run failing the transfer; `balance` asking for the caller's account; `add_account` not audited; `Icrc` allowed to name the ICP ledger; `Duplicate` not counted as sent; a refused transfer left ready; the memo dropped; every fresh call created at `now`; a ledger's `CanisterError` counted as not run; a refusal after an unknown call ending the action. The last three are Codex's findings, and the property test's model ledger now refuses before deduplication too. The property test also catches an expiry that ignores an unknown outcome, in 5 of 5 runs.

Checks run locally: `cargo fmt --all --check`, clippy native and wasm32 with `-D warnings`, unit and interface tests, the release Wasm build, and the PocketIC tests against server 16.1.0, including the upgrade from step 7.

- **Bolts, flame sprays and cones are lit along their whole length.** Each one now wears its own small light plus a row of small lights spread along it (no two farther apart than 80 units, each reaching about 2.5 times that), laid again every frame to where the art ends, where it hits something, or its range. author: phillip-hirsch
body:
## Summary

Sets up Macroscope the way [pingdotgg/t3code](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/tree/main/.macroscope) does, adapted to this repo and kept cheap.

```diff
+.macroscope/
+├── approvability.md                    # what Macroscope may not auto-approve
+├── ignore.md                           # skip list: Macroscope defaults + generated/vendored files
+└── check-run-agents/
+    └── effect-conventions.md           # reviews changed src/ code against AGENTS.md
 vite.config.ts                         # vp fmt skips ignore.md (glob-per-line, not Markdown)
```

- **Approvability:** t3code's rules (product defaults, lint or type-check suppressions), plus four areas where a mistake can lose Trip data, lock Phillip out or strand the installed app: the Access gate, Schedule store migrations, Cloudflare bindings and deploy settings, and the service worker.
- **Ignore list:** this file replaces Macroscope's built-in list, so it repeats the defaults and adds `public/map/**`, the app manifest, `rail-geometry.json`, `*.pmtiles` and the vendored ESLint Stylistic sources.
- **Effect and Trip conventions check:** uses this repo's rules, not t3code's (named imports from `effect` and `Effect.catchTag` are fine here). It checks the browser-bundle import limits, where Trip modules live, how split modules import each other, Trip writes going only through `scheduleWrite`/`tripWrite`, service keys and span names, `wrangler.jsonc` and `cloudflare.config.ts` declaring the same bindings, and new behaviour coming with a test through a public seam. It doesn't review test files, to keep cost down.

```yaml
model: gpt-6-1-sol
reasoning: medium      # t3code uses max
input: incremental     # later pushes review only new changes
conclusion: neutral    # comments, never fails a PR
maxBudgetPerRun: 1     # USD
maxBudgetPerPR: 3      # t3code: 5 / 25
```

There's no `requires: [Check]` because this repo has no CI. t3code's UI consistency agent was left out to save cost; Macroscope's built-in Correctness Check still runs on every PR.

## Evidence

- **Before:** no `.macroscope/`. Macroscope ran only its default Approvability and Correctness checks.
  **After:** `vp check` passes (0 errors). gpt-6.1-sol audited the agent rules against the code twice. All 7 findings were rules that would have flagged existing, correct code (e.g. `routeTree.gen.ts` imports, `reason: String(cause)` in `AccessGate.ts`, `Effect.withSpan` in `Trip.checklist`), and all are fixed.

The agent hasn't run on GitHub yet. This PR is its first live run.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

Configuration only. Deleting `.macroscope/` restores Macroscope's defaults.

**Blast Radius:** reviews

No app code changes. Possible effects: noisy comments from the new check, more PRs held for human review, and a file the skip list hides from review. The check never fails a PR and stops at $3 per PR.

author: medewitt
body:
## Summary

- `scripts/gp_weekly.py` fits a NUTS (NumPyro) Gaussian process to weekly CoCoRaHS rain, using log(1 + mm) on wet weeks only, and to the weekly PUC minus ERA5-Land delta at night (00-05 local).
- Each week is modeled as m0 + g(x) + u[s] + mu[w] + f_w(x) + error. g is a persistent spatial field, u is a site offset, and f_w is a weekly anomaly field. A per-week scale applies to both f_w and the error.
- mu, f_w, and (m0, g, u) are integrated out exactly. NUTS samples only the hyperparameters, and the fields are drawn from their Gaussian conditionals afterwards.
- Outputs go to `data/cache/gp_*.parquet`. The fit reruns only when a new complete week arrives or the script changes (fingerprint in `gp_key.txt`).
- `scripts/terrain.py` is a one-off script. It builds `data/terrain.parquet` from the USGS 3DEP DEM at 3 arc-seconds: TPI, D8 drainage area, derived streams, and height above nearest drainage.
- The Microclimate page becomes scrollable and gets a new row with:
  - a weekly surface map (median or 90% interval width);
  - a persistent difference map, faded where uncertain;
  - a terrain map (HAND or TPI) with streams;
  - a site offset forest plot, with distinct sites outlined;
  - site offset vs terrain.
- Methods text and README are updated. A CI step runs the fit after the seasonal fit.

## Current results (cache snapshot 2026-10-20)

- Rain: 22 gauges, 211 wet weeks, 0 divergences, max r-hat 1.01. Leave-one-site-out 90% coverage is 0.91.
- Rain: 4 gauges are distinct, from −21% to +36% vs the county-area mean. The persistent spatial field is weak, so most of the differences are site-level.
- Night delta: 5 PUC stations, 52 weeks, max r-hat 1.02, coverage 0.90. 2 stations are distinct.
- Correlation of night delta with TPI: +0.40 [0.29, 0.49] across these 5 sites. This is descriptive only.

## Notes

- The first CI run after merge fits from scratch, which takes several minutes. Later daily runs skip the fit unless a new week has completed.
- The rendered page grows by about 0.7 MB, mostly from the weekly fields.
