author: mergify[bot]
body:
## Why I'm doing:

`CREATE BASELINE` is classified `NO_FORWARD`, so it runs on whatever FE the client is connected to. Both of its branches then allocate a catalog id, and `CatalogIdGenerator.getNextId()` writes a journal entry whenever its pre-allocated batch is exhausted — which on a follower is **every single call**, because replaying `OP_SAVE_NEXTID_V2` does `setNextId(id + 1)` and leaves `nextId == batchEndId`. A non-leader may not write the journal, so on any follower:

- `CREATE BASELINE` (session-level) surfaces the raw write failure to the client:
 `ERROR 1064 (HY000): leader WAL gate is closed, submit log is not allowed`
- `CREATE GLOBAL BASELINE` is worse — `SQLPlanGlobalStorage.storeBaselinePlan` wraps its whole body in `catch (Exception) { LOG.warn(...) }`, so the client gets **OK** and no baseline is created.

Behind a load balancer over a 3-FE cluster, SPM is unusable roughly two times out of three.

**This is not a WAL-gate regression.** The leader-only `Preconditions.checkState` in `EditLog.submitLog` was already there when SPM landed (, Mar 2025); the gate only changed the wording from `Current node is not leader, but FOLLOWER, submit log is not allowed`. The three failing sqltest cases were imported *after* the gate landed, which is why they look like one.

The `NO_FORWARD` was deliberate but unfinished. Before the redirect refactor () it read:

```java
@Override
public RedirectStatus getRedirectStatus() {
 // @todo: check is global
 return RedirectStatus.NO_FORWARD;
}
```

The refactor dropped the TODO along with the comment. This PR does the split it asked for.

Fixes StarRocks/StarRocksTest#12200

## What I'm doing:

Two changes, both needed. Fixing only the redirect status would turn the session case from a visible error into a *silent* no-op: the leader runs a forwarded statement against a throwaway `new ConnectContext(null)` proxy context (`FrontendServiceImpl.forward`), and a session baseline stored there is discarded with the request.

**1. `RedirectStatus.visitCreateBaselinePlanStatement` splits on `isGlobal()`.** A global baseline is journalled and belongs on the leader; a session baseline stays local. Same shape as the `SET GLOBAL` / `SET` split in `visitSetStatement` in the same file. Forwarding is safe for the global form: `LeaderOpExecutor` sends the raw `originStmt` text plus the current database, so SPM functions like `_spm_const_var(...)` round-trip verbatim, and `FORWARD_WITH_SYNC` preserves read-your-writes for a following `SHOW BASELINE`.

**2. `SQLPlanSessionStorage` allocates its own ids** from a range reserved above every reachable catalog id (`1L << 62`) instead of calling `GlobalStateMgr.getNextId()`. Session ids only have to stay disjoint from the global ones — `SHOW BASELINE` unions both storages, and `DROP` / `ENABLE` / `DISABLE BASELINE` apply an id to both — and that no longer has to cost a journal write. Catalog ids count up one object at a time from `NEXT_ID_INIT_VALUE` (10000), so the two ranges cannot meet.

### Verified

Three full `./run-fe-ut.sh` runs over `RedirectStatusTest` + the new `SQLPlanSessionStorageTest` (273 tests):

| run | result |
|---|---|
| fix + new tests | BUILD SUCCESS, 273/273 |
| **both fixes reverted** | **BUILD FAILURE**, 1 failure + 3 errors |
| fix restored | BUILD SUCCESS, 273/273 |

The reverted run fails with the production error itself:

```
SQLPlanSessionStorageTest.testStoreBaselinePlanDoesNotNeedLeaderIdGenerator:67
 » EditLog leader WAL gate is closed, submit log is not allowed
RedirectStatusTest.testCreateGlobalBaselinePlanStmtCoverage:1902
 expected: <FORWARD_WITH_SYNC> but was: <NO_FORWARD>
```

### Observability

Reviewed the whole `CREATE BASELINE` path; no signal was removed.

- `MetricRepo.GAUGE_SPM_BASELINE_COUNT` — global baseline count, leader-aware gauge. Unchanged, but a follower-issued `CREATE GLOBAL BASELINE` now actually moves it instead of silently creating nothing.
- `SPMMetrics` — covers plan rewrite and auto-capture outcomes only, not statement execution. Untouched.
- `SQLPlanGlobalStorage`'s `LOG.warn("sql plan baselines store baseline fail", e)` — preserved.
- Leader-side `receive forwarded stmt {} from FE: {}` — the global form now flows through it, so a follower-issued global create becomes traceable on the leader.

No new signal added: the session path is now a pure in-memory append with no failure mode.

### Deliberately out of scope

- `DROP` / `ENABLE` / `DISABLE BASELINE` are `FORWARD_WITH_SYNC` and each *also* mutates `context.getSqlPlanStorage()`. On a follower that session half lands on the leader's proxy context, so a session baseline cannot be dropped or disabled there — the statement returns OK and does nothing. Fixing it needs a different shape (split the statement, or route per target); separate PR.
- `SQLPlanGlobalStorage`'s catch-all still turns a genuine failure into a client-visible OK. This PR makes the global path run on the leader so it is far less likely to fire, but the swallow itself remains.
- `docs/{en,zh,ja}/using_starrocks/SQL_plan_manager.md:92` shows a session-level (`global | N`) sample row with `Id | 646125`. Session ids now come from the reserved high range, so that one sample line is no longer representative. Not touched here, per `docs/CLAUDE.md`; happy to do a follow-up [Doc] PR.

## What type of PR is this:

- [x] BugFix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Enhancement

- [ ] UT

Does this PR entail a change in behavior?

`CREATE BASELINE` now succeeds on a follower instead of failing (session) or silently doing nothing (global). The `Id` that `SHOW BASELINE` displays for a **session** baseline now comes from the reserved range, so it is a large number rather than a small catalog id; it is still what `DROP` / `ENABLE` / `DISABLE BASELINE` take. Global baseline ids are unchanged.

body:
## Overview

`docs/guides/living-doc-document-types.md` described four things the `living-doc-utilities` `0.7.0` contracts no longer
match. This PR corrects that guide and, by owner decision, carries two of its corrections across the rest of the
documentation: GitHub issues are a planned source everywhere, and every page names the toolkit's new commands. No
example or check changes.

### The document types guide

- **Where the view is recorded.** The page said the applied view is in `meta.view.view`,
  `meta.view.filtered_user_stories` and `meta.view.filtered_acceptance_criteria`, and linked the toolkit's
  `contracts.md` § Content Views. The contracts record it in the generator input's `document` block: `document.view`,
  and `document.selection_summary` for what the filter kept and dropped. The page now says so and links
  `artifact-rules.md` § The metadata envelope. The Content Views link is gone.
- **The toolkit's commands.** `normalize-issues` is gone. `normalize-docs` selects the view with
  `--view inner|release` (default `inner`), shown as one command line, with a link to the toolkit's `README.md`. Each
  document type's generator input now names the file and the command that writes it: `generator-ready.json` from
  `normalize-docs`, `ui-test-catalog.json` from `normalize-tests`, and `coverage-matrix.json` from `coverage-matrix`.
- **How the coverage matrix's inputs combine.** "Merged into one dataset if they come from different sources" is gone.
  The prerequisites now say one project and one documentation file, and the tests may come from any repository of the
  same project, linked to `pipeline-rules.md` § One project, one pipeline, one documentation source. "Same system"
  becomes "same project" in the prerequisites, the prerequisite matrix and the At a glance table, because the
  contracts allow test data from another system of the same project.
- **GitHub issues as an input.** The "Built from" table marks GitHub issues Planned, as Azure DevOps already is, and
  lists the available source first. The prerequisite matrix and the intro's list of inputs say issues are planned.

Unchanged: every `##` heading (the `#technical-project`, `#test-catalog` and `#coverage-matrix` anchors are linked
from `agentic/skills/shared/references/` and `living-doc-utilities`' `rendering.md`), the worked examples, and the
drop rules by state.

### Issues planned and the new commands across the docs (owner decision)

- **Source code is the available source.** `README.md` § What gets mined marks source code Available and GitHub issues
  Planned. `quickstart.md` and `getting-started.md` built their one pipeline example on GitHub issues; both now build
  it on source code (`doc-source.json` → `normalize-docs` → `generator-ready.json`), with the collect step shaped like
  the source-code tutorials'.
- **Issues and Azure DevOps say planned** wherever a page presents them as a source: `README.md`,
  `getting-started.md`, `quickstart.md`, `what-is-living-documentation.md`, `architecture.md`,
  `github-collection.md`, `projects/collector-gh.md`, `projects/generator-markdown.md`, the source-code tutorials'
  related links, and the glossary's Feature Dependencies note (its agentic copy regenerated with
  `agentic/scripts/sync-canon-copies.sh`). Azure DevOps is marked only in the lists that also mark issues, so no list
  reads as if it were available.
- **The issue-only tutorials** (`gh-issues-to-markdown.md`, `technical-project-to-pdf.md`) open with one PLANNED line
  that points to the source-code tutorial and to the canonical issue-body layout, which is already fixed.
- **The new commands.** Every `living-doc normalize-issues` step is now `living-doc normalize-docs`. The source-code
  pages read `doc-source.json`. The planned issue and Azure DevOps tutorials read `doc-entities.json`, the file both
  issue-tracker collectors write. `getting-started.md`, `README.md` and the toolkit card name all three commands
  (`normalize-docs`, `normalize-tests`, `coverage-matrix`). The toolkit implements them in its next changes. Until
  then, its README still documents `normalize-issues`.

Left for the later docs rebuild: the pipeline examples' other inputs (`pip install` of the toolkit, collector inputs,
generator tags and `document-type`), the PDF pages, and `ado-workitems-to-markdown.md` § Combining with GitHub data.

### Canon rules this change states

| Rule | Page | Where |
|---|---|---|
| `document` exists on `generator-ready` and holds `document.view`; `generator-ready`'s `document` adds `selection_summary` | `living-doc-utilities` [`artifact-rules.md` § The metadata envelope](https://github.com/AbsaOSS/living-doc-utilities/blob/master/docs/contracts/artifact-rules.md#the-metadata-envelope) | guide `:95-97` |
| Legacy provenance shapes (`audit`-namespaced, free-form) are retired; no component reads or writes them | `living-doc-utilities` [`artifact-rules.md` § R8](https://github.com/AbsaOSS/living-doc-utilities/blob/master/docs/contracts/artifact-rules.md#r8-legacy-provenance-shapes-are-retired) | `meta.view.*` removed |
| The contracts' file names: `doc-source.json`, `ui-tests.json`, `generator-ready.json`, `ui-test-catalog.json`, `coverage-matrix.json`; both issue-tracker collectors write `doc-entities.json` | `living-doc-utilities` [`artifact-rules.md` § Contracts](https://github.com/AbsaOSS/living-doc-utilities/blob/master/docs/contracts/artifact-rules.md#contracts) | guide `:100`, `:132`, `:169-171`; the tutorials' normalize steps |
| A transform run takes exactly one documentation file; test data may come from elsewhere in the project | `living-doc-utilities` [`pipeline-rules.md` § One project, one pipeline, one documentation source](https://github.com/AbsaOSS/living-doc-utilities/blob/master/docs/contracts/pipeline-rules.md#one-project-one-pipeline-one-documentation-source) | guide `:17`, `:152-158`, `:181`; `README.md`, `quickstart.md` "same project" |
| The view filter that builds `generator-ready` selects records only; the release view drops `planned` and `in_review` | `living-doc-utilities` [`rendering.md` § Records and presentation](https://github.com/AbsaOSS/living-doc-utilities/blob/master/docs/contracts/rendering.md#records-and-presentation) | guide `:63-72`; drop rules `:74-83` unchanged |

Nothing the change adds contradicts a canon rule.

### Acceptance criteria

| The guide names neither `meta.view` nor `normalize-issues`, and shows `doc-issues.json` as no current input | a repo-wide `grep` outside `docs/examples/_expected/` and `docs/_integration/` finds none of the three; `doc-issues` survives as the planned collector mode only |
| The view paragraph links the toolkit's `README.md`; the applied view is `document.view` and `document.selection_summary`, linked to `living-doc-utilities` | guide `:63-72`, `:95-97`. **Owner decision:** the paragraph names `normalize-docs` instead of no command |
| The coverage-matrix prerequisites say one project and one documentation file; "merged into one dataset" is gone | guide `:152-158` |
| The "Built from" table and the prerequisite matrix mark GitHub issues Planned and ask for the same project | guide `:45`, `:179`, `:181` |
| Every `##` heading is unchanged | the guide's `##` headings match `master` |
| No other page changes | **Owner decision:** 16 other files change, listed above |
| `link-check.yml` and `examples-check.yml` green | `examples_check.py` OK and its three test files pass (118 tests); every new link target and anchor exists; lychee runs on this PR |
| `agentic-tests.yml` (the glossary changed) | the canon copies match `sync-canon-copies.sh all`; the 18 skill test scripts pass |
| In sync with the canon, each rule named with its page | the table above |

author: thomaseizinger
body:
Release builds are minified with R8, but only the Rust debug files are uploaded to Sentry, so Kotlin frames there show up as `null.oa2 in c`. Crashlytics only has readable traces because its own Gradle plugin uploads the mapping.

The Sentry Android Gradle plugin now embeds a mapping UUID in every minified build, and the mapping is only uploaded from the release workflow. Every other build does a dry run that needs neither network access nor a token. All of the plugin's other features are turned off, so it doesn't touch our bytecode or the SDK dependency.

body: ## Summary Adds the delivery path that v1.5 (landed in #217) does not cover — approval delivery failure on a clean evaluation. (This branch was #216, closed while it still carried the cross-repo fallback now superseded by #217; reopened here with the non-overlapping delta.) **manual-blocking0**: when the gate evaluates clean (verdict `COMMENTED`/`STATUS_CLEAN`/`APPROVED` + zero unresolved blocking findings) but `gh pr review --approve` fails with GitHub's exact restriction (`Actions is not permitted to approve pull requests`), the job: 1. matches the **exact** upstream message — a broad substring could launder a different restriction; 2. posts a `gate-resolved-via: manual-blocking0` audit comment via `issues/comments` — **fatal if undeliverable** (the trail is the mechanism; no silent green); 3. writes a `GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` line; 4. exits 0 — the required check records the **clean evaluation**, never a formal approving review. Any other approve error still fails the job. Idempotent via the same `gate-fallback-pairs:` dedupe convention the v1.5 fallback audit uses (per-head). Motivation: personal-agent-system#37 hit exactly this — `COMMENTED`, `BLOCKING_MAP {"37":0}`, approve denied; merged on a manually-measured blocking=0. This makes it a documented, measured second path instead of a convention. #### Test plan - [x] `tools/test_pr_approve_gate_fallback.py` runs the real run-blocks vs stubbed `gh` — 4 new cases: denial posts audit, other error fails, comment failure is fatal, same-head idempotency. **38 tests / 12 subtests green** - [x] YAML parse + `bash -n` on all 4 run blocks Generated with [Devin](https://devin.ai) ---

author: vlidholt
body:
## Problem

Users on wonky.work get signed out at random. Production runs Serverpod's **token mode** (`"cookieAuth": false`: Serverpod Cloud has no `authCookie`), where every tab reads the refresh token from shared browser storage and refreshes with no coordination between tabs. Refresh tokens are single-use, and the server revokes the session when a rotated one comes back. So two tabs refreshing at the same moment (laptop wake, tabs reloading together, tabs sharing the same expiry) sign the user out everywhere. Every page load and app switch also forced a rotation (`ClientAuthSessionManager.initialize()`), which made this more likely.

## Fix (client only, no Serverpod or server code changes)

On web in token mode, the apps replace Serverpod's JWT key provider (`SharedJwtAuthKeyProvider`, `packages/wonky_app/lib/src/auth/shared_session.dart`):

- **One shared session:** stored in `localStorage` (`wonky.auth.session`) and read fresh on every use. Other tabs pick up sign-in, sign-out and rotations through `storage` events. Existing sessions are moved once from the old `flutter_secure_storage`, so nobody is signed out when this deploys.
- **One refresh at a time:** a refresh runs under the cross-tab Web Lock Serverpod already uses in cookie mode and re-reads the session inside it. When another tab rotated meanwhile, its token is used instead of rotating again.
- **No rotation on page load:** startup checks the stored token with `status.isSignedIn()`. It rotates only when the token is about to expire, or once if the server rejects it.
- **No lost tokens on app switches:** switching apps and reloading wait (up to 5 s) for a refresh in flight.

Desktop and cookie mode are unchanged.

## Config

- **development.yaml:** `authCookie` and `allowedOrigins` are removed, so local development matches production.
- **Bundled `config.json`:** set to `cookieAuth: false` in every app.
- **Deleted files:** `config/staging.yaml` and `config/production.yaml` were never used (Serverpod Cloud generates the config from its variables).
- **Docs:** `specs/01` §2.5 and §6, `specs/13` §4 and the board's GitHub README are updated.

## Testing

- **Unit tests:** 12 new tests in `packages/wonky_app/test/auth/shared_session_test.dart`. The key one simulates two tabs refreshing at once against a fake server that revokes reused tokens like Serverpod does. It fails with Serverpod's stock refresh; the new code rotates exactly once.
- **Existing tests:** the `wonky_app` auth, bootstrap, shell and settings tests pass, as do the server config tests. `dart analyze` is clean.
- **Manual check:** local release builds of Drive and Write in token mode, in the browser:
  - a reload and a Drive → Write switch keep the session without rotating;
  - two tabs reloaded at the same instant with an expiring token make one refresh call in total and both stay signed in;
  - signing out in one tab shows "Your session expired" in the other right away.

## Not covered

- **Lost refresh responses:** a response lost to sleep, a network drop or a deploy can still sign the user out. Fixing that needs a grace period for the previous secret in Serverpod's rotation (`JwtAdmin.rotateRefreshToken`), which should go upstream.
- **Debug apps in development:** the `flutter run` apps on ports 8100–8104 now need a sign-in each, because `localStorage` is per origin.

author: bigsimmo
body:
Owner-approved (Josh): prerequisite for enabling a GitHub merge queue on `main`.

Required checks on `main` (ruleset "Protections"): `Ward Flow required`, `Ward Flow bot-author policy`, `GitGuardian Security Checks`.

- **Ward Flow CI** (`ward-flow.yml`): already has `merge_group` (all types, i.e. `checks_requested`). Under merge_group the scope plan gets no PR base and fails closed to full scope, so `Ward Flow required` runs everything. No change, to avoid conflicting with #521.
- **Ward Flow bot-author policy** (`bot-author-policy.yml`): was `pull_request_target` only, so the queue would wait forever for it. Adds `merge_group: types: [checks_requested]`. Under merge_group the job re-runs main's copy of the policy script (base-sha checkout only, still no PR code executed) for **every** PR in the group (`Merge pull request #N` commits between group base and head, plus the PR in the queue ref), and fails closed if none is found. Same check name, no checks weakened.
- **GitGuardian Security Checks**: GitHub App; it reports a neutral check run for merge groups per its docs, so no change is needed.

**Also (owner-approved):** `pull_request_target` now runs on `branches: [main, "release/**"]`, so the required bot-author check also runs on PRs into release branches (the ruleset covers `release/**` too). The test asserts both are listed.

**Review fix (Codex P1):** under merge_group the script is checked out from `merge_group.base_ref` (protected main tip), not `base_sha`, which can be an earlier queued group commit.

author: nishantjh
body:
## Summary

Adds the first persistent Wi-Fi Layout & Coverage module slice.

- Adds a dimensioned floor-plan editor with rooms, wall segments/material labels, and draggable placements linked to inventory devices.
- Persists the layout in PostgreSQL and records layout changes in the audit trail.
- Adds an explicit, sequential scan action for enrolled OpenWrt APs. It uses the existing pinned SSH host key and encrypted stored credential, discovers interfaces with `iw dev`, and invokes the fixed `iwinfo <interface> info/scan` operations.
- Parses neighbour BSSID, SSID, channel, and RSSI observations, stores them with source device/radio and timestamps, and prunes observations older than 30 days.
- Adds parser and layout validation tests. No new dependencies or services.

## Safety and scope

- Scans are manual, not scheduled; each device scan has a 30-second deadline, output limits, and a maximum of four interfaces per device.
- The scan endpoint is admin/operator-only, uses private-IP-only device addressing and pinned SSH host-key verification, and does not change router configuration.
- This is the data and layout foundation, **not yet a calibrated building-wide coverage heatmap**. Inter-AP RSSI is measured only at AP locations; a follow-up estimator must account for wall/floor attenuation and label predictions separately from measurements.
- No Redis, new container, or additional frontend dependency.

## Validation

- Added unit tests for RSSI parsing and layout bounds.
- CI has not yet been reviewed on the PR head. Keep this draft until Go formatting, frontend build, tests, and security checks are confirmed.

body:
## Summary

Before: only screens the owner paired could play, and every stream went through the owner's Hub, so there was no way to show a friend one video without giving them the owner's library, history, and devices.

After: a share link, `https://<origin>/s/<token>`, plays one item in any browser for 7 days, without pairing or signing in.

- **Making a link.** The player's new share button (`POST /v1/shares`) or the MCP tool `share` (control scope) shares an item, else what plays now. The URL is in the answer only: D1's new `share_links` table (migration `0010`) keeps the token's hash.
- **The friend's page.** `/s/<token>` is the player's own page. `main.js` starts `share.js` instead of pairing and the realtime channel, and `playback.js` sends every stream request to `POST /v1/share/<token>/stream`, whose answer is the `load` message a paired screen gets, so recovery, seeks, and quality changes work as on a paired screen. The router keeps the page at `/s/<token>`; Back, share, settings, previous/next, and the now-playing bar are hidden.
- **Nothing reaches the owner's state.** The Worker checks the link and calls the node's `/internal/v1/prepare` itself (`share-links.js`), never the Hub: no playback state, history, queue, track preferences, or Plex position. Paths are remote direct play when it is on, then the relay as the relay mode allows; never the LAN listener.
- **The node keeps friends apart.** Sessions with `share` never retire the owner's (the cap of 8 counts only the owner's), at most 2 friends' streams play at once, a third is refused with `rate_limited` before its source resolves unless one has been idle for 2 minutes, and friends' sessions are released after 15 idle minutes.
- **Revoking.** Settings list open links with their play counts (`GET /v1/owner/shares`); revoking one (`POST /v1/owner/shares/:id/revoke`) refuses it at once and stops its streams on the node (`DELETE /internal/v1/shares/:id`). Making and revoking write security log lines.

What it gives up: a forwarded link plays for whoever holds it until it expires or is revoked; friends' streams away from remote direct play cross the relay (4.8 Mbps ceiling, the owner's Workers requests); a link cannot be shown again, only made anew.

Design and alternatives (watching together, guest devices, playlists, a choice of expiry, stored tokens, passwords, the LAN path) are in the new note `.agents/notes/implemented/feature/2026-10-20-share-links.md`. The 1.0 proposal now keeps library sharing, not share links, out of scope.

A second commit fixes the owner's settings showing the text "null" under Media paths on an instance with a domain: `noDomainCard()` and `screensCard()` return null, which `replaceChildren()` printed.

No `NODE_PROTOCOL` or `CLIENT_PROTOCOL` change: a previous-release node ignores `share` and `replaces` (friends' streams then count toward the owner's 8), and the new `/v1` routes are additive.

## Test plan

- [x] `service/control/test/unit/auth.test.js`: a link plays without a credential, the prepare carries `share`, the owner's state and history stay empty, relay off is refused, `replaces` on a rebuild, 404/405/410 for unknown, wrong-method, expired, and revoked links
- [x] `service/node/test/media-pipeline.test.js`: friends' cap apart from the owner's, admission before the source resolves, `replaces` only within a link, stopping one link's sessions
- [x] `test/e2e/web-playback.test.js`: a link made with the MCP tool plays in a browser that never paired; the owner's playback and history unchanged; revoked, the page says so
- [x] Screenshots of the friend's page, the owner's share button, settings' share links (no "null" under Media paths), and a revoked link's page (Chromium)
- [x] `npm run doc-sync` (6 gates), unit and integration tests; e2e passes except "a browser plays from the LAN, then by remote direct play, then through the relay", which fails the same way on a clean `main` on this Mac (the local fixture buffers past the seek target), and `agent-claude-code`'s stdin test, which fails on `main` too on macOS (`/var` vs `/private/var`)
- [ ] In the car: the share page on a Tesla (canvas engine); paired-screen playback paths are unchanged
- [ ] WebKit (`YOLO_E2E_WEBKIT=1`) or Safari for the friend's page

## Qué cambia

Blender deja de ser el centro de Amatista. Ahora es una plataforma de 3D (modelado, diseño, render, animación, interacción y XR) que enseña en varios programas: hoy Blender y A-Frame, y Maya y 3ds Max aparecen como próximos.

- **Barra Inicio · Explorar · Mi panel** (· Admin), con una lupa. La pestaña de Blender sale de la barra; la página `#/blender` sigue existiendo y se llega desde el curso, desde Explorar y desde el pie.
- **Explorar** (`#/explorar`) reúne todos los programas, módulos y lecciones en una sola página:
  - buscador que no distingue acentos;
  - filtros por programa y disciplina, que quedan en la dirección;
  - índice lateral;
  - tarjetas de módulo con sus lecciones a un clic y un enlace directo al módulo (`#/curso/<id>?modulo=N`).
- **Portada** con el mapa del contenido. **Mi panel** muestra «Tu avance en cada programa». El **pie** es multiplataforma y el recorrido suma una parada en Explorar.
- **Accesibilidad:** enlace «Saltar al contenido», `aria-pressed` y `aria-live`, y anclas con margen para la barra fija.
- **Estudio A-Frame** (`#/estudio`):
  - editor libre con vista en vivo;
  - cinco plantillas y seis piezas para insertar;
  - descarga de la página;
  - tres modelos GLB low poly propios (`npm run modelos`), que se guardan en la caché de la PWA.
- **Curso de A-Frame con cinco módulos.** Los cuatro nuevos son escena, modelos GLB y texturas, animación e interacción, y WebXR. Cada uno tiene un reto de código que se revisa solo, un jefe final y una temática con su mascota (Taco, Glib, Muelle, Nébula).

No hay SQL nuevo; el siguiente script libre sigue siendo 013. La guía de publicación está en `docs/despliegue/2026-10-21_multiplataforma.md` (T-119: importar los módulos y publicar la PWA).

author: vgvassilev
body:
#147 stopped running brew install on Intel macOS, where upgrading an outdated llvm@21 builds it from source now that Homebrew ships no Intel bottles for the upgrade. But a version the image does not have is then never installed: clad's osx-intel-runtime19 row gets a prefix that does not exist, and fails in its own CMake with "Could not find a package configuration file provided by LLVM". Before #147 that row poured llvm@19 from its bottle in seconds.

Install on every host again, with HOMEBREW_NO_INSTALL_UPGRADE: a formula already there is left as it is, and a missing one is installed. Fail in the action when the prefix has no LLVM CMake package, rather than in the consumer's configure.

The flavor=system smoke ran on Linux only; it now also covers Intel macOS with a version the image lacks (19) and one it has (18).

author: redcat2tails
body:
## Problem
The immutable import from PR #30 does not yet have an explicit path to accept desired state for one Application in one Environment.

## Solution
- Add typed Environment, deployment, generation, ChangeSet, Plan, and commit contracts for one `DeployRevision` member.
- Resolve fake Provider aliases during planning and pin exact selections in Plans and immutable generation snapshots.
- Atomically check the ChangeSet precondition, compare exact Plan inputs, and commit desired state. Repeated apply returns the original commit; equivalent state is a no-op.
- Keep import and planning side-effect free. No Provider execution or `AppliedGeneration` advancement occurs.
- Cover the review follow-ups: missing/foreign Plan outcomes, wrong expected generation, rollback to an earlier revision, invalid IDs and catalog values, and null Provider entries in public planning inputs.

## Validation
- `dotnet restore .\HamstixHaby.slnx` passed.
- `dotnet build .\HamstixHaby.slnx --no-restore` passed (0 errors; existing prototype warnings).
- `dotnet test tests/Haby.Application.Tests/Haby.Application.Tests.csproj --no-restore` passed: 29 tests.
- `dotnet test .\HamstixHaby.slnx --no-build` passed: 302 tests.
- `dotnet format .\HamstixHaby.slnx --verify-no-changes --no-restore` passed.
- `git diff --check` passed.

## Contract gaps and deferred work
Cross-Application export Bindings and parameter definitions require the ADR-018 and ADR-019 resolvers. This checkpoint returns a typed, code-free `UnsupportedDependency` planning result for those declarations, so they cannot be committed. There is no accepted generic stable public error code for this limited-path condition; no transport error mapping is introduced. Multi-Application transactions, removal, persistence, reconciliation, and Provider execution remain separate work. No runtime package was added.

Closes #31

author: pzbhe-kt
body:
## Summary
I reviewed the archive client lifecycle (`AsyncConnect`, `Options` conclude, auth/challenge, close, archive id, keepalive) side by side with Java `AeronArchive`/`ArchiveProxy` 1.53.3 and fixed the bugs listed below. Each bug has a test that fails on `parity` and passes here.

### Bugs
1. **Failed or cancelled connect leaked pending resources.** `archive/async_connect.go:495` (`AsyncConnect.Close`), `aeron/clientconductor.go:829,844,956`
   - Java: `AsyncConnect.close()` calls `aeron.asyncRemoveSubscription/asyncRemovePublication(registrationId)` for adds the driver hasn't answered yet. `ClientConductor.removePublication/removeSubscription` drops the pending registration and sends the driver REMOVE.
   - Wrong: Go tried `GetSubscription/GetExclusivePublication`, which return nil while the add is pending, and then did nothing. `ClientConductor.AsyncRemove*` also ignored pending kinds. So once the driver answered, the subscription/publication was live and leaked on a shared (`OwnsAeronClient=false`) client.
   - Fix: `Close` removes in-flight adds by registration id. The new `removePendingLocked` forgets the pending resource (so a late ready response is ignored and no log buffers are mapped) and sends REMOVE to the driver. For a failed add whose error was never collected, nothing is sent.
   - Tests: `TestE2EAsyncConnectCloseRemovesPendingSubscription`, `TestE2EAsyncConnectCloseRemovesPendingPublication`, `TestAsyncRemoveSubscriptionWhilePending`, `TestAsyncRemoveExclusivePublicationWhilePending`, `TestAsyncRemoveAfterFailedAddSendsNothing`
2. **`RESOURCE_TEMPORARILY_UNAVAILABLE` failed the connect.** `archive/async_connect.go:347` (`awaitSubscription`/`addPublication`)
   - Java: on `RegistrationException` it resets the registration id to `NULL_VALUE` and retries next poll when the code is `RESOURCE_TEMPORARILY_UNAVAILABLE`. Any other code is thrown.
   - Wrong: Go failed the connect on every error and kept the stale registration id, so `Close` then acted on a dead id.
   - Fix: `ignoreTemporarilyUnavailable` + reset of the registration id.
3. **Control session id was random, not from the driver.** `archive/options.go:200`, `archive/async_connect.go:176`
   - Java: `Context.conclude()` always sets `session-id` on both control channels to `aeron.nextSessionId(controlRequestStreamId)` (not for `control-mode=response`).
   - Wrong: Go used `rand.Int31n(1<<30)+1` (the comment claimed Go had no `NextSessionID`; it does). It could collide with driver-allocated ids, and it kept a user-supplied request `session-id` without setting the response side.
   - Fix: `Options.applySessionID(aeron.NextSessionID)` runs in `NewAsyncConnect` once the client exists. If it fails, an owned client is closed instead of leaked.
   - Tests: `TestE2EConnectSessionIDFromDriver`, `TestOptionsApplySessionIDOverwritesLikeJava`, `TestOptionsConcludeResponseModeHasNoSessionID`
4. **Connect rejections were not `*ArchiveException`.** `archive/async_connect.go:445`
   - Java: an ERROR connect response throws `ArchiveException(errorMessage, errorCode, correlationId)`.
   - Wrong: Go returned `*ConnectError` with a nil cause, so `ArchiveErrorCodeOf(err)` returned false (for example, `AUTHENTICATION_REJECTED` could not be detected).
   - Fix: the cause is now `newArchiveResponseException(...)`. `errors.As(err, *ConnectError)` still works.
   - Test: `TestE2EConnectRejectedIsArchiveException`
5. **Archive-id request, keepalive and close-session ignored offer failures.** `archive/async_connect.go:383,397`
   - Java: `ArchiveProxy.offer` makes `messageRetryAttempts` attempts and throws on `CLOSED`, `NOT_CONNECTED` and `MAX_POSITION_EXCEEDED`. `sendArchiveIdRequest` uses it.
   - Wrong: Go made a hard-coded 3 tries and dropped the error. The archive-id request used a single `trySend` attempt with no error.
   - Fix: `AsyncConnect.offer` returns `(sent, error)` with Java's messages. The keepalive failure carries the cause.
6. **Missing `messageRetryAttempts`, and defaults differed from Java.** `archive/options.go:102,160`
   - Java: `MESSAGE_TIMEOUT_DEFAULT_NS` is 10s, `MESSAGE_RETRY_ATTEMPTS_DEFAULT` is 3 (must be > 0), and the default idle strategy is `BackoffIdleStrategy`.
   - Wrong: Go defaulted to a 5s timeout and `Sleeping{50ms}` (marked FIXME), which added up to 50ms latency to every control exchange, and had no retry option.
   - Fix: new `Options.MessageRetryAttempts` (0 means default, < 0 is an error), `MessageTimeoutDefault` set to 10s, and `IdleStrategy` left nil so conclude sets a backoff strategy.
   - Tests: `TestOptionsDefaultsMatchJava`, `TestOptionsConcludeValidation`
7. **Using an archive after Close gave an opaque error.** `archive/proxy.go:36,62`, `archive/archive_lifecycle.go:87`
   - Java: `ensureConnected()` throws `ArchiveException("client is closed")`. Offer results map to "connection to the archive has been closed", "offer failed due to max position being reached", and so on.
   - Wrong: Go reached into the (possibly owned and closed) client's publication and returned `Offer failed: -4` as a plain error.
   - Fix: `Proxy.Offer` refuses to send once the archive is closed. `offerError` returns `*ArchiveException` with Java's messages. `Archive.Close` sends CLOSE_SESSION before marking the archive closed.
   - Test: `TestE2EArchiveUseAfterClose` (owned and shared client)

### API changes
- Added `Options.MessageRetryAttempts`, `MessageRetryAttemptsDefault` and `MessageTimeoutDefault`.
- `DefaultOptions().Timeout` is now 10s and `DefaultOptions().IdleStrategy` is now nil (a backoff strategy is set on conclude).
- `Options.conclude()` no longer sets a session id; `NewAsyncConnect` sets it from the driver and replaces any user-set `session-id`, as Java does.
- Proxy request errors are now `*ArchiveException`, not `fmt` errors.
- `ClientConductor.AsyncRemoveSubscription/AsyncRemovePublication` (and so `Aeron.AsyncRemove*`) now also cancel pending adds.

### Testing (local; Actions does not run on this fork)
Run after merging the latest `origin/parity`:
- `go build ./...` and `go vet ./...` are clean.
- `go test -count=1 ./...`: all packages pass except `systests`, which needs the embedded Java driver jar and also fails on `parity`.
- `go test -race ./archive/ ./aeron/` passes.
- `AERON_E2E=1 go test -p 1 ./archive/... ./systests/conductore2e/...` passes against the docker Java 1.53.3 archive, auth archive and replication archive.

The first automatic release ([run 39555954904](https://github.com/gsamuele78/iemod-fetch/actions/runs/39555954904)) passed planning and the full CI gate, then failed in *Build distributions* with:

`cp: cannot create regular file 'dist/': Not a directory`

The cause: `python -m build`, run from the repository root, imports the repository's own `build.py` (the zipapp script) and not PyPA's `build`, so `dist/` was never created. Nobody had hit this because the release workflow had never run before.

## How it is verified

- [x] I reproduced the failure locally on `46eb8cb`: `python -m build` printed "built …iemod-fetch.pyz" and created no `dist/`.
- [x] I re-ran the whole build step locally with the fix (`pyproject-build`, then `build.py`, the copy, SHA256SUMS and the CycloneDX SBOM). It produced the wheel, sdist, `.pyz`, SHA256SUMS and SBOM.
- [x] actionlint and zizmor report nothing.
- [x] No new runtime dependency.

## If this touches a design decision

- [x] `CHANGELOG.md`: entry under `Unreleased` → Fixed.

## Anything left undone

The CHANGELOG change in this PR means merging it re-triggers the automatic v2.2.0 release.

author: sebastiangarces
body:
## Summary

WP-024/api adds the task core behind the Tasks screens. A church can now create, edit, delete, complete, reopen and close tasks as no longer needed. Lists, counts and a status history read the same records. Members act only on tasks they hold. Due and overdue reminders follow the current assignee and stop when a task is settled or deleted. Meeting finalization (WP-022) can now create one follow-up per first-time Vision guest and one evaluation task, and retries never duplicate them. There is no UI in this PR; WP-024/ui builds the screens on this contract.

## What changed and why

- **Task contract** (`packages/contracts/src/tasks/`). Request and result shapes for every task operation, with the three due kinds from REQ-TSK-018: undated, a church-local date, or a deadline entered as church-local wall time. The server resolves a deadline in the church zone. A spring-forward gap refuses with `nonexistent_local_time`. A fall-back fold refuses with `ambiguous_local_time` and both choices until the person picks one. The brief asked for the contract first.
- **Task domain** (`packages/domain/src/tasks/`).
  - Reads: `list`, `count`, `get`, `statusHistory`, `eligibleAssignees` and `relationOptions`. Each is one statement. The statement itself checks the reader's live session, account, seat, role and lifecycle (C13), so a seat ended, demoted or signed out after the viewer lookup reads no task data. The list uses page numbers (D67): default 50 rows, at most 100, null due dates last, ties broken by ID.
  - Writes: `create`, `edit`, `delete`, `complete`, `reopen`, `waive` and `changeStatus`. Each runs through the shared retry-safe command (D70). The authority check, the revision check and one audit row per changed task go in the same write statement. All status changes share one writer, so completion time, waiver and history agree (REQ-TSK-003).
  - Generated work: `ensureMeetingObligations` (also `tasks.ensureObligation`) and `applyManagedStatus` (also `tasks.settleManagedEvaluation`). They append to the meeting domain's own command, so obligations, tasks and audit rows commit with the finalization or not at all (REQ-TSK-017).
- **Status history from the shared audit record.** There is no task history table (D70). Each entry says who or what made the change, and a system cause never shows as a person (REQ-TSK-015).
- **Reminders** (`apps/web/src/server/tasks/`). The writer takes an injected reminder port, as settings takes its effects. The port takes all tasks of one write in one call. The tasks mount connects it to WP-031's `syncTaskReminders`, which now takes a list and locks, cancels and enqueues set-based in at most 10 statements, whatever the number of tasks (patterns.md). A due or overdue slot that already reached its recipient under an earlier revision is not planned again, so a reschedule never sends the same reminder twice. The mail authorization rule for task reminders lives in the tasks domain, so a reminder for a former assignee, a settled task or an older revision is refused at send time (REQ-TSK-014).
- **Migration 0018** adds the catalog's `facilities` category to the task check. Nothing else in the schema changes (D72, D75).
- **Statement census.** The task writer and `withTaskWrite` are registered in the counter, the tasks suite is in the census corpus, and every task write has a budget in `limits.json`.
- **Acceptance cases.** I repaired the 14 owned cases so their actions take real inputs, and I linked the four owned requirements that had no case (REQ-KNOW-007, REQ-MTG-020, REQ-MTG-021, REQ-PPL-024). `docs/acceptance/check.py --package WP-024` is now clean.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  UI[Task screens WP-024/ui] --> W[withTaskWrite]
  W --> C[task command: authority, revision, audit in one statement]
  C --> R[reminder port]
  R --> N[WP-031 notification service]
  F[Meeting finalization WP-022] --> G[ensureMeetingObligations in the caller's command]
  G --> C2[obligation + task + audit rows]
```

Rulings I made (recorded in the PR Context note):

1. Scope. WP-025 owns checklists beyond one level, prerequisites, recurrence and bulk changes. WP-023 owns follow-up outcomes, contact evidence, the Assignments coverage view and `reopenObligation`. WP-026 owns Markdown preview and template import. This PR keeps one-level checklist rows so counts and delete are complete. It refuses a reopen while a later occurrence of the same series is open, and the refusal names that task.
2. One producer serves both `tasks.ensureObligation` and `tasks.ensureMeetingObligations`. An obligation that already exists never gets a new task. A retry, a deleted task or a waiver therefore never brings work back.
3. Storage keeps the shipped obligation kinds `follow_up` and `evaluation`, because the shipped seat-removal contract uses them. The task contract maps them to `first_vision_follow_up` and `meeting_evaluation`.
4. The generated evaluation task is due two church-local days after the meeting, like the follow-up. The requirements name no date. This is easy to change.
5. A write calls the reminder port only when the task had or now has owed reminders (open, dated, assigned). Plain edits keep the small statement budget.
6. A stale revision refuses with the shared `conflict` code. The case text calls it `revision_conflict`.
7. `tasks.normalizeDescription` is the request parse: trim, LF line endings, at most 10,000 characters.
8. Files outside the owning paths: the tasks mount and reminder adapter in `apps/web/src/server/tasks/` (the brief asks for the reminder call in the server layer), the migration, schema and generated docs (D72), package exports, the census registration, the owned acceptance cases, and WP-031's `syncTaskReminders` and its jobs test, which now take a list of tasks.

## How it was verified

The author (Opus 5.5) ran every check on the head commit against an isolated schema on the shared development database. Fix round 1 answers the verifier's review of `24f271c`. Generated work used to sync reminders once per task, and a reschedule could send a delivered due reminder a second time. Fix round 2 answers the review of `b1d073c`: reads trusted the earlier viewer lookup, so a removed or demoted reader could still read.

- Integration tests, `corepack pnpm --filter @everyfield/domain test:tasks` (8 tests, the public operations on real Postgres):
  ```
  ok 1 - AC:TARGET-TSK-002 AC:B03-007 AC:B03-008 AC:B03-009 AC:TARGET-TSK-018 create, edit and delete keep a valid task or change nothing
  ok 2 - AC:TARGET-TSK-001 AC:B03-001 AC:B03-002 AC:B03-003 views, stable pages, counts and due state
  ok 3 - AC:TARGET-TSK-003 AC:TARGET-TSK-015 own-duty completion, one result per request, reopen and history
  ok 4 - AC:TARGET-TSK-017 AC:PERSONREF-TASK-PERSON-FOLLOW-UP-RETIRE generated follow-ups and evaluation never duplicate or return
  ok 5 - AC:TARGET-TSK-014 due and overdue reminders follow the current assignee and stop when settled
  ok 6 - INV-statements: page reads are one statement and generated work costs the same for any batch size
  ok 7 - AC:TARGET-TSK-014 a delivered due reminder is not sent again after the deadline moves
  ok 8 - INV-tenancy: a seat ended, demoted or signed out after the viewer lookup reads no task data
  # pass 8
  # fail 0
  ```
  What the tests prove, in short:
  - A fold saves 2026-11-01T06:30Z or 07:30Z, depending on the chosen offset.
  - A Chicago date-only task becomes overdue at the next local midnight, also on the 23 and 25 hour days.
  - 51 tasks with equal keys page as 50 + 2 with no duplicates, and the two checklist rows count separately.
  - A foreign team returns no rows.
  - A finalize that fails before commit leaves no tasks or obligations.
  - A waived or deleted follow-up is not recreated.
  - A retired Person keeps their historical task link but cannot be named on a new task.
  - A reassigned task's old reminders are cancelled and refused at send time.
- Generated work at the meeting-finalization caller, from

## Why

Both LongMemEval cuts saturated retrieval. Measured on the saved cognee runs:

| variant | k | questions with recall = 1 | precision = 1 | distinct sessions touched per question |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| xs | 3 / 10 | 93% / 100% | 100% at every k | 1.9 |
| xs-shared | 5 / 10 | 93% / 97% | 7% | 6.4 / 12.2 of a 28–38-session history |

`xs` had no fillers, so every retrieved session was evidence. `xs-shared`'s users were small enough that the agent read about a third of a history for each question.

## What

- **Drop `xs`.** A history built from one question's evidence needs about 46 fillers to reach `s`'s filler share, and that is `s` again (7,002 sessions).
- **`xs-shared`: 3 users with 20 fillers each** (was 10 users with 5). The evidence is the cost, so dealing it into fewer users keeps ingestion flat while each history becomes about 3.5× larger.
- **Abstention histories** get 5 fillers from their own haystack (was evidence only).

Measured from `longmemeval_s_cleaned.json`:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| non-evidence share of a question's history | 0.878 | **0.966** (LoCoMo 0.952, `s` 0.960) |
| sessions per user | 28–38 | 109–117 |
| histories / sessions / turns | 20 / 343 / 3,807 | 13 / 403 / 4,489 |
| Mem0 ingestion (extrapolated from `oracle`) | ~4 h | ~5 h |

METHODOLOGY.md, README.md and AGENTS.md are updated to match.

`runs/longmemeval/` and `plots/longmemeval/` are deleted. Every run there was measured on `xs` or the 10-user `xs-shared` cut. author: johnib
body:
## What

Bounded failure signals on query telemetry:

- `kustomcp.query.failure_category` on `kusto.query` and the execute-query span: `query_semantic`, `auth_forbidden`, `throttled`, `server_error`, `network`, `timeout`, `cancelled`, `not_connected`, `other`. Comes from outcome, error class, HTTP status and network code, never the message. `kusto.query` also gets `kustomcp.http.status_code`.
- "Connection not initialized" now records `error.type=NotInitialized` / `not_connected` wherever it's raised (requireConnection McpError, queries.ts, KustoConnectionError).
- New retry classes: `after_empty`, `after_timeout`, `after_not_connected`. `after_in_flight` spans also carry `kustomcp.session.last_completed_outcome`.
- execute-query spans get `kustomcp.session.failure_streak` (`0`,`1`,`2`,`3-4`,`5+`) and `kustomcp.hint.fired` (`none`,`failure_streak`,`timeout`), including invalid-args calls.
- README telemetry list updated.

Label change to note for dashboards: `kustomcp.tool.errors` `error_type` for not-connected calls is now `NotInitialized` (was `McpError`). Non-Error throws still report `unknown`.

## Why

Honeycomb, last 30 days: 1,694 not-connected execute-query calls were labelled `McpError` / `after_error`, 1,258 `executeQuery` spans were `KustoQueryError` from the old not-connected path, and `kusto.query` never had an HTTP status, so 13,917 `AxiosError` failures (mostly KQL 400s) couldn't be told apart from network or auth faults.

## How tested

- Lint, `tsc --noEmit`, typecheck, unit (562/562), build all pass.
- Red to green: new tests in `tests/unit/suites/query-failure-telemetry.test.ts` fail with the src changes reverted (25 on the first pass, then 5 more after review fixes: 400 `BadRequest_EntityNotFound` gives `other`, 408 gives `other`, ETIMEDOUT gives `network` / `after_error`, invalid-args spans carry streak/hint).
- One existing test changed: the not-connected case in `query-intent-telemetry.test.ts` now expects `after_not_connected` instead of `after_error`.
- E2E on the built server over stdio against help.kusto.windows.net, spans caught by a local OTLP sink: execute-query before connecting gives `NotInitialized` / `not_connected`; a bad column gives `query_semantic` + `400`; five failures in a row step the streak `1`, `2`, `3-4`, `3-4`, `5+` and the hint fires from the 3rd; `KUSTO_QUERY_TIMEOUT=1` gives `timeout`, `hint.fired=timeout` and then `after_timeout`. Not run live: `last_completed_outcome` (needs overlapping requests) and EntityNotFound inside a query (a missing DB fails at initialize-connection), so both are unit-tested only.

User-visible text is the same. Before and after, an unconnected call returns:
```
MCP Error: MCP error -32600: Connection not initialized. Please call initialize-connection first.
```

The title has `[skip ci]` so this batch releases once. The session-extent PR goes in last.

body:
## What this does
Supplier learning (the per-vendor "template") now only counts a learned spot as evidence when it has earned it. A vendor that changes or alternates its layout can no longer turn what was learned into a wrong *verified* value, or a wrong touchless invoice.

- **Unsettled template readings:** a reading taken without its label, from an unsettled spot, from a relabelled spot, or from spots that disagree is marked `template-unsettled`.
  - It has its own unmeasured evidence family and is never counted as an independent reader.
  - It still contests the chosen value, and it fills an empty field only at *check*.
- **Spots vouched for:** a spot counts after one approval where the value was printed only there, or two approvals in a row.
  - A value printed in two places is learned at both, as "twins". A twin counts only when all its twins are read.
  - A spot holding a different value from the one approved starts over.
  - Another label at a spot is another layout's spot.
- **Smaller fixes:**
  - A % value is never an amount.
  - The learned day/month order applies only to the same date form.
  - The totals solver no longer replaces a value two readers chose first.
  - The supplier's name printed again is not an anchor.
- **Bugs:** B-387 to B-393 and B-420 to B-423 are fixed with failing tests first. N-127, N-128 and N-134/N-135 are logged. Decision D-46.

## How it was checked
- **Independent reviews, English invoices only:** three rounds built Canadian English supplier streams to break it: relabels, alternating and rotating layouts, twins that coincide and then differ, stubs, missing rows, and old stored templates. The final round, against main, found no wrong value verified or touchless where main held it. Main itself sends 1–8 wrong invoices touchless in the layout-change streams; this branch sends 0.
- **Real repeat-vendor invoices:**

author: firejune
body:
Closes #198. The finding comes from the rig-c/play#150 review: npm provenance records `GITHUB_SHA`, not the checked-out HEAD.

**Choice: the card's (b), applied on dispatch.** In "Resolve the tag to publish", after the on-main check, a dispatch refuses unless `GITHUB_SHA` equals the tag's commit:
```
PROVENANCE_SHA_MISMATCH: the run's GITHUB_SHA <sha> is not vX.Y.Z's commit <sha>, and npm provenance would name the former; dispatch with --ref vX.Y.Z
```
In effect a recovery publish is dispatched on the tag itself (`gh workflow run release.yml --ref vX.Y.Z -f tag=vX.Y.Z`).

Why (b) and not (a): a tag cut before this check carries the old workflow. Dispatching on such a tag would run that older file, and nothing here can make that safe. So only tags cut after this check can be re-published. The push path is unchanged. No credential or trusted-publisher setting changes.

**Mock** (the resolve step extracted from the parsed YAML, run in a scratch clone with a fake `GITHUB_OUTPUT`; no publish, no dispatch):
| case | output | exit |
|---|---|---|
| dispatch v0.10.1 from main (GITHUB_SHA = main a9fc9cb) | `PROVENANCE_SHA_MISMATCH: the run's GITHUB_SHA a9fc9cb4… is not v0.10.1's commit a8c409ef…` | 1 |
| dispatch v0.10.1 on the tag (GITHUB_SHA = a8c409e) | passes the new check; then `RELEASE_ALREADY_PUBLISHED` (0.10.1 is on the registry) | 1 |
| push, release created | `publish=true tag=v0.10.2` | 0 |
| push, no release | `publish=false` | 0 |

YAML parses. README's Releasing paragraph says how to dispatch.

The refusal name matches what HQ asked of play#155 (`PROVENANCE_SHA_MISMATCH`), so the two repos refuse with the same code.

author: martinkadauke
body:
## Why

The push monitor `aikos-transcriber` went down ~1×/hour for ~30 s with `whisper down;` since 20.10. (41 times in 20 h), while Whisper was running. The heartbeat was an unversioned script on the Mac (`curl -m 4 http://127.0.0.1:6667/`).

**Cause (reproduced):** the Mac has been up for 51.7 days. macOS keeps TCP time in milliseconds in 32 bits, which wraps after 49.7 days of uptime (a known XNU bug, public since April 2026). After that TIME_WAIT never ends: 13,272 sockets were stuck, 5,800 of them each to Home Assistant and to Whisper, which is exactly the number of heartbeats since the wrap. Whisper itself holds ~430 of them. A connection from a local port that Whisper still holds in TIME_WAIT never opens, so the heartbeat's 4 s timeout reported `whisper down`.
- `curl --local-port 60521 http://127.0.0.1:6667/` (a port Whisper still holds): 4.0 s, no connection.
- The same request from a free port: 1 ms, HTTP 200.

The burst 05:35–05:55 UTC was the sequential port allocator crossing a range that many Whisper requests had used, not a schedule.

**"Busy = dead" does not hold:** whisper-server answers `/` and `/health` outside its inference lock (11 HTTP threads). Measured: `/health` < 1 ms during a running transcription, and false alarms also came while nothing had been transcribed for an hour.

The same fault cost a door message its final text: the worker's connection to Whisper never opened (`<urlopen error timed out>`). The receiver hands over a stream that stops mid-sentence whole; that is now a regression test.

The real fix for the Mac is a restart (operations, not this PR). This PR fixes the signal, so the monitor shows what is actually wrong. The monitor's window is not widened.

## What

- `aikos_transcriber/heartbeat.py` (`python -m aikos_transcriber.heartbeat [--dry-run] [--env FILE]`), one check per run:
  - receivers listening on UDP 5006 + 5008;
  - Whisper `/health` (503 = loading model);
  - HA `/api/` with the transcriber's token.
- A stalled connection is retried once on a new connection, which means a new local port. Refused counts at once.
- Past the wrap, with ≥ 1,000 TIME_WAIT, it reports `Mac restart needed: up N d, macOS TCP clock wrapped at 49.7 d, TIME_WAIT never ends (N now)` instead of blaming Whisper. With ≥ 8,192 TIME_WAIT it reports `TCP ports running out`, whatever the uptime. From 45 days on, the up message names the restart time.
- The push token never appears in any output.
- `deploy/launchd.py` writes `home.aikos.heartbeat` (StartInterval 30, pinned Python, from the checkout) when `AIKOS_HEARTBEAT_URL` is set.
- `deploy.sh` backs the heartbeat agent up, restarts it after the receivers, restores it on rollback, and logs its dry-run verdict. The verdict is no gate, because it also judges the Mac.
- README (heartbeat section, settings, history), `transcriber.env.example`, version 1.3.2.

The transcription logic is unchanged: monitoring and deployment only. A new receiver test was added in the roomkey maintainers' area (no code change there).

## Tests

- 95 unit tests green locally (Windows, Python 3.14; bash tests skipped there).
- `test_deploy.py` green on the Mac (Apple Python 3.9.6, `/bin/bash` 3.2).
- New: `tests/test_heartbeat.py` (20) and the deploy/launchd cases.
- New: `DoorTurn.test_a_stream_that_stops_mid_sentence_is_handed_over_whole`.
- Live dry-run on the Mac against the running setup: `down: Mac restart needed: up 51.7 d, macOS TCP clock wrapped at 49.7 d, TIME_WAIT never ends (13328 now)`.
- Privacy scan with the private denylist: clean.

## Rollout (after OK, announced first)

1. Add `AIKOS_HEARTBEAT_URL` and `AIKOS_HEARTBEAT_TOKEN_FILE` to the house settings file.
2. Run `deploy.sh transcriber-v1.3.2`. The hand-written agent is backed up and replaced, and comes back on rollback.

author: oluwajubelo1
body:
## Summary

This adds calendar and rolling budget windows, fixes attribution and budget enforcement in several places, and adds Fiber v3 middleware. Several of these came out of questions after the GopherCon Africa talk.

### Features
- **Budget windows.** `RollingWindow(d)`, `CalendarDay(loc)` and `CalendarMonth(loc)`, for both stores (`NewInMemoryBudgetStoreWithWindow`, `NewRedisBudgetStoreWithWindow`) or through `BudgetConfig.Window`. For calendar windows, `ResetAt` reports the start of the next period.
- **Limits for calls with no user.** Every LLM span and request span now carries `llm.user_attributed`. `BudgetConfig.UnattributedLimit` sets one shared limit for all calls with no user ID; before this, those calls skipped per-user limits entirely.
- **Verified identity in middleware.** `WithUserFromContext` / `WithProjectFromContext` (Gin, Echo, Fiber) read IDs that the app's auth middleware has already verified. They replace the unverified JWT `sub` and the `X-Project-ID` header, which a caller could forge to get a new budget on every request.
- **Fiber v3 middleware** in its own module, `middleware/fiber` (Go 1.25+), so Fiber and fasthttp stay out of the main module.
- `PerUserLimit` / `PerProjectLimit` replace `PerUserDailyLimit` / `PerProjectDailyLimit`. The old names were misleading because the limit applies to the configured window, not a day. The old fields are deprecated but still work.

### Fixes
- **Redis:** budget keys expired after a fixed 48 hours. With a window longer than that, a user who made no calls for two days lost their spend history.
- **`TraceStream`** ignored the user and project in the context, so streams behind middleware or `ContextWithUser` weren't attributed and skipped per-user and per-project budgets.
- **Default store race:** without an explicit `Store`, concurrent first calls on a config each created their own store, and the spend recorded in the extra stores was lost. In one run of the new test, only $0.06 of $0.50 was recorded.
- **`BudgetExceededError` / `BudgetStatus`** reported the user's budget even when the project's limit was the one that blocked the call.

## Behaviour changes

No public API is removed, so this can ship as **v1.4.0**. These changes should go in the release notes:
- `TraceStream` now enforces user and project budgets taken from the context, so streams that used to go through may now be blocked.
- `BudgetExceededError` and `BudgetStatus`, including the status passed to prompt decorators, now describe whichever budget has the least remaining.
- The in-memory store merges calls that land close together. For rolling windows, spend can count for up to 1/1000 of the window longer than before. This errs towards blocking, not overspending.

## Release steps

1. Merge, then tag `v1.4.0`.
2. Update `middleware/fiber/go.mod` to require `github.com/oluwajubelo1/otellix v1.4.0` and remove the `replace ../..` line. Until then the module only builds inside this repo, because it uses `internal/identity`, which first ships in v1.4.0.
3. Tag `middleware/fiber/v0.1.0`.

`internal/identity` is shared across the module boundary, so its API should stay stable. If it ever has to change, release a new Fiber version at the same time.

## Docs

- New: `docs/budget-windows.md`, `docs/attribution.md`.
- Rewritten: `docs/middleware.md` (Gin, Echo and Fiber, with a verified-identity setup for each) and `docs/budget-guardrails.md` (full config reference).
- `docs/streaming.md` gets a new section on attribution and budgets for streams.

## Testing

- Each commit passes `gofmt`, `go vet` and `go test -race ./...` in both modules, checked by checking out every commit separately. The Redis tests ran against a local Redis.
- New tests:
  - window start and reset times, including time zones and the December-to-January rollover
  - Redis calendar months and key expiry
  - forged-token cases for each middleware
  - `TraceStream` picking up identity from the context
  - `UnattributedLimit`, and which budget the error reports
  - concurrent first calls on one config
- The `TraceStream` and race tests were confirmed to fail without their fixes.
- CI gets a job for the Fiber module, because `go test ./...` at the root skips nested modules.
- `golangci-lint` wasn't run locally: the installed binary was built with an older Go than the local toolchain.

author: sadiksaifi
body:
## Summary

A person managing a SpaceTerm server on another computer can now start, stop, restart, uninstall and update it from SpaceTerm instead of opening a terminal on that machine. Every operation runs over the SSH route that already admitted the connection, using that account's own authority. An operation that is interrupted stays resolvable afterwards, including after the desktop is lost and after its saved connection is removed.

## Changes

- The service answers one bounded request and one bounded reply over `ssh-maintain`, and retains each submitted operation so resubmitting it returns the retained outcome instead of acting twice.
- A destructive operation is described against one exact observation and only that description authorizes it, so a Stop confirmed while the server was running cannot stop work started afterwards.
- A service operation completes only when the policy the service observes is the one the action promises. An apply that merely resumed an interrupted local activation reports an Unconfirmed Outcome instead of claiming a Stop or Uninstall it never performed.
- `ssh-stage` retains one exact verified artifact beside the approved installation; it installs, activates and starts nothing until a separately confirmed activation.
- The client retains each submitted operation privately, continues unresolved ones quietly after relaunch without ever prompting, and keeps a result presented after its saved connection is removed until the person acknowledges it.
- A maintenance exchange holds its route for its duration, so choosing Disconnect or Remove while an operation is underway cannot cut a dispatched reply.
- Settings > Servers and the sidebar machine heading offer the operations the server's observed state allows, with confirmations that name the machine and say whose Terminal Sessions end. Both read every operation the client holds for a server, and every step that retires a record names the record whose row offered it.
- An owned guard reserves each SSH process group before launch and terminates it if the desktop dies, including SIGKILL; normal cleanup also reaps both direct children.
- ADRs 0030, 0034, 0037, 0039 and 0040, `CONTEXT.md` and the local workflow say what this route may do and what it may never do.

## Verification

Final client head: `88c0bf447be5905968230b9be5f772711f290e81`.

- `mise run validate` on macOS at the final head: passed, exit 0, including native tests, both engine configurations, packaging, installation and updater checks.
- `mise run test:native:ssh` on macOS and Debian 13 Penguin: passed, including actual owner SIGKILL with null and piped IO, descendants, a second owned group, and closed standard output; the regression failed on both hosts before the fix.
- `mise run server:ssh:desktop:test ssh::process`: 19 passed; `mise run lint:rust` on both hosts, `mise run fmt:check` and `mise run lint:diff` passed.
- Settings regressions: 27 maintenance and 28 server-list tests passed; the approved-version assertion failed before the UI fix.
- Actual signed macOS Development desktop at the final head: an external watcher saw durable server admission before sending SIGKILL during Stop, a stopped-server update, and a running-server update. Every client record still had no outcome when killed. Relaunch and explicit Check Again or Finish Update recovered the same original, with one journal entry and preserved server identity. Stop stayed stopped; the stopped update stayed stopped; the running update recovered running. After every kill, the desktop's guards and SSH transports exited automatically before relaunch.
- Actual removed-connection recovery at the final head: Remove Connection retained the interrupted stopped update. Finish Update recovered its exact result without restoring the saved connection, and OK retired the record.
- Signed Linux server candidate from the final head: `dev.88c0bf447be5`, complete archive SHA256 `2987ed7f35fbc990eedc4f66635341d10a6cac0b7d238adb404c2d06eb642ed8`; native package verification and Mac signature/digest verification passed against existing update trust.
- Those final-client crash tests used the independently verified signed `eb28dec9` and `6b57e22` server archives. The `eb28dec9` archive SHA256 is `3b4fad4bca1cbc3a8256855b4cbfad5b6d964dca4e9270d195e91ab2646e037e`.
- Real OS refusal on a disposable Penguin account with the signed `eb28dec9` candidate: kernel EACCES on only that account's manager sockets caused native preparation and confirmed apply to return `authorization_required` without activation admission. The desktop backend reported `ServiceUnavailable` during discovery and sent no maintenance dispatch. Runtime PID/start time, policy and saved organization stayed identical; the same live Terminal Session accepted input during denial and survived reconnect. Restored checks passed. The test account, service, runtime and lingering were removed; no sdk policy or authorization rules were changed by this refusal test.
- `SPACETERM_SSH_NATIVE_DESTINATION=penguin SPACETERM_SSH_NATIVE_EXPECT=ready SPACETERM_SSH_SERVER_ARTIFACTS=/private/tmp/pr607-final88-candidate mise run server:ssh:maintenance:native:originals` at the final head: passed actual Stop, same-original resolution, explicit Start, stale-Stop-confirmation refusal, signed staging and running activation to the exact final-head archive. Native observe also passed on the final client; the native recovery task passed earlier at `eb28dec9`, followed by the final-head real desktop recovery checks above.
- Real Debian 13 window at the final head: Check Now showed `dev.eb28dec9a451` in both version rows; Settings and sidebar offered the running-service actions; both Stop confirmations were cancelled. PID/start time, policy and journal hashes stayed unchanged. The version briefly reads Unknown behind an open confirmation and returns after Cancel.

### Known limitations

- The surfaces added in the final round have been driven only in the GPUI test harness, not in a window: the notice shown when this client cannot save its operations record, the final word for an original the service has no record of, and the presentation of two unsettled originals on one machine.
- Acknowledging an operation on a server whose service this client never read leaves the row showing what the connection observed before the operation. Driving the real app on macOS, an explicit Start Server succeeded and Penguin reported `running: true; stopped: false`, but after OK the row read `Stopped` and offered Start Server again. Choosing Check Now corrects it, and nothing destructive is offered from that state.
- An original the service has no record of retires the client's record. That means either the dispatch never arrived, or the service evicted an original it admitted and could not validate: it keeps eight and gives up an unconfirmed one once no resolved original is left to drop. The client says it cannot tell which.
- A Restart admitted into the window where a local activation is resumed still reports completed. The retained policy shows a running, not-stopped server, which is what Restart promises, but it cannot name which operation left it that way. Stop and Uninstall are guarded exactly.
- Build strings a remote service reports are bounded and typed but are not re-validated by the client before being shown in an update confirmation. The account that would have to be compromised already owns the route.
- Describing a change reaches the service through the shared local control path, which resumes an admitted activation. Reading facts avoids that and stays read-only.
- Unresolved native cleanup makes a read refuse rather than report partial facts, so the local "retry a refused Stop" path is not reachable from here.
- About 440 production lines of recorded simplification are deliberately not applied here; they are listed in a comment on this PR. The largest changes the on-disk record format.
- The final UI and SSH lifetime fixes have targeted regres

body:
UI pass for the Profession Ledger (brief 04). Same layout and same data; the window now matches the Ashen Gate standard.

## What changes
- **Header:** "Ashen Gate | Profession Ledger" with the version and a small Help button on the right. Help still opens a dialog with Close.
- **Tabs** scroll sideways when the window is narrow. Assign and GM Setup come last and are marked GM.
- **Player Access (D4)** is now a tick box in GM Setup. Nothing changes until **Save Changes**. Cancel (or leaving GM Setup and choosing Discard changes) puts it back. Same setting key, so no migration is needed.
- **Quality uses the item rarity colours (D6):** a "Quality: Common / Rare / Exotic" badge in grey, blue and purple.
  - It shows on the gathering chat card (replacing "(rare bundle)"), the GM's last-gather note, the Exotic picker and the material lists.
  - No tier field was added; boss-tier (artifact colour) stays future.
- **Tables:** Tools and checks, the baseline preview and Assign use the shared striped table with a sticky head and `th scope`.
  - The dropdowns show their whole text; on a narrow window the table scrolls sideways (that scroll position is still kept).
  - Assign with no characters shows an empty state below the table instead of a table row.
- **Lists:** materials, party professions and the party roster use shared rows. Counts are badges. The two switches (By player / By profession, Location / Ad-hoc node) use the shared segmented control. Empty states say what's missing and the next step; player wording never mentions GM tools.
- **Buttons:** one gold button per pane. Craft, Learn, Approve and Roll are now plain; Save Changes, Start gathering, Request gather and Add all missing stay gold.
- **Hover text** uses Foundry tooltips instead of `title=`. The disabled "Open General Manager" button says why next to it.
- **Narrow and Comfortable:** narrow windows stack the two columns based on the window's own width, not the screen's. The Comfortable size (General Manager → My Appearance) opens the window 1.2× larger (`windowSize()` from the shared `ag-html.mjs`, added as an identical copy).
- **Lint:** all module rules are at 0. Only this module's line in `scripts/ui-lint-baseline.json` changed. No saved data, flags, setting keys or `data-action` names changed (the old `toggle-player-access` button is replaced by the D4 tick box).

## Tests
- `node scripts/check.mjs` passes (Ledger: 194 tests).
- New `tests/ui-pass-v0240.test.mjs` covers:
  - D4: no write on tick; Save Changes writes only Player Access; Cancel asks first, Keep editing keeps the draft, Discard writes nothing; players can't save.
  - The Comfortable window size.
  - No `title=` in any tab.
  - The visible Manager reason, the table, the segmented control and the Assign empty state.
- Gathering tests also check the Common, Rare and Exotic badges on the chat card.
- **The tests use mocked Foundry.** They prove the logic, not the look; the look needs your eyes.

## Renders
Before/after Chromium renders: every tab as GM and as a player, Standard / Stone Tablet / Parchment / Tome Pages, Compact and Comfortable, windows 1180 / 760 / 420, plus the chat card: https://claude.ai/artifact/VJE2Vn3tukcjT9WCEMCB8m (private to you). They use synthetic [TEST] data, without Foundry's core CSS or Font Awesome, so icons are missing there. Skin contrast is checked by the lint for every skin.

## Check in Forge (after merge, update the module)
1. Open the Profession Ledger as GM. The header reads "Ashen Gate | Profession Ledger" with the version and Help on the right. Help opens a dialog with Close.
2. GM Setup: untick **Players can open the Profession Ledger**. Nothing changes yet (a player's launcher stays). Press **Cancel**, choose **Discard changes**, and it's ticked again. Untick again and press **Save Changes**: now players lose the Ledger. Tick it and save again to restore.
3. Gathering: run a check that succeeds by 5+ on a node with a rare material and an Exotic candidate. The chat card shows a blue "Quality: Rare" and a purple "Quality: Exotic" badge. Common materials show grey in Individual → Materials.
4. As a player: the tabs work, the Party lists read cleanly, and the GM Setup table is striped (as GM).
5. My Appearance → **Comfortable**, then reopen the Ledger: the window is larger and nothing clips. Switch back.
6. Switch to **Tome Pages** and **Stone Tablet**: everything is readable. Make the window narrow: the tabs scroll and the columns stack.

Only you can check: the material consent and gathering roll dialogs as a player with a GM online, Foundry core CSS interplay, and real window resizing on The Forge.

author: cri4key
body:
FakeEncryptGameEbootStep assumes the program header table starts right after the ELF header. This is correct for original, untouched EBOOTs, but ELFs patched via SPRXPatcher have such table moved at the end of the file and thus the offset needs to be recomputed correctly and the table data copied at the right place. This has never been a problem so far on either PS3 or RPCS3 as it was ignored, but recent RPCS3 upstream changes now rely on it effectively making it now unusable on newer RPCS3 releases.

This is a fix on the end of AxeHax tooling (and should be used on Refresher as well) but to actually work properly the RPCS3 upstream needs to still implement some changes that I have submitted in the [PRs](https://github.com/RPCS3/rpcs3/pull/19900) that is at fault, as for the "right" way to handle it both need to implement these changes unless upstream decides to just revert everything.

author: zylkien
body:
## Summary

Implements Castle Siege tactical mini-map updates and alliance-master commands.

Continues #941 by @didiconcs, preserving the original commits and addressing the review of `65546e19`. The implementation is integrated with current master, including the previously merged Castle Siege features.

Closes #730.

## Behavior

- Participating alliance masters receive same-side player positions and living gate/statue positions every three seconds during battle.
- Commands preserve the selected command-group slot and reach only same-side players on the siege map.
- Invalid command groups, unknown command types, and truncated packets are rejected.
- Command attempts are atomically throttled before acquiring the siege lock, including unauthorized attempts.

The existing push model is retained: the client protocol has no mini-map subscription request or acknowledgment. Eligible alliance masters receive updates automatically.

## Review fixes and hardening

- Capture player sides and positions once per broadcast, preventing dictionary lookup failures when recipients leave.
- Use the injected clock for deterministic cooldown behavior.
- Recheck authorization and battle state under the siege lock.
- Reject issuers whose resolved side is `None`.
- Preserve player-before-NPC packet ordering and the broadcast cadence after failed sends.
- Bound NPC marker counts to the packet’s one-byte limit.
- Restore the resource designer’s UTF-8 BOM.
- Add regression tests, player/operator documentation, and update handler progress.

## Verification

- Server and packet-test builds succeeded.
- 179 Castle Siege tests passed.
- 154 Castle-related packet tests passed.
- Regenerated packet code, documentation, and tests from XML.
- Reviewed generated changes and checked the diff for whitespace errors.
