author: ntoufoudis
body:
Closes #223.

## What and why

The `z` of `@hostmesh/ui` runs with `jitless` (#144, #222). An app that imported `zod` itself could build a schema before that setting ran, and zod's `new Function` probe would violate the production policy again. Until now only the end-to-end suite would have noticed. Now `pnpm lint` does.

- **`web/eslint.config.js`:** a block for `apps/**/*.{ts,vue}` rejects `zod` (a `paths` entry) and `zod/*` (a pattern). The ESLint docs confirm that you need both: a path doesn't cover its subpaths (`zod/v4`, `zod/mini`), and `zod/*` doesn't cover bare `zod`.
- **The trap from the issue:** a later flat-config block replaces a rule's options rather than adding to them. So the apps block repeats the HTTP-library list, which is now a shared constant (`restrictedHttpImports`). `packages/ui` keeps the HTTP restriction only and may import `zod`.
- **`web/eslint.config.test.ts`** (the `workspace` project, added to `tsconfig.node.json`): lints sample code at app and package paths through the real configuration with ESLint's Node API (`ESLint#lintText`). The files don't need to exist.

## Tests first

1. **Red:** the 4 direct-import cases failed (`.vue` with `zod`, `.ts` with `zod`, `zod/v4`, `zod/mini`). The 5 others passed: they guard behavior that already worked.
2. **Proved the guard cases can fail:** a naive separate `apps/**` block with only the zod rule made `an app › still may not import an HTTP library` fail. That's the trap.
3. **Green:** the final config passes all 9.
4. **`pnpm lint` on a real file:** with `apps/portal/src/views/LoginView.vue` temporarily importing `z` from `zod/v4`, lint exited 1:
   ```
   4:1  error  'zod/v4' import is restricted from being used by a pattern. Import z from @hostmesh/ui: it runs zod without eval, which the production policy forbids  no-restricted-imports
   ```
   The file was restored afterwards.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] **`pnpm lint` fails when a file under `apps/` imports `zod` or one of its subpaths**, with a message that points to `z` from `@hostmesh/ui`. Shown above; covered by 4 test cases.
- [x] **The existing restrictions on HTTP libraries still apply.** Tested for an app (`axios`) and for `packages/ui` (`ky`). The app case caught the replacement trap.
- [x] **`packages/ui/src/components/form/zod.ts` and the package's tests may still import `zod`.** Tested for `zod.ts` and `typed-schema.test.ts`.

## Checks

- `… exec node pnpm check`: lint, typecheck, 54 test files / 386 tests with the coverage gate, both builds, all pass
- `make -C infrastructure/hygiene spdx`: passed

Docs: `web/README.md` (Rules) and `web/packages/ui/README.md` (Forms) say that apps take `z` from `@hostmesh/ui`, and why.

## Deviations needing your input

None.

## Follow-ups

- `packages/ui/src/components/form/zod.test.ts` (from #222) imports `../../index` with `import()` inside the test. That's what the README rule from #203 warns about: under a loaded full run, the import spends the test's own time. It passed locally and in CI, but it could become flaky. The dynamic import isn't needed: zod probes when the first object schema is built, not on import. A static import at the top, with the spy set before the schema is built, gives the same guarantee.

body: Unlit meshes render with a MeshBasicMaterial, which ignores scene lighting, so their color is drawn flat, without shading (#620). Like point clouds and images, they also skip tone mapping, so a single-color unlit mesh renders exactly the requested color. (Batched meshes are flat too, but their per-instance colors are currently off by a pre-existing sRGB-decode issue.) Accepted everywhere the existing standard/toon3/toon5 options are: add_mesh_simple, add_mesh_skinned, add_batched_meshes_simple, add_box, add_icosphere, and add_cylinder. As with the toon materials, wireframe=True still overrides the material. Unlit meshes still cast shadows; they ignore receive_shadow=True, while a float receive_shadow still draws shadows.

author: re2zero
body:
Part 6/8 of the reverse tunnel stack (recovery of #802).

This reapplies the reviewed commit on top of the corrected stack because #802 was accidentally merged into its stacked base branch instead of master.

Merge order: #805 → #806 → #807 → #808 → #809 → #810 → #811.
Retargeted to master after #808 merged.

QAbstractSocket buffers incoming bytes in user space without a limit by
default, draining the kernel even when the tunnel credit window is full.
The sender's file server therefore never blocked and reported progress up
to 100% while the receiver was still downloading a large file.

Cap each tunnel stream socket at twice the credit window so TCP
backpressure reaches the writer.

Log: cap tunnel socket read buffers for flow control
PMS: TASK-396845
Influence: large transfers apply TCP backpressure instead of reporting progress the receiver has not received.

## Summary by Sourcery

Restore TCP flow control for tunnel streams by limiting socket read buffering.

Bug Fixes:
- Cap tunnel stream socket read buffers so TCP backpressure is applied when the credit window is full, preventing large transfers from reporting progress before data is received.

Tests:
- Add coverage verifying that tunnel sockets on both sides use the configured read-buffer limit.

author: tse-wei-chen
body:
## Goal

Continue PR #47's real FFmpeg embedded-subtitle **metadata** capability into the C# runtime. This is a first-party, version-negotiated P/Invoke adapter; **no subtitle packets are decoded or presented** in this PR.

## Changes

- Add `EmbeddedSubtitleTrack` (actual `StreamIndex`, `Text / Bitmap / Unknown`, language tag, codec name) to `Lapis.Contracts.Media`.
- Add optional read-only Application port `IEmbeddedSubtitleTrackInventoryRuntime` without modifying `IPlaybackRuntime`.
- Implement the port in `NativePlaybackRuntime`: require an existing matching Session, version-check the optional native extension, probe count then read up to 64 owned descriptors, pass caller's Epoch, guard malicious counts and fields, map to immutable contracts.
- Implement `NativeSubtitleTrackInfo` as the exact 72-byte fixed layout (8 bytes of numbers + 24 byte language + 40 byte codec), with NUL-terminated UTF-8 decoding; no native pointer escapes and no UI-thread hot-path reads.
- Add the P/Invoke declarations and mockable API interface; an older DLL without the optional export throws an informative `NotSupportedException` **only when this optional feature is requested**, without failing normal player startup.
- Extend runtime tests for layout, text/bitmap metadata, container indexes, missing/unsupported versions, stale Epoch/closed state, cancellation, no lazy Session creation, count/termination errors.
- Document architecture boundary and later steps; no Native C ABI modifications, no new audio/video dependencies.

## Tests

- [x] One logical commit on branch cut from merged `develop` commit `f36a7941`
- [ ] Managed CI Build/xUnit (no local dotnet SDK)
- [ ] Existing CI outcome and code review before merge

## Limitations

**Embedded tracks are metadata-only**. Do not expose them as playable entries in Watch yet. The next milestone must implement stream-specific subtitle packet routing and actual decoded timed text before adapting `ITextSubtitleSource`. PGS is a bitmap subtitle, not plain text.

## Actions policy

One PR, one commit, no new workflow or manual run, target `develop` only. The PR's existing CI is the only intended run.

author: kcisek
body:
## What changed and why

Roadmap #40: a **`pick_and_place`** check in `check_dfm`'s assembly checks. It replaces the "pick-and-place centroids: not checked" line. Assemblers place parts by the pick-and-place file's Center-X/Y. That centre is wrong for asymmetric footprints and undefined for pad-less parts, and a misplaced board origin shifts the whole file against the Gerbers.

**How Altium computes the centre** (`server/services/dfm_assembly.py`, `centroids`):
- **Center-X/Y** is the midpoint of the box spanned by the pad centres. It counts every pad of the part (SMD and through-hole), not the copper extent.
- Coordinates are relative to the board origin (Board6 ORIGINX/Y).
- A part with no pads sits at the absolute origin.
- Rotation is the part's own, unmirrored on the bottom side.
- **Validation:** checked against 40 of Altium's own pick-and-place files found in a private set of boards (25 boards, aggregates only). It matches 2,571 of 2,571 rows exactly (0.0001 mm); the other 38 rows belong to parts edited after the file was made. The existing copper-extent centre would have missed 304 rows, by up to 1.4 mm.

**Findings:**
- **Asymmetric parts (info):** parts whose Center-X/Y is far from their 3D body or reference point. Typical cases are edge connectors, through-hole connectors and modules. The text gives the offset and the fix: send Ref-X/Y to the assembler, or centre the footprint.
- **Pad-less parts:** a placed part without pads is a warning, since Altium puts it at the absolute origin. Graphical, mechanical and no-BOM parts are info.
- **Board origin (info):** origin not set, outside the board, or away from the outline's lower-left corner (0.1 mm tolerance). Real Altium outputs were made from such boards, so this stays info.
- **Not checked** (listed in the result): Ref-X/Y, Pad-X/Y, Y-flip, and rotation against the assembler's zero orientation.
- `pcb_manufacturing_review`, the docstring, manifest, README and CHANGELOG are updated.

## How to test

- `pytest`: 2080 passed, 11 skipped (after merging main). `ruff check server tests` is clean.
- **New tests:**
  - the box of pad centres versus the copper extent;
  - mixed SMD/THT parts and bottom-side parts;
  - pad-less parts;
  - origin cases;
  - a reader test against an Altium pick-and-place file (skipped when none is present; the public examples ship none).
- **Altium examples:**
  - MiniPC, Bluetooth Sentinel, PC4-SODIMM, WiFi and SL1 are advisory; WiFi_panel passes.
  - MiniPC: board connectors J20 and J6 sit 3.65–4.15 mm from their bodies. Every finding was inspected and none is false.
  - The check takes at most 0.29 s per board.
- **Private boards** (aggregates only): no exceptions, at most 0.04 s per board, pages up to 16k characters.
- **Review:** a skeptic review fixed:
  - an origin tolerance that was too tight;
  - 7 of 8 surviving mutants, now killed by new tests;
  - an overstated oracle count in the docs;
  - an invisible BOM character in a test.

## Checklist
- [x] Tests pass (`pytest`)
- [x] CHANGELOG updated

author: sage-manas
body:
Closes #286.

## The defect

`rowsFor` applied `LIMIT 200` **per document type**; `listReconciliation` then filtered by `state` in JS and reported `total: rows.length`. Two consequences:

- `total` was the capped page (at most 1,200), not the real backlog.
- With `?state=failed`, a type holding more than 200 older pending-past-SLA rows pushed its `failed` rows outside the LIMIT, so they disappeared from the filtered view — the queue silently hid exactly the rows it exists to surface.

## The fix

- **`state` is a SQL predicate now**, parameterised and validated, so the LIMIT applies *after* filtering. `pending` keeps its SLA condition. `synced`/`local` are success states (see `config/statuses.js`), so asking for them is a 400 rather than an empty list that reads like "nothing is synced".
- **`COUNT(*)` per type over the same WHERE** returns a true `total` plus `byType`; the response also carries `pageSize`. The page header now reads `253 documents need attention · showing 200 of 253 · pending SLA 4h`.
- **Cursor paging on `(updatedAt, pk)`** — the sort key itself, so rows arriving or being fixed mid-scroll can't make the next page skip or repeat. The `pk` tiebreak is what makes the order total; six types routinely share an `updatedAt` to the millisecond. A malformed cursor is a 400.
- **One WHERE builder** feeds both the `clientId` and no-`clientId` cases and both the page and the count query, so the counted predicate cannot drift from the shown one. The duplicated SQL is gone.

## Tests

`backend/tests/reconciliation-queue.test.js` gains the scenario from the issue — 250 pending-past-SLA ASNs plus 3 newer `failed` ones for one tenant:

- the unfiltered `total` is 253 while the page holds 200;
- `?state=failed` returns all 3;
- the two cursor pages cover all 253 rows exactly once, no repeats;
- `?state=synced` and a malformed cursor both 400.

All four fail against the previous controller (verified by swapping it back in: 4 failed / 8 passed) and pass with this one. Full backend suite green: 113 suites, 1461 passed, 2 skipped. `src/app/platform/platform-routes.test.jsx` passes.

author: btncwn
body:
Order S3-2: add **Telnet 23, Docker API 2375, WinRM 5985/5986 and memcached 11211** to the network probe. The probe records an open port and any banner only. It never attempts an exploit.

## Change

- **`contract.js`:** `PROBE_PORTS` gains the five ports. `validateNetworkProbeRequest` used to carry a **second hard-coded copy** of the list; it now reads `PROBE_PORTS`, so the contract and the serialized container program cannot drift. The program now carries `PROBE_PORTS` as a constant.
- **`collector.js`:** `identifyService` recognises **Telnet** from its own unprompted IAC option negotiation (`0xFF` followed by WILL, WONT, DO or DONT). Docker API, WinRM and memcached send nothing first, so they report **`open` with `service: null`**. No service is claimed without evidence.
- **The website-content bundle**, which inlines the contract, is rebuilt.

## Safety

- **Nothing is sent.** The collector connects, reads what the service volunteers, and closes. No request, command or credential goes to any of these services. Each fixture's server **counts the bytes it received and asserts 0**.
- **No TLS handshake** on any new port. The TLS list stays `443/465/993/995/8443`; 5986 is not handshaken.
- **Per-run limits unchanged:** 16 ports, 32 targets and 256 pairs per run, and the 90 s deadline. A fixture proves that a 17-port request is still refused.
- The scan-api route still only admits explicitly entered public literal addresses for authorised network targets; nothing about authorisation changed. The UI lists ports from the API's `allowed_ports`, so the new ports appear in the existing selector with no frontend change.

## Tests (`workers/network-probe/test/collector.test.js`, 31/31; `validate-network-probe.js`, 32/32)

- The new ports are accepted, 1234 and 2376 are refused, and more than 16 ports per run is refused.
- **Telnet:** the IAC banner gives `service: telnet`, basis `unsolicited_tcp_banner`, no TLS, 0 bytes sent and a valid receipt.
- **2375, 5985, 5986 and 11211:** a silent server gives `open` with no service claimed, no TLS, 0 bytes sent and a valid receipt.
- The **serialized container program** accepts all five ports. This is the drift the removed duplicate list would have caused.

Also passing locally: network-assets, scan-queue-dispatch and trial-daily-allowance validators; the website-content bundle check (rebuilt) and the TLS-collector bundle check; entry-point inventory; date-rot; the scan-api Worker syntax check; `git diff --check`. Anchor sweep: 194 three-style anchors in the 32 harnesses touching the network probe, with **none touching the changed lines**. The 13 non-matches are file paths, `wrangler.toml` text or inline harness preambles, and are pre-existing.

No migration. No auth, tenant, billing, DNS-write or deletion change. Deploys **network-probe** and scan-api (scan-api imports `PROBE_PORTS` for request validation).

author: axelnathanson
body:
<!-- id=i_confirm_compliance -->

## What

Release 0.2.0. Any `modal.Function` or `@app.cls` method can be a workflow step, and the `workflow-artifacts` volume is removed. `ctx.map()`/`ctx.parallel()` are faster and can record failed items with `return_exceptions=True`. Several breaking API changes are listed in `CHANGELOG.md`.

## Why

Steps no longer need a special decorator or a mounted workflow volume, so existing Modal functions can be orchestrated as they are. Large `ctx.map()` fan-outs spend much less time on volume commits, polling and call-id bookkeeping, and survive restarts more reliably. Integration tests no longer assume a particular Modal environment exists.

## How it was verified

- [x] `make test` (unit tests): 221 passed
- [x] `make lint`
- [x] `make test-integration` (runs real Modal apps and costs money; say which targets)

## Notes for reviewers

- Breaking: `@workflow_function`, `ctx.artifacts_*`, `ctx.commit_artifacts_volume()` and `ctx.dashboard_url` are removed. `@workflow` returns `{"_workflow_restarted": True, "call_id": ...}` on restart. `state_name` is hashed for its Dict and step-result directory, so runs started on 0.1.x lose their cached results. Requires `modal>=1.3.2`.
- Concurrent spawning means a hard orchestrator crash can re-run up to 16 items on resume; step functions should be idempotent.
- Integration targets now require `MODAL_TESTING_ENVIRONMENT` and stop if it is unset.
- `modal_app_url()` omits the environment segment when none is configured.
- `ctx.map()`/`ctx.parallel()` check that `{step_id}_{index}` fits the 128-character identifier limit before spawning anything.

---

- [x] The title follows [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/en/v1.0.0/) (e.g. `fix(workflows): inherit call ids after restart`)
- [x] Public behaviour changes are reflected in the README and `CHANGELOG.md`

## Summary

Residents that call a Model API directly (`provider_api`) already support a per-model **reasoning effort**: `protocol_settings()` adds a `reasoning_effort` control for every model whose registry entry declares `reasoning_efforts`. But administrators had no way to declare that:

- The Model API form in **Portal 管理 → AI Backend** has no model list field.
- `CreateModelApi` does not declare `models`, so the kernel rejects it. Only `UpdateModelApi.changes.models` could set it.

So in practice an API-key backend could never offer a reasoning effort setting.

## Changes

- **ISA** (`hatg/catalog/environment.py`): `CreateModelApi` declares an optional `models` array; the `UpdateModelApi.changes` description mentions `models`.
- **Validation** (`execution/isa.py`): `models` written through Create/UpdateModelApi must be an array of objects with unique, non-empty ids that have no surrounding whitespace. `reasoning_efforts` must be an array of non-empty strings. Other per-model metadata (`support_efforts`, `aliases`, `supported_parameters`, …) passes through unchanged.
- **Admin UI** (`static/portal_management_backend.js`): an optional "模型列表（可选，JSON 数组）" textarea under 高级设置, with an example placeholder and a hint.
  - It is prefilled with the declared models when editing.
  - It is only sent when changed. Clearing it sends `[]`.

author: re2zero
body:
Part 7/8 of the reverse tunnel stack (recovery of #803).

This reapplies the reviewed commit on top of the corrected stack because #803 was accidentally merged into its stacked base branch instead of master.

Merge order: #805 → #806 → #807 → #808 → #809 → #810 → #811.
Before merging this PR, change its base to master (do not merge it into pms396845/06-read-buffer-v2).

The server kept one session per peer address. When a reconnect registered
a new session before the old one was torn down, the new entry was dropped
and the old session's disconnect then erased the address entirely, so
B -> A requests silently stopped being delivered.

Keep every session, route to the newest, and skip routing cleanup while
another session for the same peer remains. Also surface synchronous send
failures and briefly retry RPCs that no endpoint could accept.

Log: keep RPC routing alive across reconnects
PMS: TASK-396845
Influence: B -> A requests keep being delivered when a peer reconnects.

## Summary by Sourcery

Keep RPC delivery alive across peer reconnects by routing to the newest session and retrying requests that temporarily have no usable endpoint.

Bug Fixes:
- Preserve RPC routing when peers reconnect by retaining overlapping sessions, selecting the newest session, and avoiding premature disconnect cleanup.
- Retry RPC requests briefly when no connected endpoint can accept them, while surfacing synchronous send failures instead of silently dropping requests.

Enhancements:
- Improve session readiness and send-failure handling so undeliverable requests fail promptly and can be retried.

Tests:
- Add coverage for reconnect routing, real connected-session login state, and asynchronous request timeout behavior.

- GitHub Security Advisory: [GHSA-9qr9-h5gf-34mp](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/security/advisories/GHSA-9qr9-h5gf-34mp)
- React Advisory: [CVE-2025-55182](https://react.dev/blog/2025/12/03/critical-security-vulnerability-in-react-server-components)
- Next.js Advisory: [CVE-2025-66478](https://nextjs.org/blog/CVE-2025-66478)

This automated pull request upgrades the affected React and Next.js packages to patched versions that fully remediate the issue.

## What this is

The `demo1_build` role and the `demo1` playbook for [ISSUE branchLeft/workspace#2364](https://github.com/branchLeft/workspace/issues/2364). The role builds demo1's slots from the pinned ghost-platform demo-host programs: it stages them by commit and checksum, installs the three that something else runs, compares the sudoers grant that `broker_deploy` owns with the pinned generator without writing it, records the uid claims, makes the `demo-router` account, declares the socket tree and drain-flag directory, writes the colour drop-ins and the router unit, and stages the edge candidate. It runs no `reset`, no go-live, writes no sudoers file, writes no live edge, and starts nothing. The README is self-contained.

Plan: [orchestrator decision r6](https://github.com/branchLeft/workspace/issues/2364#issuecomment-6328654520), on top of [plan r5](https://github.com/branchLeft/workspace/issues/2364#issuecomment-6315996658) and [amendment r4](https://github.com/branchLeft/workspace/issues/2364#issuecomment-6315972471). This round builds r6 D1 to D4 as answers to the [verdict on the previous head](https://github.com/branchLeft/shared-infra/pull/357#issuecomment-6328642512), and answers the [review of r6](https://github.com/branchLeft/workspace/issues/2364#issuecomment-6328708527). The owner ruled on 20 Oct to build after one plan review, answering every finding in the code or this body ([ruling](https://github.com/branchLeft/workspace/issues/2324#issuecomment-6302627974)); r6 was built after one plan review that left findings open, which is that ruling and not a skipped gate.

Refs [ISSUE branchLeft/workspace#2364](https://github.com/branchLeft/workspace/issues/2364). The live apply waits on the owner and on the host's enrolment, so this does not close the ticket.

## Done when, and what review is asked for

r6 had no Done-when of its own. It is this, and it replaces the Done-when and the "Review needed" text of the earlier body, which asked for a full round and carried an unmet time bar:

- **Review asked for: narrow, covering D1 to D4 and the answers below.** The full round on the earlier head has happened; r6 says the plan does not change, and r6's accepted Lows are settled. The reviewer checks each finding below fixed by its mechanism, and the impact set of the changed lines: the order of the drain-flag run in `_dirs.yml`, the controls added for it, and the `broker_deploy` admin-keys case. Everything outside the impact set may still be raised if it is a Medium or worse.
- **CI at this head.** The `demo1_build` shards (`default`, `plan`, `refusals`) and the `broker_deploy` shard must be green. CI at this head was not read when this body was written; the builder does not wait for it. Read it with `gh pr checks 357 --repo branchLeft/shared-infra`.
- **The time bar** (the role README, "The time bar, and what to do when it is missed"): the step "Run the harness over this role or pattern, for this scenario" takes at most 20 minutes for `default` and `plan`, and 10 for `refusals`. The last full figures I can read are for the previous head, [Ansible run 39671665145](https://github.com/branchLeft/shared-infra/actions/runs/39671665145): `default` 11 minutes 59 seconds, `plan` 7 minutes 56 seconds, `refusals` 6 minutes 24 seconds. All three are inside the bar, so the earlier body's statement that the bar was unmet (figures from a run on a loaded runner, which is no longer the record) is withdrawn. The new head adds a few tasks to `refusals` and one move to `default`; its figures are for the reviewer to read from the same step with `gh run view <run id> --json jobs`. A shard over its bar at this head is a failed done-when even when green.

## What the change touches

Read it with `git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD`, or the Files tab. By area:

- the role `demo1_build` (tasks, vars, defaults, argument spec, README, the Molecule scenarios);
- the `demo1` playbook;
- the harness: `run_harness.py` (scenario selection), the new `list_shards.py`, their unit tests, and `ansible/README.md`;
- the workflow `.github/workflows/ansible.yml` (one shard per directory and scenario);
- the contract register: `hetzner/provision/test_compose_unit_contract.py` and `hetzner/README.md`;
- **the `broker_deploy` role** (`tasks/_admin_keys_dir.yml`, `tasks/main.yml`, `molecule/default/verify.yml`, `README.md`). This is beyond plan r5's file list, and it is here on purpose: it is a fail-open safety fix on the same trust boundary. `broker_deploy` runs as root and declared the broker-owned `admin-keys` directory with a file task that followed a link, so the broker could point it at `/etc/sudoers.d` and have a root apply give that directory to the broker. It is control C22. The README (the "Drain flags" premise paragraph, the check-mode row, the proves list, the sabotage table and a named limit) and the first bullet of the self-check below now state the premise. Two limits are named and not hidden: the device number does not see a bind mount of the same filesystem, and the unprivileged test container cannot mount, so the tests use `/run`, a tmpfs, as the other filesystem and cannot reach the branch that reads an existing broker directory that is itself a mount point |

body:
## Report activity to the platform's local activity socket

Stacked on https://github.com/ClickHouse/nerve/pull/537 (gate forecasts). A platform that parks idle machines may expose a local Unix socket where the application reports what it is doing. When that socket exists, Nerve now keeps it current; otherwise nothing changes.

- `POST /v1/activity {runningTurns, activeSessions, nextScheduledAt, nextScheduledName}` on every change (at most once per 250 ms; a turn start is reported promptly) and every `platform.activity_interval_seconds` (30 s): running turns (sessions + active workflow runs, counted once), connected web clients, and the next tick from `CronService.next_scheduled()` (cached; refreshed on schedule changes, turn end and the periodic report).
- Keep-awake leases (`POST/DELETE /v1/leases`, renewed at half-life, retried before they can lapse) while background work that is not a turn is in flight: memorization, workspace sync, backup, live background agents. Documented coverage in `docs/platform-activity.md`.
- Compatibility: task names are sanitised to `[A-Za-z0-9._:-]{0,64}`; a socket that answers 400 gets one retry without the task name and is then served without it; errors never reach callers or stop the gateway.
- Config section `platform:` (`activity_socket`, `activity_interval_seconds`, `lease_ttl_seconds`); `activity_socket: ""` turns reporting off; `nerve doctor` shows whether the socket is present.

Tests: 62 new (fake Unix-socket server: payloads, counts, leases, coalescing, 400 fallback, a run-later wakeup reported after the last client disconnects, inert without the socket). Full suite 6,773 passed, 38 skipped at the head of the stack; ruff unchanged.

author: larslrn
body:
## Summary

Models carry two nullable token limits, `contextWindow` and `maxOutputTokens`. Discovery reads them from the provider where it reports them, admins edit them in the model form, and chat and quota use them.

```text
discover(provider)
  listProviderModels
    anthropic            max_input_tokens, max_tokens
    openai-compatible    context_length (OpenRouter, Together AI) | max_model_len (vLLM) | context_window (Groq)
                         top_provider.max_completion_tokens (OpenRouter) | max_completion_tokens (Groq)
    openai               none
  insert new models
  on conflict: fill only the limits a model lacks   # edited limits stay
```

```diff
 turnSetup
   readModel
+    tokenLimits { contextWindow, maxOutputTokens }
-  callSettings: chatCallSettings(config)
+  callSettings: chatCallSettings(config, tokenLimits)     # maxTokens capped at max output
 meterTurn
-  reserve prompt + (call cap ?? 16,384)
+  reserve prompt + (call cap ?? min(16,384, model max output))
 message metadata
+  contextTokens (last step)   contextWindow (when known)
```

- Usage gauge: last step's tokens against the model's context window; no percentage when the window is unknown (replaces the hardcoded 128,000).
- Chat settings: max tokens above the model's max output is refused (`CHAT_MAX_TOKENS_EXCEEDS_MODEL`) on save, with the limit shown under the field.
- Model page shows both limits; form fields in en/de.
- Generated migration adds the two nullable columns; no backfill.
- Docs: administration (discovery, models, quota estimate) and chat (max tokens, usage).

## Decisions

- **Rediscovery fills, never overwrites.** `coalesce(existing, discovered)` keeps admin edits; `addedCount` still counts only inserted rows (`xmax = 0`).
- **Gauge uses the last step's total tokens**, not the turn's summed usage, which overshoots the window on multi-step replies. Older messages lack both fields and keep the plain token count.
- **Validate on write, cap at run time.** Only a newly set max tokens is checked, so a model switch from the composer never fails; the turn caps a stale value at the model's max output instead.
- **Quota estimate**: the call's cap wins; otherwise the 16,384 default, lowered to the model's max output when that is smaller. A large model limit never raises a reservation, so 64k-128k models do not get refused on nearly spent pools. Chat title generation keeps the default reservation.
- **Inference mock reports a vLLM-style context window only**, so quota reservations in other specs are unchanged.

## Evidence

- Unit: discovery mapping per provider shape (Anthropic, OpenRouter, vLLM, Groq, implausible values), estimator fallbacks, `chatCallSettings` cap, model input schema bounds (positive int32), reservation inputs. `bun run verify` green.
- E2E (`bun run stack e2e`):
  - `discovers the inference mock's models` now asserts chat model `contextWindow: 32768`, embedding model nulls.
  - `rediscovery fills the limits a model lacks and keeps edited ones`: cleared window refilled, edited max output and window kept, `addedCount: 0`.
  - `max tokens stay within the model's max output`: 2,000 over a 1,000 limit refused with the reason and params; 800 saved, model lowered to 500, turn sends `max_tokens: 500`; gauge icon visible.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

Additive nullable columns; reverting leaves them unused.

**Blast Radius:** chat

A chat whose max tokens exceed its model's limit is capped at run time; saving such a value is refused. Token reservations only shrink, for models whose max output is below 16,384.

body:
## What and why

The host-key context match in `_hostname_context` only accepted bare assignment keys, so `export HOSTNAME=deploy.internal`, `readonly server=deploy.internal` and Windows batch `set HOST=deploy.internal` all escaped the private-hostname rule while the bare `HOSTNAME=...` control matched. The `export`/`readonly`/`set` declaration prefixes are now accepted in front of a host-related key (#1920); arbitrary keys (`export ARBITRARY_VALUE=...`), compound suffix keys, member assignments (`obj.DATABASE_HOST=`), calls, code expressions and public-suffix hosts stay skipped.

Closes #1920

author: dhruv2mars
body:
Online unit U5 (`docs/online-design.md` section 8).

- Captures upload changed blobs (regular files and symlink targets) and checkpoint changes to a node through a `CheckpointSink`; the sink runs after an applied capture.
- Node: `LayerAppend` appends through the native `capture_layer`, idempotent by operation. A stale parent is refused with the current head, and a replay returns the recorded outcome, also when contents revert and a checkpoint recurs in the history. `LayerHead` returns the node head. The layer store lives in `crates/javelin-node/src/layer.rs`.
- Protocol: `javelin-protocol` sender gains `Uploader`, `append`, `layer_head`, and blob/change upload helpers (blob `Want` chunked by `MAX_WANT`); the receiver routes checkpoint-only batches to the layer store.

Not in this slice: outbox queueing on sink failure (D16) and binding operations to the wire changes ID.

Proof: `cargo test --locked -p javelin-node --test checkpoints` (6 passed; the revert/symlink test fails with the old earliest-first parent lookup), and the full `cargo test --locked --workspace --all-targets --all-features` exits 0; `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and `cargo clippy --locked --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` are clean.

author: issei0423
body:
Closes #297

## 目的

厨房状態の同期で、中継サーバーが受け付けないイベントが1件でも混ざると、その端末の同期が止まったまま戻らなかった（400 を通信断と同じに扱って同じ一束を送り続け、その間は relay の状態を取り込まない）。また relay は、誤りのあるイベントより前の分を畳み込んだまま rev を進めずにエラーを返していた。

**PR #293 の上に積んでいる**（base は `fix/kds-table-override-device-sync`）。

## 変更範囲

- `relay-server/kitchen-state.js`：`applyEvent` を検査（`checkEvent`）と書き込み（`writeEvent`）に分け、`applyEvents` は一束を全部検査してから書く。1件でも誤りがあれば状態・rev・updatedAt を変えず、`events[i]: ...` の形でエラーを返す
- `relay-server/kds-bridge.js`：400 の一束は送り直さずに捨て、次へ進む（通信断・5xx・408・429 などは今までどおり送り直す）。同期状態に `rejectedCount`・`lastRejectedAt` を残し（画面には既存の「最終失敗」の時刻で出る）、コンソールに1行 warn を出す
- テスト：kitchen-state 1件、kds-bridge 3件、kds-bridge-browser 1件
- `relay-server/README.md`：設計上の判断に1行

## 確認手順

```sh
cd relay-server && npm ci && npm test   # 193 件 pass
cd .. && npm run test:kds               # 36 件 pass
```

ブラウザ（ローカル）：不正な `timerLock` を流すと POST は1回だけで 400、送り直しは無く、relay の rev は変わらない。そのあとも別端末のコンロの変更を取り込め、後続の正しいイベントも載った。

## 残っていること

- 誤り1件と同じ一束に入っていた正しい操作も一緒に捨てる
- 413（本文が大きすぎる）は今も送り直す
- `routes/kitchen.js` の監査の "partial" は起きなくなった（コードが残る）

author: leiicamundi
body:
## What

Bump the CI Go toolchain in `.tool-versions` to `1.26.10`.
- `internal-multi-region-tests` now reads the Go version from `.tool-versions`. Before, `setup-go` read the `go` directive of the test module (`1.26.0` on `main` and `stable/8.10`) and installed that exact, older release.
- `aws/modules/.test/src/go.mod`: raise the `go` directive from `1.27.2` to `1.27.3`. The directive is higher than the local toolchain, so `GOTOOLCHAIN=auto` downloads exactly that version. With `1.27.2` it would download a release without the fix.
- `aws_kubernetes_eks_dual_region_teleport_tests.yml`: bump the Teleport client (`tsh`) to `18.11.6`. It is the first Teleport release built with a fixed Go (`go1.26.10`). Earlier releases use `go1.26.8` (18.11.2 to 18.11.5) or `go1.25.x` (18.7.4). The `camunda.teleport.sh` cluster runs `18.11.6`.

## Why

Go `1.27.3` and `1.26.10` are security releases (CVE-2026-111943) that fix certificate verification. Go 1.25 and older get no fix. Go is used only by the CI test tooling here; no user artifact embeds it.

## Checks

- `go vet` passes for the touched test modules with the new toolchain.

author: tcsweetser
body:
Replaces the Module 8 skeleton with a full deck, updates the plan docs to match, and adds the Module 8 lab kit.

## Deck (63 slides: 56 theory, 7 lab)
- What DNS reveals and to whom (RFC 9076); DoT (RFC 7858, 8310); DoH (RFC 8484), wire format only, JSON APIs vendor-specific (review C17); DoQ (RFC 9250)
- EDNS padding (RFC 7830, 8467), including BIND's documented padding over plain TCP, which departs from RFC 7830 §6
- Encrypted zone transfer (XoT, RFC 9103); opportunistic resolver-to-authoritative encryption (RFC 9539)
- Resolver discovery: SVCB/HTTPS (RFC 9460, 9461), DDR (RFC 9462), DNR (RFC 9463) (review C18); ODoH cited as RFC 9230
- Client support limited to claims with dated primary sources (Apple WWDC22, Chromium, Windows Server 2022); no legal or GDPR claims
- QNAME minimisation and DNS Cookies point to Module 6
- Knowledge check with answers in the presenter notes

## Labs (8.1-8.5: 15/25/15/20/15 min, on the Module 7 VMs)
Plaintext capture; DoT and DoH served by BIND 9.20; Unbound forwarding over TLS; DDR; padding. Each team makes its own lab CA and resolver certificate (`labs/module08/make-certs.sh`). Every lab command was run on Debian 13 packages. DoQ is an instructor demo on Knot DNS 3.4 (BIND 9.20 rejects `quic`; Debian's Unbound and dnsdist are built without DoQ).

## Plan docs
- `dns_dnssec_workshop_plan.md`: Module 8 objectives, theory, lab requirements
- `dns_slide_deck_plan.md`: Module 8 outline (63 slides); totals 680 core / 725 grand
- `dns_assessment_plan.md`: task 4B matches the labs (45 min, 30 points)
- Module 6 sections in both plans: QNAME minimisation and DNS Cookies added, slide counts unchanged

## Review
Independent review: 0 P0, 1 P1, 8 P2, all fixed. The P1 was the Module 8 pointers to Module 6 topics that Module 6's plans didn't yet list. The reviewer re-ran the full lab rehearsal on Debian 13 packages and got the author's results, and confirmed the padding behaviour and Apple's DDR private-address limit from primary sources.

## Verification
- `make -B html`: 14/14 decks
- overflow: 0 in 14 decks
- pagination: 401/401 pass
- `check.sh`: PASS
- No Ubuntu, master/slave or filler-word hits; no keys, logs or absolute paths in `labs/module08`

プレースホルダ画面：見出しは「Temp Master Dashboard」。UI に「Snake」の文字は出さない（API URL も表示しない） - **本番配信を守るためのバックエンドの最小変更**（`app/main.py`）：`resolve_frontend_index()` と `resolve_static_file()` を追加。`static/legacy/index.html` があれば、`/`・`/index.html`・`/legacy/../index.html` のような別名・存在しないパスのどれでも legacy 版を返す（判定は解決後のパスで行う）。これがないと、Dockerfile がコピーした Vite のエントリ HTML（`/src/main.tsx` を参照）がそのまま配信され、本番が白画面になるため - README の Frontend 節を更新 ### 依存バージョン（すべて固定、`package-lock.json` をコミット） リリース直後のものは避け、各メジャーの中で実績のある安定版を選びました。 | パッケージ | バージョン | 備考 | |---|---|---| | react / react-dom | 19.2.9 | 19.2 系の最新パッチ（19.3 は 9 月リリースのため見送り） | | vite | 8.3.4 | 8.3.5 はリリース当日のため見送り | | @vitejs/plugin-react | 6.1.1 | | | typescript | 5.9.3 | typescript-eslint 8.x の対応範囲（<6.1）。7.x は対象外 | | eslint / @eslint/js | 9.39.5 | 9 系の最終安定版（10 系は見送り） | | typescript-eslint | 8.71.2 | | | eslint-plugin-react-hooks / react-refresh | 7.1.1 / 0.5.7 | | | vitest | 4.1.12 | 5.x は 9 月リリースのため見送り | | jsdom | 29.1.1 | | | @testing-library/react / dom / jest-dom | 16.3.3 / 10.4.2 / 6.9.1 | | | @playwright/test | 1.64.0 | | ### 影響範囲 - (Use `node --trace-warnings ...` to show where the warning was created) ✓ 1 [chromium] › e2e/placeholder.spec.ts:3:1 › shows the dashboard placeholder (195ms) 1 passed (745ms) ``` **バックエンド `poetry run pytest`**（`tests/test_static_serving.py` を追加） ``` ============================= test session starts ============================== platform linux -- Python 3.12.13, pytest-8.4.2, pluggy-1.6.0 rootdir: /home/ubuntu/repos/temp-master/switchbot-dashboard/switchbot-backend configfile: pyproject.toml testpaths: tests plugins: cov-6.3.0, anyio-4.12.1, asyncio-0.24.0 asyncio: mode=Mode.AUTO, default_loop_scope=function collected 116 items tests/test_api_endpoints.py ..................... [100%] ============================= 116 passed in 2.00s ============================== ``` **本番配信の確認**（Docker と同じ配置で FastAPI を起動し、`/` と `/index.html` が jQuery 版を返すか確認） ``` GET /: HTTP 200 GET /: legacy jQuery/Bootstrap markers found GET /index.html: HTTP 200 GET /index.html: legacy jQuery/Bootstrap markers found ``` **`.dockerignore` の確認**（Docker と同じ `COPY switchbot-frontend/ /static/` を build context に対して実行。Docker Hub の 429 で busybox が取得できなかったため scratch ベースで確認） ``` #5 exporting to client directory #5 copying files 22.31kB done #5 DONE 0.0s Copied files: static/legacy/index.html ``` **開発プロキシの確認**（バックエンドを起動していない状態。502 は `/api` がプロキシされていることを示す） ``` GET /api/status with no backend on localhost:8000: HTTP 502 ``` **`npm run dev` のプレースホルダ画面**（http://localhost:5173、1280×800） ![npm run dev プレースホルダ画面](https://devin-gtm.devinenterprise.com/api/presigned_proxy?token=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9..k4r0Ism2PpJ9Sd683leBbkXYWq4Q9oj2_5Twq2Fn5vk) ### 人間がするべきテスト - author: streletskiy
body:
Automatic updates could leave the application closed while hidden helper and application processes were still running. Elevation could also lose the installer status path, preventing the helper from detecting completion.

Launch both windows without the Windows hide flag and acknowledge readiness after the first paint, including the installed version. Preserve the status path through NSIS elevation, signal completion after successful installation, and force a fallback launch through the existing helper. Keep a single helper instance and preserve the original profile; a persisted handoff also acknowledges native installer launches without IPC.

Validation:
- `npm ci`
- `npm test` (15 passing)
- `npm run build`
- Module syntax checks from the Checks workflow
- `npm run package` (Windows NSIS and Portable)
- Isolated current-user NSIS installation/update: helper and updated application windows visible, one application instance, profile preserved, helper closed after readiness.
- Forced helper termination: installer recovered the helper and opened the updated application with the original profile.

The isolated installer fixture uses a separate application ID and profile and omits the Python runtime. UAC prompt interaction was not exercised; the elevation path was inspected and compiled in both installers.

author: re2zero
body:
Part 8/8 of the reverse tunnel stack (recovery of #804).

This reapplies the reviewed commit on top of the corrected stack because #804 was accidentally merged into its stacked base branch instead of master.

Merge order: #805 → #806 → #807 → #808 → #809 → #810 → #811.
Before merging this PR, change its base to master (do not merge it into pms396845/07-rpc-routing-v2).

Transfer notifications reused the previous notification id because every
call passes a non-empty hint map. After the user rejected a request or the
sender cancelled it, the old bubble was already dismissed (or still running
its close animation), so the next transfer request updated a notification
that was no longer visible and the receiver never saw it again until the
application restarted.

Make replacement explicit: only progress updates reuse the current id, all
new notifications start at replaces_id 0. Drop the id when a notification
is closed, acted upon, or fails to appear, so a stale id can never wedge
later notifications. Also log received transfer requests at warning level
to tell a missing RPC apart from a suppressed notification in field logs.

Add a regression test for the notification id lifecycle.

Log: start new transfer requests with a fresh notification
PMS: TASK-396845
Influence: a rejected or cancelled request no longer hides later transfer notifications until restart.

## Summary by Sourcery

Ensure file-transfer notifications reliably reappear for new requests while retaining replacement behavior for active progress updates.

Bug Fixes:
- Ensure each new file-transfer request creates a fresh notification instead of reusing a dismissed notification.
- Prevent stale notification IDs from being reused after actions, closure, or notification failures.

Enhancements:
- Log incoming transfer requests at warning level to help distinguish RPC failures from suppressed notifications.

Tests:
- Add regression coverage for notification replacement, dismissal, closure, and action handling.

author: filipmessa
body:
## Summary

```diff
 review round
   wait for both reports
-  missing report → rerun (no limit, rerun is not a round)
+  missing report → rerun once (still not a round)
+    still missing → stop, report blocker
 fix
   re-run narrow checks
+  still failing after 3 attempts → stop, report blocker
 review brief
   earlier fixes and decisions
+    including an earlier run on the same change
+    (after an escalation or a round-3 handover)
```

Two places in `review-loop` had no stop: rerunning a round whose reports went missing, and retrying fixes until the narrow checks pass. The three-round cap covers neither. A later run that starts after an escalation or handover resets the round count, so it now gets the earlier run's decisions and the decided findings do not come back.

## Evidence

- **Before:** `SKILL.md` step 2 said "does not count: rerun it" with no limit. Step 3's "Done when" required the checks to pass and gave no other way out.
  **After:** both have a bound that ends in a blocker.
- Not exercised: no agent run against the changed text. The PR into this branch reports this as untested: "discarding and rerunning a round whose reply lacks both reports".

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

**Blast Radius:** agent workflows

The loop now stops with a blocker after one failed rerun, where it used to keep retrying. If a host's reviewers fail now and then for a passing reason, the maintainer sees that blocker where a second rerun might have succeeded.

author: aicayzer
body:
## Summary

The `blob-integrity` and `blob-replicate` housekeeping jobs asked a blob store whether it holds a blob, and `blob-replicate` opened a source's bytes, with no time limit. A store that hangs, such as an object store that accepts the connection and never answers, stalled the run for good while it held the blob's upload lock, so an upload of the same bytes waited behind it. Each of these questions now has the same 15-second bound that archive export and restore already use. A store that does not answer in that time is treated as unreachable, never as missing: no copy is struck or deleted, and the request to the store is called off. A store's write or delete is still unbounded; that is fixed separately, because giving up on one while it can still land is not safe.

## Changes

- `within` in `storage/blob-layer.ts` now rejects with `BlobStoreUnreachable` when its time runs out, whatever the store's own rejection to the abort says. Every caller already treated any rejection as "did not answer"; `blob-integrity` now also counts the store in `unreachable` instead of logging `blob.integrity_unchecked`.
- `blob-integrity` asks an object store through `within`. The disk branch already did through `copyIntact`, and a disk that does not answer is now counted as unreachable too.
- `blob-replicate` asks the target's `has` and opens the source's `get` through `within`, and closes a read that opens after the bound. A timeout ends the copies into that target for the run, as any unreachable store does, and leaves the copy in `remaining`.
- `storeCheckTimeoutMs()` reads the bound, so a server with test hooks can shorten it. The export and wholeCopies callers use it too.
- Test hooks: `hold:blob-has` and `hold:blob-read` make every store hang before it answers until the fault is cleared or the request is called off, and `store-check-deadline=<ms>` shortens the bound. A hold now accepts an abort signal and stops counting a caller that gives up. All three are documented in `conformance/README.md`, "Faults".
- Contract: new `stores/integrity-no-answer` and `stores/replicate-no-answer` in `conformance/spec/stores.md`, and the new fixture is cited by `stores/integrity-unreachable-keeps`.

## Testing

- Server unit tests, written first and seen failing on `main`: an object store whose `has` hangs (the run never finished, the 5-second guard fired), a disk read that does not open (counted 0 unreachable), a replication target whose `has` hangs (never finished) and a replication source that answers after the bound (the copy was made late instead of given up). With the fix they assert that the run finishes, the store is counted unreachable, nothing is struck or deleted, the store's request is called off, the blob's upload lock is free, a late read's stream is destroyed, and the next run with the store answering makes the copy.
- `faults.test.ts` and `test-routes.test.ts` cover the new hold points, a hold released by its caller's signal, and the new fault's argument checks.
- Conformance fixture `compliance/blob-store-silent.test.ts`, run against a fresh server with a local Garage object store: both cases pass. Run with the job fixes reverted, both cases time out at 60 seconds, which shows the hang the fixture is about.
- `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm format:check`, `pnpm test:changed` (5,501 server tests, 1,096 and 238 in the other groups, all passed), and the contract's `spec-form` and `spec-citations` checks.
- Not tested: a real object store that hangs on the network. The hold stands in for it, and `S3BlobStore` passes the signal to the AWS SDK's `abortSignal`, which these tests do not exercise.

## Notes for reviewers

Review depth: full, it decides when a stored copy is struck.

- A store's `delete` and `put` still have no time limit. Both run under the upload lock in these jobs: `delete` when a queued copy deletion is retried (`finishPendingCopyDeletions`) or a struck copy is removed, and `put` when replication writes a copy. `delete` has no signal parameter on `BlobStore`, and `put` streams a blob of any size, so a fixed bound does not fit it as it is. Left for a separate change.
- Docs for the release docs pass: the blob stores page should say that `blob-integrity` counts a store that does not answer within 15 seconds as unreachable and leaves its copies alone, and that `blob-replicate` leaves a copy into or from such a store for a later run. The test hooks are for the conformance suite only and need no public docs.

## Checklist

- [x] The title is a scoped Conventional Commit.
- [x] New behavior has a test that was seen failing first, or no test was needed and the reason is above.
- [x] Docs, comments and the contract still say what is true after this change.

author: steuart-alps
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"Steuart-alps"} -->
_Requested by **Steuart** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_017gxrQu26ZN3F7m6EsPijb2?thread=cmsg_017gxrQu26ZN3F7m6EsPijb2JKPe4LJRsc1vMP9VKztuiK)_

Before: GreenTrack had no place to log a machine's hour meter on its own. A service due "at 650 hours" was never flagged. There was also no spraying book and no record of chemical, fertiliser or top dressing stock.

After:
- **Hours tab.** Shows each machine's current hours, the hours used in the last 7 and 30 days, and when its next service falls due by hours (amber within 25 hours, red once overdue). Readings can be logged on their own, on the daily pre-use check, or from a machine's QR label. A service overdue by hours counts on the GreenTrack "Services overdue" card, on the main dashboard and on the QR scan page.
- **Spraying tab (the spraying book).** One record per spraying, spreading or top dressing. Each record holds:
  - date and times, and where it went (greens, tees and so on, plus details and hectares);
  - each product with its rate and quantity used (several products for a tank mix);
  - water volume, sprayer, nozzle and reason;
  - operator and their certificate (filled in from their last record);
  - weather, wind and temperature.
  The quantity used comes off stock. The book can be downloaded as a spreadsheet. A sprayer's QR label offers "Record spraying".
- **Stock tab.** Covers pesticides (with MAPP number), fertiliser, top dressing, seed and wetting agents.
  - You log deliveries, stock counts and write-offs.
  - Stock on hand is shown in each product's unit, with a history and running balance per product.
  - Products at or below their re-order level are flagged, with a banner on the page.
  - A product that is in use can be archived but not deleted.

How:
- **Hours.** New `green_hour_readings` table and an optional `hour_meter` column on pre-use checks. Current hours are the latest reading across hour readings, pre-use checks, fuel logs and services. A reading lower than an earlier one needs "meter replaced or reset" ticked.
- **Spraying and stock tables.** New `green_products`, `green_stock_movements`, `green_applications` and `green_application_products`, all added by runtime migrations.
- **How stock is worked out.** Stock is never stored. It is calculated from the history in date order: deliveries add, records and write-offs take off, and a stock count sets the figure. Editing or deleting a record therefore always leaves stock correct.
- **Rules the new tables follow.** All are audited, carry the 24-hour edit lock (spraying and stock records), and are in the data export. The export also gains `fuel-logs.csv`, which was missing.
- **Routes and permissions.**
  - New routes live under `/green-track` (`hours`, `hour-readings`, `products`, `stock-movements`, `applications`) and are in the OpenAPI spec.
  - Changes need `denyViewers`, and deletes are for managers only.
  - Every query is scoped to the signed-in business, and products and machines from another business are refused.
- **Bug fix.** Deleting a PUWER inspection or fuel log from the GreenTrack page called a missing path. This is now fixed.
- **Tests.** New tests `test:green-hours` (45 checks) and `test:green-spraying` (81 checks), both added to CI. The lock and export tests now cover the new tables.

Not included:
- Contractor reminders for services due by hours (these still use dates).
- The phone app.
- A link from products to COSHH assessments.

author: rayentian
body: - [x] I, the PR author, have personally reviewed every line of this PR. # What does this PR do? Adds two orthogonal, opt-in precision options for the cuDNN DSA (DeepSeek Sparse Attention) lightning indexer. Both default to the existing behavior, so models that don't set them are unaffected. - **`dsa_indexer_rope_fp32`** (`bool`, default `False`) — keeps the indexer query/key preprocessing (key LayerNorm → RoPE) in FP32 end-to-end, with no intermediate BF16 round-trip before the scoring matmul. - **`dsa_indexer_scoring_precision`** (`"bf16" | "fp8"`, default `"bf16"`) — runs the cuDNN indexer scoring matmul in BF16 (unchanged) or FP8 (E4M3 operands with UE8M0 per-vector scales). `"fp8"` requires `dsa_kernel_backend="cudnn"` and `dsa_indexer_loss_coeff=0`; SM90+ is enforced by the existing cuDNN backend dependency check. ### Motivation In RL post-training (e.g. NeMo-RL) that uses vLLM as the rollout/generation backend, the indexer's top-k selection must match between training and generation. The top-k boundary is sensitive to the precision of both the q/k preprocessing and the scoring matmul: - Megatron's default path materializes BF16 between the key LayerNorm and RoPE, and runs the scoring matmul in BF16. - The FP8 inference indexer keeps preprocessing in FP32 and scores in E4M3. That precision gap flips some top-k picks near the boundary, so training recomputes log-probs over a different key set than generation actually selected — a train/inference mismatch that hurts RL convergence. These two options make that precision configurable so the training side can reproduce the FP8 inference indexer's top-k selection bit-for-bit. The switches are orthogonal: `dsa_indexer_rope_fp32` removes the BF16 round-trip in preprocessing, `dsa_indexer_scoring_precision` controls the scoring matmul precision. Megatron Core only exposes the mechanism (both default off); enabling them for a given model/runtime is a downstream concern — e.g. NeMo-RL turns them on for its vLLM rollout path. ### Implementation - All cuDNN indexer scoring calls are routed through a single `_indexer_forward` choke point in `dsa_cudnn_kernels.py`, which dispatches on `scoring_precision` (BF16 cast vs. E4M3 quantization + `precision="fp8"` / `q_scale` / `k_scale`). `scoring_precision` is threaded through every top-k path (including the pure-torch global-row path) rather than monkey-patching the cuDNN namespace at runtime. - `forward_before_topk` keeps q/k in FP32 under `dsa_indexer_rope_fp32`. - Config validation gates `"fp8"` to the cuDNN backend with zero indexer loss. - **The default path (BF16, no `rope_fp32`) is byte-identical to before** — covered by a regression test. > Note: this adds an FP8 dispatch through the cuDNN DSA external library. Bit-exact determinism coverage under `tests/unit_tests/determinism/kernels/` is being evaluated (see the determinism pre-check below). ## Test ### End-to-end (training) Validated both options on a real MoE + MLA + DSA training path, using a toy GLM-5 (`glm_moe_dsa`) model built through Megatron-Bridge: - **Model/setup:** 2 decoder blocks, hidden 1024, 8 routed experts, DSA indexer with `index_topk=256`, `seq_length=2048` (> `index_topk`, so the sparse top-k truncation is actually exercised), random weights, mock data, 2×H100 (TP=1 / PP=1 / EP=2). - **Runs:** three matched configurations trained for a few hundred steps each, differing only by the new switches: 1. baseline — `bf16` scoring, no `rope_fp32`; 2. `dsa_indexer_rope_fp32=true`; 3. `dsa_indexer_scoring_precision=fp8` + `dsa_indexer_loss_coeff=0` (cuDNN backend). 4. `dsa_indexer_rope_fp32=true` + `dsa_indexer_scoring_precision=fp8` + `dsa_indexer_loss_coeff=0` (cuDNN backend). - **Checked:** - the options propagate to the DSA indexer config (`dsa_kernel_backend`, `scoring_precision`, `rope_fp32`, `loss_coeff`); - the `fp8` scoring path is actually hit at runtime — the E4M3 quantization/round-trip of q/k runs inside the cuDNN indexer top-k path (verified with temporary instrumentation on the scoring choke points, both the single-chunk `_indexer_forward` and the chunked global-row path); - under `rope_fp32`, the indexer q/k carry FP32 through preprocessing; - the indexer top-k selection changes under `fp8` vs. `bf16` on identical inputs, while the default path is unchanged; - all runs train stably (loss decreases, no NaN / divergence). ### End-to-end (RL) Undergoing... ## Issue tracking Linked issue: N/A — incremental DSA indexer precision option. ## Contribution process ### Pre-checks - [x] I have added relevant unit tests - [ ] I have added relevant functional tests - [ ] If this PR adds or changes a GPU kernel (Triton, `jit_fuser`/`torch.compile`, CUDA extension, TE or external-library dispatch, or a scatter/index accumulation), I have added or updated its bit-exact determinism test and registered it in `tests/unit_tests/determinism/kernels/manifest.py` ([guide](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/main/docs/developer/determinism/testing.md)) - [x] I have added proper typing to my code [Typing guidelines](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html) - [ ] I have added relevant documentation - [ ] I have run the [autoformatter.sh](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/main/tools/autoformat.sh) on my PR ### Code review Feel free to message or comment @NVIDIA/mcore-oncall to help accelerate your merge into main. The less complex your PR is, the faster it will be approved and merged! All PRs start as **draft**. If you open a non-draft PR, it will be automatically converted to draft. #### Step 1: Mark PR as "Ready for Review" 1. When your PR is ready, click **Ready for Review**. 2. An oncall reviewer is auto-assigned and expert reviewers are notified based on your changes. - Some PRs may jump straight to step 2. This is determined by `.github/CODEOWNERS`. :warning: Only mark as ready once merge-conflicts are resolved and the CI is passing. Final Review might get declined if these requirements are not fulfilled. #### Step 2: Final Review For PRs that change `megatron/core`, once all expert reviewers have approved, the `Final Review` label is applied **automatically** and final reviewers are assigned. For PRs outside `megatron/core`, this step is skipped. #### Step 3: Approved Once all required reviewers have approved, the `Approved` label is applied **automatically**. ### Merge Any member of [mcore-engineers](https://github.com/orgs/NVIDIA/teams/mcore-engineers) will be able to merge your PR.

author: therajanmaurya
body:
## Summary

This PR moves the OAuth consent relay out of `docs/consent-callback-page/` into a self-contained, tested `relay/` folder. That folder is deployed to Cloudflare Pages at **https://mifos-x-open-banking-relay.pages.dev** on the Mifos Cloudflare account. It replaces the copy hosted on a personal GitHub Pages site. The page is locked down with strict security headers, removes the authorisation code from browser history, and is branded with the Mifos identity. The site now has a privacy policy and terms of use, and the root README gains a relay section.

## Changes

**Relay (`relay/`)**
- **What gets deployed:** `site/` is exactly what Cloudflare Pages serves, and `wrangler.toml` holds the project name and output directory only, with no account ID or token.
- **Flow moved out of the inline script:** `callback/index.html` now loads `relay.js`, so the page runs under a strict CSP with no `unsafe-inline`.
- **Clears the code from history:** `history.replaceState` removes the authorisation code from the address bar and history as soon as it has been read.
- **Desktop delivery stays exclusive:** the page probes the desktop loopback first and hands off to the mobile app only when no listener answers. That avoids the "no application found" prompt on desktop.
- **Chrome Local Network Access:** the loopback probe declares `targetAddressSpace: 'loopback'`, so Chrome shows its permission prompt correctly.
- **Security headers (`site/_headers`)** on every response:
  - CSP `default-src 'none'` with `script-src 'self'`, `connect-src` limited to the loopback, and `frame-ancestors 'none'`
  - HSTS, `no-store`, `no-referrer`, `nosniff`, `X-Frame-Options: DENY` and `noindex`
- **Runbook (`relay/README.md`):** test, deploy and rollback steps, credentials pulled from the vault, guidance for forks, the security notes, and the site's file tree.

**Mifos branding (`site/assets/`, `site.css`)**
- **Logo:** the official Mifos logo from `openMF/web-app`, plus a dark-mode variant with only the wordmark lightened. The X mark is redrawn as an SVG favicon.
- **Colours:** sampled from the logo's four-part X: navy `#125EAA`, sky `#1E9DE7`, green `#21A53F`, lime `#A6CF62`.
- **Brand band:** a four-colour strip across the top of every page.
- **Self-hosted:** everything is served from the site with system fonts, so the strict CSP is unchanged.
- **Root page:** reworked around the three-step journey (approve at your bank, your bank sends you here, the app picks it up).
- **Callback page:** branded but kept minimal, with links to the legal pages.

**Legal pages**
- **`/privacy/`:** the site collects nothing; it has no cookies, storage or analytics.
  - The bank's answer stays after the `#`, so it never reaches Cloudflare, and goes only to the app on the device.
  - Cloudflare's request processing is explained.
  - The page links the Mifos Initiative privacy notice and states that this policy governs the relay where the two differ.
  - Contact is `info@mifos.org`, the Data Protection Officer and the postal address, all taken from mifos.org.
- **`/terms/`:** the site is for sandbox testing only and is not a bank or payment service.
  - Forks must host their own copy.
  - The MPL-2.0 licence covers the code but not the Mifos trademarks.
  - It also covers availability, no warranty and limitation of liability.
- **Entity facts** (Washington State non-profit, owner of the Mifos trademarks) are taken from mifos.org's Financial and Legal page.

**Tests (`relay/test/bridge.test.js`)**
- The existing `node:test` suite moved here, now 24 tests.
- **Relay flow:** driven through a fake window (history scrub, desktop-only delivery, mobile hand-off plus the reopen prompt, empty state).
- **Page rules:** no inline script or style, the `_headers` policy, root page links and disclaimer.
- **Legal pages:** static and dated, linked from every page, and stating the facts the relay is built on.
- **Assets:** the brand assets exist, and no page loads anything cross-origin.

**Docs**
- `README.md` gains a new **🔐 Consent relay** section (live URL, redirect URI, guarantees, a `curl -I` check, fork guidance).
- Section 5 and the scheme table now point to `relay/`, and `docs/consent-callback-page/` is retired.

## Verification
- `node --test "relay/test/*.test.js"`: 24/24 pass.
- **Live:** deployment `45372d86` is in production. `/`, `/privacy/`, `/terms/`, `/callback/` and the assets return 200, with the CSP, HSTS and `X-Frame-Options: DENY` headers.
- **Playwright against production:** all four pages in light and dark mode at 375px and 1280px, 16 out of 16 clean, with no horizontal overflow, no broken images and no CSP errors.
- **Earlier production checks:** history scrubbed, mobile fallback with the reopen button, empty state, iframe refused.
- **Desktop loopback delivery:** works once Chrome's Local Network Access permission is granted. Headless Chrome denies it by default; a real user gets a one-time prompt.

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)
- Register `https://mifos-x-open-banking-relay.pages.dev/callback/` as the redirect URI on HSBC DevHub, then archive the old personal GitHub Pages copy.
- Have the privacy policy and terms reviewed by the Mifos Initiative. mifos.org publishes no terms of use to align with.
- Write a separate app privacy policy before any store release. The template's Firebase analytics is currently not initialised.
- Add Android App Links / iOS Universal Links on this domain (needs the release signing-cert fingerprint and the Apple team ID).

author: benjamindemaille
body:
#425's row bound named the row: in run 39559647433, `IlluminaBasecallsToFastq` row 6 ran past 300 s on the reference side, which turned main's CI red. This PR forbids the argument pair that causes it.

**The hanging pair: `--MAX_READS_IN_RAM_PER_TILE=2` with `--NUM_PROCESSORS=2`.**

Why it hangs: Picard sets `MAX_RECORDS_IN_RAM = MAX_READS_IN_RAM_PER_TILE * NUM_PROCESSORS = 4`. That gives a single-sample run (OUTPUT_PREFIX) a FASTQ writer queue of `(4/2)/1 = 2`, with a drain threshold of 1. At that size, htsjdk's `AsyncWriterPool.PooledWriter.write` can spin forever on `offer()` against a full queue: the drain task has finished but `currentTask` was never cleared, so nothing drains again. The thread dump of a hung run shows exactly that. The writer pump is parked in `PooledWriter.write` (from `SortedRecordToWriterPump.run`), and `main` waits in `SortedBasecallsConverter.awaitExecutor`. The pool thread is non-daemon, so the JVM never exits.

Reproduced against `picard-rs-oracle:3.5.0`, 300 runs each, 8 at a time, with a 90 s limit and a thread dump on a hang:

| Row | Hangs |
|---|---|
| Row 6 as in the array | 4 / 300 |
| Only the pair kept (two lanes; no INPUT_PARAMS_FILE, inline matching or unexpected-barcode refusal) | 5 / 300 |
| Row 6 with `MAX_READS_IN_RAM_PER_TILE=-1` | 0 / 300 |

A row holding the pair needs enough records to hit the race. With one lane, the same minimal row did not hang in 300 runs.

With `NUM_PROCESSORS=1` the threshold is 0, and the reference refuses the run every time (`writeThreshold must be >= 1: 0`). The array keeps that refusal. `IlluminaBasecallsToSam` does not write through `AsyncWriterPool`, so the constraint covers Fastq only.

Changes:
- `tools/coverage/fixtures.json`: a `forbid` constraint for the pair, with the reason.
- `tools/coverage/arrays/IlluminaBasecallsToFastq.t2.json`: regenerated with gatk-rs `covering.py --verify`. The generator reproduced both committed Illumina arrays byte for byte before the change. The new array has 30 rows, 3252/3252 pairs covered, no row holding the pair, and every varied argument at two values or more.
- The tool's coverage goes back to `pending` (manifest, generated `ci.yml` and `.gitignore`), and its `measured.json` entry and corpus are removed, the same as MergeBamAlignment. The new numbers must come from this PR's CI artefact, not from a laptop. Committing them and flipping back to `measured` is the follow-up commit.

Checks: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings` (through `rtk proxy`), `cargo test --workspace --release`, `generate_ci.py --check` and `provenance.py` pass.

author: iskhakov
body:
## Problem

Opening an app (e.g. an MCP app with no required inputs) seeds the chat with the app's render as an assistant message. No turn reaches the model, so no guardrail session exists yet. The composer's APPA treated any assistant message as a reply, read "reply but no session" as a chat that started while enforcement was off, and showed it asleep with that description.

## Change

A reply now means an assistant message after the first user message. An opened app before anyone writes shows calm, like a new chat; after the first exchange the session exists and the usual trust state shows.

## Exercised

`chat-composer-security.test.tsx`: new case for a seeded `render_app` message with no user message (fails on the old code, passes now); the asleep and shades fixtures now start with a user message. Not checked in the browser.

author: lmnopstudios-dot
body:
The production WW Metorik orders runner stopped on invocation 9 at 2026-10-21T08:12:12Z after 850 reported committed records (8,850 this-run), with an unknown pending commit outcome. #356 parsed the collector failure but dropped its stage, code/reason, job ID and cancellation evidence, making the runbook's terminal-job check impossible from the runner log.

This branch starts from latest main ba7e818 containing merged #356. Runner output now retains a revalidated allowlisted failure object and preserves the exact failed-operation commit outcome separately from earlier committed records. No provider text, customer values or cursors pass through.

Add `diagnostics/customer-history-recovery.js`, an incident-specific read-only command with a shared 90-second evidence budget, bounded metadata listings and aggregate SELECTs. It uses the configured identity and dataset location, narrows the interval only from a matching bounded incident-log record when available, and verifies transactions using exact SQL plus checkpoint-key/source/adapter/revision provenance. Loads link only by verified transaction stages. It reports terminal/pending job state, current active identity jobs, local runner/child process counts, aggregate persisted evidence and checkpoint existence/completion/update time without cursors.

The suppressed failed-child job ID/stage and unlinked pre-transaction loads remain explicitly unresolved; matching by time never authorizes recovery. The command returns `safe_to_unlock:false`, does not remove locks or retry collection, and documents cross-host/identity visibility limits. Cancellation acknowledgement does not prove terminal state or rollback. Exact unlock/resume instructions are withheld pending production quiescence verification. Existing committed evidence, checkpoints, revision and completed adapters are preserved.

Read-only production-host command:
```sh
timeout --signal=TERM --kill-after=5s 100s node diagnostics/customer-history-recovery.js
```

Validation: 48 focused runner/warehouse/recovery tests and 28 existing history/migration/email regressions pass; `git diff --check` passes. Regressions cover nonzero child diagnostics, exact outcomes, allowlist rejection, transaction-abort reasons, unrelated-job rejection, linked loads, truncation, active work, duplicate checkpoints and incident-log interval validation. Initial sandbox runs of existing Python-backed regressions stalled; subprocess-capable reruns passed.

A live read-only attempt stopped at the OAuth token endpoint with HTTP 403 before warehouse evidence could be read. Production job state and checkpoint progress remain unverified. No production collection, incident-job cancellation, unlock, retry, merge or deployment was performed.

author: kniepertsebastian-spec
body:
## Änderungen
- **Berechnung (`lib/calories.ts`)**, je Satz aus Gewicht und Wiederholungen:
  1. *Mechanische Arbeit:* Last × g × Bewegungsweg × Wdh. (Senken zu etwa einem Drittel der Hebe-Kosten mitgezählt) ÷ Muskelwirkungsgrad (~22 %). Der Bewegungsweg wächst mit der Körpergröße (25 % der Größe).
  2. *Muskelaktivierung/Spannung:* 3 MET über Ruhe während der Zeit unter Spannung (3 s pro Wdh.), mit dem Ruheumsatz nach Mifflin-St Jeor aus Gewicht, Größe, Alter und Geschlecht.
  - Sätze mit 0 kg gelten als Körpergewichtsübung (60 % des Körpergewichts als Last). Satzpausen sind nicht eingerechnet.
- **Datenquelle:** Größe, Alter, Geschlecht aus dem Profil (Ernährung → Profil), Gewicht aus der letzten Körpermessung, sonst aus dem Profil. Ohne Profil keine Zahl, stattdessen ein Link „Profil ausfüllen für die kcal-Schätzung“.
- **Anzeige:**
  - Training (Fokusmodus): unter den Sätzen jeder Übung „≈ N kcal“ für die erledigten Sätze; auf der Abschluss-Seite eine Kachel „Kraft-Energie“, außerdem im Text von „Teilen“.
  - Tagebuch: pro Satz im Untertitel, darunter „Gesamt heute“.
  - Historie: pro Übung in der Kopfzeile, pro Tag als Summe neben dem Datum.
- `roadmap3.md`: Punkt ergänzt und abgehakt.

Beispiele (80 kg, 180 cm, 30 J., männlich): Bankdrücken 8 × 80 kg ≈ 5,6 kcal pro Satz, drei Sätze ≈ 17 kcal; 15 Liegestütze ≈ 7 kcal. Das sind **Schätzwerte** (typisch ±30–50 %), die nur die Hebearbeit abbilden, nicht den gesamten Trainingsverbrauch inklusive Pausen, Aufwärmen und Cardio.

## Geprüft
- Typecheck, ESLint; die Rechnung mit einem Wegwerf-Test geprüft (Größenordnungen, Monotonie in Gewicht/Wdh., Formatierung; nicht eingecheckt, das Frontend hat kein Testsystem).
- Nicht im Browser ausprobiert.

feat(admin/interview-slots): 슬롯에 면접관을 지정하고 회의 상태와 입장 링크를 보여 준다

## ✅ PR 설명

### 문제

서버는 슬롯에 면접관을 지정하면 주인 면접관의 Google 캘린더에 Meet 회의를 만들고(DDD-Community/DDD_BE#115), 지원자에게는 시작 10분 전부터 열리는 입장 링크를 보냅니다(DDD-Community/DDD_BE#116). 하지만 어드민 화면에는 면접관을 고르는 칸도, 캘린더를 연결하는 메뉴도 없어 이 기능을 쓸 수 없었습니다.

### 변경

- **슬롯 등록·수정 폼** — `components/InterviewSlotInterviewersField.tsx`
  - 면접관 후보(면접관·운영자·계정관리 권한)를 골라 순서대로 쌓습니다. **첫 번째가 주인**이고, 「주인으로 지정」으로 순서를 바꿉니다. 사람마다 캘린더 연결 여부를 보여 주고, 주인이 미연결이면 "회의를 만들 수 없고 지원자에게 보이지 않는다"고 경고합니다.
  - 면접관을 지정하면 장소는 선택 항목이 되고, 비우면 `온라인 (Google Meet)` 으로 저장합니다. 면접관이 없으면 지금처럼 장소가 필수입니다.
  - 등록은 면접관이 있을 때만 `interviewerUserIds` 를 보내고, 수정은 늘 보냅니다(`[]` 이면 기존 방식으로 되돌림). 서버는 목록이 실제로 바뀐 경우에만 검사하므로, 예약이 있는 기존 방식 슬롯을 수정해도 막히지 않습니다.
- **슬롯 목록** — `components/InterviewSlotMeetingCell.tsx`, `hooks/useSyncInterviewSlotMeetingFlow.ts`
  - 「회의」 칸에 상태(기존 방식·회의 준비 중·회의 준비됨·동기화 필요·회의 생성 실패), 실패 사유, 면접관 이름을 보여 줍니다. 준비된 회의는 「회의 열기」로 바로 엽니다.
  - 준비되지 않은 슬롯에는 "지원자에게 보이지 않음"과 「다시 동기화」 버튼을 둡니다. 동기화 뒤에도 회의가 준비되지 않으면 성공이 아니라 경고로 안내합니다.
- **Google 캘린더 연결** — `shared/ui/AdminLayout/UserMenuDropdown.tsx`, `shared/hooks/useGoogleCalendarConnectionFlow.ts`, `shared/hooks/useGoogleCalendarCallbackToast.ts`
  - 사용자 메뉴에 「Google 캘린더 연결」을 넣었습니다. 연결돼 있으면 연결한 계정과 「다시 연결」·「연결 해제」를, 토큰이 무효가 됐으면 「다시 연결 필요」를 보여 줍니다.
  - Google 동의를 마치고 `/applications?calendar=…` 로 돌아오면 결과를 토스트로 알리고 주소에서 매개변수를 지웁니다.
- **지원자 예약 완료 화면** — `pages/interview-booking/components/BookingDoneCard.tsx`
  - 회의 슬롯이면 「면접 입장 링크」 버튼과 "시작 10분 전부터 입장할 수 있다"는 안내를 보여 줍니다.

  - 면접관 후보 조회, 회의 동기화, 캘린더 상태·연결·해제의 API·쿼리 팩토리를 추가했습니다.

### 동작 변화 / 리스크

- 면접관을 지정하지 않으면 등록·수정·지원자 화면 모두 지금과 같습니다.
