author: haranishi
body: A custom attribution control that is added after a layer keeps that layer's credit for ever. With two base layers, switching from the first to the second lists both credits, separated by a comma, while the control that Leaflet adds by itself lists only the second one. `AttributionControl.onAdd()` adds the credit of every layer that is already on the map, but unlike `_addAttribution()` (the `layeradd` listener) it does not register the listener that takes the credit off again when the layer is removed. The map's own control is created before any layer exists and only ever uses `layeradd`, which is why it was not affected. A control that is removed and added again is affected too: `onAdd()` counts the layers again without a listener, so a layer that was added through `layeradd` before keeps its credit as well. `onAdd()` now goes through `_addAttribution()` for the layers it finds. That method keeps the `getAttribution` check, so layers without a credit behave as before. The `TODO` above the loop is left as it is, since the loop still reads `map._layers`. Fixes #8416. ## Testing Three new specs in `AttributionControlSpec`: a layer that was on the map before the control, two such layers with the same credit, and a control that is removed and added again. They fail on `main` at 61e0e6c6 (`expected 'prefix | foo' to deeply equal 'prefix'` and the like) and pass with this change. Two deliberately broken variants (registering the listener without adding the initial credit, and resetting the counts in `onAdd()` instead) fail the first spec. A page with two layers that have credits, the default control, and a custom control added after the first layer shows the problem in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit (Playwright): after switching to the second layer the custom control reads `© A, © B` on `main` and `© B` with this change, like the default control. The CI steps were also run locally on this branch and on an untouched `main` at that commit. Lint, `build`, `docs`, and the SSR, tree-shaking and dist checks pass. The Vitest suite passes in Chromium (also with the retina project and against the built bundle), Firefox and WebKit, each with and without `VITE_TOUCH=1`: 1143 passed and 14 skipped, against 1140 and 14 on `main`, i.e. the three new specs. Not run locally: the Deno SSR check, the Jekyll docs build and the Windows job. ## AI assistance The patch, its tests and this description were written with the help of an AI coding assistant (Claude Code), and a second AI model reviewed the diff. The numbers above come from commands that were actually run.

author: aaguirre-rdit
body: ## Summary A budget guardrail can stop an agent run when the run reaches the session cost cap, the monthly budget, or the Gateway credits limit. The preview chat shows this stop, but the session timeline does not. The timeline ends without a marker, and the user cannot see why the agent did not answer. This PR records the stop and shows it in the timeline. `ExecutionRecorder` reads the guardrail code from the stream finish chunk. It adds a `guardrail` event to the execution timeline. It also stores `finishReason` and `guardrailCode` on the `agent_execution` row. A new migration adds these two nullable columns. The threads API returns the new fields. The session timeline shows the `guardrail` event as a "Run stopped" row, with a message for each budget code. If the latest run stopped on the session cap or the monthly budget, the timeline shows the budget notice card directly below that row. A user who can edit the agent can increase the cap from the card. The LangSmith export and the Instance AI session context also include the stop. Snap: ## Why The guardrail stop exists only in the live stream. No part of the stored execution keeps it. So the timeline, the LangSmith export, and Instance AI cannot show why a run ended early. ## How to test 1. Create an agent that uses Gateway credits. In the builder, set a very small session cost cap, for example $0.01. 2. Send a message in the preview chat. Wait until the guardrail stops the run. 3. Open the session trace. 4. Make sure that a "Run stopped" row shows at the end, with the message "The session reached its cost cap." 5. Make sure that the budget notice card shows directly below that row. 6. Type a higher cap and click **Increase cap**. Make sure that the card closes and that the builder shows the new cap. 7. Open the same trace as a user without edit access to the agent. Make sure that the card shows without the increase action. 8. Send a new message that completes. Open the trace again. Make sure that the old stop row stays and that the card does not show. 9. Open a session recorded before this change. Make sure that it renders as before, with no stop row and no error. ## Related Linear tickets, Github issues, and Community forum posts https://linear.app/n8n/issue/AGENT-1326 ## Review / Merge checklist - [x] I have seen this code, I have run this code, and I take responsibility for this code. - [ x PR title and summary are descriptive. ([conventions](../blob/master/.github/pull_request_title_conventions.md)) - [ ] [Docs updated](https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n-docs) or follow-up ticket created. - [x] Tests included. - [ ] PR Labeled with `Backport to Beta`, `Backport to Stable`, or `Backport to v1` (if the PR is an urgent fix that needs to be backported)

author: georgehadji
body:
## What changed

- **`site/src/product.js`** stays the gateway (`load`, `fact`, `geometry`, `decimals`), with the same checks in the same order, and no longer imports jsdom or any chart type.
  - `load` caches rows per process under the sha256 that `manifest.json` lists for the file. A changed manifest is a new key.
  - A read is cached only after it passes every check.
  - Rows and arrays are frozen (`Object.freeze`), so a caller that changed a row would throw instead of corrupting the cache.
  - `manifest.json` itself is read on every call, as before. It is small.
- **`site/src/figure.js`** (new): `chart` and `panel`, moved unchanged. It is the only module that loads jsdom and the charts.
- **`site/src/cli.js`:** each command `await import(...)`s only its own modules.
- **Tests:** `product.test.js` imports `chart` from `figure.js`. A new test checks that a file is read once, its rows cannot be changed, and a failed read is not cached.
- **`site/src/CONTEXT.md`:** a row for `figure.js`, and updated rows for `product.js` and `cli.js`.

## Why

Audit findings F4 and F5, plan step **S6** (`docs/AUDIT-FIX-PLAN.md`). Every `{{< fact >}}` runs its own Node process, and each one loaded jsdom and every chart type before doing any work. `pages.js` also re-parsed the same CSV once per region and indicator.

## Measured (S6c, this Windows machine, 3 runs each)

| Import | Time |
|---|---|
| `product.js` (a fact) | 77–80 ms |
| `figure.js` (a chart; the old `product.js` loaded all of this) | 820–1000 ms |

So each `fact` process starts about 10× faster. Batching facts per document is not needed for now. The plan keeps it as a later step, only if render time demands it.

## For the reviewer

- An earlier version also cached `manifest.json` per directory. `pages.test.js` rewrites the manifest in the same directory between tests, and that version failed 3 of them. Keying the rows by the listed sha256 is correct even when the manifest changes during a run.
- **To confirm on this PR:** the Build workflow renders the site, the two deliberately wrong pages still fail, and the link check passes. Ideally `_site` is byte-identical to the last Build artifact.

## Checks

- Local (Windows): `site` `npm test` 19/19, `charts` `npm test` 103/103, `test_context.py` passed.

author: momo-momokaya[bot]
body:
## Cause
The sweep plans worktree removals at survey time and applies them one by one later (the failing pass took about 87 s). If something else removes a planned worktree in that window, for example a child's `done` handoff or `dogsled close`, then `validate_tree` no longer finds it in `git worktree list` and refuses with `worktree identity disappeared`. The pass records that as a failure, even though the worktree is already gone.

Evidence on the Mac: `sweeps.jsonl` shows this failure for `/Users/oisin/dev/oisinpi/.worktrees/tiers-case` in one pass only (finished 1792588142002). The next pass (1792588178071) had 0 failures. `worktrees.json` holds no record for the path. The failure that is still visible is the one-time owner gate message in `gate.json`.

## Fix
`validate_tree` returns `None` when Git no longer lists the worktree **and** its path is absent (ENOENT). `remove_tree` then drops the registration through `drop_registration`, which rechecks absence under the `worktrees` lock, and reports `<path> was already removed; dropped its registration`.

Safeguards stay the same:
- A path that Git no longer lists but that still exists is still refused (`worktree identity disappeared`).
- A listed worktree goes through the same identity, loss, and hold checks as before (dirty, unlanded, live pane, lock).
- Nothing on disk is deleted on the new path. Only the record is dropped.

## Test
`cleanup::tests::planned_worktree_removed_by_another_actor_is_reconciled_not_failed`: when the path is unlisted but still on disk, the removal is refused and the record kept. When the path is unlisted and absent, the removal succeeds and the record is dropped. Without the fix, the test fails.

`cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings`, and `cargo test --bin dogsled` (170 passed) pass. The commit hook ran the full suite.

body:
## What
The basketball Scoring Rules page had football leftovers ("AP Poll until the CFP Poll", football icon) and several lines that didn't match the hoops engine. Every line was audited against `hoops-detectors.js` / `scoring.js` / `hoops-ranks.js` / `hoops-quadrants.js` / H2H + Captain code.

## Changes (basketball only)
- **Rankings Used**: T-Rank → adjusted efficiency → NCAA NET; rank going into the week; quadrant band table (test pins it to `BANDS`).
- **Regular season**: "base points plus every bonus" → each win scores one quadrant; conf tournament games count. Conf-title stacks note now renders.
- **Postseason**: says the NCAA ladder stacks and that NCAA games don't also score as quadrant wins / NIT doesn't score. "Reached the NCAA tournament" → "Reached the first round (Round of 64)". Upset note: per win over a better seed.
- **Game modes**: H2H/Captain are regular-season weeks only; tip-off lock; auto-captain.
- **Draft**: "by preseason T-Rank". Basketball icon on Regular Season header.

## Football
Every line audited against `scoring-detectors.js` / `scoring.js` / `h2h.js` / `captain.js`:
- "Non P5 team beats a P5 team" → "Non-power team beats a power-conference team", with the league's real power list underneath (default ACC, Big 12, Big Ten, SEC; Graham's config adds FBS Independents).
- Base points / stacking are regular-season only; conference championships and other postseason games score only postseason points.
- Postseason: each playoff game scores its own round, so a run adds up.
- Claunts: "National Championship appearance (win or lose)".
- H2H ends at the last full slate; Captain locks at first kickoff, auto-picks, is off in bowls/CFP.

body:
## Summary

Desktop Home now uses the shared activity-card presentation and a compact Strava-style layout while retaining ORider's five primary tabs, cycling community card, and footer. The profile sidebar shows real friend/activity counts, the latest activity, weekly streak, and a training-log link.

- Keep saved activity memos first, use deterministic default summaries for eligible blank memos, and show AI analysis only in the activity-detail overview.
- Align sidebar and monthly training-log spacing, prevent text overflow, and use the shared term and chart tooltips.
- Hide swimming entry points with a reversible frontend flag while preserving backend data and existing calculations.
- Add independent subscriptions: profile subscribe/unsubscribe controls, public-only subscription feed/search, and subscription/subscriber/outbound-block management inside the existing friends page. Existing friend requests and friend-only access stay separate.
- Discard stale account/relationship results, load all subscription IDs before querying, preserve global feed pagination, and validate candidates before rendering.

## Backend dependencies and activation

- Subscription server and rules: https://github.com/miranae/orider-g1-web/pull/3302
- Deterministic Strava default memo and canonical overview contract: https://github.com/miranae/orider-g1-web/pull/3303

The subscription UI is disabled in production. Local preview requires `VITE_ACTIVITY_SUBSCRIPTIONS_ENABLED=true`; leave `VITE_ACTIVITY_SUBSCRIPTIONS_BACKEND_READY=false` against the current production backend. Explicit production activation is a separate change after the subscription callables, rules, and the new `validateActivitySocialFeedCandidates` implementation supporting `publicOnly: true` have been deployed and verified. A schemaVersion 1 response from the old validator alone is not readiness evidence. Subscription, admission, and unblock callables use `asia-northeast3`; stage/custom-base and emulator routing are preserved.

There is no data backfill or production data mutation. The optional activity-overview preview adapter is restricted to DEV/loopback; the normal callable path remains the production path.

## Validation already completed during implementation

- Feed/search integration: 181 tests; relationship/management: 54 tests; regional admission follow-up: 3 tests.
- TypeScript, scoped ESLint, design-system/quality budgets, production frontend build, and independent source review passed.
- Authenticated local QA covered the desktop layout, real friend count, profile controls, friends/request views, and subscription/block tab navigation with backend readiness disabled.
- Successful new subscription mutations and nonempty-list behavior were tested with component mocks and the backend emulator, not against production.

PR creation performs static checks only; full merge gates are deferred to an explicit merge request. No merge or deployment is included.

author: thomas-jacque-schultz
body:
🤖 Claude : tournée du 21/10, tout le Todo. Cette PR reprend front#74 (tournée du 20/10, détail dans sa description), que je ferme.

⚠️ **À fusionner par un commit de fusion, pas par rebase** : les jeux arrivent de schub-together-games avec leur historique (`git subtree`), comme pour #131.

## Ce qui change

**Schub#139 : les mini-jeux deviennent la troisième application du front.**
- `src/games/<jeu>/` et `games/<jeu>/index.html`. Les entrées Vite sont trouvées seules dans `games/`.
- nginx gagne un bloc `server` pour `(dev-)<jeu>.premadelab.eu` : la page du jeu, `frame-ancestors` PremadeLab, `/assets/` et `/api/` communs, 404 sinon. `nginx -t` passe sur le gabarit rendu, et le routage a été vérifié par hôte dans un nginx jetable.
- En dev, le même middleware reconnaît le jeu à son hôte, et `/ws` part vers `RELAY_URL`.
- ESLint : un jeu n'importe que `common` (par sa porte) et `games/commun`. Il n'importe ni Schub, ni PremadeLab, ni un autre jeu, et aucune autre zone n'importe les jeux. Vérifié avec un import interdit.
- Les tests des jeux passent par vitest (`npm test`, ajouté à la CI).
- `src/premadelab/games.ts` devient `queueKiller.ts`, pour ne pas tomber sous la règle des jeux.
- Les nouveaux jeux sont bâtis sur le design system (`games/commun/ecrans.tsx`). Le design system gagne `SideLayout` et `PageContainer`, avec leurs stories. Scribble et Zoom gardent leur CSS.

**Schub#133 : Indices.** À chaque manche, un joueur choisit champion ou objet. Les indices viennent de Data Dragon : classes, portée et ressource, un sort, le titre ; ou le prix par tranche (ta réponse), les statistiques, les composants, la description. Un indice tombe à chaque quart du chrono, pour 100, 70, 45 puis 25 points. J'ai gardé le nom « Indices » (« Clues » en anglais).

**Schub#136 : Questions pour un invocateur.** Un QCM à quatre choix, avec le même barème que Zoom.
- Objets, histoire (extrait de la biographie avec le nom masqué, ou le titre), nombre de skins (hors chromas, que Data Dragon range parmi les skins) et monde (région, date de sortie, via l'index d'Univers) sont générés.
- Les joueurs pro viennent d'une banque de 33 questions datées et sourcées (pages Wikipedia des Worlds et du MSI, Sheep Esports).
- La bonne réponse reste chez le meneur pendant la question : elle n'est ni dans la page ni dans l'état diffusé. Un meneur qui reprend sans elle annule la question.
- Le plus rapide à avoir trouvé choisit le thème suivant ; si personne n'a trouvé, c'est le joueur suivant.
- Sans Univers, le thème Monde est retiré.
- Le lien « Une question fausse ? » ouvre `/contact?sujet=mini-jeux` dans un nouvel onglet.
- Sur Rekkles, la source confirme la bague mais pas qu'il serait « le seul Européen » : la question ne le dit donc pas.

**Schub#137 : la banque dans Schub.** Un onglet PremadeLab › Quiz, réservé à `QUIZ_QUESTION_EDIT` (l'OWNER seul) : la liste filtrable, l'ajout, la modification, la désactivation. Le quiz relit `/api/quiz/questions` à chaque partie, et garde `banque.json` en secours. Contrat du cœur recopié.

**Schub#138 : le sujet du contact.** Un menu obligatoire avec cinq sujets. `?sujet=mini-jeux` (ou `compte`, `stats-fausses`, `fonctionnalite`, `autre`) le choisit d'avance.

**Schub#140 : In-vo-posteur.**
- L'imposteur ne le sait pas. Son champion partage la classe principale ou la région de celui des autres (ta réponse).
- Les mots sont affichés sur le plateau, sous chaque joueur. Un mot qui contient le nom de sa carte est refusé avant l'envoi, avec la raison.
- Le vote est simultané. Démasqué (strictement le plus de voix), l'imposteur donne 1 point à chacun des autres et tente sa dernière chance à 2 points. Sinon, il marque 3 points.
- Limite acceptée : les cartes de tous sont dans l'état diffusé.

Au passage, `APP_URLS` reconnaît le dev sur `dev-<jeu>.premadelab.eu`. Sans ça, le lien du quiz vers le contact visait la prod.

## Tickets

Fixes thomas-jacque-schultz/Schub#133
Fixes thomas-jacque-schultz/Schub#136
Fixes thomas-jacque-schultz/Schub#140
Refs thomas-jacque-schultz/Schub#137
Refs thomas-jacque-schultz/Schub#138
Refs thomas-jacque-schultz/Schub#139

Repris de front#74 : Fixes thomas-jacque-schultz/schub-front-servers#70, #71, #72, #73 ; Refs Schub#128, #129, #132, #134.

## Poids de chaque jeu (gzip, page comprise)

| Jeu | Avant (together-games) | Après |
|---|---|---|
| Scribble | 81 ko | 73 ko |
| Zoom | 79 ko | 70 ko |
| Indices, Quiz, In-vo-posteur | — | 253 à 267 ko, dont 214 ko de chunks partagés avec PremadeLab |

Les deux jeux en CSS maigrissent : React est désormais le même chunk que celui de PremadeLab. Les nouveaux jeux chargent le design system. Ce chunk est déjà en cache quand on arrive par Queue Killer, il reste donc 40 à 50 ko propres à chaque jeu.

## Existait-il déjà ailleurs ?

- Les écrans des jeux en CSS (`salon.tsx`, `jeu.tsx`) restent pour Scribble et Zoom. `ecrans.tsx` en est l'équivalent sur le design system, et `useContexte` est sorti de `JeuApp` pour servir aux deux.
- Data Dragon : `catalogue` (noms) existait. `ddragon.ts` ajoute la lecture complète, et `memorise` remplace la mémoire écrite à la main de `catalogue`.
- Le select des réglages réutilise `SelectField`, et le menu du contact aussi.
- Pas de composant « mise en page avec colonne de côté » ni « conteneur de page hors coquille » dans le design system : je les ai ajoutés.

## Seuils

Aucun fichier écrit à la main au-delà de 500 lignes (le plus long : `games/commun/ecrans.tsx`, 493). `contrat.ts` est généré.

## Test sur le dev

- Lint, 42 tests (dont 22 nouveaux sur les règles et la banque), build et prérendu.
- Parties jouées dans Playwright contre un relais construit depuis together-games (conteneurs jetables) : Indices à trois navigateurs (dont un à 390 px), le quiz à trois, In-vo-posteur à quatre, du lancement à la révélation. Zoom et Scribble tournent toujours depuis le front.
- Les questions générées ont été relues sur les vrais fichiers de Data Dragon et d'Univers.
- Déploiement sur le dev : voir le commentaire qui suit.

## Gestes à toi

- Dev : DNS `dev-indices`, `dev-quiz`, `dev-imposteur`, et leurs règles de tunnel (`/ws` vers le relais, le reste vers `dev-schub-front`). Les règles de `dev-scribble` et `dev-zoom` hors `/ws` passent aussi sur `dev-schub-front`.
- Prod, dans l'ordre : ce front, puis le tunnel (`*.premadelab.eu` hors `/ws` vers `schub-front`), puis le relais allégé (together-games).

body: Seção **F · Compartilhar treino no story** do protótipo `NexaGO Agenda.html`, no app do atleta. ## O que muda - **F1 · Agenda:** a aula do aluno que já acabou (sem falta/justificada, não cancelada) ganha **"Postar no story"** no card. Tocar no card abre o detalhe. - **F2 · Detalhe do treino** (`ClassSessionDetailPage`): duração, treino do mês, sequência de semanas, professor + tipo da turma, local/horário e situação da chamada; "Compartilhar no story" no rodapé. - **F3 · Montar story** (`ClassStoryPage`): o mesmo editor do story da reserva (`BookingStoryEditorScaffold` + mixin): Foto/Brasa/Noite/Areia, chips **Números**, **Arena e horário**, **Coach e turma**, salvar ou postar pela folha nativa. - **F4/F5 · Arte** (`ClassStoryCard`): a moldura `BookingStoryArtFrame` da reserva, só com o conteúdo trocado: selo "TREINO FEITO", "Treino pago.", números, arena · quadra · dia e hora, @ do atleta "com Prof. X e a turma", rodapé "TREINE TAMBÉM". Só app, sem mudança de backend nem de rules. ## Decisões (o protótipo inventava 3 coisas) - **@ do atleta:** é o `nickname` do perfil; sem apelido, vai o primeiro nome. - **Números:** vêm da chamada real. Treino do mês = aulas com presença no mês até esta (contando a própria). Semanas seguidas = semanas (seg–dom) com presença até a da aula, lidas de `getMyClassAgenda` nas ~14 semanas anteriores (o servidor aceita até 100 dias; a agenda só traz 30). A sequência só aparece na arte a partir de 2 semanas. - **Recado do coach e plano do treino:** ficaram de fora porque o backend não guarda nenhum dos dois. Dá para entrar depois, se o professor passar a gravar isso na aula. - **"Marcar coach e turma" virou "Coach e turma":** o chip só mostra o professor (iniciais) e o atleta. Não avisa ninguém nem mostra colegas, porque a callable não manda dados de outros alunos (privacidade). O aviso para repostar precisa de backend. - Aula de hoje sem chamada já pode ser compartilhada depois do horário de fim, porque o professor costuma fechar a chamada mais tarde. - Aula dada como professor não tem story nem detalhe aqui (G1–G3 do app do professor ficam para outro PR). ## Prints (fontes reais) | Agenda (escuro) | Agenda (claro) | Detalhe | Editor | |---|---|---|---| | | | | | | Arte · Brasa | Arte · Areia | |---|---| | | | ## Testes - `class_story_test.dart`: quando dá para compartilhar, treino do mês, sequência (com semana quebrada), dados da arte e legenda. - `agenda_class_story_test.dart`: card → editor, chips desligando números/turma, sem botão em aula futura, com falta ou dada como professor, card → detalhe → editor, PNG opaco nos 4 fundos. - `flutter test test/features/athlete/agenda test/features/arenas` + contraste: 680 verdes. `flutter analyze` limpo nos arquivos novos. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

author: chanmeng666
body:
PS3.4: openings by relation (ADR 0028 §5). With this PR, card PS3.4 is `done`.

```
door|opening [id=] [<kind>] between <A> and <B> [at <pos>] width <mm> …
door|window|opening [id=] on <room>.<edge> [at <pos>] width <mm> …
<pos> := center | <mm> from start|end | <mm> from <room>.<edge> | axis <label>
on <wall> at <mm> from start|end | <mm> from <room>.<edge> | axis <label>     (hosted datums)
```

## Lead rulings (accepted before implementation)
1. **Offsets.** An offset is measured to the opening's **centre**, as `on <wall> at <mm>` always was. It runs along the shared run or the edge, from its smaller-x/y end (§3's direction rule), never along the host wall.
2. **Position words.** Only §5's words are accepted. A plain `at <mm>`, `at <pct>%` or `from axis` on a relational form is `E_OPENING_DATUM`. The card's `at <t>` is dropped; the README card records this, dated.
3. **Missing position.** A door is refused (§5 requires a position). A cased opening is refused too: §5 says nothing about it, so the compiler refuses rather than chooses. A window on an edge defaults to `center`, which §5 states.
4. **Host.** The host is the one straight wall body on the run, derived or authored.
   - None: `E_OPENING_NO_SHARED_WALL`. On an edge form, a partition there also counts as none.
   - More than one: `E_OPENING_HOST_AMBIGUOUS`. A coexistence `~n` piece is never chosen, so an authored span beside a derived remainder refuses.
   - No shared run, or a room named twice: `E_WALL_BETWEEN_NOT_ADJACENT` (reused; text widened).
   - A pair declared `open`: `E_WALL_BETWEEN_OPEN`, spanned on the door's `between` clause, with the `open` clause as a related span. The derived partition now carries `_derived.open`.
5. **Edge form.** `on <room>.<edge>` takes a door, a window or a cased opening; a door needs a position. `window … between` is refused at parse.
6. **Nib.** Refused, never slid, with the lint's own measure.
   - `junctionsOn` moved verbatim to `src/opening-junctions.ts` (`junctionSpans`). Lint and the resolver share it, and the default nib values (`JUNCTION_NIB_DEFAULTS`, which `DEFAULT_RULESET` reads).
   - `E_OPENING_NIB` also covers a meeting wall inside the span, and a span past the run or the host.
   - The hint names the nearest legal position, grid-snapped and checked, measured from the end the author wrote (`at 600 from end`).
   - The hosted-datum forms are not refused: they warn exactly as their `on <wall> at <x>` twins do.
7. **freedom.** The between/edge forms are `relational`, with an `openings.relational` count present only when there is one. The hosted datums stay `attached`. The `open between` derived opening stays `absolute` (the PS3.0c decision is kept), because changing it would move the four pinned PS3.0 rows and §6 does not require it.
8. **Plan JSON.** Root-level relational openings carry an additive `relation {between|edge, at?}` beside the resolved `x`/`y`. It is validated (`E_JSON_SCHEMA`), the schema is regenerated, and it is round-tripped. An opening inside an instance exports by coordinates, as every instance element does.

## Architecture
- **`src/opening-relation.ts`** (new):
  - `placeBetween` and `placeOnEdge` find the run, read the position, find the host and judge the nib;
  - `hostedDatumDistance` serves the `on <wall>` datums;
  - `relationText` and `relationalClause` are for describe and the lint hints.
- **`src/attach.ts`**:
  - the parser reads `between`, the `from`/`axis` positions, and an `on <room>.<edge>` with no `at`;
  - `resolveOpeningLead` is the one entry the three elements call.
  - `on <name>` is still a wall reference whenever a wall has that id or category, exactly as before. A name that is both a wall and a room edge of the group is `E_DATUM_NAME`.
- **`ResolveCtx.datums`** (optional, append-only) holds the group's frozen table and a read through the group's own `tableReader`. So a room edge in a position is refused exactly as a datum anywhere else is (`E_DATUM_COMPASS`, `E_ROOM_NOT_RECTANGLE`, `E_UNKNOWN_REF`, `E_DATUM_UNPLACED`).
- **Steps** are charged before every scan: the body scan (one per wall plus one per point), the junction scan (one per segment), the axis lookup and the legal-position search. A test asserts at least 4 steps per extra wall.
- **AST.** `OpeningAttach.pos` gains `from`/`axis`/`default`, and door and opening gain `between`. The printer (`statement-print.ts`) prints every form, so `arch fmt`, `emitOpening` (the hinge-flip fix) and Plan JSON re-emit them.

## Addressing
- **describe.** The opening's row (`doors[]`/`windows[]`/`openings[]`) gains `relation`, as written (`"between a and b at 800 from end"`), present only on a relational opening.
- **Lint move hints.** A relational opening's hints (`W_OPENING_AT_JUNCTION`/`W_OPENING_OVERLAP` via `placeClause`) quote `` `between a and b at 1900 from start` `` or the `on <room>.<edge>` form. `W_DOOR_NEAR_CORNER` names the relation. No hint, fix or message quotes `A|B` (tested).
- **Unchanged.** Hints for a hand-placed opening on a derived host still quote `at (x, y)`, so every existing lint byte holds.

## Proof
- **Twins** (`test/openings-between.test.ts`). SVG and `lint()` are byte-identical, and `describe()` is identical once `relation` and `placement` are set aside:
  - `door between a and b at 800 from end` vs `door at (4000,4200) … wall partition`;
  - `door between b and a at 1200 from a.top … swing into b`;
  - `opening … at center`;
  - `window on b.top` and `… at center`;
  - `window on b.right at 1200 from b.top`;
  - `door on a.left at 1500 from end`;
  - an authored host drawn bottom-to-top (the position reads the run, not the wall).
- **Hosted datums vs their absolute twins:** SVG, `describe()` and `lint()` all byte-identical, for `800 from end`, `800 from start`, `1200 from a.top`, `axis A` and `300 from end` (with axes). A crossing at two points, a datum lying along the wall, and `cx` are refused.
- **Instances.** The relational door and window inside a component under **all eight frames** (rotate 0/90/180/270 × mirror x) give SVG and `lint()` byte-identical to the hand-placed twin.
- **Refusals.** Every code is tested with its span text: `E_OPENING_DATUM` (7 shapes), `E_OPENING_NIB` (start/end, tee, hint value checked legal, the flush exemption for a cased opening only), `E_OPENING_NO_SHARED_WALL`, `E_OPENING_HOST_AMBIGUOUS` (authored half; narrow room over a wide one), `E_WALL_BETWEEN_NOT_ADJACENT`, `E_WALL_BETWEEN_OPEN` (related span = `open between a and b width 900`), `E_UNKNOWN_REF`, `E_ROOM_NOT_RECTANGLE`. Every catalogue example is executed.
- **Widening drill.** `widen-4000` → `widen-4500` (`test/openings-between-plans.ts`):
  - the door `between a and b at 800 from end` moves from (4000,4200) to (4500,4200) and keeps 800 from the end;
  - `window on b.top` moves from (6000,0) to (6500,0);
  - the widened plan draws byte-identical to the hand-edited one.
  - SVG delta of the door's swing: `M 4800,3800 A 800 800 0 0 1 4000,4600` → `M 5300,3800 A 800 800 0 0 1 4500,4600`. The 30/56 changed elements are that shift plus the pen width rescale of the wider drawing.
- **Byte identity.**
  - Every existing digest suite is unchanged with no re-pin: resolve-order, room-edge-datums, roof-void, height, iso, outdoor, garage, while, fixture, walls-from-rooms-digests (all 13 rows), example-svgs-drift, doors, site, axes, visual, equivariance-corpus, opening-tags-corpus (17 files, 615 tests).
  - A second, differently shaped check: a corpus sweep (`allStoreysDigestWithDiagnostics`, 226 rows: examples, fixtures, recovery corpus, walls-from-rooms, defect corpus, plan repros, every `arch` fence in `docs/`). It ran on `git archive ac1ad21d` and on this branch, and moved exactly one row: the new language-reference fence, which `main` cannot parse.
  - The new table, `test/openings-between-digests.test.ts` (6 plans), is pinned last, in its own commit (7a84c076).

author: diogoribeiro7
body: Review item: asymmetry between expansions and contractions, one of the standard analyses both reviews listed as missing. ## Protocol [ASYMMETRY_PROTOCOL.md](eu-okun-law/ASYMMETRY_PROTOCOL.md) was committed and pushed (39b6b00) before any asymmetric estimate was computed. - **Inspected beforehand.** Only GDP: the number of negative-growth quarters per country in the headline sample. These run from 1 (SK) to 25 (EL), with a median of 12 and 320 in all. The symmetric classical sums were already published. - **Model.** The negative part of GDP growth, `min(g, 0)`, is added with lags 0–2 to the headline regression, on the headline sample. - **Primary test (P1).** A pooled model in which every country keeps its own intercept and Okun slopes, with a common extra response to negative growth. Its statistic is C, the sum of the common coefficients. It uses all 320 negative-growth quarters. - **Secondary test (P2).** The mean of the country-by-country asymmetries, over the countries with at least 8 negative-growth quarters. There are 23; SK, LT, BE and MT are excluded. - **Inference.** A synchronised circular block bootstrap over quarters: block 4, B = 1999, seed 20261027. The case-study p-value is used, with Holm over P1 and P2. A draw with a singular country design is dropped, and a test with more than 5% of draws dropped is labelled unreliable. ## Results ([docs/ASYMMETRY.md](eu-okun-law/docs/ASYMMETRY.md)) | Test | Estimate [95%] | Draws dropped | Holm p | Verdict | | --- | --- | ---: | ---: | --- | | P1, pooled common asymmetry (27 countries) | −0.10 [−0.19, +0.03] | 0.0% | 0.262 | not determined | | P2, mean group (23 countries) | −0.10 [−0.38, +0.11] | 2.1% | 0.262 | not determined | - **Magnitudes.** In the pooled model, unemployment moves −0.25 per point of positive growth and −0.35 per point of negative growth. - **Sensitivity.** The pooled difference is negative in all seven settings: lags 1 and 4, a mean-growth threshold, block 8, without IE and LU, without EL, and before 2020. No test is decided in any of them. The block-8 mean group is labelled unreliable (6.8% of draws dropped). - **Reading.** The point estimates lean towards a stronger response to contractions, but the data do not establish it. Contractions cluster in 2009–2013 and in the euro-area crisis countries, so even a decided difference could reflect the shocks. ## Checks of the estimator - **Reproduction.** With the asymmetry fixed at zero, the 27 country sums equal the case study's unemployment elasticities, to 1e-9. - **Direct fit.** The pooled estimator, which eliminates each country's own block, equals a direct least-squares fit with all country dummies and slopes, to 1e-10. - **Known asymmetry.** On synthetic data, both statistics recover a known asymmetry. ## Implementation correction (96858bd) - **The problem.** CI on Linux computed a different descriptive interval for Lithuania than Windows did. Lithuania has 2 negative-growth quarters. 42 of its draws passed the determinant cutoff for "singular" with condition numbers up to 2e20, and their solutions were dominated by rounding. - **The fix.** A design is now singular when its condition number exceeds 1e8. - **The effect.** For every other country this classifies exactly the same draws: those it rejects have condition numbers above 1e8, and those it keeps at most 3.3e5. Only Lithuania's descriptive row changes. Lithuania is outside the mean group, so P1, P2 and every sensitivity result are identical. The change is recorded in the protocol's change log. - **Verified.** The asymmetry tests pass on Linux (WSL) at this commit before pushing. ## Manuscript, article and docs - **§4.** A new paragraph, "Expansions and contractions". - **§10.** - A new Negative item: no decided asymmetry, although every point estimate has unemployment responding more strongly to contractions. - Asymmetry is removed from "Standard analyses not done". - **Medium article.** One paragraph. Asymmetry is removed from its list of missing analyses. - **Registry.** A new entry in the registry and the reproducibility table, the command in the publication README, and a README section. - **ROADMAP.** - Asymmetry is checked off. - The motivating post is recorded as not cited, by the author's choice. - The external archive is recorded as deferred, by the author's choice. - **Tests.** - New `tests/test_asymmetry.py`: synthetic recovery, the direct fit, a check that the text's claims match the committed results, and regeneration of the outputs. - New `WORD_CLAIMS` entries for the "none decided" phrases. ## Checks (local) - `ruff check src tests`, `mypy src` and `poetry check --lock` pass. - The full test suite passes. - `eu-okun publication --check` reports 0 failed audit checks and 0 stale files. - latexmk builds the manuscript with no warnings. --- ## Summary by cubic Adds the asymmetry analysis between expansions and contractions that both external reviews flagged as missing, with the protocol committed before any estimate was computed. The study splits negative GDP growth out of the headline regression, reports pooled and mean-group estimates, and applies the case study's block bootstrap with Holm adjustment. **Results** - The pooled extra response to negative growth is −0.10 [−0.19, +0.03] and the mean-group asymmetry −0.10 [−0.38, +0.11]; neither test is decided (Holm p 0.262). - The pooled difference is negative in all seven pre-registered sensitivity settings, with no test decided in any of them; the block-8 mean group is labelled unreliable. - Unemployment responds −0.25 per point of positive growth and −0.35 per point of negative growth in the pooled model; contractions cluster in 2009–2013 and the euro-area crisis countries, so even a decided difference could reflect the shocks. **Publication and docs** - Adds a registered protocol, results report, CLI command, `eu_okun/asymmetry` module, regression tests, and registry entries. - Updates the manuscript (§4, §10), the medium article, the ROADMAP, and the publication manifest; asymmetry is removed from the "standard analyses not done" lists. - An implementation fix classifies a bootstrap draw as singular by condition number instead of determinant; only Lithuania's descriptive row changes, and no registered statistic is affected. Written for commit 96858bdfe0e9ccab9053a97da0e15bc634abbf2d. Summary will update on new commits.

author: jurooravec
body:
Part of #207, stacked on #230. It implements the proposals approved in `docs/design/issue_207_proposals.md`, which this PR also adds as the design record for #207.

## What changes
1. **Templates of components whose base class lives in another module are checked.** Once the app is loaded, the editor and `citry check --types` accept the classes the app registers in a file, so those templates get checked too (proposal 1, Option 2). If the app can't load, or a class changed since it loaded, the notice from #230 stays.
2. **Server event argument checks run in the editor too** (proposal 3).
   - **Two new keys in the handler description** (`Citry.inspect_components`, `events.md` §9.1):
     - `extra_fields` (`"reject"` or `"ignore"`);
     - `validated_by` (`"citry"` or `"pydantic"`). A Pydantic model with `extra="forbid"` still converts values and reads aliases, which `extra_fields` alone can't express.
   - **An older citry** that omits the keys turns these checks off for that handler.
3. **The server drops the CSRF field before checking a form's data class** (proposal 4a). Django's `csrfmiddlewaretoken` hidden input can stay inside the form, and posts with and without JavaScript both work.
   - The names come from `extensions_defaults["events"]["_csrf_field_names"]`; the default is `csrfmiddlewaretoken`.
   - A data class that declares that name, directly or through a Pydantic alias, still receives it.
4. **A form submitted with JavaScript is converted like one posted without it** (proposal 4b). The browser marks calls it collected from a form with `argsSource: "form"`, a new optional field in `citry-events/1`, changed in place. The server then applies the same text conversion as for a form posted without JavaScript.
   - **Who notices:** a handler that reads `event.args` directly, or a strict Pydantic model, now gets `"3"` where it used to get `3`. The changelog says so.
   - Older browser code keeps today's behaviour.
5. **New rules for form fields** (m44): `citry.browser.unknown-form-field` (error) and `citry.browser.missing-form-field`. They compare a form's static control names with the handler's data class. Both run in `citry check` with the app loaded and in the editor. They handle named submit buttons, image buttons, spreads and `#c-ignore`.

## Evidence
- **Benchmark:** m44 is now a static error. No other Citry cell moves, and the clean benchmark app stays silent.
- **Fast gate:** every Python phase passes. The Rust phases couldn't run in this worktree because a git submodule wasn't checked out; no Rust changed.
- **Reviews:** two independent code reviews, a re-review of their fixes, and a separate prose pass.
- **Not run locally:** the browser end-to-end tests and the docs-site tests. CI runs them.

author: gedaiu
body:
## Summary

Found while investigating `re-cinq/Otto#158`: its last loop task had already settled `failed`, and the user manually revived it via "Run this station". The run was genuinely live again (fresh commits landing on its branch), but the backlog page still showed it under "Next up" + "Recently addressed" with no sign the work was in progress.

Two root causes, both from the same fact: **a by-hand start never writes to Postgres** — it only posts a floor event (ADR-049/FR18.3).

- **Display**: the backlog's `current` bucket is driven purely by `pipeline.tasks.status` (`OPEN_TASK_STATES`), which a by-hand revival of a settled task never updates. `current` is now a **list**: a task counts as current either by its own stored status, or because its newest run is live on the floor right now (`running`/`queued`) — independent of what Postgres says. More than one ticket can be current at once (the loop's own pick, plus any by-hand revival), and the same live-run check keeps a revived ticket's issue out of `next` and its task out of `recent`.
- **Settle-on-finish**: once a revived run finishes, the settle station's CAS (`setStatusIf(taskId, "running", …)`, `apps/stations/.../station.ts`) silently no-ops, since the task row was never flipped back to `running` in the first place — so the ticket's stored outcome stays frozen at the *old* failure. `handleRunNode` (`apps/lore-api/.../run-node.ts`) now does that flip itself, once the floor has taken the ask, for any `implementation-loop`/`onboard` run carrying a `task_id` start item.

Also: moved the 3-line `startValueOf` helper (reading a floor run's start items) out of stations-only code into `libs/shared`, since lore-api now needs it too; split `backlog-ticket.ts`'s Postgres/floor run-context reads into their own `backlog-run-context.ts` (the file was pushing past the repo's 300-line cap).

## Test plan
- [x] `libs/shared`, `apps/lore-api`, `apps/stations`, `apps/web-ui` full vitest suites green
- [x] `tsc --noEmit` clean in all four packages
- [x] `gen:openapi` + `gen:api-types` regenerated, diff scoped to `current`'s shape change
- [x] `NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=8192 eslint .` (the CI `format` job's own check) clean repo-wide

author: dryn85-max
body:
## What does this PR do?

Closes #1999. `task: simpo` with `backend: mlx` was refused at config load. It now trains natively in Soup's own MLX preference loop, the one MLX DPO (#1846) and MLX ORPO (#2073) use. The objective is pinned to **TRL 0.29.1 `experimental/cpo/cpo_trainer.py` with `loss_type="simpo"`**, which is what the transformers backend runs for `task: simpo`. It is reference-free and runs no Torch/TRL on the native path.

**Objective** (`trainer/mlx_simpo.py`). `a` and `b` are the **mean** log-probs of the chosen and rejected completion tokens (`average_log_prob` for simpo, `:741-742`, `:804`).
- The preference term is `-logsigmoid(beta * (a - b) - simpo_gamma)`. TRL writes it `beta * ((a - b) - simpo_gamma / beta)` (`:669-676`). The margin sits **outside** the temperature, so this is not mlx-tune's `beta * (delta - gamma)`, as you pointed out on the issue.
- **beta = 0.1, fixed.** `trainer/simpo.py` forwards no beta, so `CPOConfig`'s default applies (`cpo_config.py:113`); label smoothing is TRL's default 0 (`:120`). A test pins both, and one AST-checks that `simpo.py` still passes neither. The value is written to the adapter metadata as `simpo_beta`. `dpo_beta` and `orpo_beta` are not read.
- `loss = mean(pref) + cpo_alpha * NLL` (`:844`). The NLL is CPO's cross-entropy on the chosen **completion** only (prompt and padding are `-100` in its labels, `:524-531`, `:600-610`, `:780-799`), and it is a token mean over the micro-batch. ORPO's NLL is different: it covers the whole sequence. `cpo_alpha: 0` stays refused by the schema (`gt=0`).
- Metrics follow TRL (`:845-866`): `nll_loss`, rewards `beta * logp`, accuracy (strict `>`), margin, and chosen/rejected logps. The mean-logit metrics are left out because the vocab head runs in checkpointed chunks and the full logits never exist.
- A nonfinite loss stops the run.

**Tokens = TRL's CPO `tokenize_row`.** It is byte-identical to ORPO's apart from TorchXLA padding, so `MLXSimPOTrainerWrapper` subclasses the ORPO wrapper and reuses its rows, chat-template rendering, merge shift, BOS/EOS and collation unchanged.
- **One difference from the transformers path, documented:** over-long rows get the same Soup cap as MLX DPO/ORPO (prompt to `max_length // 2`, `keep_end`, answers to the remaining room).
- On transformers, `CPOConfig` 0.29.1 has no `max_prompt_length` and `simpo.py` does not call `enforce_preference_sequence_limit`, so the prompt is never cut and only the answers are.
- Rows that fit in `max_length` give identical ids on both backends (shown below). I can open a separate issue for the transformers SimPO prompt cap if you want the backends to agree on long rows too.

**Config.**
- `simpo` joins `MLX_TASKS`.
- Refused at load on mlx, as for ORPO: `quantization: 8bit`, `lora.r: 0`, non-text `modality`, LoRA+.
- `task: preference` with `preference_loss: simpo` stays refused on mlx, and the message now names `task: simpo`. The same hint now covers `orpo` and `dpo`: before, the `dpo` alias was told to use transformers although native `task: dpo` exists. All three hints are asserted.
- `backend_support` declares `(simpo, mlx, text)` with the #755 drift guards passing; `soup doctor --config` reports the ignored fields.
- The #1358 `add_new_tokens` / `new_special_tokens` refusal has simpo rows, and the dispatch-parity table has the simpo row.
- Transformers routing and forwarding are unchanged (tested).

**Shared code.**
- ORPO's `--resume` metadata guard now reads the objective's name and task, so SimPO reuses it. It is tested from both sides: an ORPO resume refuses a SimPO adapter, and the reverse.
- The only ORPO message change: "an ORPO adapter" now reads "a task='orpo' adapter".
- DPO is unchanged apart from a comment.

## Tests: `tests/test_mlx_simpo.py`, 61 (33 run without MLX)

- **TRL facts:** effective beta and label smoothing read from `CPOConfig`; `simpo.py` passes no beta.
- **Tokens vs TRL:** text and conversational rows through TRL's own `CPOTrainer.tokenize_row` on a real `PreTrainedTokenizerFast`. Ids are equal, and the label spans equal the completion. Also covered: BOS/EOS, the merge shift, `keep_end` through the trainer, the no-room refusal on the builder, and ties.
- **Loss vs a float64 NumPy oracle** on nonconstant, unequal-length, right-padded logits, with gamma and `cpo_alpha` varied independently:
  - completion means, NLL, and total, for the full and the chunked head;
  - gradients vs finite differences;
  - prompt and padding logits move nothing.
- **The oracle vs TRL itself, without MLX:** `CPOTrainer.get_batch_loss_metrics` on a stub, compared to rel 1e-9 on loss, NLL, logps and margin, plus torch gradients vs finite differences of the oracle. So Linux CI checks the oracle too.
- **Edge values:** a tie gives `softplus(gamma) + NLL`; extreme scores stay finite; NaN is not turned into a quiet zero.
- **Tiny native training** (random 2-layer Llama, real MLX):
  - LoRA B moves while every base tensor stays bit-identical;
  - the held-out margin rises against the same model untrained;
  - the metadata is written;
  - 2×1 equals 1×2 after one SGD update;
  - a trailing partial batch is dropped, and validation chunks are weighted by rows;
  - a nonfinite loss stops the run.
- **Resume:** from its own adapter. It refuses an ORPO adapter, another base, or missing metadata.
- **Fresh-process reload:** a subprocess reproduces the in-process logits, and a base-only control differs.
- **Source mutations, each failing a named test:**
  - summed scores; reversed pair; no margin; margin inside the temperature;
  - NLL removed; NLL as a mean of per-row means; NLL over the sequence mask;
  - `simpo` removed from `MLX_TASKS`; the routing entry removed.
  - The no-margin mutations correctly pass the gamma=0 case only.

**New native tests for the maintainers to add to `mlx-smoke`:** `pytest -o addopts= -q tests/test_mlx_simpo.py`. The TRL parts need `trl`/`transformers`/`torch` and skip without them. `ci.yml` is untouched, as on #2073.

## Native evidence (Apple M4 Pro 48 GB)

Python 3.12.8, mlx 0.32.3, mlx-lm 0.32.0, trl 0.29.1, transformers 5.19.0. Source on `main` `9497fa5d`.
- **Models:** `Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct` converted locally to MLX bf16, and `mlx-community/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct-4bit`.
- **Data:** the same split as #2073, 600 train / 200 held-out UltraFeedback pairs.

**Parity with TRL on real weights** (16 held-out pairs, `max_length` 1024). TRL `tokenize_row`, `get_batch_logps` and CPO's chosen NLL in torch fp32, versus MLX bf16:
- token ids identical **16/16**;
- worst relative total-loss gap **0.77%**, from bf16 vs fp32;
- example, pair 3 (540/557 tokens): loss 1.9729 vs 1.9709.

**Training.** `soup train --config …`, 1 epoch, lr 5e-5, `simpo_gamma` 0.5, `cpo_alpha` 1.0, batch 2 × accum 4, LoRA r16/α32, gradient checkpointing, seed 42. Held-out metrics are computed **in a fresh process** with `mlx_lm.load(base, adapter_path=out)`:

| | train loss | time | peak RSS | held-out pairwise acc | mean logp margin `a - b` | chosen completion NLL |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| bf16 base, before | | | | 0.540 | 0.073 | 2.227 |
| bf16, after | 2.806 → 2.345 | 258 s | 8.6 GB | 0.565 | 0.139 | 1.280 |
| 4-bit base, before | | | | 0.545 | 0.042 | 2.272 |
| 4-bit, after | 2.907 → 2.461 | 276 s | 7.5 GB | 0.550 | 0.131 | 1.388 |

What this does and does not show:
- **It shows** the mechanics on a real pretrained model. The objective moves in the intended direction: the held-out margin rises ×1.9 (bf16) and ×3.1 (4-bit), and the held-out completion NLL drops.
- **It does not show** alignment quality. Pairwise accuracy barely moves after one epoch on 600 pairs.

- [x] Documentation

## Description
- Promotes `foss-sandbox` to `foss-main` for Twenty: one merged sandbox PR (#34), 21 files, +1052/-76. The merge was checked with `git merge-tree` and is clean.
- #34: [FOSS-490](https://pm.moneta.askii.ai/moneta/browse/FOSS-490/) stops the SSO proxy-login redirect loop and makes the in-app sign-out deterministic.
  - Loop: `SignInUp` redirected to proxy-login with no token-pair check and `returnToPath=/welcome`, and the proxy-login controller redirected back to `/welcome`. The two raced, and each lost race minted one unused refresh token (16 to 34 per minute and 2k to 6k ForwardAuth checks per minute on askii).
  - Server: new `resolve-sso-return-path.util.ts` makes the controller return `/` for the sign-in page (matched case- and encoding-insensitively) and for unsafe values; other same-origin paths with their query strings, such as `/authorize?client_id=...`, are unchanged.
  - Front end: `useSsoProxyLoginRedirect` skips the redirect when SSO is off, a token pair exists or a sign-out is in progress, and caps proxy-login at 3 attempts per 60s (kept in `localStorage`). A `SsoLoginRecovery` screen with "Try again" and "Go to the portal" replaces an endless loader when the cap trips or a sign-out stalls. Sign-out sets an in-progress flag first so the sign-in page cannot hijack the portal navigation, and other tabs now go to the portal on a cross-tab sign-out.
- Behaviour change to know about: a user who trips the cap (more than 3 proxy-login attempts in 60s) sees the recovery screen instead of a silent loop. Non-SSO deployments are unchanged. `buildPortalUrl` still sends a 3-label host back to Twenty (pre-existing).
- Validated on staging as `v26.10.2-rc.1` (`0b1ae4f`, the sandbox head): twenty, twenty-worker and twenty-bootstrap on one image, healthy, bundle contains the new code, proxy-login unauthenticated behaviour unchanged.
- Merge with a merge commit, not squash.

## Testing
- `npx jest src/modules/auth src/pages` in `twenty-front`: 23 suites, 108 tests passed; server `sso-proxy-login.controller.spec.ts` and `resolve-sso-return-path.util.spec.ts`: 34 tests passed.
- Two adversarial review rounds (round 2 APPROVE); mutation checks failed as expected when the fix was reverted. Copilot could not review (quota reached), merged at Usama's direction.
- Staging login test of the sign-out, refresh-token count, multi-tab sign-out and `/authorize` deep link was done by Usama on `twenty.foss.arbisoft.com`.
- Not run: the full `nx test` suites.

author: arcanumruna
body:
Batch B4 (sev:high, area:auth / area:broker). #113 is left out: its fix is #10's, see below.

## Fixes #118: no shared-MDC record fallback under authentication

**Root cause.** When a Subscribe's per-session record egress could not be created or resolved, it reached the owning worker with `egressPub = null`. This happened with no egress endpoint, when the add threw, when the resolve timed out or errored, and on the queued retry. The worker then pushed the topic on its shared dynamic-MDC publication. Every party joined to the worker's advertised control port received it, whether or not it held READ.

**Fix.**
- `ClientGateway::enqueueSubscribeOp_` is the single point where a null-egress Subscribe can reach a worker, and the queued retry in `trySubOp_` is its twin. Under `GatewayAuthMode::Required` both now call `retireWithoutRecordEgress_`, which retires the subscription retriably:
  - a plain subscription gets the position note plus `NotLeader` on its correlation id, and the client's moved-subscription path re-subscribes from its position;
  - a group member's subscription evicts the session's members, and the consumer rejoins.
- The synchronous failures (no endpoint, add threw) are parked as a failed resolve, so the retirement is sent after the Subscribe's OK.
- As a second, independent check, an authenticating broker's workers (`Worker::requirePerSessionEgress`, set next to `requireEnforcement`) refuse any Subscribe op without its own egress.
- Outside authentication the MDC fallback is unchanged.

**Tests** in `broker/libs/gateway/tests/gateway/RecordEgressLifetimeTest.cpp`:
- `AuthEnforcementRegression.NoRecordIsEverBroadcastToAnUnauthorizedSubscriberRegression`
- `AuthEnforcementRegression.AFailedRecordEgressResolveNeverFallsBackToTheSharedEgressRegression`
- `AuthEnforcementRegression.AnAuthenticatingWorkerNeverRegistersACursorWithoutItsOwnEgressRegression`
- `AuthEnforcementRegression.ASessionWithItsOwnRecordEgressStillReachesTheWorkerUnderAuthRegression` (positive control)

The first three failed before the fix. The worker test was also mutation-checked.

## Fixes #117: admin-log read ends are never dropped, and every admin-log frame is checked on the control thread

**Root cause.** Three ways an end could be dropped or delayed:
1. **Dropped.** `forwardCatalogUnsubscribe_` treated the `-2` / `-3` ends like single unsubscribes and dropped them when the waiting queue was at its cap ("it ends with the session").
2. **Delayed.** Even when an end was not dropped, the only thing that stopped the stream was the admin thread processing it. Until then, Records kept flowing to a principal that had already lost ADMIN.
3. **Out of order.** The admin thread can apply and stream a REVOKE, and the CREATE USER after it, before the control thread applies the REVOKE. These are separate rings, so the verifier could leak through that window.

**Fix.**
- The ends are now per-session pending state (`Session::pendingReadEnds`). They are coalesced, take one entry per session, are retried every duty cycle and are never dropped. A close supersedes them. A later Subscribe of the same kind waits behind an owed end, so the end can never cut off the new read.
- `CatalogReadFlow` asks the sink to admit each Records frame (`Sink::admit` → `ClientGateway::admitAdminLogFrame`). This check runs on the control thread and does not depend on the admin thread:
  - a `__security` frame needs ADMIN ON CLUSTER now;
  - a `__catalog` frame needs DESCRIBE ON CLUSTER now;
  - a `__security` frame whose newest event (control batches excluded) this broker's SecurityView has not applied yet is held. It is paused and re-read from the log, like a back-pressured frame.

**Tests** in `broker/libs/gateway/tests/gateway/CatalogGatewayTest.cpp`:
- `AuthLiveChangeRegression.SecurityReadEndNeverDroppedUnderAdminRingPressureRegression`: failed before the fix.
- `AuthLiveChangeRegression.AdminLogFramesNeedTheReadersGrantAtSendTimeRegression`

## Fixes #259: permission compile is per grant set, not per session

**Root cause.** Every login and every live refresh compiled the session's own table, at O(objects × grants) per session on the control thread. Each session's full WRITE bitmap was shipped to every worker. A created topic re-shipped the whole bitmap of every session that gained WRITE on it.

**Fix.**
- **`gateway/PermissionPool`.** There is one compiled table per distinct effective grant set. The key is the exact sorted grant list, ref counts are plain integers on the control thread, and ids are dense and bounded at 4096. A login or refresh now costs one `effectiveGrants()` call and one lookup. A created or dropped object updates each live table once.
- **`PermissionShipper`.** It is a strict FIFO of Table / Patch / Bind / Drop items sent to every worker. Nothing is coalesced or reordered: a bind always follows the table it names, and a drop follows the rebinds away from it. A table is shipped once per grant set. A session gets a one-op bind. A created topic sends a one-word patch per live table.
- **Workers.** A fixed store of `WritePermTable` with stable addresses. Each session slot points at its table, so `allowsWrite` is one pointer load, one bounds check and one bit load, with no allocation. A drop resets any slot still on that table to deny.
- **Refresh.** The old table is kept alive until the rebind is queued, so a session whose WRITE did not change is never denied in between. The same set means the same table, so nothing is shipped.

**Tests:**
- `PermissionPoolRegression.{SessionsSharingAGrantSetCompileOneTable, TheLastHolderFreesTheTableAndItsIdIsReused, AnObjectCreatedUpdatesEachLiveTableOnce, AnUnpooledRefIsItsOwnTableAndDenyByDefault}Regression` in `broker/libs/gateway/tests/PermissionTableTest.cpp`
- `PermissionShippingRegression.ARoleOfManySessionsShipsOneTableAndOneBindEachRegression` in `broker/libs/gateway/tests/gateway/RecordEgressLifetimeTest.cpp`. With 200 sessions × 4 workers it asserts 1 compile, `4 × tableWords` words shipped plus one bind per session, and exactly one word per worker for a new topic.
- `WorkerWriteGrantRegression.{SessionsSharingATableSeeItsPatchAndItsDrop, ABindToNoTableDeniesEverything}Regression` in `broker/libs/node/tests/node/WorkerWriteGrantsTest.cpp`
- `PermissionShipperRegression.{ItemsReachEveryWorkerInQueueOrder, APatchIsOneOpOfItsWordsOnly}Regression` in `broker/libs/node/tests/node/PermissionShipperTest.cpp`

The existing worker and shipper tests were moved to the table + bind protocol with their assertions kept. In the one out-of-order-chunk test, the epoch now belongs to the bind.

Mutation check: disabling the pool lookup turns the compile-count, created-object and shipping tests red.

## Left out: #113

The right fix for #113 is #10 (mandatory TLS under auth). The combined-fix spec closes X002 with the TLS fix, decision M1. A plaintext-session refusal cannot land on its own yet:
- the `rune` CLI cannot use TLS (#13), and `rune security bootstrap` and every `CREATE USER` go through it;
- `auth-e2e` runs over plaintext;
- no test runs authentication over TLS (#137).

The diagnosis and the required order (#13 → #10) are in a comment on #113.

## Design calls
- #118: under auth a failed record egress is answered NotLeader (retriable), not `Internal` as the spec draft says. A bound subscription answered `Internal` is not ended by the client, so it would hang silently. NotLeader goes down the bounded moved-subscription retry path.
- #117: the confidentiality guarantee comes from the control thread's per-frame admit, not from the admin thread's acknowledgement. The ends are still never dropped, which reclaims the admin's read slots.
- #259: per-pass resumable refresh was not added. With pooling, a refresh is O(sessions) small binds, and the shipper is already resumable per worker.
- #259: the worker table store is bounded at 4096, the same as `SessionAckSink::kMaxSessions`. When the pool is full, a new set gets deny-all (fail closed) and an err

author: ashipaek0
body:
The box now sets its Wi-Fi regulatory country itself, so it can use the channels its country allows.

## Why
- Without a country, the radio uses the world rules, where channels 12 and 13 are listen-only.
- On the Pi 3B today, the 2.4 GHz router "NXNEW" on channel 13 (2472 MHz) in Nigeria was never seen, neither by iwd nor by a raw `iw dev wlan0 scan`.
- After `iw reg set NG` it appeared at once.

## What
- **Which country:** the one given with the Wi-Fi settings (`wifi.txt`, Raspberry Pi Imager) if any; otherwise the site time zone's, from tzdata's `zone.tab` (Africa/Lagos → NG). With neither, the world rules stay as before.
- **When it is applied:**
  - at boot, by `epilykos-wifi-import`;
  - when wlan0 appears, by a udev rule running the new `epilykos-wifi-country`, since the driver can come up after boot set it;
  - when the time zone changes in Settings, by `epilykos-hostd`.
- **Docs:** the Wi-Fi template and the README say when to fill in `country=` by hand. A first setup reaches Wi-Fi before the time zone is chosen, so a router on channel 12/13 needs `country=` in `wifi.txt` or Imager's Wi-Fi country that first time.

## Tests
- `test_wifi_provisioning.py`:
  - looking up the country in `zone.tab`;
  - a country from the Wi-Fi settings wins over the time zone;
  - `epilykos-wifi-country` and `epilykos-wifi-import` run `iw reg set NG` for Africa/Lagos, with a fake `iw`;
  - nothing runs with no country.
- `test_host_actions.py`: changing the time zone sets the country once.
- `make test`, `make contracts` and pyflakes are clean.

body:
## Revisão técnica do repositório

Baseado no `main` depois do merge da PR #30 (`bf89fc5`). Não havia outra PR aberta para esta revisão. O catálogo navegável, evidências, decisões e limitações estão em [docs/TECHNICAL_REVIEW.md](https://github.com/Shiroz1n/spinda-stop/blob/chore/repository-maintenance-review/docs/TECHNICAL_REVIEW.md).

## Achados e correções prioritários

- **Segurança — corrigido:** o rate limit aceitava `X-Forwarded-For` sem verificar proxy quando não havia endereço de socket. Uma reprodução com 30 valores diferentes contornava o limite. Agora usa esse header apenas no contexto Vercel, cuja borda o sobrescreve; fora dele usa IP de socket ou a chave comum `unknown`. Teste novo confirma 24 respostas de OAuth e seis `429` para 30 cabeçalhos forjados no adaptador Fetch.
- **Hardening — corrigido:** `VERCEL_ENV` agora prevalece sobre `APP_ENV`; Preview/Production não ativam `/api/test/session` mesmo que `APP_ENV=test` tenha sido configurado.
- **Código morto/CSS:** nenhum componente, rota ou folha CSS foi removido por inferência. As três folhas são importadas em `main.jsx`; as rotas API seguem em uso.
- **Assets — limpos:** removidos 63 PNGs de revisão gerados por CI (27 antes + 36 depois) e quatro PNGs que repetiam os quatro quadros da sequência composta. Saíram 7.009.624 bytes de imagens do HEAD. As comparações continuam acessíveis no histórico/artefatos da PR #30; imagens únicas de teclado e mobile, 69 referências e 15 capturas DataDex permanecem.
- **Performance:** mantidas divisões lazy. Pokédex (478 KB; 58 KB gzip) e calculadora (522 KB; 126 KB gzip) são os maiores chunks; sem medição de runtime não foi feito split especulativo.
- **Bun/Elysia/PostgreSQL:** a migração já estava concluída antes desta PR (#30, commit `2e75f41`); as rotas e o banco PostgreSQL foram preservados. Esta PR corrige apenas o adaptador de confiança do IP e cobre os limites novos.
- **Docs/textos:** atualizados estados remotos da PR #30, comportamento de segurança e destino das capturas. Nenhum documento de fonte de verdade ou teste foi removido.

## Verificação local

- `npm run lint`: passou.
- `npm test`: 132 casos; 127 passaram, zero falhas, cinco PostgreSQL ignorados porque este ambiente não tem `DATABASE_URL`.
- Runtime Elysia: 9/9 passaram.
- `npm run build`: passou; permanece o aviso de chunk >500 KB.
- `npm audit` e `npm audit --omit=dev`: zero vulnerabilidades.
- Scan de padrões de credenciais no HEAD e patches alcançáveis de 180 dias: sem correspondências.
- Visual Review local: o build passou, mas a captura local não abriu por falta do Chromium do Playwright. No HEAD final `8d8a2fd`, o modo rápido de Salas/Torneios passou em **3,8 s**, com 16 observações desktop/mobile e 0 falhas; o modo completo passou em **778,2 s (12 min 58 s)**, com 464 observações em 1440/390/320/720 px, axe e 0 falhas. Resultado em [Visual Review #163](https://github.com/Shiroz1n/spinda-stop/actions/runs/39609085180); [artefato de capturas e relatórios](https://github.com/Shiroz1n/spinda-stop/actions/runs/39609085180/artifacts/12351010174). O modo rápido é um subconjunto e não substitui o gate completo.
- Bun smoke, sincronização de dados, migrações, testes com PostgreSQL 16 efêmero, lint e build passaram no CI do HEAD final (`CI #211`: https://github.com/Shiroz1n/spinda-stop/actions/runs/39609085546). Bun/PostgreSQL não estão instalados no ambiente local.

body:
Fixes #68.

The TADS 3 status line is a text banner with the tab-align style. It was opened as a buffer window drawn in the buffer's Preformatted style, so it ignored the Grid font settings, and "Games can set colors and styles" behaved differently for it than for other games' status lines.

Like the [TADS Runner](https://github.com/tads-intfic/tads-runner), a text banner with the tab-align style and no scroll style now opens as a text grid. That covers the adv3 status line and the menu header; the menu contents scroll and stay a buffer.

- The T3 VM pads a right-aligned `<tab>` with spaces to the banner width it saw when the text was written. Each banner remembers that width, and when it is reopened at a different width (every resize closes and reopens the banners), the widest space run of a right-aligned line grows or shrinks so the right part stays at the edge.
- `sizeToContents` sets a grid banner's height to the number of rows its contents reach.

author: martingallagher-code
body:
This pull request carries three rounds: 1.22.0, 1.23.0 and 1.24.0. Only 1.24.0 is published.

## 1.22.0: explain these results by the network

There is a new checkbox under any per-host load. It assumes every server tried the same load: the Load generator's pattern, at the best server's result. It then finds the cables that would hold the other servers back to exactly what they measured.

The panel reports:

- **Each such cable** and the capacity the results give it. It is **degraded** if that capacity is below its `gbps=`, and **full** if it is simply oversubscribed.
- **Servers held back by themselves.**
- **A target above the best result**, when even the best server was held back.
- **How closely the model, with those cables changed, reproduces every server's result.**
- **A new cable view**, *explained by the network*.

All of this is `explainResults` in `js/traffic.js`. It is a greedy search over cables, ranked by contrast between the short servers and the rest, with capacities refined through `contend`. It has a 20 s budget and runs asynchronously in the browser.

## 1.23.0: a server's own limits

Two new keys on a server, both counted in `contend` the same way a full cable is:

- **`stream=`** is the most one connection carries, in Gb/s. It applies at either end, so a flow carries at most its connections times it.
- **`cpugbps=`** is one CPU budget for sending and receiving together. **`rxcost=`** weights receiving against sending.

The key is `cpugbps=`, not `cpu=`, because the examples (and so probably real layouts) already use `cpu=epyc-9654` to name the part. Reusing `cpu=` would change how those files load.

Where they show up:

- The headline counts *hosts out of CPU* and *hosts at their stream=*.
- A server's tooltip shows its per-connection ceiling and how full its CPU is.

The explain panel also gains a third answer: **the servers themselves**. When most servers stop at one figure and the network would carry more of the same load, the limit is theirs. The panel then gives the `stream=` or `cpugbps=` that would reproduce it.

## 1.24.0: `busy=`

- **`busy=20%`** takes that share off a server's `cpugbps=`.
- **CPU busy elsewhere:** with servers that have a `cpugbps=`, the routing box offers this choice. Picking a per-server CPU metric (in per cent, or unitless and named for the CPU) reads each server's share from it in place of `busy=`. This is `busyOf`, passed to `contend` as `opts.busy`.
- **Explain** names servers **short by their own load**: the ones the layout's limits, busy included, already reproduce.
- **A gap from 1.23.0, fixed:** *connections a flow* now shows whenever a server has a `stream=`, packet spraying included.

## Tests

- `node tests/run.mjs --strict`: 1663 passed. New tests:
  - per-connection caps, the shared CPU budget with `rxcost=`, and the keys' parsing;
  - `busy=`, written and measured, the measured share winning, and `busyOf` reading per cent and fractions;
  - explain's own-limit answer, and its servers short by their own load.
- `node tests/browser.mjs --strict`: 250 passed. New tests:
  - the explain panel's own-limit lines;
  - the headline and a server's tooltip with `stream=` and `cpugbps=`;
  - choosing a CPU metric for busy, and what the tooltip then says.

author: devadanendra
body:
Follow-up to devadanendra/expense-tracker#19: the jump from card 5 to card 1 (and 1 to 5) was visible.

## Why it jumped
Cards peek in from both sides. The strip had one copy at each end, so on the copy of card 1 nothing peeked from the right. When it swapped to the real card 1, card 2's edge popped into view. The same happened on the left going from 1 to 5.

## Changes
- **Two copies at each end:** `[copy 4, copy 5, 1 … 5, copy 1, copy 2]`. On a copy, the neighbors peeking in are the same as on the real card, so the swap can't be seen. A quick second swipe past the end also has a card to land on instead of hitting the end of the strip.
- **Wrap only on `scrollend`** where the browser fires it. The 150 ms quiet-scroll timer could jump while a finger rested mid-swipe, so it now runs only as the fallback for browsers without `scrollend` (older Safari).
- **One card per swipe:** `scroll-snap-stop: always`, so a hard flick stops at the next card.
- Cache `et-v20`.

The branch also carries a merge of its own pre-squash history (already in `main` as #19), so the push didn't need a force. The diff against `main` is only the three files above.

## Testing
- `npm test`: 169 pass.
- Headless Chromium, phone emulation, raw touch drags: 1 → 5, 5 → 4, 4 → 5 and 5 → 1 each land on the real card with the right dot. Two quick swipes 5 → 1 → 2, and 2 → 1 → 5, go straight through. Strip order checked: `Top notes*, Stood out*, Pace, Safe to spend, Weekdays, Top notes, Stood out, Pace*, Safe to spend*`.

body:
## What

The session-start handoff now forwards the repository marker's `[briefing]` opt-in, so Hermes receives the same compiled project brief the official hook clients do:

- `config.marker_briefing(cwd)` walks up from the session `cwd` through capture-only markers and stops at the nearest settings marker (or `$HOME` / filesystem root), mirroring ai-memory's own settings walk. It reads `inject_on_session_start` and the optional `max_chars` with a line-based parser that accepts quoted or bare values, like `parse_flag_in`.
- `AiMemoryClient.fetch_handoff()` sends `briefing=<opt-in>` plus `briefing_budget=<max_chars>` when the marker opts in. Falsy values never enable it; the budget is clamped server-side.
- `AiMemoryProvider.initialize()` now passes the session `cwd` on the handoff fetch (it was already sent on hooks), which the marker walk needs.

## Why

`docs/marker-file.md` (ai-memory) states that hook capture and handoff lookup send the same `cwd`, `workspace`, `project`, ..., `briefing`, `briefing_budget` query params **when a marker declares them**, and that the session-start handoff returns the pinned / `_rules_` / `_slots_` pages only for opted-in repositories. The official install lists Hermes as supported via hooks + this community plugin, but the plugin predates that parameter: in practice Hermes consumed the pending handoff and never received the project brief (`GET /handoff` returned 0 bytes with a valid `[briefing]` marker).

## Behaviour / compatibility

- Off unless the nearest settings marker enables `inject_on_session_start`; a capture-only marker stays transparent, and a nearer settings marker that does not opt in stops the walk (no leaking from an outer marker).
- No marker, no `cwd`, or a falsy flag → identical request to today (no new params).
- `max_chars` is forwarded only when present; the server still clamps it.

## Tests

- New unit tests for the marker walk, quoted/bare flags, capture-only skipping, settings boundary, falsy values, and the handoff query params; one provider test pins `cwd` forwarding.
- `tests/test_directory_scope.py` handoff assertion updated to include `cwd`, which the official clients also send.
- `uv run pytest`: 228 passed. On this Windows host 3 unrelated tests fail because `tmp_path` sits under the real `$HOME`, whose `.ai-memory.toml` declares `hermes` scope; those same 3 fail on unmodified `main` here and pass where `$HOME` is not an ancestor of the temp dir. `ruff check` and `mypy` are clean.

## Windows validation (native, before submitting)

- ai-memory 3.1.1 on Windows, Hermes session cwd `C:\Users\Taiwue\AppData\Local\hermes\profiles\botmaker`, marker at `C:\Users\Taiwue\.ai-memory.toml` with `[briefing] inject_on_session_start = "true"`.
- `marker_briefing(cwd)` → `{'inject_on_session_start': 'true', 'max_chars': ''}`.
- `GET /handoff?agent=hermes&cwd=...&briefing=true&workspace=hermes&project=hermes-default` → **3451 bytes**, including the `_rules/registro-pos-recuperacao` brief; the pre-fix call (no `briefing`) returned no brief.

Happy to adjust naming or split the provider `cwd` change if you prefer a narrower first patch.
