author: gbirman
body:
## Why

Pilot feedback on CRM settings: the page "looks weird/bad and isn't really relevant". Two causes:

- **Its content predates pipelines.** "Deal stages" was described as "the pipeline stages deals move through on the CRM board", but #7787 removed the company board, and every pipeline now has its own Stage column. The team stage set is now two things: the Stage property on companies, and the stages copied into each new pipeline. "Closed stages" only fed the removed board's closed-deal move restriction: `canMoveClosedDeals` has no callers, and the backend stores the ids but nothing reads them. Its copy also pointed at a Permissions section that no longer exists.
- **It didn't look like other settings pages.** A red "Disable CRM" button was the first control on the page. Stage names were a column of pill inputs. Every stage got the same accent dot instead of its color. The dialogs were hand-rolled, and permission explanations lived only in tooltips, which never show on touch.

## What

- **Team CRM switch.** General is now one `Team CRM` row with a ToggleSwitch, like the rows in Notifications and Integrations. When an admin flips it, the same dialogs as before appear: backfill or start fresh to enable, and typing `Disable CRM` to purge. Members see the switch disabled, with the reason in the row's description.
- **Stages.** The section is renamed from Deal stages and now says what it controls: "The Stage options on companies. New pipelines start with these stages." Each row shows the stage's color as used in the CRM list groups and filters (`CrmStageIcon`). Customize and Reset to defaults sit in the section header. Customized stages are renamed inline in a borderless field. Reorder, delete, and add work as before: a drag handle or arrow keys on desktop, up/down buttons on touch.
- **Dialogs.** Delete stage and Reset use the shared `@ui` ConfirmDialog, which becomes a drawer on phones. The delete copy no longer mentions the board.
- **Closed stages removed** from the page, the stage editor, the CRM context, and the web team-config model. The settings search entries and `docs/agent-guide/settings.md` use the new labels.
- **Tests.** `crm-settings.test.tsx` covers enabling, typed disabling, the read-only member view, customizing, renaming, and deleting.

## Coordination

- The page is still the single `Crm` export from `views/crm-settings.tsx` with no required props, so the work to open CRM settings inside the Customers pane can mount it unchanged.
- #8045 (draft, email consent) replaces the enablement section with email-sharing settings. `CrmEnablementSection` is still self-contained, so that rebase deletes and replaces one component. The page description and the `DealStagesSection` → `StagesSection` rename will cause small conflicts.

## Follow-ups

- The backend still stores and prunes `closed_stage_ids`, plus the `move_closed_deals_role` and `delete_records_role` thresholds. The app enforces none of them. Dropping them is a separate backend change.
- The `canMoveClosedDeals` and `canDeleteRecords` capabilities have been unused since #7787. I left them alone here.
- Pipeline stages are still edited on each pipeline. Settings doesn't list pipelines.

author: jgambera
body:
## Why

"Make sure we are testing the right versions." The default is newest main, and testing a prior release is valid, but only on purpose. Twice now a stale result drove real work: an Oct 4 BrowseComp verify regression led to a feature build, and a comparison reused arms from an older commit. Until now nothing recorded which code produced a result, and `benchmarks/transfer/` had no notion of a commit.

## What changed

- **Results are stamped.** `benchmarks/run-version.ts` adds `stamped()`, which writes `marina: {commit, dirty, describe}` read once per process from local git. Dirty counts tracked files only, so the results a run writes do not make it dirty. It is wired into:
  - `resultForDisk`, so every harness result: short-answer, FRAMES, HLE and the rest
  - each BrowseComp-Plus `evals/run_N_eval.json` file and the BrowseComp-Plus result (a resume across commits shows up as mixed)
  - FutureX `score.json` and `summary.json` (clean-run and the `futurex` script)
  - ForecastBench/Metaculus `selection.json`
  - `arena evaluate --out` reports

  `arena shadow paired-score` is deliberately left unstamped: it scores forecasts made earlier, so the scoring commit is not the code that produced them.
- **Ledger runs carry the stamp, with no migration.** `ledgerFromHarnessResult` stores it in `config_json.marina` and leaves it out of both `config_hash` and `stableResultHash`, so re-filing a run is still a no-op. Stamps reach the ledger from the `/v1/benchmarks/runs` filing body, the FutureX and forecasting backtest runs, and in-world runs (through the harness file). A FutureX rescore of saved answers records `marina: null`, because this process did not produce them. In-world runs also already name their code in `target_json.source`, and the reader uses that.
- **Reading and reporting.** Adapters have a new `versions(source)` method (default: the file or directory stamps; FutureX reads `score.json`; BrowseComp reads each query file; the ledger reads per-run stamps). The transfer report adds a "Commits (baseline / candidate)" column and labels the version rule in the header. The inventory shows each variant's commits and marks each pair `same commit`, `MIXED commits` or `commit unknown`.
- **The guard is strict by default** (`benchmarks/transfer/versions.ts`, `checkVersions`, pure apart from an injected `GitInfo`).
  - Every source of both arms must come from one clean commit.
  - Mixed commits, including across one arm's replicates, make the suite `version-mismatch`.
  - An unstamped or dirty source, or a declared tag that does not resolve, makes it `version-unknown`.
  - Either way the suite is reported with what the statistics alone said, but it is excluded from the two-group verdict, as an improvement *and* as a regression. The verdict reason names it.
  - When the shared commit is behind `origin/main` the report warns (`git rev-list --count`, local only, no network).
- **Deliberate prior-release tests.** A spec, or a single suite, can declare `versions: {baseline: "<sha|tag>", candidate: "<sha|tag>"}`. Each arm must then match its own ref (a resolved sha, a sha prefix, or a stamp whose `describe` is the tag). The suite is `version-comparison` and the report header says "Version comparison (declared)". No behind-main warning is given, since the old version is intended.
- **`--allow-unversioned`** lets old unstamped files count as `unversioned`, under a WARNING banner in the report and on stderr. It never hides mixed commits among the stamped sources, and it never admits dirty ones.

No env vars, no migration, no new dependencies.

## Release impact

Operator-visible behaviour change in `eval:transfer`: existing result files have no stamp, so a spec over them now reports `version-unknown` (exit 2, not counted) until they are rerun on current code, or until `--allow-unversioned` is passed deliberately. The CHANGELOG has an Unreleased/Added entry.

## Verification

- [x] `bun run test` passes (9312 pass, 4 skip, 0 fail)
- [x] `bun run typecheck` passes
- [x] `bun run lint` passes
- [x] Tests added/updated: new `test/eval-versions.test.ts` (injected git throughout; nothing paid). It covers:
  - stamping and `resultForDisk`, ledger filing body, git reader
  - per-record, directory, ledger `config_json` and source-revision stamps
  - `config_hash` and stable hash unchanged by a stamp
  - same commit with the behind-main warning, mixed/unstamped/dirty, allow-unversioned
  - declared sha/tag comparisons, a mismatched arm, an unresolvable tag
  - a mismatched suite dropping out of the verdict (improvement and regression)
  - Markdown labels, spec validation, the inventory commits column and pair status
  - the CLI exiting 2 on unstamped files and 0 with `--allow-unversioned`

  The existing transfer CLI test's fixtures are now stamped.
- [x] CHANGELOG `[Unreleased]` entry
- [x] Docs: `benchmarks/README.md` (Transfer report → "Test the right versions"), `docs/architecture/benchmarks.md`, `docs/guides/scripts.md` (CLI reference), and one CLAUDE.md key-file line
- [x] No credentials, databases or private data

author: cramforce
body:
First half of scope-B milestone NI-1 (Node islands): the runtime loads Node.js into the scriptc process the first time a program calls into it, from a prebuilt libnode pack. The second half, the `@scriptc/node` call API and its tests, is the stacked PR on top of this one.

### What changes

- **`scr_node_island.c`** (new optional runtime unit) dlopens the bridge library of a libnode pack on the first call, with `RTLD_NOW | RTLD_GLOBAL`. It checks the bridge ABI and that the bridge links exactly the Node version recorded at build time, starts one Node environment and runs the embedded bootstrap (`scr_node_island_host.cjs`, embedded as `scr_node_island_host.h` by `scripts/node-island-host.mjs`). A run that never calls into Node never maps libnode.
- **`scr_node_bridge.h`** is the C ABI between the runtime and the bridge. The runtime includes no Node or V8 header.
- **The bridge** (`packages/libnode-common/bridge/scr_node_bridge.cc`) is built against one exact Node release and ships next to libnode in its pack. It:
  - initializes Node once, without default signal handling, the debug-signal handler, the inspector or stdio reinitialization, and with one platform worker thread;
  - creates the environment from Node's built-in snapshot;
  - routes Node's process exit (`process.exit`, uncaught exceptions) to scriptc's exit sequence;
  - promotes libnode to the global scope so native addons resolve `napi_*`;
  - runs each call in a `CallbackScope` with a nested `TryCatch`.
- **`build-pack.mjs`** assembles a pack (libnode, the bridge, `manifest.json`, Node's license) from a Node `--shared` build and the matching headers. Published `@scriptc/libnode-<platform>` packs are milestone NI-13. Until then a pack is found through `SCRIPTC_LIBNODE` or `--libnode`.
- **The `SCR_NODE_ISLANDS` build of `scr_async.c`** adds one loop slot. Until NI-3 moves scriptc's queues onto Node's libuv, scriptc's loop drives Node's through this slot: the program stays alive while Node has ref'd work, the loop sleeps on Node's backend fd up to Node's next timer, and each loop turn runs one non-blocking turn of Node's loop.
- **Compiler plumbing:**
  - the `nodeIsland` runtime feature: rule, link features, unit table, pack matrix row and the `scr_async.c` variant;
  - the `nodeIsland.call` and `nodeIsland.callSync` libCalls;
  - `scr_node_island_install(pack, version)` in main;
  - `node-islands/libnode.ts`, which records the pack: `--libnode=<pack dir>|beside`, or `SCRIPTC_LIBNODE` at build time. It reports SC8005 when no pack is usable and requires Node >= 24.13.1.
- **Zero-cost enforcement:** the zero-cost gate and the bench `nm` test now require that no good-code executable defines a Node island symbol.

### Locating Node, and bundling it

`SCRIPTC_LIBNODE` overrides the recorded pack directory at run time. A recorded path that starts with `$ORIGIN/` resolves against the directory of the running executable. PATH is never searched, and a pack of another Node version or bridge ABI is a fatal error at first use, never a silent fallback.

`--libnode=beside` copies the pack next to the executable as `<output>.libnode/` and records `$ORIGIN/<output>.libnode`, so the program and its Node travel together. This is the first form of shipping Node with the program, which the maintainer asked the design to support. The `$ORIGIN` hook is also what the default `embedded` packaging (NI-4) will use: the pack's compressed libnode and bridge are appended to the executable and extracted on first use to `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/scriptc/node-islands/<hash>/`, recorded as a cache-relative path. The same pack serves as the in-process backend, as the bundled Node, and as the build-time probe environment (DESIGN §2.13, §2.16.4). No `node` executable is ever shipped or required.

### Zero cost

Programs without a `nodeIsland.*` libCall are unchanged:

- no new unit is linked;
- the plain `scr_async.c` object is selected (the variant code is entirely under `#ifdef SCR_NODE_ISLANDS`, so the default object is byte-identical);
- main gains no line.

**Zero-cost gate** (`scripts/zero-cost-gate.mjs --set=bench,self,corpus --corpus=all --timing-runs=3`, Linux Vercel Sandbox, baseline `0237d70df`): 3541 of 3542 programs produced byte-identical IR, LLVM and release executables. In the remaining program, `corpus/fs-extra-package`, the LLVM and the executable are identical. Its IR differs only in source locations inside the fs-extra shim (`packages/compiler/shims/fs-extra`), which record each checkout's absolute path (`/vercel/sandbox/prev/...` against `/vercel/sandbox/cand/...`). That difference comes from the gate setup, not from this change. Compile time: bench geomean −0.68% [95% CI −2.06%, +0.99%]; the self-hosted compiler +0.27%. Both are within tolerance. The bench `nm` test passes, and no executable links a Node island symbol.

### Tests

- Unit tests: pack recording (`libnode.test.ts`) and the host header's freshness (`node-island-host.test.ts`).
- End-to-end evidence is in the stacked PR, which adds the API: differential corpus programs against Node 24 run as binaries that load libnode (plain and sanitized lanes), plus harness tests for loading on first use, beside packaging, a missing pack, mismatched versions, and the executable's symbols.

Not yet covered: macOS has no libnode pack yet (NI-13). Process-state integration, signal routing and the hosted loop are NI-3.

body:
**Upfront about how this was made:** I'm not a programmer. The change, the test and this description were written by Claude (Claude Code, Opus 5.5), on Windows 11.

Closes #1012.

## The request

In PowerPoint, holding the left mouse button during a slide show shows the laser dot for as long as it's held, and letting go doesn't advance. In DeckCraft, the laser needed Ctrl+L or the on-screen button, which is awkward with a mouse or clicker in hand.

## The change

In the slide show, pressing the left button on the slide and holding it for 0.3 s shows the laser dot in the show's laser colour. The dot follows the pointer and leaves no ink. Letting go hides it, and that release is not a click, so the slide doesn't advance and no build or trigger runs. A quicker click advances exactly as before.

The hold only applies where a click on the slide would: not with the pen (it keeps drawing), not with the Ctrl+L laser already on, and not on See All Slides, a black or white screen, a zoom, the reading-view bar or the media controls. The dot also appears if the pointer doesn't move during the hold.

The pieces of the request I left out:
- the setting to turn the gesture off
- long-press on touch
- the dot in Presenter View and on recordings

Presenter View and recordings are close to #636, which is still open.

## Testing

- New UI test `show::tests::holding_the_left_button_shows_the_laser_without_advancing` (egui_kittest, real pointer events):
  - a quick click advances
  - a hold shows nothing before 0.3 s and the dot after it, and letting go hides the dot without advancing
  - with the pen on, a hold shows no dot and doesn't advance

  With the hold detection switched off it fails: no dot appears.
- `cargo xtask ci` passes locally on Windows 11: fmt, pdf-deps, clippy, tests, assets, layers and wasm.

author: thijsvanessen
body:
A123, P7 of the transposition-table study (`~/Development/audit2/opvolging-bronnen.md`; decision 27). Transposition tables whose columns of articles stand in groups are now read. Before, a head with more than two columns of articles placed nothing (`columns not recognised`). The rows go through the same path as the rest (`core/succession.place`). Nothing is filled in by hand.

## What

- **A column of leden beside a column of articles** (`artikel WVO | lid/onderdeel`, kst-35297-3). The cell names the leden of the article beside it, e.g. `lid 1 t/m 3 en 5`. A remark in brackets, like `(deels)` or `(1e volzin)`, is no lid. On the old side the cell is the part as written (`from`). On the new side it is checked against the new law's leden (`no_lid`).
- **One proposed law's column beside several old laws' columns** (`artikel WVO | … | artikel WVO-BES | … | artikel WVO 20xx | …`): one table per old law. The same holds for the table back. This applies only when each old column names its law.
- **One column of articles that names no law, beside several that do, under a title that names the old regulation** (Invoeringsbesluit Omgevingswet, Stb. 2020, 400: `b. Transponeringstabel Bouwbesluit 2012` over `Artikel | Artikel Omgevingswet | Artikel AMvB`). The reader makes a table from the old regulation to each column.
  - A column whose cells mostly name their law at the end (`1.1 Bbl`, `2.13 Bal en 8.28 Bkl`) holds places in several laws. It gives one table per law its cells name (`law_parts`).
  - Cells with a figure that name no law go to one table under the column's name (`AMvB`). That table places nothing and is noted.
- **A law at the end of a cell** is now also read after a part (`4.834, eerste lid Bal`). A roman numeral, a single capital or a division word is not a law (`5.4 Bijlage VII`, `bijlage X Bkl` → Bkl). Titles `aa.`/`cc.` count as table labels.
- **Laws by name.** A name is resolved by its citation title first, then by its abbreviation (`code_choices`: the WTI's short titles and abbreviations, plus the curated ones, including one that several laws share), then by the citation extractor. The extractor match must cover the whole name. Before, `WVO-BES` read as `WVO` and `Waterleidingwet of Waterleidingbesluit` as the Waterleidingwet. When a proposed law's table finds several old laws of one name, the reader takes the one that had not expired when the new law came into force. Example: the WVO BES has two BWB ids, BWBR0028424 (expired 2011) and BWBR0030284.
- **"No row" once per old law.** When an old law has tables to several new laws, an article no table names is now one gap, counted in the pair that places the most. Before, it was counted in every pair (the Activiteitenbesluit has five).
- Docs: `pipelines.md` (semantic tk-transposition-tables), plus the module docstrings.

## Measured

Command: `lawgraph succession-gaps` on a test DB on 5433 (`lawgraph_a123_tables`). It is a copy of `lawgraph_a81_tables`, plus the current BWB toestanden of WVO, both WVO BES ids and WVO 2020. It also has the 33 old and new regulations of Stb. 2020, 400, all except Brzo 2015, whose BWB id was not found. "Before" is origin/develop 2ef7d586, which includes #879. "After" is this branch, on the same DB.

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| the 38 pairs of laws that were already read | 817 gaps | 817 (every pair identical) |
| WVO → WVO 2020 (kst-35297-3) | places nothing | 246 old articles placed in 307, 173 gaps |
| WVO BES → WVO 2020 | places nothing | 187 placed in 254, 108 gaps |
| Stb. 2020, 400 (simulated: stored as if P8/A124 had fetched it) | 29 tables place nothing | 75 pairs (29 old AMvBs → Ow, Bal, Bbl, Bkl, Ob, Or), 513 gaps, 27 notes (19 `AMvB` remainders, Brzo 2015 not in the DB, `OW` without WTI aliases in this DB) |

WVO gaps by kind: 84 `no_new_article` (WVO 2020 was renumbered after the bill: 7.45–7.64 and 2.28 do not exist as enacted), 78 `no_old_article` (41b, 41k, 85a… were repealed before 2022; prod has `bwb-history`, so most become historical identities there), 54 `no_row`, 20 unreadable (`12.*` ×19: "chapter 12", which stays a gap), 8 `no_lid`.

Reader check over all 63 stored Kamerstukken plus Stb. 2020, 400: every table reads exactly as on develop, except the two WVO tables, the Stb tables, and one row change in kst-29359-3 (`54 lid 1 sub d BBA` now names law BBA; that table places nothing either way). The Sv/Ow guard (`transposition_xml_rows_sv_ow.json`) is unchanged.

## Tests

- Red on develop, green here:
  - 3 unit tests: WVO groups, Invoeringsbesluit per new law, one no-row gap per old law.
  - 1 integration test (`test_a_column_per_old_law_with_its_leden`): edges with the leden from the lid column, WVO BES of 2011 chosen, `12.*` reported.
- Real excerpts, cut from the source XML:
  - `kst_35297_3_excerpt.xml`: 11 rows of the forward table and 4 of the back table, plus the dossier title.
  - `stb_2020_400_excerpt.xml`: tables a and b, with rows `2.13 Bal en 8.28 Bkl` and `2.17, 4.1136 en 4.1137`.
- mypy src: clean (502 files). ruff: clean.
- Unit tests, on the files this change touches plus tests/conventions: 4,354 passed.
- Serially on 5433: `tests/integration/test_transposition_tables.py` and `tests/integration/test_eu_concordance.py`, 13 passed.

## Rollback

No schema change, no new raw kind, no step 0, no schema_drift. Every run derives the edges in full. After a rollback, a run of that release's `semantic tk-transposition-tables` removes the WVO edges again.

## After deploy (prod, go from Thijs)

`lawgraph semantic tk-transposition-tables`, then `lawgraph succession-gaps` for the counts. kst-35297-3 is a stored Kamerstuk, so the WVO tables are read right away. The Stb. 2020, 400 tables are read only once P8 (A124) stores the Staatsblad source; the reader already handles them.

The Python 3.9–3.13 matrix and live API checks remain enabled.

- Both workflows pass actionlint 1.7.12.

The recent [Run Tests failure](https://github.com/SootyOwl/yt-transcript-fetcher/actions/runs/25472830473) reached the test step successfully. body:
Connections to large or elongated target facets could fail, or bind to a farther facet, when nearby centroid cells excluded the true nearest triangle. Search a balanced triangle-bounds tree for the globally nearest target within the existing tolerance. Closest-point calculations, shape functions, units, and the penalty formulation are preserved.

Six regressions cover large and elongated facets, distractors, farther in-tolerance candidates, edge/vertex projections, tolerance boundaries, deterministic ties, and 288 generated queries checked against an independent exhaustive geometric oracle at three scales. A 4,096-facet test bounds projection work to small tree leaves.

- All 17 current repository-required commands pass on Node 22.23.3, including ESLint, 160 CPU tests, and 1,481 root tests (one optional skip).

author: dastinovds
body:
Closes #317

**Статус.** Сделано: всё из issue и мелочи владельца от 2026-10-21, CI зелёный. Осталось: мерж. Следующий шаг: squash-мерж и закрытие #317.

### Что сделано
- **Симуляция (DEC-30, `SIM_VERSION` 16 → 17).** У группы счётчик `Group.ticks_in_defense`. Его обнуляют `SetMode(DEFENSE)`, выход из режима (`SetMode(ATTACK)`, `CancelOrder`, `Move`) и вступление в бой (`combat._join`). Система `orders` в конце тика прибавляет 1 группе в «Защите», которая стоит в узле не в бою. Бонус боя `OrderRules.defense_bonus(ticks, charged) = min(ticks // defense_ticks_per_bonus, charged)` считает `active_bonuses(state, rules)` в тике контакта. `Group.bonus` теперь только бонус плана. Слияние сохраняет счётчик целевой группы, новая группа после деления в «Атаке» со счётчиком 0.
- **Рулсеты** `mvp-0`, `mvp-1`, `test-short`, а также тестовые `dec07` и `siege`: добавлен `orders.defense_ticks_per_bonus = 60`, сняты `orders.defense_delay_ticks` и `orders.defense_bonus`, комментарии поправлены.
- **Протокол (`PROTOCOL_VERSION` 19 → 20).** Добавлены `GroupView.defense_bonus` (накопленное с потолком, то есть бонус боя, начавшегося сейчас) и `GroupView.defense_cap` (потолок: заряженные юниты), оба `null` вне «Защиты»; валидатор модели это проверяет. В `ruleset_public.orders` поле `defense_delay_ticks` заменено на `defense_ticks_per_bonus`, `combat.defense_bonus` снят. Перегенерированы схема и `protocol.gen.ts` (`api.gen.ts` не изменился), поправлены фикстуры.
- **Туман.** Чужая группа показывает только режим. Тест `test_dec30_the_gathered_defense_of_the_enemy_is_hidden` (уровни PRESENCE и EXACT); в property-тест `_hide` добавлен случайный счётчик чужой «Защиты».
- **Тесты.** `packages/sim/tests/test_dec30.py`: таблица примеров DEC-30 (строки 1-7, ожидаемые значения из mechanics.md) и детали (рост в бою, сброс при выходе из режима, повторное включение, деление, слияние). DEC-08, DEC-20 и векторы боя переведены на накопление: «Защита» (+2) в векторах означает 120 тиков в режиме.
- **Боты.** `defender_pool` и `shots_to_take` принимают число, а не флаг: оценку накопленного противником сверху, `(tick - created_tick намерения) // 60`, с потолком по заряженным (`Bot.defended`). `ReactiveBot` включает «Защиту» в ответ на видимый план, только если к самому раннему прибытию удара она накопит хотя бы +1 (Дейкстра по `travel_ticks` карты при самой быстрой скорости рельефа). `fortify` у тактических ботов больше не включает «Защиту» повторно. `lint-imports` чист.
- **Клиент (минимум для сборки, остальное в #318).** Снята дуга задержки «Защиты» (задержки больше нет), литералы `GroupView` дополнены новыми полями.
- **mechanics.md.** Детали DEC-30 пп. 1-6 и DEC-31 пп. 7-8 переведены в [принято] (2026-10-21). Для DEC-30 добавлен абзац «Как это считает симуляция», обновлены строки DEC-30 и DEC-31 в разделе 21. Сделаны пометки DEC-30 у примеров 10 и 16 таблицы DEC-07 и у DEC-20 п. A4.
- **Решения владельца 2026-10-21.** `compose.yaml` и образ `app` теперь по умолчанию на `rulesets/mvp-1.toml`. `mise run tournament` по умолчанию на `mvp-1`. В AGENTS.md (раздел 3, строка `tournament`; раздел 8) записано, что дымовые турниры агентов идут только на `mvp-1`, а `mvp-0` остаётся тестовым рулсетом. README, `docs/qa/manual-match.md` и `docs/balance/README.md` поправлены. Устаревшая фраза «дорога, казарма и склад занимают одну стройку» в `[city_upgrades]` обоих рулсетов исправлена: по коду `CITY_BUSY` проверяет только `city.build` (казарма и склад), дорога строится на ребре (`EDGE_BUSY`).
- **Золотые реплеи** `packages/sim/tests/golden/v17/` и архив трёх новых рулсетов.

### Турнир ботов (`mvp-1`, 10 seeds, все карты и боты, 1470 матчей)
`mise run tournament -- --seeds 10` на этой ветке; для сравнения тот же турнир на `origin/develop` (`SIM_VERSION` 16, `--ruleset rulesets/mvp-1.toml`).

| | develop (`SIM_VERSION` 16) | эта ветка (17) |
|---|---|---|
| причины конца | capital 177, double_defeat 4, draw 81, vp 1208 | то же |
| средняя длина партии | 829.5 с (медиана 900) | 829.5 с (медиана 900) |
| win-rate против других | expander 0.50, idle 0.00, random_legal 0.18, reactive 0.79, rusher 0.90, strangler 0.81, turtle 0.33 | то же |
| сторона 0, все матчи | 0.49 [0.46; 0.51] | 0.49 [0.46; 0.51] |
| успех осад reactive / rusher / strangler | 0.92 / 0.85 / 0.89 | 0.92 / 0.85 / 0.89 |

Финальные состояния различаются во всех 1470 матчах (в состоянии новое поле, ход боёв меняется), но **победитель совпал во всех 1470**; захваты за матч отличаются в сотых. Вывод: текущие боты почти не опираются на «Защиту», поэтому значение 60 турнир не различает. Баланс `defense_ticks_per_bonus` вне рамок, его надо проверять после умных ботов (#282).

### Критерии приёмки
- [x] Таблица примеров DEC-30 покрыта тестами с ожидаемыми значениями из mechanics.md (`test_dec30.py`, строки 1-7).
- [x] Тест тумана на поле накопленного бонуса; тесты зеркальности и детерминизма зелёные.
- [x] Турнир ботов и отчёт в PR (выше).

### Отклонения, вопросы, новые зависимости
- `SetMode(DEFENSE)` группе, которая уже стоит в «Защите», теперь отклоняется `NO_CHANGE` (раньше разрешалось и снова стоило 2 CP). Повторное включение только обнулило бы накопленное, а после боя накопление идёт заново само. Записано в абзаце «Как это считает симуляция» блока DEC-30.
- Клиент тронут минимально (типы и дуга задержки), чтобы job `web` собирался; отображение бонуса остаётся за #318.
- Новых зависимостей нет.

### Definition of Done
- [x] Все критерии приёмки issue выполнены и отмечены в PR.
- [x] CI зелёный: `py` (с `test:perf`), `web`, `docker`, `e2e`, `py-slow`, `visual`. Локально зелёные `check`, `test`, `test:slow`, `golden:check`, `build`. `test:perf` локально красный при load average 35 (машина занята другими агентами; падает и `supply`, который PR не трогает); решает job `py`.
- [x] Новые правила покрыты тестами с ожидаемыми значениями из mechanics.md.
- [x] Версии повышены, артефакты перегенерированы.

- [x] В коде нет `TODO` без номера issue.

## O que muda

- **Bug corrigido:** ao publicar, o servidor validava `data + horário` das atividades com `new Date("AAAA-MM-DDTHH:MM")`, que usa o fuso de quem executa. No servidor (UTC) isso deslocava as atividades 3h para trás, então atividades válidas (ex.: check-in 08:30 num evento que começa 08:00 de Brasília) eram recusadas como "fora do período". author: abdulrhmanbashniny-jpg
body:
Adds the **paint craftsman platform** (منصة معلمي الدهانات · Paint Masters), a B2B2C platform for the Saudi paint trade, as a third independent app in `craft/` (Next.js 16 + PostgreSQL/Drizzle, the same stack as `platform/`). It markets the craftsmen, and markets the paint factory that runs it. It is Arabic-first RTL with full English and works as an installable PWA. Nothing in `/` or `platform/` changes apart from one row in the root README.

**Live demo:** https://paint-masters-three.vercel.app. The login code is shown on screen until an SMS provider is connected.

The architecture is in **[craft/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md](craft/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md)**: data schema, `/api/v1` contracts, anti-fraud, PDPL and milestones.

## What's in it

- **Design:** rebuilt on the owner's Stitch screens: navy and amber Material tokens, IBM Plex Sans Arabic + Space Grotesk, a sidebar shell for the craftsman app and the console. Pages follow the matching screens:
  - landing with a sign-up card
  - public profile
  - craftsman dashboard
  - console overview
- **Membership card:** works as an ID card: the craftsman's photo, name, classification, member number and tier, plus a QR that opens his public profile.
  - The craftsman adds his photo with crop and zoom, and can remove it. Staff can remove it from the console.
  - The card downloads as a PNG with correct Arabic shaping.
  - Member numbers carry a **Damm check digit**.
- **Portfolio:** each craftsman shows **up to 3 works**. Each work is one photo or video, plus an optional "before" photo for a comparison slider, and can be tagged with the factory products used.
- **Factory marketing:** a product catalogue and factory identity managed from the console (`/admin/products`), shown on the landing page and on each work.
- **Reviews:** client reviews, moderated in the console (`/admin/reviews`).
- **Public profile `/c/{code}`:** tier and verification badges, trust score, a live verification seal, the 3 works, reviews and a paint estimator. Phone numbers never appear in page HTML.
- **Sign-up funnel:** the landing card prefills login and onboarding (city, district, declared classification, referral code).
- **Invoices:** camera scan, ZATCA TLV QR decoding, Phase 2 signature checks against known dealer keys, an AI reading of the photo, and risk scoring.
  - Auto-approval requires all of the following; anything else goes to a review queue:
    - a valid signature from a known key;
    - the AI reading confirms both total and date;
    - the account is under the velocity cap.
  - A processing lease stops double claims.
- **Points:** an append-only ledger with idempotency keys and row locks, tier multipliers, campaigns, referral commissions (welcome bonuses held while a referral is under review) and a rewards store.
- **Console `/admin`:** KPIs and trends, a density map, the invoice review queue, craftsman management, verification, a fraud monitor, incentives, rewards, dealers, reports and settings.
  - Four-eyes rules: staff cannot review their own work or adjust their own points.
  - Every action is audit-logged.
- **Security/PDPL:**
  - Atomic rate limits and trusted client-IP resolution.
  - Per-phone OTP limits and a daily ceiling.
  - Open-redirect-safe `next` handling.
  - Encrypted IDs and voucher codes.
  - Private invoice images; uploads checked server-side.

## Deployment

- **Vercel:** project `paint-masters` (root directory `craft`, functions in `fra1`, Node 22). The build runs `db:migrate` and an idempotent `db:seed`, then `next build`.
- **Database:** Postgres is a separate `paint_masters` database with its own role on the existing Supabase server. That role has no access to the other database there. The app reaches it through the transaction pooler.

## How it was checked

- `npm run typecheck` is clean, `npm test` passes (66 tests, including secp256k1 signing and the new security cases), and `next build` passes.
- A fresh clone of the branch ran the whole Vercel build script (migrate, seed, build) against an empty database.
- On the live site, phone login through the real UI worked for the demo craftsman and the admin. The landing page, profile, dashboard, card, portfolio, console and products pages all returned 200 with no page errors.
- Ran against PostgreSQL 16 with the demo seed. These were checked end to end with Playwright:
  - the photo upload, crop and remove, and the card PNG download;
  - the sign-up funnel from the landing card to a new craftsman with a pending referral.
- Screenshot checks against the Stitch screens: desktop and 390px phone width.

## Not in this milestone

- An SMS provider (Unifonic or Twilio). Until one is connected, the login code is shown on screen (`ALLOW_DEV_OTP`).
- Production media storage (S3/R2). Media is currently stored in the database, with a 4.4MB upload limit.
- An AI key for invoice photo reading. Without it, invoices go to manual review.
- A deeper restyle of the secondary pages (invoices, rewards, referrals, console lists). They use the new tokens and shell.
- Apple Wallet, Nafath, dealer and brand portals, HLS video and points expiry (architecture doc §8).

author: rvolosatovs
body:
Switch the ledger from `wrpc-pack` to `pack_ready`/`unpack` in
  `wrpc-transport`, pinning wrpc to `main` at a1ad72ea:

  - bytecodealliance/wrpc#1553 moves `wrpc-pack` into `wrpc-transport`.
    `pack` is now async there, so packed values can contain futures and
    streams.
  - bytecodealliance/wrpc#1555 adds `pack_ready`, a synchronous `pack`. It
    fails with `WouldBlock` if any asynchronous value is still pending.

  Nothing the ledger packs (transactions, genesis outputs, `/rpc` results)
  contains futures or streams, so every call site uses `pack_ready`, and
  `Ledger::new` stays synchronous. The `wrpc-pack` dependency is dropped.

  `wrpc-wave` renames `WaveEncoder` to `ValueEncoder`, and `read_value` is
  now generic over the value type, so the CLI asks for
  `wasm_wave::value::Value` explicitly.

author: poyrazk
body:
## Milestone

ADR-566 cost controls, follow-ups to #4885. This PR combines four branches: the strict-budget release flag, budget alert delivery, object storage in budgets, and strict project and environment caps.

## What

- **Strict budgets released per account** (ADR-1750 release gate). The new `strict_budgets` platform flag (ADR-1700) is off until an operator writes it. apid refuses to create or enable a strict budget for an account the flag excludes, returning 422 `financial_budget_activation_unavailable`. A strict budget that is already enabled stays editable, and disabling or deleting one is never gated.
- **Budget alerts on notification channels** (ADR-20261019193500). You can bind up to 5 Slack, PagerDuty or email channels to a budget with `PUT /v1/billing/budgets/{id}/channels` or `gregale billing budgets channels`; the SDKs support it too. meterd delivers each alert to each channel through a fenced, retried outbox and abandons it after 12 attempts. Money text is exact millicents, and one PagerDuty incident covers each budget-month.
- **Projected-overrun alerts** (same ADR). Each monitored evaluation projects month-end spend from run-rate forecasts. When the projection reaches the limit while known spend is below it, meterd sends one warning per policy revision and month. These alerts never stop a workload.
- **Ledger dual run** (ADR-20261019193600). meterd compares the ledger's compute quantity with provider receipts for each paid account. The comparison is read-only and publishes metrics only.
- **Object storage in budgets** (ADR-20261020160000). apid records each account's live object-storage estimate every 5 minutes, and the cost report adds an account-level `object_storage` meter priced exactly like month close. Monitored account budgets can select it; strict budgets cannot.
- **Strict project caps** (ADR-1750, amendment 1). `scope={kind:project}` gives every app in the project one shared gross book. A denial holds the whole project. Activation needs a quiet project. Jobs are not covered.
- **Strict environment caps** (ADR-1750, amendment 2). `scope={kind:environment}` gives every deployment that runs in the environment one shared book, across the project's apps.
  - Environment lookup: a deployment counts toward its recorded runtime environment, else the project environment with the same name. vmmd passes the wake's `DeploymentID` in-process, so there is no RPC change. An attempt that names no deployment fails closed while any environment of its project is capped.
  - Holds: a held environment stops only its own deployments, at the gateway, scheduler and app-command checks. Calls that name no deployment, such as service-proxy calls, are not held at the gateway; acquire and renewal still bound them.
  - Floors: capacity floors are app-wide, so environment caps neither count nor waive them.
  - Owner capability: nodes now record whether their vmmd enforces project and environment caps (`scope_compute_incarnation`). Older vmmd nodes get no strict work, which also closes this version-skew gap for project caps.

## Fix for main's route insight migration (#5115)

`20261020161647152_route_insight_alerts.sql` skipped creating `route_insight_alert_metric_base` when *any* schema had one (`pg_proc` filtered by `proname` only), then called it unqualified. Up keeps the helper for rollback. In a database shared by per-test schemas, every schema after the first therefore failed with 42883, so the `S3 multipart integrity` PostgreSQL tests failed on every PR that runs them. The check now uses `to_regprocedure('route_insight_alert_metric_base(text)')`, which resolves the helper the same way its callers do.

This edits an issued migration, by explicit decision. A single-schema production database behaves as before; the only change is to the existence check. The migration is already marked `contract`, so the release that includes it is a full release.

## CI repairs while landing

- The object-storage migration now guards `financial_budget_policies_spec_v2_check` with a `pg_constraint` check, so replaying it succeeds.
- `pkg/alertchannels`: kept both `Message.Notes` (main) and `Summary`/`Severity`/`IdempotencyKey`/`Footer` (this PR). PagerDuty summaries also carry the notes.
- `nilerr`: the scope lookups check UUIDs with `validUUID` instead of returning nil after a parse error.
- gofmt on one billing test.

## Spec / ADR impact

- ADR: ADR-1750 (release gate, amendments 1 and 2), ADR-20261019193500, ADR-20261019193600, ADR-20261020160000
- Migrations (all `expand`): `financial_budget_channels`, `financial_object_storage_estimates`, budget meter CHECK widening (add NOT VALID, validate, drop old), `financial_compute_scope_books` plus the owner capability column.
- Production: strict budgets stay off until `strict_budgets` is written. Native KVM acceptance is still required before releasing them to an account.

## Verification

Run locally on the merged head:

- Gates: memstore-stubs, env-contract, runbook-sql, migration-version-hygiene, migration-expand-contract, teststorecheck, migrations-check, generate-check, spec-check, sdk-check, sqlc-check, migration digest, ADR uniqueness and docs-links all pass.
- `schema.sql` regenerated from migrations on a scratch database matches the committed file.
- Type-check passes: 520 packages, 0 errors.
- `go test ./pkg/state/financialtest` passes on the merged head: the full suite on both the memory and Postgres stores, 2,260 s.
- On their own branches before combining, these passed: `pkg/state` financial and clone-registry tests, `pkg/sched` financial and budget tests (Postgres included), `pkg/fcvm`, `pkg/meter`, `pkg/billing`, `pkg/financial` and `pkg/apid/financialbudgets`. A local re-run on the merged head was stopped because the machine ran low on memory, so CI is the check for those on this head.
- Not run locally: `make lint` (golangci-lint), `make test-metal` and the native acceptance runbooks. CI covers lint.

author: jpduchesne
body:
Implements [dev#275](https://github.com/d3mlabs/dev/issues/275) under [ADR-0008](https://github.com/d3mlabs/dev/blob/main/docs/DECISIONS.md#adr-0008--a-data-root-belongs-to-a-build-host): the Mac's build container is a build host and owns its data root.

## What changes

- **Two named volumes replace the data-root bind mount.** `BuildContainer` mounts `dev-data-root:/var/lib/dev` and `dev-linuxbrew:/home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew` on every run (one-shot and service), `docker volume create`-ing both first (idempotent). Nothing of the host's `~/.dev` is mounted. Docker initialises an empty volume from the image's content and ownership at the mount point, so against `ue5.8-3` (builder-owned mount points) both come up writable with no chown in dev. The `/project` bind mount stays until dev#192.
- **Inside is a host.** `Registry` loses the `HOST`/`CONTAINER`/`BOTH` scope axis and `container_integrations`; `dev deps install` runs `host_integrations` on every build host and excludes nothing by default (the `--except build` default is gone). Dated note under ADR-0008 records that ADR-0002's axis collapsed with the shared root.
- **Linuxbrew bootstrap.** `bin/container-provision-dev.sh` installs Homebrew into the prefix volume when the image carries none (same pinned installer commit as the image bootstrap, `NONINTERACTIVE=1`, trust before tap), then proceeds as before. `docker-install-build-deps.sh` is marked superseded.
- **`GH_TOKEN` on the in-container install.** `ContainerDepsInstaller` passes the host's `gh auth token` as `-e GH_TOKEN` (injected callable, never logged; a run_env `GH_TOKEN` wins), since the container now fetches its own private releases.
- **`dev deps path`** for a tree locked to another host names that host's data root instead of suggesting `dev up`.
- **`resources.disk_gib`**: a grow-only disk floor the colima provisioner applies (`--disk` only above the VM's current size; same idle/busy rules as cpus/memory). Threaded through `EngineProvisioner`, the agent bootstrap and label contracts.
- README and in-code docs updated to state what is true now.

## Verification

Test-first throughout; full suite 2234 tests green, `srb tc` clean, rubocop clean on touched files.

Consumer follow-up (cellbound-3d: `FROM ue5.8-3` without the brew/verify layers, `disk_gib: 250`, `gh "UnrealEngine"` `host: :linux`) lands after this releases, with the cold `dev up` / warm probe / `dev package` measurements on the Mac going to plans#48's log.

author: jcelisstratton-blip
body:
**Activas desde ya** (no cambian nada visible): `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin`, `X-Frame-Options: DENY` (nadie puede incrustar la app en otro sitio) y `Permissions-Policy` sin cámara, micrófono ni ubicación (la app no los usa).

**Política de contenido (CSP) en modo solo reportar** (`CSP_ENFORZAR = false`): el navegador no bloquea nada; cada violación llega a `/api/csp`, que la escribe en los registros de Vercel como `[apriscol:csp]` sin parámetros ni tramos largos de la ruta (pueden traer tokens). La política permite lo propio, Supabase (datos y fotos firmadas) y `data:`/`blob:` (vista previa de una foto); bloquea scripts, estilos e imágenes de cualquier otro sitio, `object`, y que la app se incruste en otros sitios. `script-src`/`style-src` llevan `'unsafe-inline'` porque Next incrusta scripts en cada página; quitarlo exigiría nonces por petición, un cambio mayor. Solo en producción.

**Por qué en modo reporte primero:** una política demasiado estricta puede romper una pantalla autenticada que no puedo recorrer en local. Tras unos días de uso real sin violaciones en los registros, se cambia a `true` y bloquea de verdad.

**Verificado:** Chromium con la política en modo **bloqueante** sobre las páginas públicas (login, registro, recuperar, términos, privacidad; 1280 y 360 px): cargan, se hidratan y no hay ninguna violación. Una violación provocada llegó a `/api/csp` y quedó en el registro sin el token de la dirección. 2 pruebas nuevas, `tsc`, `lint`, `build` y `npm test` limpios.

author: ymp112
body:
# מה השינוי?
מיד אחרי חשיפת החלון נשלח `LoadLibrary`, ו-`buildLibraryCatalog` הריץ על החיבור של ה-UI isolate את שלוש שאילתות הקטלוג (ספרים, קטגוריות, מחברים). בספרייה מלאה זו חסימה של כ-60ms, ובהרצה הראשונה יותר, בדיוק כשהמשתמש מתחיל לעבוד.
עכשיו השאילתות רצות ב-isolate חד-פעמי דרך `DbReadWorker.runOnFreshIsolate`, ולכן כתיבה חיצונית עדיין ממתינה לשחרור הקובץ. הן רצות באותה טרנזקציה, על חיבור read-only עם אותם דגלים, ומחזירות אותן שורות. בזמן השהיה לכתיבה חיצונית או החלפת דור הקריאה, `DbReadWorkerSuspended` מתפשט לקורא ומבטל את בניית הקטלוג. כך לא מופעל מסלול ישיר שעלול לפתוח מחדש repository שכבר שוחרר. המסלול הישיר נשמר רק כשאין נתיב מסד.

**מדידה:** seforim.db אמיתי (7,876 ספרים, 1,423 קטגוריות). "חסימה" היא הפער הארוך ביותר בלולאת האירועים של ה-UI isolate במהלך `getLibrary`, כולל בניית העץ, שנשארה על ה-UI isolate.

| | חסימה, הרצה ראשונה | חסימה, הרצות חוזרות | זמן כולל |
|---|---|---|---|
| לפני | 91–171ms | 64–102ms | 77–198ms |
| אחרי | 45–75ms | 20–42ms | 73–189ms |

השאילתות לבדן: ישירות על החיבור הראשי 60–63ms (180ms בהרצה הראשונה), ב-isolate 58–80ms. ה-spawn עצמו לוקח 0.3ms. במסד קטן (fixture) הזמן זהה: חציון 2–3ms לפני ואחרי.

**בדיקות:**
- `test/data_providers/official_catalog_off_ui_test.dart`:
  - השורות מה-isolate זהות לשאילתות על החיבור הראשי במסד מלא, במסד מינימלי ובמסד בלי טבלאות מחברים.
  - בניית הקטלוג עובדת כשהחיבור הראשי באמצע טרנזקציה. לפני התיקון היא נכשלת (`cannot start a transaction within a transaction`), וגם במוטציה שעוקפת את ה-isolate.
- `flutter test` על test/data_providers, test/attached_libraries, test/library, test/user_content_import ועל בדיקות הקוראים: 1473 עברו. נכשלה בדיקה אחת, `book_preview_pdf_context_menu_test`, והיא נכשלת גם על dev נקי. `flutter analyze` על הקבצים ששונו: אין בעיות.

## תיקון ביטול ואימות מקומי לאחר ריבייס

- הוסרה בליעת `DbReadWorkerSuspended`, ששחררה את הקריאה מהמעקב אך הפעילה שאילתה על חיבור ראשי ישן אחרי סגירתו. מסלול הקריאה הרגיל ב-isolate נשמר.
- נוספו שתי בדיקות רגרסיה: השהיה אינה מפעילה שאילתה על חיבור ראשי בעל טרנזקציה פתוחה; סגירה תוך בניית קטלוג מבטלת את הבנייה ומשאירה את החיבור הישן סגור. נבדקו גם שינוי שם הקובץ הלוך וחזור ובנייה תקינה אחרי פתיחה מחדש.
- שתי הבדיקות נכשלו לפני התיקון ועברו אחריו. בדיקות הקטלוג הקיימות ממשיכות להוכיח שוויון שורות וקריאה מחוץ לחיבור הראשי.
- לאחר ריבייס ל־`origin/dev` (`36c64f17c3cb192245af3a8f17d368323eee8a51`), `flutter pub get --enforce-lockfile`, `flutter analyze` מלא ו־160 בדיקות ממוקדות עברו. הסוויטות: `official_catalog_off_ui`, `db_read_worker`, `database_library_provider`, `sqlite_data_provider_write_session`, `seforim_optional_tables`, `books_cache_catalog_seed`, `attached_library_catalog`, `data_repository_library_cache`.
- האימות המקומי בוצע ב־macOS; Windows לא הורץ מקומית. לא המתנו ל־CI.
- חפיפות: בעת העדכון לא נמצא PR פתוח אחר שנוגע בשני קובצי השינוי, ולכן אין חפיפות לבדיקת `merge-tree`.

## הצהרות התורם

- [x] אני מאשר שה-PR שלי עומד ב[תנאי התרומה המפורטים ב-README](https://github.com/Otzaria/otzaria/blob/dev/README.md#תנאי-תרומה-חובה-לקריאה)
- [ ] פיצ'ר חדש? — התייעצתי לפני כן (בפורום או ב-issue)
- [ ] שינוי UI? — צירפתי צילומי מסך לפני/אחרי בסוף התיאור
- [x] הרצתי `flutter analyze` על הקוד ואין שגיאות

body:
## Why

thepastaclaw reviews the whole PR range first, then each pushed commit against the findings it carries forward, and approves only when nothing is left at any severity. Most of its later-round findings sit on code written to fix the earlier ones (#1584 took 17 rounds). One review with the same model and the same rules before the push is the cheap round.

## What

- `.claude/skills/pre-review/` — a `/pre-review` skill for Claude Code. It runs GPT-6.1 "Sol" (the model of the bot's second phase) through the Codex CLI, using the bot's public review prompts (fetched at run time from a pinned commit of `thepastaclaw/skills`, not copied here), over `merge-base(origin/master, HEAD)..HEAD`. Claude then verifies each finding against the code, fixes the whole class of it on every sibling path, and reviews again.
- `prereview.sh` caches verdicts per commit (`~/.cache/prereview`). A verdict counts only for exactly that commit's range over the PR's base (`PREREVIEW_BASE`, default `origin/master`, fetched first): a base that moved means a new review.
- **Scope:** for reviewing our own branches before push — code the developer already builds and runs. It is not a sandbox for hostile branches; the isolation below is defence in depth.
- The model's commands run under a Codex permission profile and an environment allowlist: they see the review's own `--shared` clone of the commit, its borrowed object stores, the pinned prompts and the minimal system paths — not `~/.codex`, not the user's git config, no MCP servers, Apps, browser/computer use, web search or lifecycle hooks (each read back; the review refuses otherwise).
- **Opt-in push gate, per clone:** `prereview.sh --install` adds a git `pre-push` hook (a copy under `.git/hooks`) that refuses a push to dash-wallet when a pushed ref's tip has blocking findings or no review of its range. From a terminal it runs the missing review itself. From a non-interactive shell (an agent) it refuses and says to run `/pre-review`. `git push --no-verify` is the deliberate bypass.
- A short section in `CLAUDE.md`.

No wallet code changes. Nobody needs the Codex CLI unless they turn the gate on.

## How it was checked

- `test_prereview.sh`: 86 cases with a fake `codex` on `PATH`, offline. They cover cache coverage across bases, malformed counts, re-review invalidation, the per-commit lock (`flock`), interrupted reviews, annotated tags, deletions, terminal vs non-interactive pushes, install/uninstall failures, and `TMPDIR` with spaces. All pass on macOS and Linux.
- The skill reviewed its own branch with GPT-6.1 Sol: 11 rounds until clean at codex's default effort (blocking per round 4, 3, 3, 4, 2, 2, 2, 0, 1, 1, 0), then, after thepastaclaw's first review here found two more, 4 rounds at effort high (2, 2, 2, 0); after its second review (the security auditor: credentials reachable from the model's commands) 9 more rounds — each a real but smaller hole in the previous fix. That is the pattern this tool exists for, seen from the other side, so the skill now says: at most two local rounds per push, then push and let the bot judge. The review runs at effort high, the bot's own setting; every finding was verified and fixed by class.

author: cramforce
body:
Second half of scope-B milestone NI-1 (Node islands), stacked on the libnode loader PR: an explicit API for calling a JavaScript module's export in Node.js from a compiled program. It replaces the hand-written `node` subprocess that the build container's api currently patches in to parse `vercel.ts`.

```ts
import { call, callSync } from "@scriptc/node";

const sum = callSync<number>("./math.cjs", "add", 1, 2);
const config = await call<VercelConfig>("@api/vercel-config-parser", "parseVercelTsToJson", source);
```

### Semantics (the same under Node and compiled)

- The module loads with `require()` from the calling module: relative specifiers resolve from its directory, bare ones from its `node_modules`, and ES modules load through `require(esm)`. The function runs with the module namespace as `this`.
- Arguments cross as `JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(args))`. The result crosses as its JSON copy (`undefined` stays `undefined`), and scriptc checks it against the declared type like `JSON.parse(s) as T`.
- A thrown `Error` crosses as a new error of its nearest intrinsic class, with its `message` and string `code`. Other thrown values cross as JSON copies.
- `callSync` throws a `TypeError` for a function that returns a promise, and drops that promise without an unhandled rejection. `call` awaits it and rejects instead of throwing.
- The package's Node implementation (`packages/node/index.js`) applies the same copies and messages in-process, so the differential corpus is exact.

### Compiler

- `node-api-import.ts` recognizes the named imports (renamed ones too) and namespace member calls.
- `lower-node-island.ts` lowers them to the `nodeIsland.callSync` and `nodeIsland.call` libCalls. Each call carries the caller's real path, the specifier, the export name and the boxed argument array, and its result goes through the checked boundary into the declared type.
- Arguments and results whose types are not JSON data are refused at build time. So are the functions and the namespace used as values.
- The lowering marks the module, and the executable build records the libnode pack (previous PR).
- Programs that do not import `@scriptc/node` take none of these paths.

### Tests

- **Corpus** `6800-node-call-sync`, `6801-node-call-errors`, `6802-node-call-async` and `6803-node-call-exit` cover:
  - sync and async results, records, arrays, unicode, `undefined`, module state, and ES modules;
  - errors: intrinsic classes, codes, custom classes, thrown strings and objects, a missing export or module, a promise from `callSync`, an unserializable result;
  - `Promise.all` over calls, a synchronous call while asynchronous ones are pending, and calls from promise reactions;
  - Node's pending timers keeping the program alive after main returns;
  - `process.exit` in Node running the program's exit listeners and exiting with its code.

  They match Node 24 byte for byte in the plain and sanitized lanes, with libnode 24.22.0 loaded in-process. `// @requires-libnode` skips them where `SCRIPTC_LIBNODE` names no pack, because there is no published pack yet (NI-13). CI skips them until then.
- **`tests/harness/node-island.test.ts`** checks, with the same skip condition:
  - Node is mapped only after the first call, and never in a run that does not call (`/proc/self/maps`);
  - `process.exit` after Node has loaded keeps its exit code;
  - `--libnode=beside` runs without `SCRIPTC_LIBNODE`;
  - a missing pack, a pack of another Node version, and a bridge of another ABI each fail the first call with a message and exit 1;
  - the executable links no V8, Node or libuv code, and exports no symbol that libnode could bind to.
- **TS7 order baselines** are recorded for the new corpus programs.

**Zero-cost gate** (`scripts/zero-cost-gate.mjs --set=bench,self,corpus --corpus=all --timing-runs=3`, Linux Vercel Sandbox, baseline `0237d70df`): 3541 of 3542 programs produced byte-identical IR, LLVM and release executables. In the remaining program, `corpus/fs-extra-package`, the LLVM and the executable are identical. Its IR differs only in source locations inside the fs-extra shim (`packages/compiler/shims/fs-extra`), which record each checkout's absolute path (`/vercel/sandbox/prev/...` against `/vercel/sandbox/cand/...`). That difference comes from the gate setup, not from this change. Compile time: bench geomean −0.68% [95% CI −2.06%, +0.99%]; the self-hosted compiler +0.27%. Both are within tolerance. The bench `nm` test passes, and no executable links a Node island symbol.

### Not in this PR

Handles and identity for non-JSON values (NI-4/NI-5), the hosted event loop and process integration (NI-3), and published libnode packs (NI-13). Docs come with NI-11.

body:
### Related Issues

- None. This is a version bump for a security fix in the Weaviate server image used by the tests.

### Proposed Changes:

This bumps `integrations/weaviate/docker-compose.yml` from `weaviate:1.39.4` to `weaviate:1.39.13`.

Weaviate 1.39.13 is 1.39.12 rebuilt on Go 1.26.10. That Go release makes `crypto/x509` reject certificate chains that contain any of eight leaked eMudhra intermediate certificates (CVE-2026-111943, [golang/go#82345](https://github.com/golang/go/issues/82345)). It's a patch release in the same minor version, so there is no compatibility impact. This compose file is the one CI uses, and the one contributors copy to run Weaviate locally.

### How did you test it?

I ran the integration's test suites against a `1.39.13` container started with the compose file's settings:
- `hatch run test:integration`: 190 passed, 1 skipped.
- `hatch run test:unit`: 124 passed.

### Notes for the reviewer

There's no code change. Only the server image tag moves.

- I have read the [contributors guidelines](https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack-core-integrations/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) and the [code of conduct](https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack-core-integrations/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)

author: mhanavan4-prog
body:
Three interior follow-ups after the Café furnishing (#470).

## 1. Seated players face the table
The dining seat facings were set for backless benches, so sitters looked *outward* — which read as sitting backwards once the KayKit chairs gave them a visible back. North-of-table seats now look +z toward the table, south seats -z, matching which way each chair opens. Applies to both rooms that use dining sets (the Café and, as of #470, the Phantom Parlor).

## 2. "Champions' Table" banner no longer lands on the shop NPC
The banner floated at a hardcoded `(0, 95, -40)`. In the scaled 1080×612 interior frame that's the NW corner — right on top of Barkeep Joss — so walking up to it only offered *"browse the shop."* It now floats over the café's centre-front dining table, clear of every NPC. (The table is still claimed from the Coven menu; this only fixes the marker's placement.)

## 3. Town Pass statue reskinned with KayKit
Swapped the blocky procedural robed figure for a KayKit **decorated stone pillar crowned with a glowing crystal** — a proper little shrine. Pillar + gem are gating assets (loaded before spawn), so it's the normal path; the procedural figure stays as a fallback.

## Verify
- Statue rendered offline (Playwright/swiftshader): pillar + gem stack cleanly at a believable monument height next to a person-scale reference.
- Seat facing is logic (matches the validated chair orientation convention, `facing 0 = +z`).
- `node -c` clean on sources + bundle.

Client-only. Deploy: `git pull && npm run build:client`.

OpenSpec-Change: amend-modifier-duplicates
OpenSpec-Change: amend-modifier-tiebreaks
OpenSpec-Change: amend-modifier-tiebreaks-2

Duplicate effects collapse only on (source id, statistic, type, bonus or penalty) when the condition ids match. Bonuses and penalties split before conditions group. The group key is (condition, statistic, bonus or penalty, type) after frightened and sickened penalties are rewritten to status, so different types stack. Within a group the worst penalty or the highest bonus wins. For frightened and sickened that is the highest condition value. Then the highest rank, the newest sequence, and the lowest source id. Equal source ids keep the higher level, a level over none, and the duplicate-key comparison decides what remains. Stacking keeps the lowest sequence, then the lower condition id, a missing id losing, then the lower source id. `Modifier::bonus` and `Modifier::penalty` take a required `Statistic`. There is no Attack default.

The known defect in `docs/designer/rules-deviations.md` is resolved. Rules 2282 keeps the worse penalty. The non-derived larger-modifier choice is ruling R-01, not a deviation.

author: vifar
body:
## Intent

Closes `#64`.

Fix vifar/no-mistakes issue #64: explicitly cancelling an unchanged, fully validated CI watcher must keep the success already posted for that exact head while the run itself stays cancelled with its reason. Preserve the existing durable certificate binding the exact head, gate executions, configuration digest and push generation. Repair entry, validation reset and a replacing status POST must revoke that certificate first; cancellation afterward remains failure. Terminal settlement must retry until its outcome is durable, without downgrading proof merely because its write failed. A Git command killed by a signal is uncertain failure, never a qualifying cancellation.

Current main already implements most of #31. The reproduced regression is a certificate cancellation transaction failing storage: fallback retries as ineligible and destroys success. Distinguish actual Git/worktree inspection uncertainty from a failed certificate write, and retry the same decision through existing terminal ownership machinery with fresh proof checks. Once inspection fails, later storage retries cannot restore eligibility. Keep the existing certificate schema and strict validation receipt rules; do not loosen gate qualification.

Shutdown/restart and ci_monitor_interrupted (#62), supersession and pending-to-error handling (#40) are out of scope and must remain unchanged. Do not change the merge bar, review/approval gates, CI retry/repair policy or account/settings configuration. Read #31, #62, #105, #87, and overlapping #132/#133/#134/#138. Preserve #105's durable-write conventions and step around the other PRs; integration notes are in the private fleet DEVIATIONS.md. No merge, deployment, installation or shared daemon restart. Publish only through this laptop's registered no-mistakes gate, as Victor I <vifarinde@gmail.com>, with no attribution trailers. Open and maintain one PR for #64; the Studio alone merges.

Validation: tests were written first. The new storage-fault certified-cancellation test failed on fresh main with status POSTs [success failure] instead of [success], then passed after the fix. New tests also cover ordinary success preservation, exact certificate bindings, each revocation path separately, actual signal-killed Git, supersession, pending cancellation and durable cancelled reason after reopening. Existing shutdown recovery and newer-publication ownership regressions are included. Use the fork helpers and real observable behavior. author: sootyowl
body:
Language discovery previously classified most HTTP failures as unavailable videos and wrapped connection/timeouts in a generic exception. Introduce consistent transport and protocol errors across language discovery and transcript retrieval, and stop retrying HTTP 400 with default sessions.

The compatible transcript fix from #11 has been merged and released as [v1.2.2](https://github.com/SootyOwl/yt-transcript-fetcher/releases/tag/v1.2.2). This PR targets main for the subsequent breaking release; its Conventional Commit title and explicit BREAKING CHANGE footer identify the major version change.

- Preserve Requests HTTP, connection, and timeout exception types where appropriate; retain VideoNotFoundError for HTTP 404 discovery responses.
- Raise YouTubeAPIError consistently for FAILED_PRECONDITION and invalid API/JSON responses.
- Preserve retry behavior for HTTP 429 and retryable server errors, and leave injected sessions under caller control.
- Document the migration and cover the old/new behavior boundaries with transport regression tests.

Validation: 110 tests passed on Python 3.13, including all five live API tests; 105 offline tests passed on Python 3.9. Semantic-release 10.3.1 recognizes the actual commit and its explicit footer as a major release.

GitHub validation: after retargeting to main and updating this branch with the merged main changes, the [pull request test run](https://github.com/SootyOwl/yt-transcript-fetcher/actions/runs/39636388367) passed all five Python 3.9–3.13 jobs, including live API tests, at head `12fb319`. The earlier [branch test run](https://github.com/SootyOwl/yt-transcript-fetcher/actions/runs/39633635544) also passed; the local 110-test run includes seven additional research checks.

BREAKING CHANGE: Language discovery now propagates requests.HTTPError for non-404 HTTP failures instead of VideoNotFoundError, and preserves requests connection/timeout exceptions instead of wrapping them in Exception. Both endpoints raise YouTubeAPIError for FAILED_PRECONDITION and invalid API/JSON responses. Default sessions no longer retry HTTP 400. Update exception handlers and retry expectations when upgrading.

author: henri-colibritd
body:
Identical sampling results can belong to multiple stored executions with different result IDs, including repeated executions of the same job. The long-local storage tests currently compare every matching row against the first row's ID, causing intermittent failures.

Build expectations from all fixture rows matching data, error, and shots, with job filtering where required. Compare complete result/job lists without relying on query order, preserving duplicate entries and catching missing or extra matches.

Add three deterministic cases through the public storage API, covering different insertion orders, repeated results sharing a job, equal samples on another device, and exclusion of different samples. Each case uses an isolated temporary database and settings file and runs in the short suite without executing a simulator.

Confirmed in [the September 26 long-local Actions job](https://github.com/ColibrITD-SAS/mpqp/actions/runs/36240789475/job/108400768362): both result-fetch tests failed with `id: 5 != id: 1` despite identical payloads; the job comparison also failed.

Validation:
- Original assertions with Aer seeded before database setup: 2 failed, 28 passed.
- Patched worktree with the same deterministic Aer collision: 30 passed.
- New deterministic regression cases: 3 passed in the short suite.
- Combined seed and collision checks: 9 passed with `--seed 351`, and 9 passed without `--seed`, including real Aer sampling and subprocess checks with reversed test order.

The previous tests were failing non reliably because Aer was not affected by the `--seed` test argument. This argument is now used to seed ordinary Aer runs before database setup. Database setup and each pytest node ID use separate reproducible streams, with a new simulator seed for each automatically seeded call. Explicit run/backend seeds take precedence, including zero; omitting `--seed` preserves existing Aer behavior. Document the scope and reproducibility limits in CONTRIBUTING.md.

author: mangelsnc
body:
## What

Enhances the `_FileInfoTile` in the send page with three improvements:

### 1. Info button replaces expand chevron
The small chevron arrow is replaced with a proper `_InfoButton` — a circular bordered container with `Icons.info_outline`. When the metadata section is expanded, the button highlights with the accent color. A tooltip shows "View metadata" / "Hide metadata" on hover.

### 2. Rich metadata fields
The expanded metadata section now shows:

| Field | Source | Example |
|-------|--------|---------|
| **Type** | Extension + MIME (magic bytes) | `PNG (image/png)` |
| **Dimensions** | Image header parsing (PNG/JPEG/GIF/WebP/BMP) | `1920 × 1080` |
| **Pages** | PDF `/Type /Page` scan (first 10KB) | `~3` |
| **Size** | Human-readable + exact bytes | `2.4 MB (2,515,968 bytes)` |
| **Signature** | First 8 bytes as hex | `89 50 4E 47 0D 0A 1A 0A` |
| **Path** | Full file path | `/home/user/documents/photo.png` |

All extraction is **synchronous** and operates on header bytes only — no image decoding, no async calls.

### 3. Human-readable file sizes
- `< 1 KB`: `512 B`
- `< 1 MB`: `345.2 KB`
- `< 1 GB`: `2.4 MB`
- `>= 1 GB`: `1.25 GB`
- Metadata shows both: `2.4 MB (2,515,968 bytes)` with thousand separators

## Files changed

- **`app/lib/src/file_metadata.dart`** (new) — Pure, testable helpers: `formatFileSize`, `formatByteCount`, `formatSizeWithBytes`, `fileSignature`, `guessMimeType`, `parseImageDimensions`, `countPdfPages`
- **`app/lib/ui/send/send_page.dart`** (modified) — `_InfoButton` widget, `_buildMetadataSection()` with all new fields, shared `formatFileSize` in `_SendingScreen`
- **`app/test/file_metadata_test.dart`** (new) — 20+ unit tests covering all helpers and edge cases

## Design notes

- Info button uses `DeadDropColors.textSecondary` at rest, `DeadDropColors.accent` when expanded — subtle but discoverable
- Label column widened from 56px to 72px to accommodate "Dimensions" and "Signature"
- Graceful degradation: if `file_picker` doesn't provide bytes (web), metadata fields that need bytes are simply hidden
- No new dependencies — `formatByteCount` implements thousand separators manually (no `intl` needed)

## ⚠️ Verification status

I could **not** run `flutter analyze` or `flutter test` — the sandbox environment has no Flutter/Dart SDK reachable. The code is reasoned from reading the existing codebase and follows established patterns. **A maintainer must run `flutter analyze` and `flutter test` before merge.**

## Acceptance criteria checklist

- [x] Info button (not chevron) expands/collapses metadata
- [x] Images show dimensions (width × height)
- [x] PDFs show approximate page count
- [x] All files show magic bytes / signature
- [x] Sizes use KB/MB/GB appropriately with thousand separators
- [ ] `flutter analyze` passes (needs CI or manual run)
- [ ] All existing tests still pass (needs CI or manual run)

Closes board task `task_832f77c3b50a2424`.

author: garrison
body:
Qiskit raised its own minimum supported Python to 3.11 in https://github.com/Qiskit/qiskit/pull/17135, where qiskit 2.6 is named as the last release supporting 3.10.  This does the same for sqd.

Python 3.10 itself went end of life on 2026-10-01.

Version knobs: `requires-python`, the 3.10 classifier, `[tool.mypy] python_version`, `[tool.pylint] py-version`, the tox `env_list`, and the Python version in `docs.yml`, `lint.yml`, `test_minimum_versions.yml`, `test_latest_versions.yml`, `test_development_versions.yml`, and `nightly_qiskit_prerelease.yml`.

The `qiskit>=2.0, <3` range is unchanged: 17135 is not in a release yet, so nothing in the supported range requires a newer floor.

No other dependency floors needed raising either.  I pinned every declared minimum with `extremal-python-dependencies pin-dependencies-to-minimum` and ran the suite on 3.11: 63 passed.  Every floor already ships a cp311 wheel.

Two things beyond the mechanical bump:

- The `base_python` pins in the `lint` and `docs` environments are gone.  They date to the initial commit and pinned the then-current minimum rather than expressing a real constraint, so CI's chosen interpreter should decide.
- Dropping those pins lets `lint` resolve a current numpy (2.5.4 here), and that surfaced two separate issues.  `bitstring_matrix_to_integers` needs an explicit annotation, since `np.zeros` with a variable `dtype` is no longer inferable.  Separately, numpy's stubs use PEP 695 `type` statements, which mypy rejects unless it analyzes as 3.12 or later — so `[tool.mypy] python_version` is now 3.12, with a comment saying why it is deliberately ahead of `requires-python`.

That last one is the judgment worth a look.  The alternatives were dropping `python_version` entirely (mypy then follows the interpreter) or restoring the `base_python` pin so an older numpy resolves.  3.12 keeps an explicit analysis target at the cost of the number no longer tracking the supported floor.

`tox -e lint` and `tox -e py311` pass.  I could not run `tox -e docs` locally: `sbd-eigensolver` publishes no wheels and its sdist needs MPI, which my machine lacks.  That is unrelated to this change — it fails the same way on `main`, including on 3.10.

Ruff's `target-version` stays at `py39` here.  Moving it is left to a follow-up PR.

<hr>

This pull request was drafted by Claude Opus 5 under my guidance.

author: ianalexis
body:
Port of the travel optimization that Bambu Studio 2.8.4 lists as "Optimized Top Surface Monotonic Line Infill Path to Reduce Travel Moves" ([bambulab/BambuStudio@60b545d](https://github.com/bambulab/BambuStudio/commit/60b545d56cdf3beb914d94b9d3f5222a87ced9ab)).

Monotonic and Monotonic line fills keep their print order, so the G-code export cannot reorder them. Orca printed all of a surface's gap fill after its last line, so the nozzle finished the surface and then came back for every piece, most of which lie along the walls where the lines end. Now each piece is printed where the nozzle passes it.

This only applies to surfaces that get gap fill (**Apply gap fill** set to *Everywhere* or *Top and bottom surfaces*). With *Nowhere*, the default, the G-code is byte-identical.

## Results

Same build with and without the change, sliced from the CLI with `--filter-out-gap-fill 0`:

| Project | Settings | Print time | Travel | Retractions |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Organic object, 592 layers | Top and bottom, Monotonic line top | 15h 21m 57s → 15h 20m 13s (**−104 s**) | 1166.1 → 1162.8 m | 88,981 → 88,443 (**−538**) |
| Same | Top and bottom, Monotonic top | 15h 22m 14s → 15h 21m 24s (**−50 s**) | 1163.0 → 1160.6 m | 88,886 → 88,639 (**−247**) |
| Same | Gap fill *Nowhere* | identical G-code | identical | identical |
| OrcaCube v2 | Top and bottom | 32m 21s → 32m 15s (−6 s) | 21.55 → 21.26 m | 1,344 → 1,314 (−30) |
| Same, scaled ×4 | Everywhere | 4h 18m 17s → 4h 17m 42s (−35 s) | 245.1 → 244.1 m | 7,324 → 7,146 (−178) |
| Three-part figure, Monotonic internal solid | Top and bottom | 2h 12m 23s → 2h 12m 19s (−4 s) | 142.31 → 142.20 m | 3,517 → 3,496 (−21) |
| Same | Everywhere | 2h 12m 29s → 2h 12m 22s (−7 s) | 142.73 → 142.19 m | 3,520 → 3,498 (−22) |

- Filament and gap fill volume are unchanged; only the order changes.
- Slicing time is unchanged within run-to-run noise.

On the organic object with Monotonic line, gap fill had caused 557 of the 713 travels over 1 mm inside top surfaces.

## Implementation

- `Fill::_create_gap_fill()` hands the gap fill of a fixed-order (`no_sort`) fill to the new `insert_gap_fill()`. Fills that the G-code export can sort, such as Rectilinear, are unchanged: the export already chains their gap fill together with their lines.
- Each gap fill piece, in turn, goes where it adds the least travel: between two extrusions of the fill, before the first or after the last, flipped when that is shorter. A closed piece counts from its point nearest the nozzle, where `GCode::extrude_loop()` starts it.
- The fill's own extrusions keep their order and direction, so a monotonic fill stays monotonic.
- If the result travels no less than the previous order (all gap fill after the lines), the previous order is kept, so a fill never gets more travel.
- This is a reimplementation of Bambu's idea, not a cherry-pick. Bambu changed `FillMonotonicLineWGapFill`, which Orca replaced with PrusaSlicer's `FillMonotonicLines` while moving gap fill to `Fill::_create_gap_fill()` for every pattern. Bambu's version attaches each piece to its nearest line end, with extra rules for its wipe-merged lines and per-island fills. Orca needs neither, so cheapest insertion covers it.
- Because the change sits in the shared gap fill step, it also covers Monotonic, bottom surfaces, internal solid infill and the other fixed-order patterns (Concentric, Spiral Inset, Archimedean Chords, Octagram Spiral), whenever they get gap fill.
- Not ported: the *Global monotonic line* top surface pattern from the same release ([bambulab/BambuStudio@fa19554](https://github.com/bambulab/BambuStudio/commit/fa1955438f8a3fdb296f02fcd3d545052a780f87)). It sweeps the whole surface column by column to avoid seams between monotonic regions, which adds travel.
- `docs/HLSD/travel-optimization.md` describes the design.

## Tests

- New fff_print test, *Monotonic line top surfaces print their gap fill next to their lines and keep the lines in order*. It slices the letter A with and without top gap fill and checks three things:
  - the lines are the same, in the same order and direction;
  - some gap fill is printed before the last line;
  - the order travels less than printing the gap fill after the lines.
- The test fails with `insert_gap_fill()` disabled.
- The fff_print suite passes. libslic3r passes except two TextureImport JPEG tests, which fail the same way on `main` in my local build.
