author: binaricat
body:
## Summary

Closing a copied session window through the operating-system window close button could leave its terminal backend running while the main application stayed open. Explicit tab close did clean it up. This change makes owning-renderer destruction use the existing session-close path.

- Track logical terminal lifetime ownership independently of the output display route in worker mode.
- Close owned pending/established sessions through normal backend cleanup, including output routes and session-close notifications; preserve the existing SSH/SFTP reference-counted release path.
- Preserve attached-popup sessions, external agent/provider sessions and newer same-ID owners. Explicit restore into a new home renderer transfers lifetime ownership; mere display rebind does not.
- Cover supported in-process fallback by tracking session-object ownership, including asynchronous opens completing after renderer destruction.
- Use an unscoped normal close for whole-renderer lifetime teardown so cancellation of a queued replacement cannot leave the previous boot alive. Ordinary UI epoch-scoped close behavior remains unchanged.

## Reproduction before the fix

On clean baseline `38ff20ca80ddb8135f57b27e1b42c5ddfe90042c`, Linux Electron production build, fresh isolated profile:

1. Keep the main window open.
2. Open a local terminal, then use the actual tab context-menu action “Copy Tab to New Window.”
3. Run a bounded foreground workload in the copied terminal.
4. Close the child using the native OS window close button.

Three consecutive child-window closes left three PTY shells and their foreground workloads alive under the terminal worker. Recorded workloads continued for 230, 129 and 67 seconds after their respective window closes, until the test app was stopped. A matched explicit tab-X close terminated both shell and workload. This demonstrates a backend lifecycle defect; it does not establish a historical macOS memory/heat cause or quantify an RSS/CPU improvement.

## Tests

134 tests passed across these four focused suites on the candidate:

- `electron/bridges/terminalWorkerManager.test.cjs`
- `electron/bridges/rendererSessionLifetime.test.cjs`
- `electron/bridges/terminalBridge.closeReusedSession.test.cjs`
- `electron/bridges/terminalBridge.outputFlood.test.cjs`

New coverage includes established/pending owner destruction, attached display and home handoff, newer same-ID owners, failed replacement, external-agent exclusion, explicit-close/shutdown idempotence, backend-assigned IDs returned after renderer removal, direct-mode local integration, and shared shell/SFTP lease retention through the actual normal close implementation. A linked worker-runtime regression confirms cancelling queued boot2 also closes surviving active boot1. Existing pending-start cancellation tests remain green.

Local syntax checks, `git diff --check` and the 134 focused tests passed. Exact-head CI subsequently passed lint/full tests and the package-build matrix. A separate local full-suite/build run is not claimed; native smoke used the unchanged production renderer with the candidate CJS.

## Acceptance gates

- [x] Independent source review of the exact tested diff: no remaining actionable blocker.
- [x] Candidate native regression: explicit tab-close control and all three actual copied owning-window OS-close cycles passed, main kept alive, no accumulating PTY/workload pairs.
- [x] Native preservation controls: actual hide-to-tray retains the same source processes; a separately instrumented real first-party attached popup preserves its source on native popup close.
- [x] Exact-head remote Codex review is clean; CI lint/full tests and package builds passed.
- Native live SSH/SFTP transport-safety validation is not claimed. Shared-lease protection has deterministic coverage through the actual normal close implementation.

Implementation commit: `0d361131962107d6034c7365a1d3a571c9bd0457`.

No merge is requested until candidate native verification and review gates pass.

author: bslayton
body:
Fixes the search spinner on phones. CSS only (`src/css/custom.css`).

## Bug
When the search box was open on a phone, the loading spinner showed **under the magnifying glass**, before typing and after results loaded.

## Cause
The rule that widens the search box on phones targeted `[class*='searchBar']`. The spinner's class is `searchBarLoadingRing_*`, so it matched too and was forced visible whenever search was open.

## Fix
- The widen rule now targets only the search wrapper (`[class^='searchBar_']`). The dropdown rule is narrowed the same way.
- The spinner shows **only while the search index is loading**, and **replaces** the magnifying glass instead of stacking under it.

| State | Shows |
|---|---|
| Search open, before typing | 🔍 |
| Search index loading | spinner (in the 🔍 spot) |
| Results showing | 🔍, results full width |

Previewed on the live site at phone size by injecting the CSS, in all three states. Full build OK.

Independent of #18, so they can be merged in either order. Merging publishes the site.

author: kartik-limbachiya
body:
## Problem
Data entered in the app was never saved to Supabase (all 9 tables had 0 rows) and was lost on uninstall.

## Root causes
1. **Server couldn't reach the database.** `server.js` used `db.<ref>.supabase.co`, which is IPv6-only; Render is IPv4-only. Every query failed, errors were swallowed, the server fell back to ephemeral JSON files, and the API still returned `success: true`.
2. **Movements and carriers never saved.** `POST /api/sync/movements` and `/logistics` take an object, but the route's "single record" branch discarded it and re-saved the old copy.
3. **Nothing was written on the phone.** In SDK 57 the path-based `expo-file-system` API throws unless imported from `expo-file-system/legacy` (and `documentDirectory` is undefined on the main entry). Errors were caught silently.

## Changes
**Server**
- Connect via the Supabase Session pooler (IPv4), derived from the existing `DB_URL`; fall back to the original URL; retry in the background.
- Database is the only source of truth (no local-file fallback). Failed reads/writes return 503/400/500 with `success: false`.
- Saves run in one transaction with a savepoint per record, so one rejected record no longer blocks the batch (returned in `failed`).
- Fix the movements/logistics object payload bug; whitelist collection names; `/health` does a live `SELECT 1` and reports `databaseConnected`.

**App**
- Import `expo-file-system/legacy` in `storageHelper`, `authService`, `excelReportGenerator`.
- `masterService` / `carrierService` honour `init(forceReload)` so synced data appears without a restart.
- `masterService` now persists requisitions, categories, product types, damage logs, reports and schedules (were memory-only).
- `cloudSyncService` fetches before reading local data, merges the master blob's logs/reports/schedules/categories instead of dropping the cloud copy (which was then pushed back empty), and logs rejected pushes.

Also adds `CLAUDE.md`.

## Testing
- Ran the real save code for every collection shape against the real Supabase **inside a rolled-back transaction**: rows saved, a conflicting record was rejected on its own while its neighbour saved, database unchanged afterwards.
- Simulated a reinstall (empty phone, data in cloud) with mocked storage/server: all 5 collections restore and the push-back keeps logs/reports. The same test **fails on the original code**.
- Not tested: running the app on a device, or the fixed server on Render.

## After merging
Render should redeploy on its own (no settings change needed). Verify `GET /health` shows `"databaseConnected": true`, then save a warehouse in the app and confirm a row appears in Supabase.

## Known limitation
Deletes don't propagate: the sync only adds, so deleted items return after the next sync. Needs tombstones across all entity types; not in this PR.

body:
## What this changes, and why

Fixes #7989. An apostrophe makes no sound, so "kubernetes's" sounds like the bare entry. `WordCorrectionEngine.spellings(of:in:)` read the whole word first and only added the ending-aware reading for entries the whole reading had not found, so the entry came back bare and the possessive was deleted ("the kubernetes's status" became "the Kubernetes status").

For a heard word ending in `'s` or the curly form, an entry that the name reading also finds is now offered with the ending reattached, in place of the bare one. A bare `s` ending keeps the existing order, because an entry such as "Redis" may end in s.

## How you know it works

- New `PossessiveDictionaryTests` (Kubernetes, Redis, Postgres, curly apostrophe; a bare `redis` stays whole; a written `Kubernetes's` is left alone). Before the fix: 4 cases fail (`redis's → ["Redis"]`, `kubernetes's → ["Kubernetes"]`, ...); after: pass. Also green: `InflectedDictionaryFormsTests`, `CorrectionRestraintTests`, `DictionaryCandidates*`, `NonWordCorrectionTests` (49 tests).
- Corpus case `dictionary-possessive-kept-7989` (the entry runs through the correction engine, which the rules lane does not, so `rules.golden` records the unchanged rules output; the failing-then-passing evidence is the unit test). It says the doubtful run twice, as `PositionalEvidenceTests` requires. Regenerated: `rules.golden`, `degraded-path-matrix.md`, `destination-matrix.md`, `bakeoff.md` counts, `DataManifest.json`; `seam_baseline.json` gains the 6 cuts of the new case (`--update --after-merge`).
- `make eval`: exit 0, rules scorecard accepted regressions 0, seam-audit passes. `make lint`: clean.

Not rerun in full after the final corpus-text edit; `make eval` and `make lint` were.

author: juanmarboledao2304
body:
## Why

Nexus had drifted from what Claude Code was actually doing:

| Symptom | Cause |
|---|---|
| Finished background jobs showed "Trabajando" / "Espera tu aprobación" | Hooks can't tell a finished job from an idle prompt; the end-of-turn wait was mapped to `waiting_approval` |
| The idle interactive terminal showed "Pide aprobación" | `mapTelemetryStatus` labeled **every** wait (Stop, resume, notifications such as "X finished") as approval |
| Dead sessions stayed active | `session-liveness.js` returns `available:false` on Windows, so `livenessReap` never closed anything |
| Titles like `Session a906e6d3` | The registry's real name was never read |
| Quota "43h 24m to fill the 5-hour window" | Tokens counted against an invented 2.5M cap |
| `agy-cascade` dispatch "Completado" with a DIGEST and commit `4f8b2d1` | cmd.exe can't run the bash script → canned fallback with fake digest/commit; the session stayed "En espera" with no way to reply |

## What changes

- **`server/lib/claude-live-registry.js`**: reads `~/.claude/sessions/<pid>.json` (pid-checked) and `jobs/<id>/state.json`. Every `NEXUS_LIVE_SYNC_MS` (5 s) it maps `busy` → working, permission/dialog → approval, job `blocked` → **"Espera tu respuesta"** (new kind in Te necesitan), job `done` → completed, `failed` → error, idle → plain wait. It also fills in the real name. On Windows the same registry serves as the liveness probe for `livenessReap`.
- **`mapTelemetryStatus`**: `waiting_approval` only for a PermissionRequest or a blocking notification; everything else is `waiting_input`.
- **Real quota**: `statusline/nexus-statusline.js` forwards Claude Code's `rate_limits` (five_hour / seven_day) to `POST /api/quota/claude-limits` (hook-guarded, persisted to `<data dir>/claude-rate-limits.json`). The meter, the Home card and the details show the real % used, the reset time and the weekly %. Without a statusline, the estimate is labeled as such.
- **Dispatch**: `server/lib/command-resolver.js` runs `.exe` directly (multi-word prompts stay one argument), shebang scripts via Git Bash, and `.cmd` with quoting. A missing CLI → visible `error`. The simulation only runs with `NEXUS_DISPATCH_SIMULATE=1`. When the process exits the session closes, and its real output goes to Stop so the digest is parsed.
- Docs: README (5 languages, i18n parity clean), ARCHITECTURE, HOOKS, statusline/README. UI keys in 5 locales.

## Verification

- `npm run verify` locally: headers OK, Prettier OK, `tsc -b` OK, server **1474 pass / 0 fail**, client **58/58** files.
- New `server/__tests__/live-sync.test.js` (18 tests): registry → DB, approval vs. reply, quota endpoint, Windows resolver, failing dispatch, Windows reap.
- Manual: `agy-cascade` now runs through Git Bash; a dry run against the real registry derives the expected state for each live session.

## After merging

1. Restart the Nexus server (main checkout) to load the server code.
2. Add the statusline to `~/.claude/settings.json`:
   `"statusLine": { "type": "command", "command": "node \"C:/Users/juanm/Claude/dual-agent-nexus/statusline/nexus-statusline.js\"" }`

No version bump in this PR (would be 3.3.0 via `version-release` when cutting a release).

author: 3rav
body:
## Summary

This PR adds optional IEEE binary16 storage for ILU(k) and ILUT preconditioner numerical factors.

The feature is storage-only. Solver arithmetic, vectors, residuals, convergence checks, and diagonal inverse values remain in the normal LIS scalar precision.

## Configuration

Build-time support is enabled with:

    --enable-half

Runtime selection uses:

    -precon_half {0|1|2}

where:

- `0` disables half factor storage
- `1` enables half storage with a quality probe and safe fallback
- `2` skips the quality probe while retaining hard safety checks

Unsupported scalar configurations safely retain normal factor storage.

## Implementation

- IEEE binary16 conversion with round-to-nearest-even
- power-of-two row scaling
- finite-value, overflow, and underflow checks
- quality-probe fallback
- ILU(k) lifecycle and numerical refresh support
- ILUT support
- release of normal numerical factor values after accepted half compression where supported
- borrowed symbolic ILU pattern without duplicate index storage
- optional runtime x86 F16C decoding
- scalar decoder fallback
- optimized row scaling
- F16C row kernels for the common decode path

The diagonal inverse remains in normal precision.

## Environment controls

- `LIS_HALF_PROBE_TOL` overrides the default quality-probe tolerance
- `LIS_HALF_NO_SIMD=1` disables the F16C path and uses the scalar decoder

## Validation

- exhaustive binary16 conversion coverage
- factor storage and quality checks
- ILU(k) lifecycle and memory-release tests
- ILUT tests
- scalar/F16C equivalence checks
- OpenMP testing with 1, 4, and 8 threads
- MFAMG regression checks after rebasing onto current `develop`
- final full test suite: 50/50 tests passed

The tested ILU/ILUT cases reduced owned numerical factor storage by approximately 59%.

No existing LIS option or parameter array lengths are changed.

author: speranzaemiliano-rk
body:
Se tocaba **Enviar al cliente**, se abría la pestaña «Preparando el correo…», aparecía **«Adjuntando los papeles…»** y ahí quedaba. Para siempre. Sin error, sin aviso, sin bajar nada.

## La causa

El respaldo ya existía: si algo **falla**, el `.catch` baja los papeles y abre el correo igual. El problema es que no estaba fallando — **estaba esperando**. Una promesa pendiente no rechaza, así que ningún `catch` corre, el respaldo no se dispara, y nadie cierra la pestaña: lo único que llama a `soltarPestana()` es justamente ese `catch`.

Tres pasos sin reloj, ninguno con forma de darse por vencido:

- **El permiso de Google** — su promesa sólo la cierran `callback` / `error_callback` de GIS. Si la librería no llama a ninguno de los dos (popup detrás de la pestaña esperando un login, cookies de terceros bloqueadas, red caída), no hay nada en el programa que la despierte.
- **La lectura de los papeles** — `once("value")` no falla sin conexión: espera.
- **La subida a Gmail** — `fetch` sin `AbortController` ni timeout.

## Qué cambia

`conLimite(promesa, ms, queEs)` le pone reloj a cada paso y al vencerse **rechaza**, que es lo que hace entrar al respaldo ya escrito. Plazos generosos a propósito (30 s el permiso, 25 s cada papel, 2 min la subida, 20 s el índice): el objetivo no es cortar rápido sino que **exista un final**. El reloj se limpia al resolver, así que no deja rechazos sueltos.

- La subida se **corta de verdad** con `AbortController`: un `fetch` abandonado sigue ocupando la conexión y el intento siguiente competiría contra él.
- Un papel que no vuelve **se saltea** (el `.catch` interno ya estaba para eso) en vez de frenar el envío entero.
- A los 15 s la pestaña deja de mostrar una palabra quieta y cuenta qué pasa: *«está tardando. Si no responde, bajo los papeles y abro el correo igual»*. Una palabra congelada no distingue «está trabajando» de «se colgó».

`VERSION_APP` y `sw.js` a **v83**.

## Cómo se encontró

Auditoría en paralelo de los cuatro tramos del flujo (20 agentes, cada hallazgo con un verificador adversario que intentaba refutarlo). De **16 hallazgos sobrevivió 1**; pero las 15 refutaciones coincidían en el mismo hecho de código, y eso es lo que guió el arreglo: en todo `index.html` no había **un solo** `Promise.race`, `AbortController` ni timeout (`grep` → 0).

## Pruebas

Nueva suite `correocuelgue.js` (12 verificaciones) que **reproduce el cuelgue real**: un `initTokenClient` cuyo `requestAccessToken` no llama a ningún callback —el silencio absoluto— y verifica que la pestaña **termina en el correo** en vez de quedarse en `about:blank`; lo mismo con la subida a Gmail estancada; que un papel trabado se saltea y el resto se manda; y el helper en seco (rechaza, respeta el plazo, deja pasar lo que vuelve, no disfraza un error de verdad como timeout, no deja rechazos sueltos). `municipal.js` sigue en verde.

---

author: devin-ai-integration[bot]
body: ## Summary Fixes the `n-plus-one` incident (`DocumentListLatencyHigh`). `DocumentService.list_documents` used to run one `document_versions` SELECT per document. It now runs one batched query for the whole page, so a request makes 5 SQL statements however large the page is. ```python # before: N statements for doc in documents: select(DocumentVersion).where(document_id == doc.id).order_by(version_number.desc()).limit(5) # after: 1 statement ranked = select(DocumentVersion.id, row_number().over(partition_by=document_id, order_by=version_number.desc()).label("rn")) .where(document_id.in_(page_ids)) select(DocumentVersion).options(defer(content)).join(ranked).where(ranked.c.rn <= RECENT_VERSIONS_LIMIT) # grouped in Python -> doc.recent_versions ``` The 5 statements are: count, page, the existing `versions` and `comments` selectin loads, and the batched recent-versions query. **One change beyond the batched query:** the page query now uses `selectinload(Document.versions).defer(DocumentVersion.content)`, and the batched query also defers `content`. - Why: `DocumentListResponse` contains no version data, but the `versions` selectin load was pulling every version body on every request. That is about 800 rows × ~7 KB for a 100-row page. - Without the defer: statements were already at 5, but p95 stayed at 1-2 s because the single uvicorn worker and Postgres were both CPU-bound decoding that payload. - With the defer: p95 drops to about 80 ms. - Effect on callers: `recent_versions` now holds metadata only, with no `content`. Nothing in `app/` reads `.versions`, `.comments` or `recent_versions` today. **Migration `004_add_list_indexes`:** adds `ix_documents_owner_deleted_template_updated` on `documents(owner_id, is_deleted, is_template, updated_at)` and `ix_document_versions_document_id_version_number` on `document_versions(document_id, version_number)`. `001_initial_schema.py` is unchanged. EXPLAIN shows Postgres using the first index for both the count and the page query. **Test:** `test_list_documents_query_count_is_constant` seeds 120 documents with 7 versions each. It checks that `size=10` and `size=100` issue the same number of statements (no more than 5) and that `recent_versions` is `[7, 6, 5, 4, 3]`. Against the old code it fails with `14 == 104`. `main` is not modified; it stays the before-state for the demo. ## Verification - `poetry run ruff check .`: clean. - `poetry run pytest -q tests/test_telemetry.py tests/test_document_service.py`: 17 passed. - Full suite: 9 failed, 68 passed. The 9 failures are the known `main` failures in `test_documents_api.py` (401 vs 200). - Rebuilt `document-service` (migration 003 → 004 applied on start), with the scenario still armed. | | queries/request | p95 | `DocumentListLatencyHigh` | |---|---|---|---| | before (armed, unfixed image) | 104 | 3.93 s | firing | | after (`make incident-verify SCENARIO=n-plus-one EXPECT=after`) | 5.0 | 0.115 s | inactive | After gate: **GREEN**, request_rate 23.53 rps, 0% 5xx, 0 shed. Host: 8 vCPU / 32 GB, local Compose stack. The formal `EXPECT=before` gate wasn't run as a gate: it fingerprints the working tree, which already contained the fix. The "before" numbers above come from `make incident-status` while the unfixed image was running under the armed load. Link to Devin session: https://partner-workshops.devinenterprise.com/sessions/b562c336ee8d4f3c9cae9332daef6526 Open in Devin Desktop: https://partner-workshops.devinenterprise.com/desktop/session/b562c336ee8d4f3c9cae9332daef6526?variant=devin ---

## Problem
On an AutoCAD drawing, zoomed out, the area labels ("Lounge Area 312.375 Sft") were bigger than the rooms and covered the plan.

The takeoff lays a DWG on an A0 sheet at the plot scale that fits its whole model space. For a model space holding many plans that is 1:960, about 0.9 pt per ft. A label of its set size (11.5 pt) is then about 13 ft tall on the drawing, taller than a room. Labels also stopped growing past 250 % zoom, so on screen they stayed one big size.

## Change
- **Bluebeam behaviour:** labels follow the zoom at every zoom, in step with the drawing. There is no 2.5 × stop any more. On screen, labels under 6 px are still left out, and the selected object's label stays readable.

- The marked-up exports use the same size. A plot (Ctrl+P) keeps its labels' paper size.
- `takeoff.js?v=2026-10-21g`

The image build matrix in `images.yml` sets runners as matrix values (`{runner: "ubuntu-24.04", ...}`, `{runner: "ubuntu-24.04-arm", ...}`), so the ubuntu 26 bump (#56) left the build legs on 24.04. After merge, #56 should regenerate to include the matrix.

author: falopass
body:
## Qué cambia y por qué

Main quedó en rojo tras #596 (GPACK-09): agregó un `<script type="module">` en línea a `web/lista.html` sin declararla en la CSP. Dos consecuencias:

- `tests/test_security.py::test_every_inline_script_page_is_declared_in_csp` falla en main (rompe `dev.py check` y el CI de cualquier PR).
- **En producción la CSP bloquea ese script**: el puntaje de «Mi casa preparada» de la hoja imprimible no funciona en el sitio desplegado.

Corrección mínima, por la vía que sugiere la propia guarda:

- `backend/security.py`: `web/lista.html` se suma a `INLINE_SCRIPT_PAGES` y el regex de `inline_script_hashes()` ahora cubre también `<script type="module">` (antes solo `<script>` sin atributos; los que llevan `src` no aplican).
- `deploy/cloudflare/src/index.ts`: CSP regenerada con el hash nuevo (la guarda exige que sea idéntica a la del backend). Se toca `deploy/` porque la corrección lo exige — sin esto el script seguiría bloqueado.
- `scripts/local/presupuesto_peso.py`: el tope sube de 238 a 245 KB (medido 241,4 KB): `lista-score.js` + `lista.html` (GPACK-09) y `map.js` (PERF-141) sumaron ≈5,5 KB sin que nadie moviera el presupuesto, que en main ya venía 3,4 KB excedido. No se actualizó `CHANGELOG.md` a propósito (la fábrica lo hace en bloque); el motivo queda aquí y en el docstring del script.

Alternativa descartada: mover el script a `web/js/lista.js` exigiría tocar el SHELL del service worker (`test_recursos_de_lite_y_lista_cacheables` lo exige) y rehacer el contrato de `test_paginas_livianas`, que documenta la decisión de tenerlo en línea. Se respetó esa decisión.

## Verificación

- `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_security.py tests/test_service_worker.py` → **10 passed**.
- `flock /data/workspace/.heavy.lock .venv/bin/python dev.py check` → **verde completo**: ruff OK, 1960 pytest passed, 530 tests JS, presupuesto 241,4/245 KB, reglas de diseño (1 warn preexistente) y paleta.
- **Smoke del camino crítico** (obligatoria por tocar `backend/security.py`), con `dev.py run --demo` en :8011:
  - `POST /api/reports` → **201** con id.
  - Duplicado cercano (±0,001) → **200**, mismo id, `corroboraciones: 1`.
  - Mendoza, Argentina → **422** `FUERA_DE_CHILE`.
  - Foto → sube; `GET /api/reports/{id}/photo` da **403** en `no_verificado` (correcto: solo la moderación la ve) y **200** JPEG tras verificarla con el token admin del demo.
  - `GET /api/reports/mine` con `X-Brasa-Token` → el reporte aparece con `status_label: "En revisión"`.
  - 7.º POST en la hora → **429** `RATE_LIMITED`.
  - Datos de prueba borrados de `data/demo` (reportes, corroboración, log de moderación, suscriptor y foto).
  - No verificado: la vista de portada en navegador (cubrí la fuente `/api/reports/mine`, que es lo que la portada pinta) y el rechazo Turnstile con clave real (no hay `TURNSTILE_SECRET` en la máquina; el cambio no toca esa lógica).

## Riesgos

- La CSP gana un hash de script en línea más: el de `lista.html`, necesario para que la página funcione. No se abrió nada nuevo: sigue sin `unsafe-inline` para scripts.
- El tope de peso sube por decisión documentada en el propio script (misma convención de siempre).
- Sin datos personales tocados (SEC-01..05): solo política de seguridad y umbral.

author: lucasbrandaocabral
body:
## O que muda

Antes, a edição de texto pegava uma linha por vez e, em muitos boletos e faturas, só **uma palavra**: esses PDFs desenham cada palavra separada (às vezes alternando entre cópias da mesma fonte), e cada pedaço virava uma "linha" editável. Agora a edição funciona como no Acrobat: um clique pega o **parágrafo inteiro**.

### Linhas inteiras
- Pedaços na mesma linha de base, da mesma fonte e do mesmo tamanho, perto um do outro, formam a linha inteira, mesmo quando o PDF desenha cada palavra separada.
- Cópias da mesma fonte ("ABCDEF+Arial", "GHIJKL+Arial" ou "Arial-8358") contam como uma só.

### Parágrafos
- Linhas seguidas da mesma fonte, tamanho e cor, com a mesma distância entre elas e alinhadas (à esquerda, centralizado, à direita ou justificado), formam um bloco.
- Cada linha termina numa quebra de verdade ou continua na de baixo, conforme a próxima palavra caberia ou não. Listas continuam com uma linha por item.
- Linhas interrompidas por outra fonte (uma palavra em negrito no meio) continuam sendo editadas uma a uma, para não perder a formatação. Colunas lado a lado e valores de tabela ficam separados.

### Caixa de edição
- A caixa tem a largura do parágrafo, a mesma entrelinha, o recuo da primeira linha e o alinhamento; o texto reflui ao digitar.
- O cursor fica onde se clicou (uma tecla não substitui o texto todo).
- Enter quebra a linha e Ctrl+Enter conclui; numa linha sozinha, Enter continua concluindo.
- A alça da direita muda a largura do parágrafo.
- A prévia sem o texto antigo vale para o parágrafo inteiro.

### Escrita no PDF
- O texto antigo do parágrafo sai do arquivo e o novo é escrito com as linhas como aparecem na caixa, a mesma entrelinha (que acompanha o tamanho da letra) e o alinhamento; no justificado, o espaço que sobra é dividido entre as palavras.
- A fonte original é usada no que ela tiver, com todas as cópias dela; o espaço que ela não tem vira só um avanço, como no PDF original; a fonte que completa as letras que faltam leva o nome da original, para o parágrafo continuar sendo reconhecido na próxima edição.

## Como foi testado
- PDFs de teste imitando o boleto: parágrafo normal, cada palavra separada, palavras alternando entre cópias da mesma fonte, justificado, centralizado, negrito no meio da frase, duas colunas, tabela e lista. Os parágrafos são reconhecidos em todos (e o negrito no meio, as colunas e a tabela ficam separados); editados e salvos, continuam sendo reconhecidos numa segunda edição.
- No app, no navegador do computador e do celular (toque): clicar numa palavra abre o parágrafo inteiro com o cursor no lugar do clique; texto acrescentado no começo reflui, o justificado continua justificado, Enter cria um item novo na lista; o PDF salvo fica igual à caixa.
- Sem mudança na edição de uma linha sozinha e no "Adicionar texto": os testes anteriores (PDF estilo Canva, letras espaçadas, fonte original, zoom com a caixa aberta, Esc, desfazer, página girada, mover a linha) continuam passando.
- Página densa (duas colunas de 60 linhas, cada palavra separada): o agrupamento leva cerca de 5 ms.

## Commits
1. Texto do PDF em linhas inteiras e parágrafos
2. Editar o parágrafo inteiro com um clique, como no Acrobat

author: monitorelnino
body:
Resposta ao **"PARA A B2 E A B3"** do #946 (B1) e ao exercício que o #941 (B2) pediu: procurar nas páginas da faixa não o número de hoje, mas o **caminho de ausência e de zero** que o dado de hoje não exercita e que nenhum portão pega.

Na Defesa civil há três, e os três estão no mesmo punhado de linhas do topo.

## O que estava errado

1. **Zero medido saía como "0".** `texto('topoInmet', n(rAl.municipios_inmet))` e os outros três cartões de contagem escreviam o número cru. `layout/regras.json` → `numeros.zero_por_extenso_em_cartao` manda zero em cartão por extenso, e `verificar_conformidade.py:223` reprova o cartão renderizado com `"0"`. **Este não é caminho hipotético:** aviso e alerta em vigor vão a zero sempre que nenhum está em vigor — hoje o Cemaden está em 3.
2. **Ausência virava zero.** `n(undefined)` é `"0"`: se o resumo dos alertas não trouxesse o campo, o cartão afirmaria "nenhum município sob aviso" onde o certo é "sem coleta até o corte" (`numeros.sem_dado_nunca_e_zero`). É o pior dos três, porque a página passaria a afirmar uma medição que não fez.
3. **O guarda era do número, não da fonte** — exatamente a família do item 2 do #941. `if (decretados.length)` deixava os cartões de decretos e reconhecidos com o `"sem coleta até o corte"` da reserva do HTML quando o consolidado estava lido e nenhum município tinha decreto: dizer que não coletamos o que coletamos.

## O que o PR faz

Uma definição de valor de cartão por página, `nCartao`, usada pelos seis cartões do topo:

- `null`, vazio ou não-número → **devolve null**, e `texto()` não escreve: o cartão fica com a classe nomeada que o HTML já carrega;
- `0` → **"nenhum"**, que é a palavra que esta página já usava no cartão da pendência (uma palavra por página; "zero" é a de `saude.js`, `prefeituras.js` e `imprensa.js`, e não vou importar vocabulário de outra página para esta);
- resto → o `n` de sempre, pt-BR.

`texto()` passa a distinguir `null` de valor (`if (e && v != null)`), igual ao `pôr` da B2 — testa a fonte, nunca a verdade do número. O guarda dos decretos passa a ser `if (DECRETADOS && DECRETADOS.municipios)`, e o `if (pop != null)` da população sai, porque `nCartao` já responde por ele.

## Linhas líquidas

**+8** (+17 −9) em um arquivo. **Código +0:** as oito linhas novas são comentário (seis em `nCartao`, duas no guarda dos decretos) — é o que impede a causa raiz de voltar na próxima vez que alguém escrever um número neste topo. Nenhuma função nova fora da definição única, nenhuma camada, nenhum portão novo.

## Prova

Os caminhos de ausência só se exercitam interceptando os arquivos no navegador, como a B1 fez no #946. Seis casos, **a 375 e a 1280 px**, sem erro de JS, sem rolagem horizontal e sem estouro do número grande:

| caso | antes | agora |
|---|---|---|
| a · dado de hoje | 802 · 3 · 988 · 887 · 41 · 34,5 milhões | **igual** |
| b · `municipios_inmet: 0`, `municipios_cemaden: 0` | `0` · `0` | **nenhum · nenhum** |
| c · os dois campos ausentes do resumo | `0` · `0` | **sem coleta até o corte** |
| d · consolidado lido, `municipios: {}` | sem coleta até o corte | **nenhum · nenhum** |
| e · `pop_sob_decreto: 0` | `0` | **nenhum** |
| f · `pop_sob_decreto: null` | sem coleta até o corte | **igual** (já estava certo) |

Portões rodados no local, todos verdes: estrutura, runtime, runtime dos mapas, acessibilidade, texto público (e `--forma`), runtime da resposta, móvel, segurança, grades de números, **conformidade** (9 páginas) e `--regras-cobertas`, consistência visual, CODEMAP e coerência da Imprensa.

**Uma divergência registrada, pela regra do mais conservador:** no caso (d), o cartão da pendência diz "não calculado até o corte", porque `calculado` nasce de `decretados.some(m => m.dias !== undefined)` e com o conjunto vazio não há como saber se o gerador escreve o campo. Com zero decretos, "nenhum" também seria verdade e mais informativo; não troquei, porque o caminho é inalcançável enquanto houver um decreto no ciclo (hoje, 988) e porque a opção conservadora não afirma nada que não se saiba.

author: madmax91310
body:
Le classement annuel permet d’ajuster un profil prédéfini depuis le catalogue compatible complet, sans modifier ni sauvegarder sa source. Les actifs peuvent être ajoutés ou retirés dans les limites de 2 à 6 participants et 2 à 7 années complètes. Les couleurs des actifs conservés restent stables. « Réinitialiser le profil », le changement de profil et le rechargement abandonnent les ajustements temporaires.

Les calculs, le tableau et les deux téléchargements PNG suivent la sélection, la période et la devise actuelles ; les noms de fichiers utilisent les actifs sélectionnés. Le texte édité est copié à l’identique et conservé quand les paramètres changent, avec une indication et une action explicite de régénération. Les phrases adaptent le nombre et le type des participants et indiquent la devise. Un historique insuffisant propose une période commune valide ou explique pourquoi deux années complètes sont impossibles. Les données et règles financières restent inchangées.

Les composants partagés conservent leur comportement par défaut : le sélecteur accepte une option désactivant ses écritures de préférences, et l’aperçu accepte un nom de fichier spécifique. Les attentes obsolètes de tests DCA bloquant déjà master ont été alignées sur la poche actions documentée, les conventions physiques qualifiées, les observations figées et la signature anonyme existante ; aucun code de cet autre outil ne change.

Validation : compilation, audits, tests Python et tous les groupes navigateur réussis avant fusion puis en production. Les tests couvrent ajout hors profils, retrait, copie exacte d’un texte retouché, protection du brouillon, PNG après ajout/retrait et depuis l’aperçu, couleurs, dates/devise, réinitialisation/changement/rechargement, absence d’écriture persistante et historique insuffisant. Les 30 configurations de 2–6 actifs et 2–7 années passent ; les PNG aux limites ont aussi été inspectés visuellement.

Publication effective vérifiée par le workflow https://github.com/madmax91310/shinny-potato/actions/runs/39645306459 : code et données `96b8b3d0d49679e1dbb51be5cd551712cb2cfc26`, avec 342 fichiers de données contrôlés sur le site public.

author: robertohluna
body:
## What

Build and test on Elixir 1.19.5 / OTP 28.5.0.5 (`hexpm/elixir:1.19.5-erlang-28.5.0.5-debian-bookworm-20260824-slim`).

OTP 28.0 to 28.2 segfault the VM when a process is killed while `re:run` is yielding inside a large match (erlang/otp#10432, fixed in OTP 28.3). Since 0.3.7 the classification time limit kills a late detection worker, so on the image's OTP 28.1.1 a large document whose detection or entity read runs past its limit could take the Engine down. CI reproduced it on #159 (test-current exit 139, no ExUnit summary).

- `deploy/Dockerfile.engine`: `BUILDER_IMAGE` moves to the tag above; the header names the pair and says never to build on OTP 28.0 to 28.2.
- `ci.yml`: test-current runs OTP 28.5.0.5 (the cache key changes, so the first run compiles RocksDB cold).
- CONTRIBUTING and the quickstart name the pair; `versioning-and-releases.md` says the two pins move together from 0.3.10 and that a host with its own `BUILDER_IMAGE` must be on OTP 28.3 or later.

## Evidence

- The tag is active on Docker Hub for amd64 and arm64; it is the newest 1.19.5 / 28.x bookworm slim.
- Evidence branch `tmp/otp-on-159` (not for merge): #159 plus this change plus a commit that asserts `TimeLimit.kill_safe?()` and kills a worker mid match on 940 KB; CI dispatched.
- CI does not build the image; the release build host verifies it with `build-release.sh`.

author: facorreiaa
body:
## What

Phase B1 of the music scrobbler (owner exception, 2026-10-21). Aaru speaks ListenBrainz's submit protocol, so scrobblers that let you set a ListenBrainz server send listens to Aaru: Web Scrobbler (YouTube, YouTube Music, Spotify and Apple Music on the web), Pano Scrobbler, Navidrome, Jellyfin's plugin. No Spotify OAuth, no native Apple Music path (see the BACKLOG decision).

- **Token:** new `music` kind, prefix `aaru_lb_`, `scrobble:write` only, its own group (music and video tokens never cross surfaces).
- **Transport** (outside `/v1`, ListenBrainz shapes): `POST /listenbrainz/1/submit-listens` (`single`, `playing_now` stores nothing, `import` ≤ 1,000 / 10 MB), `GET /listenbrainz/1/validate-token`, OPTIONS + CORS `*`. Errors are `{code, error}`.
- **Data:** `listens` table, append-only, separate from the library, cascade-deleted with the user. Same normalized artist + track within half the track (≤ 90 s, 30 s unknown) is one play and is dropped; inserts run under a per-user advisory lock.
- **Reads:** `GET /v1/me/listens` (cursor by `before`) and `GET /v1/me/listens/top?by=artist|track|album` over a stats period. Listens are in the account export.
- Regenerated AaruAPI and web types; "Music scrobbler" label on web and iOS.
- Docs: BACKLOG decision + MUS-004 re-scoped to history imports, MUS-005…008; CLAUDE.md stack row and **Listen**; ARCHITECTURE.md transport.

## Not in this PR

- No Settings surface yet (MUS-007, Phase C), so a music token can only be minted via the API.
- No MusicBrainz lookup (MUS-006): covers only when the scrobbler sends a release-group MBID.
- Not tried with a real scrobbler; needs a deploy (manual promote PR in platform/infra).

## Checks

- `swift test` (aaru-server): 300 tests passed, incl. 8 new `ListenBrainzRouteTests`
- swiftformat / swiftlint clean
- `swift test --package-path aaru-api`
- web `check`, `lint`, `typecheck`, `test`
- iOS simulator build

author: servincharles
body:
Adds **accessibility scenarios to the BDD suite** (axe-core, WCAG 2.1 AA), a **Jenkins choice** to run them, and an optional **BrowserStack Accessibility Testing** switch.

## Scenarios: `features/features/dip-accessibility.feature` (`@a11y`, also in `@regression`)
| Scenario | WCAG 2.1 |
| --- | --- |
| Show an accessible empty application form | A and AA rules (axe-core) |
| Show an accessible Accepted / Referred / Declined result (Scenario Outline) | A and AA rules |
| Complete the journey using only the keyboard | 2.1.1 Keyboard |
| Show where keyboard focus is on every form control | 2.4.7 Focus Visible |
| Announce the decision to screen reader users | 4.1.3 Status Messages |
| Fit the journey on a 320 pixel wide screen without scrolling sideways (plus an axe scan) | 1.4.10 Reflow |
| Give the page one main heading | 1.3.1 (best practice) |

- `features/support/accessibility.js`: runs axe-core (`@axe-core/webdriverio`) with the WCAG 2.0/2.1 A and AA tags, **attaches the full results to Allure**, and fails on `critical` and `serious` violations (`A11Y_IMPACTS` to change). The failure message lists each rule, impact, an example element and the help link.
- Page objects: keyboard helpers (`tabTo`, `requestDecisionWithKeyboardFor`), focus style, viewport and overflow, heading count, and the live region around the decision. Steps stay thin.

## Running it
| Where | How |
| --- | --- |
| Local | `npm run test:accessibility` (mock or `BASE_URL`) |
| BrowserStack | `npm run test:bstack:accessibility` (Chrome, Firefox, Safari); `BROWSERSTACK_ACCESSIBILITY=true` adds BrowserStack Accessibility Testing scans in its dashboard |
| Jenkins | **`TEST_SUITE=accessibility`** (new choice), with `BROWSER=local` or `browserstack`; new choice **`BROWSERSTACK_ACCESSIBILITY`** `off`/`on` |
| GitHub | Smoke workflow: against the mock. E2E workflow: against the real web app, as part of regression |

`npm run test:a11y` (the standalone `a11y-test.js`) is now `npm run test:accessibility:scan`. The scenario tag stays `@a11y`.

## CI test errors as annotations
The test steps in both workflows now save their output to `logs/`, and on failure `scripts/report-test-errors.sh` turns the error lines into **GitHub annotations**. The real error then shows on the run summary and in the **CI failure triage comment**, instead of only "exit code 1". It found the one failure on the first run of this PR: `expect().not.toBeNull()` takes no arguments, so the screen reader step needed `assert` (fixed).

## Mock change
The mock's result panel is now an `aria-live="polite"` section, like the real web app, so the screen reader scenario holds on both.

## Checked
- Cucumber dry run: all 13 UI scenarios (4 existing, 9 new) have step definitions.
- Pre-check of the same rules with Playwright and the same axe-core engine, on the **mock** and on the **real web app** behind its own nginx config: no critical or serious violations on the form or any result, keyboard-only journey reaches Accepted, focus outline on all four controls, `aria-live="polite"`, 0px overflow at 320px, one `<h1>`.
- CI: smoke (mock) and E2E (real web app) both green with the 9 scenarios running in Chrome through WebdriverIO.
- Lint passes.

Automated checks cover part of WCAG only; screen reader behaviour and zoom to 200% stay manual (stated in the feature file and README).

author: wuxnz
body: ## Root cause After #58, `/play` could call `performJoin()` while `socket.connected` was still false. Join UI surfaced “Not connected to the game server yet” immediately. Battle **auto-join** could stick with `battleAutoJoinStarted` true and never retry. The same race affects **hosted live games** when players join via PIN and submit a nickname. ## Fix (frontend only) - `waitForPlaySocketConnected()` / `warmPlaySocketConnection()` — connect if needed, deduped warm-up, resolve on `connect` or timeout. - `performJoin()` awaits warm connect before `join_game`; resets battle auto-join on timeout. - Warm socket when PIN is visible on join UI and on `/play` pin effect (battle + live PIN join). - `preparePlaySessionForPin` warms connect instead of forcing reconnect (preserves #55/#58 pin guards and handler binding). - E2E `joinPlayer` helper retries past transient “not connected” copy. - Local dev/preview with `PUBLIC_SOCKET_URL` pointing at Render: try polling before websocket (does not change production `cmaclash.com` transport order). ## Verify | Target | Result | |--------|--------| | `player-socket-session` unit tests | pass | | `live-multi-question` (Standard) on **production** `cmaclash.com` | **fails** — join screen shows “Not connected…” (reproduces reported bug on current prod) | | Vercel **preview** e2e | blocked — cloud agent cannot mint Vercel protection bypass (403) | | Local preview `127.0.0.1` + prod API | socket blocked by cross-origin from browser to Render (expected); not a substitute for preview | **Please run on the PR preview** (or merge and re-run): `battle-after-live-game` ×3, `battle-host-flow`, `live-multi-question.production` (Standard + On player devices through Q3). Preserves #55/#58 behavior otherwise.

author: stevenvictor247
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"stevenvictor247"} -->
_Requested by **Steven Victor** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01SCgswBLpVDSW2ZAmBfScQS?thread=cmsg_01SCgswBLpVDSW2ZAmBfScQSCc4f4d2LCa5kUCcx2brp5h)_

Makes setup and updates hands-off: no more ZIP downloads, `git pull`, or editing `.env`.

## What changed
- **`Install-Agent-HQ.bat`** (one double-click, safe to rerun): installs Git, Python 3.12 and ffmpeg with winget if missing, clones HQ to `%USERPROFILE%\CHADCLIP`, moves an old non-git folder aside, brings over the newest `data/`, `.env`, `config/secrets/` and any *edited* config files from old copies (ZIPs in Downloads etc.; unedited config is recognised by its git blob hash and skipped), makes a `.venv`, installs requirements, creates the Desktop icon and opens HQ.
- **Settings page** (`/settings`, ⚙️ button on the dashboard): fields are generated from `.env.example`, so new agents' settings appear automatically. Saves to `data/settings.json` (outside git), which overrides `.env`. Secrets are never sent back to the browser (only "ends in 1234"). Posting accounts can be switched on there (edits `accounts.yaml` in place, keeping comments). "Save and restart HQ".
- **In-app updates**: HQ checks GitHub every 30 min; the dashboard shows "Update ready (N changes)" with **Update and restart**. ZIP copies get a banner pointing at the installer.
- **Updates can't get stuck any more**: edited `config/` files (e.g. the Boss appending to `vision.md`) are kept; other edited files and clashing untracked files are copied to `data/update-backups/<time>/` first; local commits are kept on a `before-update-*` branch.
- Restart: `start-hq.bat` and the cloud systemd unit restart HQ on exit code 3; otherwise HQ relaunches itself and the new process waits for the port.
- Settings/update/restart POSTs require an `X-HQ: 1` header so other websites can't trigger them.

## Testing
- `pytest`: 45 passed (new `tests/test_settings_update.py` covers settings masking/saving/override, account toggle, the API guard, and an update against a real git remote with local edits and a clashing file).
- Ran HQ, used the Settings page in Chromium, saved, and confirmed it restarted itself.
- The installer's PowerShell parses cleanly in pwsh 7, and its migration step was run against a fake ZIP folder + clone. Not run on a real Windows machine.

[LAB-2894](https://linear.app/protocollabs/issue/LAB-2894) · Goal [LAB-2910](https://linear.app/protocollabs/issue/LAB-2910) · OpenSpec `mcp-agent-grant-safety`

## Summary
- `GET /v1/ai-apps/me` takes an optional `appId` query parameter. When an app session is presented and `appId` names a different app than the one it was minted for, `/me` answers `401 Invalid or expired app session`, with or without `Origin`, before the session is read or slid.
- Without `appId`, `/me` behaves as before. A LabOS token ignores the parameter. `access-check` is unchanged.
- Starter kit 1.18: the member-context skill tells an app's server to call `memberContextEndpoint + "?appId=<appId>"`. Prod serves 1.17, so this is a version bump. WHATS_NEW is replaced with the 1.18 note.
- `docs/AI_APPS.md` → "App-scoped sessions" documents the parameter.

## Testing
- `guards/ai-app-member-context.guard.spec.ts`: 14/14. New cases: another app named without `Origin` → 401 and the session is not read; another app named from the session app's own origin → 401; own app named → 200; LabOS token with `appId` → unchanged.
- `ai-apps-member-context-routes.spec.ts` (7) and `ai-apps-session-routes.spec.ts` (9) pass.
- `ai-apps-starter-kit.spec.ts` (42 + 1 skipped; version pins moved to 1.18, new `?appId=` assertion), `ai-apps-kit-update.spec.ts` (7), `ai-apps-kit-update-notification.spec.ts` (14) pass.

author: 404soonotfound
body:
Fixes BRD-81

> 컴포넌트 코드(첫 커밋 `1162044`)는 작성자가 직접 썼어요. PR 설명과 리뷰 수정 커밋(`424cf50`·`74a0d2f`·`d5b0c84`)은 AI가 작성했어요.

기준: Rev.2.2 · 노션 화면 설계서 [3. 컴포넌트 명세](https://app.notion.com/p/3fa587f5074781f9954dcc66c2b22c6d) · 4. 디자인 시스템

## 바뀐 것

화면(페이지)은 바뀌지 않았고, 공통 부품 8개와 스토리만 추가했어요.

| 부품 | 파일 | 요약 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Banner | `ui/banner.tsx` | amber·red·gray 세 가지. 2줄 구성(무슨 일 → 영향·다음 행동). 배너 전체를 링크로 쓰는 `href`와 끝에 붙는 `action`은 둘 중 하나만 받음(타입으로 막음) |
| Skeleton | `ui/skeleton.tsx` | 실제 행 모양 `BeachRowSkeleton`·블록, 첫 로딩 로더 `RisingSkeleton`. 모양은 `aria-hidden`, 화면 읽기에는 아래 문구만 읽힘. 동작 줄이기면 멈춘 그림 |
| Toast | `ui/toast.tsx` | 하단 탭 위 96px, 4초. `role="status"` 영역은 늘 둠. 포인터나 포커스가 안에 있으면 시간을 멈추고, 행동 버튼(되돌리기)을 누르면 닫힘 |
| EmptyState | `ui/empty-state.tsx` | 원형 아이콘 + 한 문장 + 도움말 + 행동 하나 |
| BeachRow | `beach-row.tsx` | 파고 글리프(값 없음은 "–"와 점선) + 3줄. 변형: `status`(왼쪽 4px 상태색 줄 + 상태 글자), `highlight`, `changedFrom`, `onRemove`(✕). `onRemove`·`removeLabel`은 같이 줘야 함 |
| Chip | `ui/chip.tsx` | default·on·sel, 36px(lg 42px), 제거 가능한 칩(✕ 30px) |
| ViewToggle | `ui/view-toggle.tsx` | 세그먼트. `value`·`onChange`만 받음 |
| SearchField | `ui/search-field.tsx` | 46px, `<label>` 필수(시각적으로 숨김), 포커스 시 파란 2px |

`globals.css`에 첫 로딩 로더 키프레임(`skeleton-rise`·`skeleton-pop`·`skeleton-grow-a/b`)을 추가했어요.

### 새 문구 키 (ko·en 짝 맞음, `check:messages` 72개 통과)

- `row.noValue`: 파고 값 없음 / No wave height
- `row.changed`: 방금 바뀜 · 이전: {previous} / Just changed · was {previous}
- 함께 들어간 키: `verdict.*.sentence`, `verdict.avoid`, `info.offSeason`. 컴포넌트 명세 VerdictCard 결론 문장(S17)과 InfoBadge 문구예요. 이 PR의 부품에서는 아직 쓰지 않아요.

### Figma와 다르게 한 것

- **첫 로딩 로더 `RisingSkeleton`**: Figma에는 없어요. 10/22 사용자 결정으로 새로 추가했고 노션 3장 Skeleton '첫 로딩 변형'에 반영돼 있어요. 색은 `brand-default`의 투명도 단계만 쓰고 새 색 토큰은 만들지 않았어요.
- **토큰 반올림**: Figma 수치를 가까운 기존 토큰 값으로 맞췄어요(새 토큰 없음).
- **토스트 반전색**: 바탕 `text-default`, 글자 `bg-surface`로 반전해 써서 다크에서는 밝은 토스트가 돼요.
- **BeachRow 24시간 미니 선**: 파고 이력(history.json)이 필요해서 상세 차트와 함께 BRD-32에서 붙여요.
- **세그먼트 마지막 선택 기억**: 저장 위치가 화면마다 달라서 쓰는 화면이 맡아요. 부품은 `value`·`onChange`만 받아요.

## 리뷰 전 확인

`/code-review high --fix`를 두 번 돌렸어요(첫 번째는 세션이 끊겨 지적 목록이 사라져서 한 번 더 돌림).

고친 것:
- `424cf50`: BeachRow `onRemove`·`removeLabel` 짝을 타입으로 강제, 빈 텍스트 노드 제거 · 스켈레톤 `<ul>`이 빈 목록으로 읽히지 않게 `aria-hidden` · SearchField에 `id`를 넘기면 label 연결이 끊기던 문제, `outline-none` → `outline-hidden`(고대비 모드에서 바깥선 유지) · `ChipVriant` 오타 · 스토리 파일 이름 `ui-toggle` → `view-toggle`
- `74a0d2f`: 토스트가 '되돌리기'에 포커스가 있어도 4초 뒤 사라지던 문제(WCAG 2.2.1), 행동 버튼을 눌러도 닫히지 않던 문제 · Banner `href`와 `action` 동시 사용을 타입으로 막음 · BeachRow 링크 이름에 지표 이름("파고")을 숨긴 글자로 붙임
- `d5b0c84`: 칩 `sel`과 제거 가능한 칩의 글자색이 판단 상태 토큰(`status-clear-fg`)이던 것을 `brand-default`로 바꿈. 근거: 4. 디자인 시스템 "브랜드 파랑은 선택·버튼·링크에만, 상태 색은 판단 표시에만". 대비는 라이트 4.73, 다크 4.70

고치지 않은 것:
- **BeachRow `status`와 `highlight`를 같이 주면 상태색 줄이 강조 줄에 덮임**: 컴포넌트 명세 BeachRow는 `withStatus`(가까운 순·즐겨찾기)와 `highlight`(PC 지도 선택)를 쓰는 곳이 다른 별개 변형으로 적고, 둘을 함께 쓰는 경우를 정하지 않았어요. 함께 쓰는 화면(PC 지도)을 만들 때 명세를 정하고 맞춰요.
- **Banner·BeachRowSkeleton의 live region이 내용과 같이 나타남**: 컴포넌트 명세에서 live region은 Toast(`role="status"`)와 VerdictCard(`aria-live="polite"`)만 정했고, Banner는 정하지 않았어요. Skeleton은 "장식이라 화면 읽기에는 아래 문구만 읽힘"이라 지금 구현과 맞아요. 나타나는 시점은 부품을 붙이는 화면에서 정해지므로 화면 작업 때 확인해요.

### Codex 리뷰

- P2 1건(토스트 포인터 멈춤과 포커스 멈춤이 서로를 풀어 버림): `ff75787`에서 고침. 포인터·포커스를 따로 세고 둘 중 하나라도 남아 있으면 타이머를 멈춤

## 화면 확인

페이지는 바뀌지 않아서 Storybook(`npm run build-storybook`)에서 확인했어요. 일회성 Playwright 스크립트(커밋 안 함)로 스토리 14개를 390×844·1280, 라이트·다크로 캡처하고 같은 페이지의 `#storybook-root`에 `@axe-core/playwright`(WCAG 2.0·2.1·2.2 A/AA)를 돌렸어요.

- 스토리: UI/EmptyState(Favorites·No Result), UI/Chip(Variants·Toggle), UI/ViewToggle(Playground), UI/SearchField(Default·With Value), UI/Banner(All Tones), UI/Skeleton(Beach Rows·Blocks·First Load), UI/Toast(Visible), Components/BeachRow(Korean·English)
- 결과: 56회 모두 axe 위반 0, 페이지 오류 0, 가로 스크롤 없음, `data-theme` 적용 확인
- 눈으로 본 것: 다크 BeachRow(상태색 줄·강조·점선 값 없음·✕ 변형 구분), 라이트 Chip(sel 글자 브랜드 파랑), 다크 Toast(반전색), 1280 라이트 Banner
- 검사: `typecheck`·`lint`·`test`(152개)·`check:messages` 통과. `prettier --check`는 이 브랜치에서 바뀐 파일 모두 통과(`apps/web/AGENTS.md`·`scripts/check-tokens.mjs` 경고 2건은 main에 이미 있음)
- 확인 안 한 것: E2E 스위트 없음(BRD-39)이라 `test:e2e`는 돌리지 않았어요. 실제 화면에 붙인 상태는 해당 화면 이슈에서 봐요.

## 안티그래비티 점검

### 결과 반영 (`397c500`)

- **P1 · 문구 키**: BeachRow `English` 스토리가 한국어 예시 값(해변명·메타·✕ 이름 등)을 넘겨 한국어가 섞임 → 스토리 예시 값을 언어별로 나눔. 다시 재 보니 영어 스토리의 글자·`aria-label`에 한글 0자
- **P2 · 터치 44px**: Banner 2줄째 행동 버튼('다시 시도'·'위치 정보 켜기') 높이 16.8px → 슬롯에서 `min-h-touch` + 위아래 음수 여백. 44.9×44, 69×44로 바뀌고 배너 높이·줄 모양은 그대로
- **포커스 · 잘림**: BeachRow 링크·✕의 포커스 선이 목록 카드(`overflow-hidden`)에 잘림 → 안쪽 바깥선(`-outline-offset-2`)
- **포커스 · 대비**: 다크 토스트(밝은 바탕)에서 파란 포커스 선 대비 약 2.36:1 → 토스트 안 버튼은 반전색(`bg-surface`) 안쪽 선. 라이트는 흰 선/어두운 바탕, 다크는 어두운 선/밝은 바탕
- 다시 확인: 56회 캡처·axe 위반 0, typecheck·lint·test(152개)·check:messages 통과

author: betagoal
body:
## What & why

Stacked on #507 (`feat/lineage`). This PR re-applies **phase-injection** — the clean,
in-persona replacement for the weak-driver scaffolds that #509 deleted — onto #509's turn
path. The thin `workflow.md` carries only phase titles; the active phase block (and, during
gathering, the active stepped-skill slice) is injected each turn so the live step's
full instructions stay in the freshest position.

## Mechanism

- **Prompts:** thin `workflow.md` (phase titles only) + per-phase
  `agents/<agent>/phases/<slug>.md` + stepped-skill `steps/<NN>-<slug>.md` + orchestrator
  `identity.md`. #509's "Reporting facts & identifiers" persona section is restored into
  `orchestrator/identity.md` and a compact version into the three thin subagent
  `workflow.md` files, so none of #509's correction-ladder content is lost.
- **`api/phases.py` loader** — phase blocks + per-step skill slices, opt-in by file
  presence.
- **Injection (`api/agent.py`)** — the active phase block is injected on each subagent turn,
  at the delegation handoff, on resume, and on the orchestrator turn
  (intake/delegate/monitor/resume/fulfill_help picked by control-flow path, since the
  orchestrator never signals). Delivered on #509's **system channel** (not prepended to the
  user text), so clean user text still flows downstream and orchestrator-only guidance never

author: omega68nova
body:
## Why

The user's OpenStarbound log shows repeated client disconnects with `InvalidMaybeAccessException` at `StarUniverseClient.cpp:1090` while processing `FindUniqueEntityResponse`, `SystemWorldUpdate`, and `ClientContextUpdate`. The client invokes Lua `on<PacketType>Packet` hooks and unconditionally calls `value()` on `maybe<LuaBoolean>()`. Any hook returning `nil` (or a non-boolean result) throws, aborts packet processing and disconnects the client.

## Change

Use `.value(false)` to interpret a missing/non-boolean result as **do not suppress the packet**. Explicit boolean `true` and `false` continue to behave as before.

This is independent of the test mod's separate OpenStarbound-style `require` bug, which is addressed in the mod's v0.1.2 package.

## Validation

Confirmed against the supplied logs and source. No C++ build or game runtime validation available in this session; keep as a reviewable PR until tested.

## :bulb: Motivation and Context

The `posthog-js` LangChain handler records `$ai_web_search_count`, and so do the Python OpenAI, Anthropic and Gemini wrappers, but the Python LangChain callback handler never did. When Anthropic reports `usage.server_tool_use.web_search_requests` (as a dict or an object), `_parse_usage_model` now reads it into a new `web_search_count` field of `ModelUsage`, and the handler adds `$ai_web_search_count` to the event, including a count of 0. Nothing is added when the provider reports no count. `langchain-anthropic` passes the raw Anthropic `usage` (with `server_tool_use`) in `llm_output` for non-streamed calls, which is where the handler reads it; streamed calls only carry the standard `usage_metadata`, so no count is recorded for them. Only this exact count is handled; `posthog-js` also infers a single search from citations or grounding metadata for other providers, which is not ported here.

## :green_heart: How did you test it?

- `TestWebSearchCount` in `posthog/test/ai/langchain/test_callbacks.py`: a response with two web search requests, one with zero, and one without `server_tool_use`. The first two fail on `master` and pass with the change; the third guards the omitted case.
- `posthog/test/ai/langchain/test_callbacks.py`: 83 passed, 8 skipped. `ruff format --check` passes on the touched directories. The rest of the suite and a live LangChain call with the Anthropic web search tool were not run.

Dette er en **samlet faglig og teknisk produksjonsbolk**, ikke flere parallelle PR-er.

### Research
Systematisk gjennomgang av 10 offisielle fagressurser fra FIFA Training Centre, England Football Learning og The FA om tredjemann, sideskifte, pressutløsere, kompakthet, bakrom, restforsvar, gjenvinning, kontring og å spille av press. Full kildeliste, 18×5-tabell med årsaksmekanisme, motgrep og bruddrisiko: `docs/TACTICAL_FOUNDATIONS_RESEARCH_2026-10-21.md`.

### Spillmotor og pedagogikk
- 18/18 kampplaner har nå: konkret mekanisme, årsak til motgrep, egen bruddrisiko, observasjon i kampen, taktisk fase og 2 offisielle kildepeker.
- **Seks uholdbare motgrep** basert på generell `tacticalComplexity` byttet til mer relevante eksisterende motstanderdata (`pressIntensity`, `defensiveStructure`, `pressResistance`, `possessionControl`). Disse er forsiktige proxyer, ikke dokumentasjon på faktisk gjennomførte handlinger.
- Managerens Analyseavdeling forklarer nå hvorfor en kjede kan virke, hvorfor motspill kan bryte den, hvilken risiko den har og hva treneren må se etter.
- Presiserer absolutte/overlovende katalogpåstander («svært få sjanser imot», «trygt», «mange avslutninger») til betingede fotballmekanismer.
- Eksisterende rollebidrag, formasjoner og kildebelagte spillerferdigheter bevares; ingen ny personlig rating eller parallell xG-score. Numeriske modellterskler er spilldesign, ikke verdier hevdet av fagkildene.

### Tester
`audit:tactics` krever kilder, fase, mekanisme, risikogrense og konkret motgrepsdimensjon for **samtlige 18 planer**. `sim:match-plan` beskytter tilsvarende og gamle effektkjeder. CI/relevante tester før merge.

Referanser: [FIFA high press](https://www.fifatrainingcentre.com/en/game/game-analysis/out-of-possession/high-press.php), [FIFA switch of play](https://www.fifatrainingcentre.com/en/game/game-analysis/in-possession/switch-of-play.php), [FIFA counter-attack](https://www.fifatrainingcentre.com/en/game/game-analysis/transition-to-attacking/the-counter-attack.php), [FIFA third player](https://www.fifatrainingcentre.com/en/game/game-analysis/in-possession/third-player-combinations.php), [FA principles](https://learn.englandfootball.com/articles-and-resources/coaching/resources/2022/What-are-the-principles-of-football).

author: wood1974
body:
## What
`server/app/time_audit.py` runs on each upload and the result is stored as `time_label` / `time_notes` and returned as `time` by `GET /shield/captures`. It never blocks a photo (same as the Apple check).

It compares what the server has:
- the record with the one before it in the same chain: same boot, the wall clock must move by the monotonic clock's amount (120000 ms limit, strict, both directions); a restart, a missing boot identity or a backward monotonic clock gives `UNVERIFIED TIME` (not tampering, no interval to judge);
- GPS time with the phone's wall clock;
- the phone's clock with the server's: a photo cannot have been taken after the server received it. Waiting a long time for signal is never flagged.

Labels: `CONSISTENT`, `UNVERIFIED TIME`, `DEVICE CLOCK MISMATCH`, `NOT CHECKED`. `CONSISTENT` needs a real comparison to have passed and nothing unverifiable; the server-clock check alone never earns it. Any one disagreement is a mismatch.

The phone's own app already computes the same rules against its local ticket; this is the server-side check on what it uploads. Rules are the old `Tradedeck-api/shield/time_audit.py` rules, adapted because the server has no ticket clock (tickets are local today).

## Honest limits
- It checks the phone's clocks against each other. It is not a timestamp, and `CONSISTENT` does not show a photo was taken when it says (see the outside-timestamp item, not in this PR).
- A record whose predecessor is not on the server (uploaded later, or refused) reads `NOT CHECKED`; it is not recomputed when the predecessor arrives.
- The result is not yet shown in the app or in the share-code compare reply (#11): the app change goes in its own PR, and the compare reply after #11 merges.

## Data
`captures` gains two nullable columns on startup (idempotent `ALTER TABLE`). Existing rows keep NULL and read `NOT CHECKED` ("stored before the clock check existed"). Test covers upgrading an old-shape table.

## Verified
`cd server && pytest`: 163 passed (fresh virtualenv): boundary 120000/120001 both ways, restart, boot id, backward monotonic, GPS agree/disagree, ahead-of-server, long wait, first record, label priority, chain through real uploads, never blocks, old table upgrade.

## Not verified
Not tried against records from a real phone or the live server. Merging deploys to production within seconds; the column change runs on the live database at startup.

author: mykyta
body:
[LAB-2895](https://linear.app/protocollabs/issue/LAB-2895) · Goal [LAB-2910](https://linear.app/protocollabs/issue/LAB-2910) · OpenSpec `mcp-agent-grant-safety`

## Summary
- Each MCP refresh rotates the pair and remembers the hash of the refresh token it replaced (new table `McpUsedRefreshToken`, FK to `McpAuthorization`, cascade).
- A rotated refresh token presented again revokes the grant through the existing `revokeAuthorization`: current access and refresh tokens stop working, and the grant's agent app sessions end. The request gets 401. PostHog event `mcp-refresh-token-reuse` (`memberUid`, `authorizationUid`, `clientName`).
- Rotation is a conditional `updateMany` on the token still being current, in one transaction with the hash insert. Of two concurrent refreshes with one token, one succeeds and the other is handled as reuse (strict OAuth 2.1 reuse detection).
- A new consent (code exchange) clears the grant's remembered hashes, so tokens from before it get a plain 401 and can't revoke the new grant. Unknown tokens also get a plain 401.
- A daily cron (`mcp-used-refresh-token-cleanup`, 03:45) prunes hashes older than `MCP_REFRESH_TOKEN_TTL_MS`.

**Why a new table:** keeping only the last rotated hash on `McpAuthorization` is too weak. A thief who refreshes twice pushes the stolen token out of that slot, and the real agent then gets a plain 401 instead of tripping revocation. The table holds about one row per hour per active agent and is pruned.

**Trade-off:** an agent that retries a refresh after a lost response is revoked and the member reconnects once. The event shows how often real clients hit this.

## Testing
- New `mcp-oauth-refresh-reuse.spec.ts` (7, in-memory Prisma fake through the real approve → code → refresh flow): rotation; reuse revokes the access token, the refresh token and the agent sessions, and emits the event; concurrent refreshes yield one success; other grants of the member stay live; a pre-re-consent token gets a plain 401 with no revoke; an unknown token gets a plain 401; the cron prunes only old rows.
- All `src/mcp` suites: 9 suites / 106 tests pass.
- Migration SQL applied on the local DB inside a rolled-back transaction. The local DB has an older failed migration (`20260606120000_add_investor_lists`) that blocks `migrate deploy`, unrelated to this PR.
- `tsc -p apps/web-api/tsconfig.build.json`: no errors in `src` (258 pre-existing `node_modules` errors).

author: dimchansky
body:
Prepares the next release: two reader-error fixes, stronger tests, a rewritten README and a non-mutating `make check`. Exported API, `String()` names and performance are unchanged.

## Fixes (both present since v1.1.1)

- **Error lost after empty reads.** A read that returned an error was counted as an empty read, so a source that returned `io.EOF` or a real error after 99 `(0, nil)` reads got `io.ErrNoProgress` instead. Only `(0, nil)` now counts.
- **Timing-dependent UTF-16 detection.** `FE FF 00 41` returned together with a non-EOF error was `Unknown` (BOM kept), but the same bytes with the error on the next `Read` were `UTF16BigEndian`. With 4 bytes read, UTF-32 is already ruled out, so UTF-16 is now detected in both cases. The historical 2–3-byte `FE FF`/`FF FE` + non-EOF error case still yields `Unknown`.

A differential run of old vs new detection over ~5.7M read schedules found differences only in these two cases.

## Tests

- Regression tests for both fixes (they fail without the fix).
- Exact `Encoding.String()` names; `Skip` on a `*Reader` returns the same reader; 1–4 byte destination buffers.
- `FuzzSkip` against an independent BOM table (EOF-terminated streams, whole and one-byte reads).
- Benchmarks. benchstat before/after (Go 1.27.1, Apple M1 Max, count=10): no change in time, 68 B/op and 2 allocs/op both.

## Docs and tooling

- README rewritten: purpose and boundaries, Go 1.19+, one complete example, BOM table, Behavior section, pkg.go.dev badge.
- Go doc comments fixed (`Encoding` is a defined type; `Read` does not search for a BOM on each call).
- Examples print readable output; `ExampleSkip_utf16` shows the payload is not transcoded. The `QF1010` lint exclusion is no longer needed.
- `make check` only checks; `make task` runs fix, fmt, then check sequentially.

Verified locally on Go 1.27.1 and 1.19.13: vet, race + shuffle tests, golangci-lint v2.15.0, 30 s fuzz, README example compiled and run.

author: ronger-x
body:
## Summary

Role-play replies mix speech with parenthesised stage directions whose tone changes within one reply. `instructions` applies to the whole request, and splitting the reply into several requests changes the voice between them.

- `POST /v1/audio/speech` accepts `segments: [{text, instructions}]`. Each sentence gets the request-wide `instructions` joined with its segment's style as the parenthesised control prefix.
- All segments share one reference in one request, so the voice stays fixed. Segment styles never take part in voice selection (`X-Voice` is unchanged).
- Upstream ignores the control prefix in transcript ("Hi-Fi") cloning ("When Hi-Fi mode is enabled, the control instruction is ignored."). A request with any segment style therefore clones from the reference audio only. Requests without segments behave as before, including those with only a top-level `instructions`.
- `docs/api.md` documents the field and how to phrase acoustic descriptions.

## Verification

- `python -m unittest discover -s tests` — 19 passed, 1 skipped (CUDA); `node --test tests/pcm-ring.test.mjs` — 3 passed
- Deployed to 192.168.88.155:7860 (branch checked out on the host). A 43 s role-play reply built by Rodak, with 3 styled segments: 200, `X-Voice: default`, SenseVoice transcription similarity 0.93, no control words read aloud.
- Effect of the controls is measurable but small. On one sentence with reference-only cloning, "轻声，语速放慢" lowered median F0 240 → 225 Hz. "情绪激动，语速很快" shortened it 6.2 s → 5.4 s. Upstream notes control results vary between runs.

author: fernanda-rabacal
body:
Closes #35

## O que muda
Adiciona "Continuar com Google" no `/login` e no `/cadastro`. O fluxo é Authorization Code com PKCE: o Next.js é o redirect URI e o client secret fica só no backend.

- **Conta já ligada ao Google** → entra direto.
- **E-mail que já tem conta com senha** (e verificado pelo Google) → a conta é vinculada e passa a aceitar senha e Google.
- **Conta nova** → `/cadastro/google` pede CPF e se a pessoa é organizadora; só então o usuário é criado e logado.

### Backend
- Migração `20261021120000_google_login`: `password` opcional e `google_id` único (guarda o `sub` do Google).
- `POST /login/google` (rate limit `login-ip`) e `POST /signup/google` (rate limit `signup`).
- O token de cadastro dura 10 minutos, usa a audience `google-signup` e é recusado como token de acesso.
- `GoogleIdentityClient` é o único ponto que fala com o Google, o que facilita o mock nos testes.
- A validação de CPF virou o decorator `IsCpf()`, usado também em `POST /users`.
- `google_id` fica fora das respostas da API, como a senha.

### Frontend
- Route handlers `/auth/google` e `/auth/google/callback`; `state` e `code_verifier` ficam no cookie httpOnly `golden_oauth`.
- Tela `/cadastro/google` e a Server Action `completeGoogleSignUp`.
- `/login?erro=google` mostra o aviso de erro.

## Configuração
- `backend/.env`: `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID`, `GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET`, `GOOGLE_REDIRECT_URI`
- `frontend/.env.local`: `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID`, `GOOGLE_REDIRECT_URI`
- Google Console: cadastrar `http://localhost:3000/auth/google/callback` (e a URL de produção) como URI de redirecionamento autorizado.

## Testes
- [x] Backend: lint, typecheck e testes unitários (210)
- [x] E2E `google-auth.e2e-spec.ts` (7) e as suítes de usuário e rate limit (37)
- [x] Frontend: lint, typecheck e prettier
- [x] Manual com client ID falso: redirect para o Google, `redirect` malicioso sanitizado, erro e cancelamento caem em `/login?erro=google`
- [ ] Fluxo completo com o cliente Google real
- [ ] Suíte e2e de pagamentos e Playwright (não rodadas)

## Fora do escopo
- Usuário só do Google definir uma senha no perfil
- Desvincular o Google no perfil
- Teste Playwright do fluxo com o Google
