author: jacklionheart
body:
## What changes for users

A launch now says where its runs may go:

```sh
etude pool add lab                                   # machines you own
etude machine add mini me@mini.local --pool lab      # cost $0, never expires
etude ondemand add cpu --provider runpod --vcpus 2 --memory-gb 4 --max 1 --max-usd-per-hour 0.20
etude availability --rent cpu                        # asks the provider; rents nothing
etude launch job.py --rent cpu --quote               # first wave and maximum spend; rents nothing
etude launch job.py --pool lab --rent cpu            # free owned machines first, then rent
etude machines --all                                 # owned: cost, expiry; rented: hardware, cost
```

- **Pool** is only machines you own. Owned machines gain `cost_usd` (committed, default 0) and `expires_at` (default never; `machine add --cost-usd/--expires-at`). At expiry a machine leaves its pool; an attempt still on it ends `lost/machine_lost` and retries wherever the run may go.
- **OnDemand** (`etude ondemand add|max|image|startup`, `etude ondemands`) is a `MachineTemplate` plus a budget: machines at once and `max_usd_per_hour`, shared by every launch that names it.
- `--pool P` uses only P's machines; `--rent R` only rents from R; both use a free machine of P before renting. Python mirrors this: `queue/launch/queue_cohort/launch_cohort(..., pool=, rent=)`, plus `quote(...)` and `availability(rent)`, also over the SSH controller.
- `etude availability --rent R [--timeout S]` (wait) and `etude launch ... --quote` (wait; records and rents nothing).
- `etude default --pool P --rent R` replaces `etude pool default`; `etude rent --ondemand R` replaces `rent --pool`.
- Removed with no compatibility path: `Pool.on_demand_template`, `Pool.max_on_demand`, `MachineTemplate.max_usd_per_hour`, `pool add`'s provider/template/max flags, `pool max`, `pool image`, `pool default`. Executions answer `offer()` (hardware, price, availability) instead of `price()`.
- Pools and on-demands share one namespace; each has its own placement lock and `tick` visits every pool before any on-demand. Sessions read their supply from their machine.
- Prototype database schema 7 → 8; older files are refused.

Deferred: used/idle accounting for owned machines' committed cost (shown, not yet apportioned); a per-period dollar budget on an on-demand.

## Checks

`uv run pytest` (386 passed), `uv run mypy`, `uv run ruff check .`, `uv run ruff format --check .`. New tests cover pool-only, rent-only, pool-then-rent placement, expiry with retry, `--quote` (one provider call, nothing created) and `availability` (one provider call), and `machines` showing cost and expiry.

## Live smoke (RunPod CPU, fresh ETUDE_HOME under /tmp)

- `availability --rent cpu`: cpu3c 2 vCPUs at $0.06/hour, rentable.
- `launch job.py --rent cpu --quote` → "rent cpu3c 2 vCPUs at $0.06/hour, at most $0.02; nothing rented", then `launch --rent cpu`: succeeded on a rented cpu3c pod, job output read back, pod deleted.
- `launch pair.py --pool local --rent cpu --cohort mixed --parallel 2`: seed 1 ran on this computer, seed 2 on a rented pod; both succeeded and the pod was deleted.
- `etude machines --all` and RunPod's pod list confirm both pods ended. Spend under $0.01.

author: gmr714
body:
## O que é

Terceira fatia do plano (`docs/specs/mapeamento-obsidian.plano.md`): a rodada passa a alimentar o `agenda-data.json` do app com tarefas sugeridas e projetos.

> **Base: a branch da F2 (#2).** Depois do merge da #2, troque a base deste PR para `main`, se o GitHub não trocar sozinho.

```bash
node sync/run.js --vault --desde AAAA-MM-DD [--dry-run] [--agenda-file arquivo | --sem-agenda]
```

## Regras das tarefas

- **Origem:** tarefas novas saem só do resumo mais recente de cada projeto. Os próximos passos de dias antigos ou já foram feitos ou foram substituídos pelos do dia seguinte.
- **Entrada:** chegam como `sugerida`, com contexto, prazo (quando houver) e um id estável.
- **Sem repetição:** o mesmo título, mesmo com outra caixa, acento ou pontuação, nunca volta depois de descartado ou feito.
- **Fechamento:** as tarefas abertas do projeto vão no prompt. As que a sessão mostra feitas fecham sozinhas (`doneAuto`), com evidência e com o status anterior guardado para desfazer.
- **Projetos:** nascem com prioridade média. Prioridade, meta e prazo definidos por você nunca são sobrescritos.
- **Segurança:** a rodada guarda um backup diário do arquivo antes de gravar. No dry-run, grava só na prévia.

## App e servidor

- `agenda-merge.js` é compartilhado entre servidor e navegador e faz vencer o `updatedAt` mais novo. Assim, uma cópia velha do navegador não desfaz o que a rodada fechou.
- `server.js` guarda `projects` e `opens`, e só sobe quando é executado direto, o que permite testá-lo.
- As telas atuais (semana, lista, prazos, contadores) ignoram as tarefas da rodada até o checklist da F4 existir.

## Verificado

- `npm test`: 74 testes passando.
- Dry-run com uma cópia da agenda real: as 12 entradas manuais foram preservadas, e entraram 56 tarefas sugeridas em 15 projetos. O arquivo real não mudou (mesmo hash antes e depois).
- No navegador, com a prévia:
  - a lista mostra só as 12 entradas manuais e nenhum bloco da semana vem de tarefa sugerida;
  - os 15 projetos continuam no servidor depois que o navegador manda a cópia dele;
  - nenhum erro no console.

## Fora deste PR

- Gravar a agenda real: só depois do merge, para o app antigo não mostrar as 56 tarefas como tarefas comuns.
- Checklist (F4) e rodada diária (F5).

author: vitorssemilio-afk
body:
## Causa raiz

O Prompt 62 corrigiu o **cálculo** dos 40 dias (`calcularDiaCiclo` já só lia `cliente.kickoff_realizado_em`, nunca data agendada/criação), mas não corrigiu a **navegação**: o CTA "Agendar Kickoff" na tela do Mapeamento (`src/pages/Mapeamento.tsx`, seção "Kickoff") só era renderizado quando `implementacaoExistente` já existia:

```tsx
{implementacaoExistente && (
  <Link to={...}>Agendar Kickoff</Link>
)}
```

Sem implementação criada, essa seção só mostrava texto informativo, sem nenhum botão — o único caminho restante era subir até o cabeçalho e clicar em **"Iniciar implementação de CRM"**, que cria o registro em `implementacoes_crm`. Na prática, o consultor continuava sendo obrigado a "iniciar a implementação" antes de conseguir agendar o Kickoff — exatamente o problema que o Prompt 62 deveria ter eliminado, mas só tratou pela metade (corrigiu o motor de cálculo, não o fluxo de UI que leva até lá).

## Achado da auditoria (seção 16 do pedido)

Consulta real no banco mostrou que, em **8 dos 10 clientes mais antigos** da base, `kickoff_realizado_em` é **idêntico, ao segundo**, ao `created_at` da implementação (Casa Mineira, D'AZUL, Sass Nutri, Mansão Fato, Emporium Car Multimarcas, Bill Motos, Colégio Ieprol, Refine Grooming Concept). `git log -S "kickoff_realizado_em" -- src/pages/Mapeamento.tsx` confirma que versões anteriores do Mapeamento.tsx (commits `0954efc`, `6d34a1d`, revertido em `d1a6987` do Prompt 62) escreviam esse campo como efeito colateral de uma ação do fluxo antigo — coerente com o padrão observado. Ou seja, o cronograma oficial (Dia X/40, ciclo) desses 8 clientes está rodando a partir do momento em que a implementação foi *criada no sistema*, não do Kickoff real com o cliente.

**Não alterei nenhum desses registros.** Por instrução explícita do prompt ("não reiniciar implementações que já começaram legitimamente", "apresentar diagnóstico antes de modificar"), este PR só documenta o achado — a correção desses marcos históricos exige decisão administrativa (já existe mecanismo de correção auditável de datas de marco, usado em outras telas da implementação) e dados que só o Vitor/consultor responsável têm (a data real de cada Kickoff). Os 2 clientes mais recentes (Gustare, Ecila — criados já depois do Prompt 62) não têm esse padrão: Gustare tem `kickoff_realizado_em` real e distinto da criação, Ecila está `null` corretamente aguardando.

## Correção

- `handleAgendarKickoff` (novo): se a implementação já existe, só navega pro formulário de agendamento (`?aba=reunioes&tipo=kickoff&acao=agendar`); se não existe, cria o registro (mesmo insert de sempre, em `preparacao_crm`, nunca grava nenhum campo de Kickoff) e já cai direto no formulário ao fechar o `AplicarTemplateModal` — nunca exige um clique isolado em outro botão antes.
- Botão do cabeçalho renomeado de "Iniciar implementação de CRM" → **"Preparar implementação"**: ele nunca iniciou os 40 dias (só cria o registro em `preparacao_crm`), mas o nome antigo dava a entender que era um passo obrigatório de "início". Continua existindo como ação administrativa opcional (ex.: abrir a implementação antes de agendar, pra revisar checklist/template).
- `criarImplementacaoCrm` extraído como função compartilhada entre as duas ações, pra não duplicar o insert.

## Fluxo resultante

```
Funil pronto pra apresentação → [Agendar Kickoff] → formulário de reunião
  (implementação criada nos bastidores, se ainda não existia — sem nenhum
   campo de Kickoff/cronograma tocado)
→ reunião agendada, Implementação: preparacao_crm, contador: não iniciado
→ Confirmar realização (aba Reuniões) → kickoff_realizado_em = data real
→ 40 dias/ciclo calculados a partir daí (nenhuma mudança neste ponto —
   já estava correto desde o Prompt 62)
```

## Dados

- Data prevista: `reunioes.data_hora` (tipo kickoff) / `clientes.kickoff_agendado_para` (sincronizado por `sincronizarMarcoCliente`, já existente).
- Data real: `clientes.kickoff_realizado_em` — única fonte do `calcularDiaCiclo`, só gravada pela confirmação explícita na aba Reuniões.
- Início oficial da implementação: nenhum campo próprio — é derivado (implícito) de `kickoff_realizado_em` existir; `implementacoes_crm.status` descreve a fase operacional (`preparacao_crm` → `crm_em_configuracao` → …), não controla o contador.

## Interface

Botão "Agendar Kickoff" aparece em: Mapeamento/Funil (seção Kickoff, corrigida aqui), Resumo do cliente e Home (ambos via `resolverProximoPassoGeral`/`resolverAcaoOperacional` em `acaoOperacional.ts`, que já direcionava pro Mapeamento quando a implementação não existia — nenhuma mudança necessária ali, só precisava que o destino funcionasse).

## Testes

- `tsc`, `lint`, `vitest` (48/48) e `build` — todos passando.
- **Teste B do pedido (obrigatório), verificado por leitura de código + auditoria real**: com `implementacaoExistente == null` e `mapeamento.status` em `pronto_kickoff`/`kickoff_agendado`/etc., o botão "Agendar Kickoff" agora está presente e seu `onClick` cria a implementação e navega pro formulário — sem passar por nenhum botão "Iniciar implementação".
- **Teste H (permissões)**, verificado via SQL real: a policy RLS `implementacoes_crm_por_vinculo` (USING e WITH CHECK) já exige `sou_administrador() OR consultor_responsavel_id = meu_consultor_id() OR ... cliente.consultor_responsavel_id = meu_consultor_id()` — como `criarImplementacaoCrm` usa o mesmo insert de sempre, essa proteção já se aplica sem nenhuma mudança.
- **Testes C/D/E/F/J (contador, remarcação, confirmação, consistência)**: nenhuma lógica de cronograma foi tocada neste PR — já cobertos pelo Prompt 62; não há regressão possível aqui porque `calcularDiaCiclo` nem é chamado neste fluxo.
- **Dependem de validação manual (não executados interativamente)**: clicar o fluxo completo na aplicação real (Teste B/E ponta a ponta), Teste I (mobile) e Teste G num cliente com Kickoff já realizado — recomendo abrir um cliente em "Pronto para Kickoff" sem implementação ainda criada e clicar "Agendar Kickoff" pra confirmar visualmente.

author: chrisgoddard
body:
Stacked on PR 30 (`feat/durable-worker-role`). Retarget to `main` after PR 30 merges.

## Why

intel/pi-voice runs one long-lived durable Pi `AgentSession`, with Pi extensions loaded, inside its own daemon. pi-fabric builds that session internally, but the only public durable entry is `./durable` (`createPiDurableRunner`), a leaf adapter with no `AgentSession` and no extensions. Tracked in intel/pi-voice issue 13.

## Change

New public subpath `pi-fabric/durable-host` (`src/durable-host.ts`), exporting:

- `createDurableAgentSession`, `DurableAgent`
- `createDurableWorkerRuntime`, type `DurableWorkerOptions`
- `openDurableWorkerStorage`
- `declareWorkerSessionRole`, `DURABLE_WORKER_POLICY_ENTRY_TYPE`, type `WorkerRoleSessionManager`

`declareWorkerSessionRole(sessionManager): "seeded" | "already-seeded"` is added to PR 30's `src/durable/worker-role-seed.ts`. It writes the `context-aware.policy.v1` worker-role entry into an existing session before the first prompt. It shares one private `workerRolePolicyData()` with `workerRoleEntry`, so there is a single copy of the entry shape, and it writes nothing when a worker-role entry is already present.

Also: `package.json` exports and `scripts/build.mjs` entry; `scripts/assert-build-artifacts.mjs` lists `durable-host.js` as a stable entry allowed to import the Pi SDK by name (it runs in the embedding host's Pi install) and forbids `src/durable-host.ts` and `src/durable/session.ts` in the startup graph; a `docs/durable-pi.md` section on embedding, including the host's own supervise-and-restart duty.

## Tests

- `tests/durable-host-entry.test.ts`: exact export list; a faux-model session runs to the end of its first turn through the built entry.
- `tests/durable-worker-role-seed.test.ts`: writes the literal entry once; a repeat call writes nothing; still writes when the only policy declares a different role. Mutation check: changing the written role to `foreground` turns 10 tests red.
- `tests/build-artifacts.test.ts`: exports map shape, startup-graph marker, required `durable-host.js`.

## Checks (on `a9c319c0`)

| Command | Exit |
|---|---|
| `bun run typecheck` | 0 |
| `PI_TEST_BASE=70b1f483 bun run test:affected` (1068 + 255 tests) | 0 |
| `bun run build` (artifact check) | 0 |
| `bun run assert:lazy-graph` | 0 |

Startup byte budget (753314) and file budget (38) unchanged.

Not sent upstream to fabric-runtime/pi-fabric.

author: bob-stewart
body: Fixes #860 ## Summary `validate_avc` now walks `parent_avc_id` and denies the credential when any ancestor is revoked, missing, suspended, or quarantined. An ancestor cycle or a walk past 16 hops denies with `AncestorDepthExceeded`. Signed standing records cover suspend, quarantine, and resume: - Domain `exo.avc.standing.v1`. The signer must be the credential issuer or principal. - No standing record leaves the credential Active. - The latest record is verified at read time. A forged or unverifiable latest record is `StandingUnknown` and does not fall through to an older record. - A revoked ancestor still reports `Revoked` after higher ancestors are checked. A missing ancestor is `AncestorMissing`. - `POST /api/v1/avc/standing/suspend`, `/quarantine`, and `/resume` store only a record whose standing matches the route. Un-revoke stays out of this change. Stacked on #872 because this changes the same AVC node route surface (`crates/exo-node/src/avc.rs`). ## Path classification - `crates/exo-avc/src/standing.rs` — EXOCHAIN core - `crates/exo-avc/src/lib.rs` — EXOCHAIN core - `crates/exo-avc/src/registry.rs` — EXOCHAIN core - `crates/exo-avc/src/validation.rs` — EXOCHAIN core - `crates/exo-node/src/avc.rs` — EXOCHAIN core (node AVC runtime) No `governance/`, CI, or deployment contract changed. Gates 6 and 7 remain the known quinn-proto failure in #864. ## Tests - `cargo +1.98.1 test -p exochain-avc --lib` — 270 passed - `cargo +1.98.1 test -p exochain-node --bin exochain standing_` — 11 passed (AVC standing cases plus existing passport/zerodentity standing filters) - `cargo +1.98.1 test -p exochain-node --bin exochain validation_denies_child_of_revoked_or_missing_ancestor` — 1 passed - `cargo +1.98.1 clippy -p exochain-avc -p exochain-node --all-targets -- -D warnings` — passed - `cargo +nightly-2026-09-21 fmt -p exochain-avc -p exochain-node -- --check` — passed - `RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo +1.98.1 doc -p exochain-avc --no-deps` — passed Do not merge. author: jbachorik
body:
**What does this PR do?**:
Removes the remaining instance of the unreachable dead code flagged in #592: the musl variant of `t07_body` in `ddprof-lib/src/test/cpp/thread_teardown_safety_ut.cpp` still ended with `ProfiledThread::release(); return nullptr;` after the `while (true) { pthread_testcancel(); usleep(100); }` loop — statements that can never execute, because the only exit from the loop is cancellation, which calls `pthread_exit(PTHREAD_CANCELED)` (musl `src/thread/pthread_cancel.c::__cancel()`), runs the registered cleanup handler and terminates the thread.

`pthread_cleanup_pop(0)` is kept: musl's `pthread_cleanup_push`/`pop` are paired macros that open/close a `do { ... } while (0)` block, so the pop is lexically required even though it is unreachable. The tail is now marked `__builtin_unreachable()`, mirroring the glibc variant.

Also updates AGENTS.md / README.md / utils/README.md to recommend colima-backed Docker (`--container=docker`) for container tests on macOS instead of podman: podman aborts container commands locally because its credential-helper lookup for the Datadog registries (ddtool) cannot reach vault outside the CI network. The script's default runtime is unchanged.

**Motivation**:
Closes #592 (sphinx review finding). The glibc half of the issue — the `__pthread_unregister_cancel` / `sigaction` restore / `ProfiledThread::release()` dead tail in the same function — was already removed on main; this PR completes the fix by removing the analogous musl-path dead code that survived, so the issue is fully addressed.

**Additional Notes**:
Reachability verified against primary sources:
- musl: `pthread_testcancel` → `__testcancel` → `__cancel()` → `pthread_exit(PTHREAD_CANCELED)` (declared `_Noreturn`); `__pthread_exit` walks the `cancelbuf` chain, running the cleanup handler.
- glibc: `nptl/unwind.c:unwind_stop()` longjmps to the `cancel_jmp_buf` registered by `__pthread_register_cancel`.

**How to test the change?**:
Behavior-preserving (test-only) change; `thread_teardown_safety_ut` passes before and after:

```
./utils/run-containers-tests.sh --container=docker --libc=musl --config=debug --gtest --gtest-task=thread_teardown_safety_ut --mount --run
./utils/run-containers-tests.sh --container=docker --libc=glibc --config=debug --gtest --gtest-task=thread_teardown_safety_ut --mount --run
```

Both report `BUILD SUCCESSFUL`; the executable's gtest output shows `14 tests ... PASSED` on musl, including `ForcedUnwindWithConcurrentSignalDoesNotCrash`.

**For Datadog employees**:
- [ ] If this PR touches code that signs or publishes builds or packages, or handles
  credentials of any kind, I've requested a security review (run the `dd:platform-security-review`
  skill, or file a request via the [PSEC review form](https://datadoghq.atlassian.net/jira/software/c/projects/PSEC/forms/form/direct/7861446195161534/37715)).
  `bewaire` also runs automatically on every PR.
- [x] This PR doesn't touch any of that.

author: greenhat616
body:
## Why

On Windows, `ProcessHandle::graceful_kill` terminates the Job Object straight away, so a core never runs its own cleanup. Meow restores the adapter DNS on Ctrl+C; a hard kill leaves it pointing at `127.0.0.1` (libnyanpasu/clash-nyanpasu#5883).

The core runs with `CREATE_NO_WINDOW` and owns a hidden console, while the GUI and the service have none. Sending it Ctrl+C means attaching to that console, which changes the caller's console state, so the attach happens in a short-lived helper process instead of the host.

## Change

- `Command::windows_shutdown_helper(path)` names an executable that dispatches `windows_shutdown_helper_entry()` before its normal startup. The method exists on every platform; Unix ignores it and keeps sending SIGTERM.
- The first `GracefulKill` starts `<helper> --nyanpasu-process-shutdown <pid>`, which attaches to the core's console, ignores Ctrl+C itself and sends it. The helper runs within the existing `kill_grace` deadline.
- Repeated stops neither resend Ctrl+C (some cores treat a second one as an immediate exit) nor extend the deadline.
- A missing, failing or hung helper kills the process tree at once; a core that ignores Ctrl+C is killed when the grace runs out.
- The engine holds the child's process handle until it reaps the child, and disarms the helper then, so a request never reaches a reused PID.

## Downstream

- nyanpasu-runtime #457 wires the helper through the core manager and the service.
- clash-nyanpasu #5916 passes the packaged service binary from the GUI.

## Test plan

- [x] `process_kill`: Ctrl+C lets the child exit 0 and run `Drop`; an ignored Ctrl+C is sent once and the tree is killed after the grace; a missing helper falls back without waiting; a hung helper uses the same grace and is reaped.
- [x] Unit and kill/output/stdin/supervisor tests, 47 in total, in the nyanpasu-runtime workspace on Windows. The Ctrl+C tests need a host with a console: they pass under PowerShell and fail under Git Bash, where the helper cannot attach.
- [x] Clippy and rustfmt; the remaining warning is already on main.
- [x] Before the helper was simplified, a real CoreManager ran it under a GUI host and under an SCM service as LocalSystem in Session 0: the dummy core exited 0 after cleanup, and the host never gained a console.
- [ ] Linux and macOS builds. A local Linux cross-check hit a compiler crash in dependencies, so CI is the first run.
- [ ] Real Meow restoring the adapter DNS, in a packaged build.

author: patrick-m-bourget
body:
Closes #24.

## Summary

Style is a stored, non-automatable host parameter (`style`, listed first) in the frozen order. It picks the Character the Engine plays. Choosing a Character Style through the Plugin Shell writes its defaults as one undo step. The lab came first.

```text
tools/dyn-lab        STYLE_DEFAULTS, `styles`, --style on transfer/step/bursts/autogain/colour; USAGE.md "Styles"
comp1/Style.h        enum class Style (frozen), one row per Style: Character + optional StyleDefaults
                     characterOf(), hasDefaults(), applyStyle() (ADR 0002's fields only), styled()
SettingsReader       .character = characterOf (Style)        // Style alone decides it
PluginProcessor
  offeredStyles()    the four Characters
  chooseStyle(s)     beginTransaction; setTogether(Style + defaults); endTransaction   // false for a Source Style
```

| Style | Threshold | Ratio | Knee | Attack | Release | Auto Release | Hold | Range | Colour |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Clean | −18 | 4:1 | 6 dB | 10 ms | 100 ms | off | 0 | 60 | 100% |
| VCA | −18 | 4:1 | 3 dB | 10 ms | 100 ms | off | 0 | 60 | 100% |
| FET | −18 | 4:1 | 3 dB | 0.5 ms | 50 ms | off | 0 | 60 | 100% |
| Opto | −18 | 3:1 | 12 dB | 10 ms | 100 ms | off | 0 | 60 | 100% |

Every Style writes the Gate and the Limiter off, at their defaults. The brief's starting values stood; USAGE.md gives the reasons. For #25 and #26: each Style is one `StyleDescription` row. #25 adds its Comp Curve and Comp Follow to it, #26 fills the Source Style rows, and `offeredStyles()` picks them up from `hasDefaults()`.

## Evidence

- `StyleTest`: the table matches `dynlab.py styles` row for row, Clean's row equals a default `Settings`, and `applyStyle` touches only ADR 0002's fields.
- `StyleParameterTest`:
  - VCA, FET and Opto compress differently from Clean at host level, and Bus plays bit for bit as Clean.
  - `chooseStyle` from a state with every parameter moved writes exactly the Style's defaults, inside gestures, as one undo step, and undo and redo put everything back.
  - Restore, Preset load, A/B, undo and redo never write the defaults.
  - States at version 1 and 2 with no Style, and a Preset with none, restore as Clean. Saving, loading and saving again gives the same bytes.
- **Before:** with the `SettingsReader` mapping taken out, "Style alone decides the Settings' Character" and "Style set by the host reaches the Engine" fail (2 of 11 Style cases). **After:** all pass.
- `ClickFreeTest`: four new Style rows (Clean→VCA/FET/Opto, FET↔Opto) are click-free and give the same output at every block cut. `RealtimeSafetyTest`: a Style change doesn't allocate.
- Harness on the tip: `docs`, `build`, `test` and `cpu` pass. `null 6c37484`: every existing scene reads `exact`, and the 4 Style scenes are `new`. `test_dynlab.py` passes (136 tests).
- CPU figures (Apple M3, 48/96 kHz): VCA's Style defaults 0.53%/1.07%, FET's 0.75%/1.51%, Opto's 0.82%/1.64%, the same as each Character at the defaults.

## Deviations

- **Auto Gain on FET's Style:** `autogain --style fet` measures −1.38 dB, outside the ±1 dB tolerance, so it exits non-zero and USAGE.md cites it inline rather than as an example. The cause is the 0.5 ms Attack: Clean at 0.5/50 ms reads −1.02 dB too. FET's Attack stays at 0.5 ms because a fast attack is what FET's Style is for. No Style writes Auto Gain, but #25 turns it on through Comp Follow, so #25 should weigh this.
- The test helpers `SessionHost.h` and `ParametersOnly.h` moved out of `SessionTest.cpp` and `ColourParameterTest.cpp`, unchanged, because a second test needs them.
- `cpu <ref>` against `main` can't build this PR's CPU scenes, since `main`'s Engine has no `comp1/Style.h`. That limit is by design (performance.md, "CPU A/B").

## Merge Danger

**Door:** one-way once released: Style's choice order is frozen (ADR 0003). Before release, two-way.

**Blast Radius:** sessions. A new parameter, but older states restore as Clean with no version bump.

## What's New

author: plajjan
body:
$InitRoot used the generic $ContD___deserialize__, which allocates with $DNEW($Cont, ...) and so gives the restored object the class of a plain $Cont, whose __call__ is NULL. When the root actor waits for the first time, its bootstrap message is committed with $InitRoot as its continuation, so a program killed during the root actor's init crashed on every restart, at the continuation call in wt_work_cb.

$InitRoot now has a deserializer that sets the class back, the way $Done and $Fail do. A new regression test round-trips $Done, $Fail and $InitRoot through $serialize and $deserialize and checks that each keeps its class.

body:
<!-- orca-pr-loc -->
<!-- Programmatic LoC summary. Do not edit by hand; rewritten on every commit. -->

| | Files | Added | Deleted | Net |
| :--- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Test | 4 | $\color{#1a7f37}{\Huge{\mathbf{+}}}$​6 | $\color{#cf222e}{\Huge{\mathbf{−}}}$​11 | $\color{#cf222e}{\Huge{\mathbf{−}}}$​5 |
| Prod | 13 | $\color{#1a7f37}{\Huge{\mathbf{+}}}$​13 | $\color{#cf222e}{\Huge{\mathbf{−}}}$​29 | $\color{#cf222e}{\Huge{\mathbf{−}}}$​16 |

<!-- /orca-pr-loc -->

## ELI5

Several SSH and orcad files passed along names they had imported from somewhere else, so callers imported each name from the wrong file. Callers now import every name from the file that defines it. Nothing changes for users.

## What Changed

Users see no change. Seven pass-through re-exports (`export { X }` / `export type { X }` of an imported name) are gone, and each importer now names the defining module:

| Name | Was re-exported by | Now imported from |
|---|---|---|
| `fingerprintRuntimeSshTarget` | `runtime-ssh-access` | `runtime-ssh-target-fingerprint` |
| `RUNTIME_ENVIRONMENT_DIAGNOSTICS_CHANNEL` | `runtime-environment-diagnostics-broadcast` | `shared/runtime-environment-diagnostics` |
| `ORCAD_SHUTDOWN_DEADLINE_MS` | `orcad-lifecycle` | `orcad-stop-deadlines` |
| `RELAY_INSTALL_LOCK_NAME` | `remote-install-lock` | `shared/relay-install-lock-name` |
| `PortForwardEntry`, `PortForwardCloseReason` | `ssh-port-forward` | `shared/ssh-types` |
| `LegacyRelayPty` | `legacy-relay-bridge-leases` | (no importer left) |
| `SshIpcMocks` | `ssh-ipc-module-mocks` | `ssh-ipc-mock-shapes` |

Two re-exports in this area stay for now, because open PRs edit their files: `runtime-environment-connectivity-handlers` (#30672) and `orcad-entry` (#31507).

## Why

The repo rules forbid re-exports. A re-export hides which module owns a name, and it adds import edges that aren't needed. For example, the SSH target CRUD handlers loaded the whole runtime-SSH-access graph just to fingerprint a target. Pointing each importer at the owning module removes those edges without changing a single binding.

## Linked Issue

None. This is maintainer cleanup.

## Visual Proof

N/A: no UI or behaviour change.

## Testing

- [x] I manually tested these changes locally
- [x] Automated tests added/updated, or explained why not below

What I ran:

- `pnpm tc` (all configs): clean.
- `pnpm test` on `src/main/managed-server/install`, `src/main/managed-server/activation`, `src/main/ipc/ssh`, `src/main/ipc/runtime-environments`, `src/main/ssh/legacy-relay`, `src/main/ssh/port-forwarding` and the touched orcad and tunnel tests: 1,522 passed. Two tests failed, and both fail the same way on unmodified main on this machine: `orcad-stop-request-shutdown.integration` (needs a fully built orcad artifact) and `runtime-environment-preference` (file-watch timing under load).
- Full static job: every step passed except the orcad terminal smoke. That step also fails on unmodified main here, because the file-watcher readiness check times out after 5 seconds under load. It runs in CI.

## Review

- Codex review: clean.
- Independent Opus review: no P0–P2 findings. It confirmed that every repointed import is the same binding, that no test mock now misses a name, and that no import cycle was added.
- Opus's one P3: a few `vi.mock('./remote-install-lock')` factories still supply `RELAY_INSTALL_LOCK_NAME`, which nothing reads through that module any more. Those entries are harmless, and I've left them for the follow-up that renames the install helpers.

## Agent skill upstream boundary

- [x] Not applicable, or this change copies or mechanically translates no upstream skill-installer source, tests, fixtures, registry entries, path tables, comments, or documentation.

## Notes

body:
## Summary

Adds an **Explore** view beside the existing forum, which becomes **Conversations**. Explore is the default for a plain visit; the shell (header, nav rail, hero banner, sidebar) is unchanged apart from a wider right sidebar on large screens.

- **Explore / Conversations switch** in the sticky toolbar. The slice pill, New/Top, search and Post move under Conversations, unchanged. `/post/:id` links, notifications and the signed-out pending-post replay all open Conversations.
- **Explore content** (centre column): welcome intro; a featured topic card using the space's own credited banner photo (never the one already on screen; falls back to an illustration); *Imagine a better neighborhood* (SVG block that changes per choice, with a text caption as its equivalent); *Questions for your community*; *Explore nearby* (time picker → suggestion → detail page).
- **Explore → topic → conversation.** Topic pages show summary, why it matters, sources (real meeting agendas for the local-proposal topic only) and a focus question. "Join the conversation" opens the **existing composer** pre-filled with an editable draft — nothing is ever published automatically.
- **Drafts** live in localStorage, are bound to the member's most local *own* slice (never a sibling shard or whichever tab is showing), survive sign-in through the real accounts redirect, and are refused if the member is no longer in that slice.
- **Evening suggestion uses real events:** the city's next scheduled meeting (`/api/meetings`), else the area's next election (`elections-by-area`), else a general suggestion. Nothing invented.
- **What's new** card in the sidebar on Explore (bottom of the column below `md`), with a detail page per update and "View all updates".
- **Sidebar width:** 320px (md) → 340px (lg) → 380px (xl). `CLAUDE.md` layout note updated.

## Data this needs from the API

All three are sample data today, in one module — `src/mocks/civicSpacesExplore.ts` — read only through `src/lib/exploreData.ts`. Route names are proposals; each mock export is already shaped like the response.

| Proposed route | Stands in for | Shape (see the mock) | Used by |
|---|---|---|---|
| `GET /api/civic-spaces/explore/topics` | Conversation-starter topics: featured topic, the two question cards, every topic page | `{ featuredTopicId, questionTopicIds, topics: ExploreTopic[] }` | Featured card, Questions for your community, topic detail, Imagine → Explore this topic |
| `GET /api/civic-spaces/explore/suggestions` | "Explore nearby" suggestions per time slot (15 min / an hour / an evening) | `{ suggestions: AdventureSuggestion[] }` | Explore nearby card and its detail page |
| `GET /api/civic-spaces/updates` | "What's new" product notes | `{ updates: ProductUpdate[] }` | What's new card, update detail page, View all updates |

Notes for the backend task:
- **Topics should be per space.** Today every space gets the same sample topics; a real route should take the slice (or geoid).
- **Topics can't link to existing posts yet** — posts carry no topic id, so "Join the conversation" always opens the composer with a draft. A `topic_id` on `civic_spaces.posts` (or a topic→post link) would let a topic open its real discussion.
- **Updates need a published date.** The UI shows none because none was ever published.
- **Already served and used live:** meetings, elections and the hero photo — none of that is mocked.
- **Considered, not a fit:** On the Record's `GET /api/topics` groups meeting agenda items, not neighborhood conversation starters. It could later back the local-proposal topic's sources.

- **No Follow button** — nothing stores or acts on a topic follow yet.
- **No named places** in Explore nearby, by decision (no places source in the platform).
- Saves (draft, saved suggestion) are **this device only** and the UI says so.
- The Imagine card fits one screen with an option selected at 1280px and wider; at 1024px and on phones it stacks and scrolls.

- [x] Scripted Playwright pass against `?dev=1` (50 checks): Explore default; view switching; forum search, New/Top, Post, opening a thread; direct `/post/:id` link opens Conversations; every Imagine option changes the scene and caption; arrow keys move the options; Explore nearby picks; topic → Join → composer pre-filled with the community named and nothing posted; draft survives switching views and level tabs; signed-out draft → real sign-in URL → composer reopens with the draft bound to the member's city; no horizontal overflow at 1440 / 1024 / 900 / 390 / 360 in light and dark.
- [x] Header, nav rail and sidebar pixel-compared against the pre-change commit (identical; banner differed only by photo load timing).
- [ ] **Not verified: live `/api` data.** On my machine the dev proxy failed every `/api` request with `getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND accounts-api.empowered.vote`, so the sidebar showed fixtures. Please confirm real Asheville officials and 200s under `?dev=1` on a machine where the proxy resolves.

author: vinceackermann2-sys
body:
## Summary

This is an additive engineering repair of the user-selected **SI Original V2** memory storage, named **RWM1** (Revisable World Memory v1). It follows the 21 October component diagnostic in draft #1528, which found these defects:

- **D1:** revised facts return stale values. Duplicate keys append and cosine argmax returns the first: revised accuracy was 8/16 in all 3 seeds.
- **D2:** the native export omits replay: 0/56 replay records were restored.
- **D3:** memory and replay share one global FIFO, so one world can evict another world's facts.
- **D4:** memory keys ignore the executed action.
- **D5:** any nonempty world always returns its nearest record.
- **D6:** stored keys carry no fingerprint of the backbone that produced them.

The new `SIOriginalRevisableWorldMemoryV1` subclasses V2 and replaces **only the storage objects**. The inherited V1/V2 ingest validation, fast-weight rule, forward path and every parameter/buffer are unchanged, and state dicts load strictly in both directions.

- **Latest-wins identity:** records are keyed by (world, action, key). Each keeps `writes`/`changes` metadata, and superseded values go to a bounded audit log that retrieval never reads.
- **Per-world quotas:** memory and replay are bounded per world, and a world evicts only its own oldest-written record.
- **Misses:** reads are identity-only by default, so an unknown context gets zeros and `memory_hit=False`. An optional cosine threshold exists for descriptive measurement only.
- **Lifetime persistence:** `save_lifetime`/`load_lifetime` cover weights, fast state, memory, audit, replay, skills and counters, and load with `torch.load(weights_only=True)`. Loading refuses V1/V2 schemas and representation-fingerprint mismatches, and saving never overwrites an existing file.

The name "V3" is already used by `experiment/si-original-factual-sensor-replay-v3-20261020`, which is a different change; this branch builds directly on the V2 branch.

## Verification (local, CPU)

- `tests/test_si_original_revisable_world_memory_v1.py`: 22 passed (T1–T22, untrained developer fixtures).
- Inherited V1/V2/crossmodal/hybrid SI tests: 34 passed. Phase-two foundation/reporting checks: 8 passed.
- Diagnostic `--smoke` (untrained width-16 models, temp output): all 9 preregistered gates pass in 3 runs, and the paired V2 control reproduces the archived feedback digest and the 8/16 stale result.

The preregistered trained-checkpoint diagnostic lives in the local research package `research_si_rwm1_20261021`, and its result will be reported here.

## Scope

This covers storage mechanics only. It is **not** evidence of continual learning, better decisions, planning or a breakthrough. Keep this PR in draft; do not merge.

author: kylegutierrez51
body:
A webhook event's payload was kept "for auditability and replay", but nothing could replay it: re-running a delivery meant going to GitHub's Recent Deliveries. A **Replay** button on the event modal now sends a stored event's payload through the same decision logic a GitHub delivery takes, judged against the webhook's current settings, and starts the run as the signed-in user. 

Typical use: a delivery failed because the pipeline had no saved definition or a validation error -- a user can fix it, then replay.

## What changed

- **One decision path for GitHub and Replay.** The route's branch logic moves unchanged into `processDelivery(webhook, githubEvent, payload, triggeredBy)` (`lib/webhooks/process-delivery.ts`), which returns `{ status, reason, httpStatus, runId? }`. The route keeps signature verification, parsing, recording, `settle` and its `catch`; its responses are identical. The logic now has its own unit tests, one per branch.
- **Events know their webhook.** `WebhookEvent.webhookId` (FK, `ON DELETE SET NULL`, indexed) links each event to the webhook it arrived on, so a replay can load that webhook's current filters, pipeline and environment. The back-relation is `Webhook.deliveries`.
- **Replay action.** `replayWebhookEvent(id)` (`lib/actions/webhook-events.ts`, `"use server"`) checks the session first and takes only the event id from the client. It records a **new** event (`source: 'replay'`, the original's payload and headers), runs `processDelivery` with the signed-in user as the run's trigger, and settles the new event with its reason. Replays do not touch `Webhook.lastDelivery`, and are audited as the new `WEBHOOK_REPLAYED` action by the user.
- **One rule for what can be replayed.** `replayBlocker` (`lib/webhooks/replay.ts`) refuses, in order: a still-pending event, anything but push/pull request, an event whose payload was dropped (ignored events), a webhook that no longer exists (including every event recorded before this change), and an inactive webhook. The data readers expose it as `replayBlockedReason`, so the button and the action cannot disagree.
- **UI.** The event modal gets a Replay button (disabled, with the reason on hover, when blocked), a confirmation warning that it may start another run for the same commit, and a toast linking to the run: a checkmark for a run started, a gray info icon for an ignored outcome, red for a failure, including a rejected request. It then opens the new event. A **Source** field reads "GitHub" or "Replayed from Deplo", and replayed rows in the events table carry a small "Replay" tag.
- **Smaller fixes alongside.** A webhook deleted mid-request is reported as such instead of blaming the pipeline (the FK error is attributed by field); the stalled-event reason now suggests replaying from Deplo or redelivering from GitHub.

## Notable decisions

- **A replay is a new event, not a re-run of the old row,** so the original keeps its own outcome and the history stays honest.
- **Replays use current settings, not the original settings.** The point is to retry after fixing something; the confirmation says the replay runs through the webhook's current settings.
- **No signature check on replay.** The payload was verified when it first arrived; the replay is authorized by the user's session like every other action.

## Breaking changes / migration

- Migration `20261021041408_webhook_event_replay`: `WebhookEvent.webhookId` + FK + index, and `AuditAction.WEBHOOK_REPLAYED`. Run `npx prisma migrate dev`, then `npx prisma generate` with the dev server and runner stopped.
- Events recorded before the migration have no `webhookId` and cannot be replayed (they show "The webhook this event arrived on no longer exists."). Seeded events are in the same state.
- `addWebhookEvent` takes an optional second argument `{ replayedBy }` and now writes `webhookId` on every event.

## Testing

- New: `lib/webhooks/process-delivery.test.ts` (every branch's status, reason and HTTP code), `lib/webhooks/replay.test.ts` (each blocker and their order), `lib/actions/webhook-events.test.ts` (session, blockers, the recorded event, the current webhook, outcomes, a throwing `processDelivery`). Extended: `lib/webhooks/webhook-events.test.ts`, `lib/data/webhook-events.test.ts`, `WebhookEventModal.test.tsx`, `WebhookEventRow.test.tsx`, `runner/db.test.ts`.
- `npx jest lib/webhooks lib/actions/webhook-events.test.ts components/webhook-events lib/data/webhook-events.test.ts runner/db.test.ts`: 250 passed. `npm run lint` and `npm run typecheck` are clean.
- Multiple replays against a live GitHub delivery end to end have been exercised successfully.

## Follow-ups

body:
Closes #450

## Summary

The Start dialog's worktree preparation now shows one row per nested repo (#653), between the branch row and the setup steps. Each row has its status, its time and, once done, its branch and base or `reaproveitada`. A nested repo that fails, for example its folder checked out on another branch, fails its own row, and that row's log shows git's words.

Spec: dennys-bd/docs#164, `docs/agent/hive/specs/2026-10-21-setup-progress-nested-rows-design.md`
Plan: `docs/agent/hive/plans/2026-10-21-setup-progress-nested-rows.md`

## Changes

- **Rows** (`src/types.ts`, `src/setup-rows.ts`): `SETUP_ROW_KINDS` gains `'nested'`, with no new field. Nested rows are queued from `setupStarted`, then start, end or fail by their path. `preparedRows` now ends only the worktree and branch rows.
- **Nested step** (`src/worktree-nested.ts`): `prepareNested`, `ensureNestedWorktrees` and `switchNested` take an optional `NestedObserver` (`started` / `ended` / `failed`). The hive.log lines are unchanged. `switchNested`'s pre-checks now run one repo at a time, so a second refusal never reports after the run ended.
- **Run** (`src/task-setup.ts`): each run gets a `nested` observer. It writes `> nested <path>` before that repo's git, which is where the dialog cuts its log, and dispatches the rows. `runTaskSetup` passes the run to `prepare` (`PrepareHooks`).
- **Wiring** (`src/server-spawn.ts`, `src/server-open.ts`): the worktree and branch rows end right after the outer git, before the first nested repo. The observer goes to `prepareNested`.
- **UI** (`src/ui/hooks/use-setup-log.ts`, `src/ui/components/SetupProgress.tsx`, `src/ui/i18n.ts`): `rowTails` opens a nested row on its header line. The dialog draws `repo aninhado <path> · branch <branch> a partir de <base>` or `… reaproveitada`. Two new copy keys, each in English and Portuguese.

Assumptions taken in planning, now reflected in the spec:

- Local (checkout) tasks still open no setup run, at spawn or first open, so they show no nested rows yet. `switchNested` already reports to the observer.
- The base is drawn as the branch row draws it, not in mono.

Review findings left open:

- LOW: when the setup fails before any step is planned, after every nested repo is done, `failedRows`' fallback marks the last row failed. That row is now the last nested repo, where it used to be the branch row.
- LOW: a nested repo path with control characters would print them in the `> nested <path>` header. The path comes from the user's own config, and it was already echoed in `> git -C <path> …` lines. The fix would be to reject `[\x00-\x1f\x7f]` in `nestedPathProblem`.
- LOW: `openWorktreeRun` groups some locals in destructured tuples to stay under 50 lines.

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm test`: lint and both `tsc` pass. In the full parallel run, node had 3943 pass / 3 fail and vitest had 25 of 419 files fail, all on timeouts in files this change does not touch (`daemon`, `server-diff`, `shell-init`; `FilesPanel`, `Dashboard.*`, `Settings`…). Re-run alone, those pass: the 3 node files are 32 pass / 0 fail, and the 24 vitest files plus `FilesPanel` are 163 tests, all passing. The touched suites (`setup-rows`, `worktree-nested`, `task-setup`, `server-worktree-setup`, `use-setup-log`, `SetupProgress`) are green.
- [ ] Manual checks (`pnpm start`):
  1. In a workspace with `docs` under nested repos, Start a task with no worktree. `repo aninhado docs` shows queued from the first frame. The worktree and branch rows turn done first. `docs` ends `· branch <branch> a partir de origin/main`, and its git lines are under its own entry in the log select.
  2. Delete the worktree with Keep branch, then Start again. The row ends `reaproveitada`.
  3. Pre-create `<worktree>/docs` on another branch. The `docs` row fails, its log shows `is checked out on …`, and the steps stay queued.
  4. In a workspace with no nested repos, the rows are exactly #390's.

## Screenshots

N/A. The copy and states are covered by `test/ui/SetupProgress.test.tsx`; a manual check is still pending.

author: soykandiso
body:
Implements the approved plan (Vesti.mk source, all MK + region stories, one switch for auto mode).

## Phase 0
- `sources/vesti.py`: parses "топ.ВЕСТИ" via the stable `/c/<id>` link and merges the mobile and desktop copies. If the layout changes, it fails loudly instead of guessing.
- `extract.py`: full article text (trafilatura → JSON-LD → meta) and respects each outlet's robots.txt.
- `llm/`: prompt with JSON output and a verbatim evidence sentence. Providers are Groq, Gemini and optionally Claude, behind a fallback router with throttling and retries.
- `validate.py`: checks one sentence, Cyrillic, length, banned intros and emoji, that the evidence appears verbatim, and that every number and name in the sentence is in the article.
- `scripts/probe_sources.py` (cluster-ID stability) and `scripts/eval_models.py` (CSV for scoring).

## Phase 1
- State lives on a `state` branch and is committed and pushed after every post on each platform, so a crash can't cause a repost.
- Dedupe by cluster ID, by shared article URL, and by headline similarity ≥0.8 within 48 h.
- Telegram drafts with ✅/❌. Presses are read with `getUpdates` and only the admin counts. Drafts expire after 6 h.
- Telegram, Bluesky (link card, checks the last 30 own posts) and Facebook publishers. A failing platform never blocks the others, and you get an alert in your private chat.
- Posting window 06:00–23:59 Skopje, at most 2 posts per run and 30 per day.

## Workflows
- `tests` (pytest + gitleaks) on every push.
- `probe`: on by default; stops itself after 120 snapshots.
- `eval`: manual.
- `run` and `healthcheck`: only run when the variable `BOT_ENABLED=true`.

Step-by-step manual setup is in `docs/SETUP.md`.

## Tests
82 tests: parser on a fixture built from the real card markup, extraction, validator cases, router fallback, dedupe, the git-pushed state, approval, and end-to-end runs. The end-to-end runs cover manual, auto, dry-run, a platform failing, models down, duplicates, the window and the limits.

This is the last batch of moving every niche berry (all berries except Sitrus and Lum) onto **Harvest, Ripen or Cheek Pouch** holders, following #676, #678 and #679. No suitable existing sets were left, so it adds **40 new sets** and changes the item on 49 existing ones.

author: urbanchrisy
body:
## Summary

`Flow` draws its edges, background, connection preview and minimap with Skia instead of `react-native-svg`. The background becomes a runtime shader that stays sharp at any zoom.

> **Stacked on #251** (react-native-skia 3 + the reload fix). This PR's base is `feature/skia-v3`, so the diff shows only the Flow work. Merge #251 first, then retarget this PR to `develop`.

## Related Issue

N/A. Follows up the Flow canvas work; depends on #251.

## Changes

- One Skia `Canvas` under the node layer. `Canvas` is a separate reconciler, so React context doesn't reach inside it: theme colours and calm motion are resolved above it and passed back in through `FlowCanvasLayerProvider`
- Background: a runtime shader for dots, lines and cross, sharp at every zoom level. `flow-svg.ts` is removed
- Edges, the connection preview and the minimap are Skia paths that read the same shared values, so dragging still never renders React
- `useThemeColors` resolves several theme colours in one lookup
- `flow.tsx` imports `lib/skia-native-id` (from #251), so edges, minimap and background draw on the first load after a JS reload. Before, they appeared only after something re-rendered the canvas, such as pressing the lock button
- `react-native-skia` (>=3) is a devDependency of `react-native-ui` and an optional peer Flow now needs, like Chart and Sketch. The installation docs say so
- Flow `AGENTS.md`, its docs page, the changeset (`minor`), the registry and the install manifest are updated

## Type of Change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [x] Breaking change: consumers using `Flow` must install `react-native-skia` >=3
- [x] Refactor
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Chore / tooling

## Test Plan

- `bun test` (whole repo), `bun run check`, `bun run typecheck`: all pass. `flow.variants.test.ts` covers the new pure helpers
- Registry rebuilt; `gen-install` leaves no diff
- iOS simulator, dev client: edges, background dots, connection preview and minimap draw on first open and after three consecutive JS reloads. Dragging nodes, panning, zooming and lock/unlock all behave as before

## Risk

- Rendering should look the same as the SVG version. The background is now a shader, so dot and line antialiasing may differ slightly at fractional zooms
- Android was not run on a device in this change

author: thesherwood
body:
Closes #247. This is jacl_impl's half of theSherwood/unir#282, slice 4b (unir decision #282.5). A person's session there grants the JACL shell the mounted directory's control, and a subscription to its syncs.

## What changes

- **`[service-schema S NAME]`** returns the schema of a service's catalog entry `NAME` alone: the service's types, with that entry as entry 0 (`unir_service_schema`). `transcript-block` takes it.
  - It runs through every layer `service-send` does: the head id (appended last, before `HEAD_ID_COUNT`, in `ast.c` and the `jacl.h` mirror), codegen's table, `jaclrt.h`, `transcript_unir.c`, and `chan.c`'s stub without vats.
- **Subscriptions.** unir's C ABI now opens a service granted without `NAME.requests` as a subscription. It hears what the service writes and sends nothing, so `service-call` and `service-send` on it are errors. The runtime needs nothing new beyond the re-vendored units.
- **`shell.jacl`:**
  - It opens `mount`, then `events`, when granted. That is the mount's order: it connects controllers before subscribers.
  - Each pass that hears events writes them as one block at the end of the transcript, typed under the entry's schema. The shell knows nothing of the mount: it shows what any subscription granted as `events` hears.
  - A job's context carries the shell's store session and the mount's control, as `$ctx->store` and `$ctx->mount` (-1 when there is none), declared before the commands are evaluated. unir's person commands (`log`, `show`, `restore`, `note`, `notes`, `rate`, `pull`, `push`) use them.
  - Before its first prompt, it evaluates the session ref `~shell/commands`, then the person's own `profile`, each if present. unir's root commits the commands at every start, so they are always the image's. The person's `profile` is never overwritten, and what it defines wins.
- **unir's units** re-vendored at theSherwood/unir 1dcf9b3: `unir.h`, `unir_cabi.ll`, `unir_store_vat.ll`.
- **Docs:** `UNIR_SERVICES.md` (subscriptions, `service-schema`) and `SYNTAX.md`'s services row.

## Tests

- **`cargo test --release --test repl`:** all 5 pass, among them `the_shell_runs_each_line_in_its_own_domain` on every engine, with the re-vendored store unit.
- **unir's `session-files`** passes on the tree-walker, bytecode and the JIT with the image built at this commit.
  - It drives two sessions as a person does, reading each screen back from its glyphs.
  - Each sync shows as a block typed under the mount's schema, and `service-schema` gives that block its schema.
  - It also covers `log`, `show`, `restore`, notes and the rate, through `$ctx->store` and `$ctx->mount`.
- **Baselines:**
  - `./build.sh`: 25/25.
  - `./build.sh --asan`: 25/25.
  - `bash codegen/tests/sanitize_corpus.sh`: 578 programs, no ASan or UBSan reports.
  - `./build.sh --tsan`: 24/25. The one failure is `chase_lev_stress`, the data race #205 records, which fails on main. This change touches nothing in `lib/`.
- **The shell image** built at this commit (`jacl_shell_image`, 2,646,383 bytes) is byte-identical to the one theSherwood/unir#282's slice 4b PR vendors, whose `JACL_REV` names this commit.

There is no harness test of `service-schema` alone: the harness has no service with an events entry to subscribe to. unir's `session-files` exercises it end to end.

## For consumers

- **unir** vendors the image at this commit. Its slice 4b PR carries the root's side: the grants, and the commands as `~shell/commands`.
- **A root that still commits its commands as `profile`** keeps working: the shell evaluates `profile` as before, after `~shell/commands`, which it skips when absent.

body: ## Summary On `main` the library's `sanity` devDependency (`^5.31.2`) and the blog apps (`^5.31.1`) resolve to two different versions. Because `@sanity/astro` is a workspace link, `dist/studio/studio-component.tsx` imports `sanity` from `packages/sanity-astro/node_modules` while the app's `sanity.config.ts` imports its own copy. `vitePluginSanityModuleDedupe` only aliases in `astro dev` (`apply: 'serve'`), so a production build bundles both and the embedded Studio hydrates blank: ``` [astro-island] Error hydrating /_astro/studio-component.*.js TypeError: Duplicate instances of context "sanity/_singletons/context/active-workspace-matcher" with incompatible versions detected: Expected 5.31.1 but got 5.31.2. ``` This is reproducible today with `pnpm build:example && cd apps/example && astro preview` and opening `/admin`; the deployed `sanity-astro-example` preview has the same blank Studio. Published installs are unaffected because the peer resolves to the consumer's single copy. ### Changes - `packages/sanity-astro`, `apps/example`, `apps/example-ssr`, `apps/movies`: `sanity` / `@sanity/vision` → `^6.2.0`, the version `apps/example-latest` already uses, so the whole workspace resolves one `sanity`. - `apps/example`, `apps/example-ssr`: `deskTool` (`sanity/desk`, deprecated) → `structureTool` (`sanity/structure`). - New integration test `src/integration/astro-build.test.ts`: runs `astro build` on `apps/example`, asserts content rendered through `sanity:client`, asserts the prerendered `/admin`, then serves `dist/` with `astro preview` and drives `/admin` in Chromium, failing on any `Duplicate instances of context` error or if the Studio island never mounts. - `src/integration/dev-server.ts`: exports `repoRoot`, `astroBin`, `spawnAstro`; `startAstroDevServer` gains `command: 'dev' | 'preview'`. - `vitest.integration.config.ts`: `fileParallelism: false` so the two integration files do not race for dev servers. - AGENTS.md: gotcha describing the alignment rule. - Lockfile: the `sanity`/`@sanity/vision` 6.x resolutions plus pruning of packages only sanity 5 pulled in. ### Relation to renovate PRs #477 bumps only the library and #470 only the apps; either one on its own leaves the skew in place (or inverts it). This PR does both at once and adds the test that catches the skew. ## Behaviour No library source changes; the published package is unaffected. Defaults unchanged. ## Dependencies Independent, based on `main`. Part of the split of #451. ## Verification - `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` - `pnpm build` (5/5 tasks) - `pnpm --filter @sanity/astro test` (26) and `test:integration` (8, including the `/admin` hydration check, which fails on `main` with the error above) - `pnpm oxfmt --check`

author: wrackedfella
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"WrackedFella"} -->
_Requested by **Justin** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01UMEK4qS3gSAqZ2mecN2eJK?thread=cmsg_01UMEK4qS3gSAqZ2mecN2eJK5zKyoiPi364iAfgxvA7524)_

## Issue
Closes #378

## Summary
**Before:** Mouse look turned the same per count whatever the mouse speed; there was no acceleration option.

**After:** Settings → Controls has a "Mouse acceleration" toggle (off by default) and an "Acceleration strength" slider and value box (0 to 1, default 0.04), enabled only while the toggle is on. With it on, fast movements turn further than slow ones over the same counts. Both save to prefs (`mouse_acceleration`, `mouse_acceleration_strength`) and apply on Save.

**How:** Source `m_customaccel 1` with exponent 1, measured by speed so it doesn't depend on frame rate: per-count turn = `look_per_count + acceleration × v`, where `v` is the smoothed counts' length per millisecond of the frame (0 when the frame time is 0). The stick is never accelerated. `look_settings` passes `source_look_per_count(strength.max(0))` when on, else 0. The sensitivity and strength rows share one `slider_row` helper.

Deviations from the spec:
- `LookSettings` keeps `look_per_count` and gains `acceleration` (look units per count, per count/ms) instead of adding a `sensitivity` field. `source_look_per_count` is linear, so `source_look_per_count(sens + s·v) = look_per_count + source_look_per_count(s)·v`: same result, and `moho_input` stays unit-agnostic with no churn for searchlight or `ActionMap::new`.
- `AppConfig` gains a mirrored `mouse_acceleration` field so `build_actions` (startup and Save) applies it, following the existing mirrored look fields. Folding these into one `LookSettings` is still the follow-up noted on #508.
- The pinned default save-format test now includes the two new keys (a deliberate format change); files without them still load the defaults with no warnings.
- The strength drag value clamps an out-of-range value from the file (for example 1.5 or -0.2) to 0..=1 when Settings is shown, as the sensitivity row already does. The wiki prefs table says so.

## Test evidence
- [x] `just check` passes (1792 tests, clippy `-D warnings`, doctests, comment refs, layering)
- [x] New or changed tests fail without the change (test-first history: 7f7a19a, dc88b6b before 6e3e348)
- [x] Gate class: domain. Tests reviewed before implementation by `devflow:test-critic`

### Test review
- 18 KEEP, 0 STRENGTHEN, 0 MERGE, 2 REMOVE (`acceleration_off_by_default_in_raw_settings` and `acceleration_builders_and_mut_edit_the_values`, judged redundant).
- Gap accepted (material): nothing proved the setting reached the game. Added `initializer::tests::build_actions_applies_mouse_acceleration_from_prefs`.
- Gap accepted (minor): `negative_acceleration_strength_loads_unchanged`.
- Mutation testing later showed one of the removed tests was not redundant (the `_mut` accessors); replacements were added (`mouse_acceleration_mut_edits_the_flag`, `mouse_acceleration_strength_mut_edits_the_value`).

### Adversarial challenge
No failing case found. Checked: zero, tiny and long frame times; NaN or inf strength (the prefs reader rejects non-finite values and `.max(0.0)` maps NaN to 0); smoothing carry; diagonal motion; mixed stick and mouse.

### Refactor
One `slider_row` helper replaces the inline sensitivity row and the new strength row (a644ca9). From `/simplify`, skipped: guarding the speed computation when acceleration is 0 (a few flops per frame; zero strength already equals off) and clamping inside `set_look` (the spec puts the clamp at use, in `look_settings`).

## Mutation testing
`just mutants`: 52 mutants. **46 caught / 0 missed / 6 unviable.** The first run left 6 survivors: the two new `_mut` accessors, and `>`→`>=` in the slider's epsilon dirty check. The existing sensitivity epsilon test was vacuous, because 3.0 + `f32::EPSILON` rounds back to 3.0. Tests were added for all three, and a re-run of those functions gave 18 / 18 caught. No exclusions are proposed.

## Quality passes
- [x] `/devflow:comment-audit`: 2 doc comments tightened (`look_settings`, `build_actions`), 0 removed.
- [x] `/devflow:wiki`: not run as a skill. The implementer and reviewer updated `wiki/reference/prefs-format.md` (two keys, the Source carry-over caveat, the UI clamp, the live-apply list) and `wiki/architecture/input-and-state.md` (acceleration step in the look pipeline). No new pages.
- [x] Independent review (`devflow:reviewer`): one material finding (the UI clamp contradicted the wiki), fixed in the docs. Two wiki drifts fixed. Minor, not changed: `LookSettings.acceleration` has no invariant of its own, because `look_settings` is its only producer.

## Risk and manual verification
- Blast radius: flagstone look input, prefs file format (two new keys), and the Controls tab layout (the acceleration rows sit under sensitivity, above invert-Y and smoothing).
- **In game (flagstone):** with acceleration off, fast and slow sweeps over the same mouse distance turn the same. Turn it on at about 0.04 to 0.1: fast flicks now go further than a slow sweep. The strength control is greyed out while the toggle is off. Save, restart, and both values persist.
- searchlight ignores prefs look settings (existing FPS-line gap), so it has no acceleration.
- Board Status changes are left to the board automation (cloud threads can't reach Projects).

author: gobernaciondenarino
body:
El panel devolvió dos errores al verificar las claves. De los dos, solo uno era configuración; el otro era un defecto del plugin disfrazado de error de configuración, que es la peor forma de un fallo porque manda a buscar el problema donde no está.

1. EL 400 DE GEMINI ERA NUESTRO, no de la clave.

La verificación es la única petición del plugin que va sin herramientas, y el adaptador construía el bloque de todas formas: salía `"tools":[{"functionDeclarations":[]}]`. Gemini exige al menos una declaración dentro de cada Tool y rechaza la petición ENTERA. Por eso fallaba solo la verificación: una conversación de verdad manda las diez y ese bloque va lleno. Claude y ChatGPT toleran `tools: []`, así que se veía únicamente en Gemini.

Las pruebas no lo vieron porque todas mandaban las diez herramientas, y la verificación se probaba contra dobles del HTTP. Un doble no valida: obedece.

2. EL DIAGNÓSTICO EXISTÍA Y SE TIRABA.

Gemini explicaba con todas las letras qué campo estaba mal. El plugin guardaba esa frase y `motivo()` la descartaba para publicar una traducción fija del código HTTP. Ahora la traducción va primero y lo que dijo el proveedor detrás, nunca en su lugar, buscando el mensaje en los cuatro sitios donde cada proveedor lo anida. Sin URLs: se imprimen en una página del panel y en una URL puede ir la clave.

3. LA VOZ SÍ ERA CONFIGURACIÓN, y el panel lo ponía difícil.

El identificador guardado tenía forma válida pero no era de la cuenta —el de los ejemplos de la documentación de ElevenLabs—. El panel listaba las voces por su NOMBRE cuando el campo pide el IDENTIFICADOR, de modo que no se podía copiar nada de ese texto, y cortaba la lista a ocho sin decirlo. Ahora es una lista desplegable con las voces de la cuenta: no se puede elegir una que no exista, y la guardada que no esté sale marcada en rojo con su consecuencia.

Por el camino aparecieron tres defectos más: la verificación probaba el modelo en crudo mientras la ruta real lo sanea, de modo que no probaba lo que corre; un 200 sin contenido se publicaba como «responde» con un «Contestó: «»» vacío, que afirma que está todo bien; y la verificación de voz consultaba un host distinto del de la síntesis. Y en el navegador, un 503 por voz sin configurar se le anunciaba al visitante como «alcanzó su límite de consultas de hoy»: una cifra que no se había gastado y un límite que no existía.

MENSAJES DE CONSOLA. Antes había tres líneas de registro en todo el plugin y ninguna en el camino que usa un administrador: el botón de verificar no escribía nada. Ahora todo sale por `anotar()` y por `avisar()` con el mismo prefijo, y cubren los cuatro caminos por los que el audio puede no sonar y los cinco por los que el micrófono puede fallar, que eran mudos: desde fuera, «no suena» por una clave mal puesta y «no suena» porque el navegador bloqueó la reproducción se ven igual. Lo que se le pinta al visitante no cambia.

Se revisó app-ondas como referencia. Coincide en lo esencial —dictado con SpeechRecognition, TTS con Blob y createObjectURL— y se apartó a propósito en lo demás: allí la clave viaja al navegador en un JSON público, el identificador de voz es un campo de texto libre con uno de ejemplo (el mismo fallo que ocurrió aquí) y los errores del proveedor se descartan sin leerlos. Eso no se copió: es justo lo que este commit corrige.

614 comprobaciones de datos y 130 de navegador en verde. Reporte completo en docs/voz/diagnostico.md.

author: coffeegoddd
body:
Every node a tree read read was read from the store: the journal index
looked up in shared memory, the record read from its file, its CRC
checked and its chunk decompressed, roots and upper levels included,
every time.  A fold's seeks into the baseline, a diff's walk and a
commit's apply read the same nodes call after call.

- prolly_chunk_cache_size (kB, default 16 MB, 0 off): decoded chunks
  the session's store read from its files, kept by hash, least recently
  used let go of past it.  A chunk is named by its content, so one kept
  is never stale.  Kept on its second read from the files, not its
  first (the hashes of those read once remembered, as many as the cache
  holds chunks): a fold of many rows reads each leaf once, and filling
  the cache with them cost more than it saved (Q=10,000 commits 8% slower).  Not the transaction's own (pending, transient: an
  abort takes them back), nor one read through a source, nor one past an
  eighth of the cache.
- pg_stat_prolly counts chunk_cache_hits (PGSTAT_FILE_FORMAT_ID bumped).

Tests: chunk_cache (a third read from the cache, none with it off, the
same rows either way, a rolled-back commit's chunks not kept);
diff_memory reads with it off, measuring what reading the rows holds.



## Measured

Micro-benchmark, 100k rows of 1 KB, 5 reps, both builds on master `f470ce69ac`:

| | before (#661) | this | change |
|---|---|---|---|
| status, 1,000 dirty rows | 20.0 ms | 13.3 ms | −34% |
| commit, 1,000 dirty rows | 19.8 ms | 13.1 ms | −34% |
| diff HEAD → WORKING, 1,000 dirty rows | 8.90 ms | 5.85 ms | −34% |
| status, 10,000 dirty rows | 147.1 ms | 140.8 ms | −4% |
| commit, 10,000 dirty rows | 150.7 ms | 142.8 ms | −5% |
| diff HEAD → WORKING, 10,000 dirty rows | 78.9 ms | 74.2 ms | −6% |

The first version admitted a chunk on its first read, which made 10,000-row commits and statuses 8–9% slower: 10,000 scattered rows touch about 40 MB of leaves, more than the 16 MB cache. Admitting on the second read fixes that.

## Status

Draft, part of the #656 stack (#658 → #663). test_prolly's regression and TAP suites pass on master `f470ce69ac`.

author: felipeldfonseca
body:
Third PR of Phase 3c, stacked on the domain PR (`fase-3c/dominio`, #34), which is stacked on the database PR (`fase-3c/banco`, #33). It adds the screens for partial exits, stop moves («Registrar stop» / «Breakeven») and the rule «mover para o breakeven com +N pontos», built from the boards the owner approved on 21 Oct (RegistrarOperacao, 16 scenarios, and Personalizar). The paste (`fase3c_aplicar.sql`) is already on the live database (21 Oct); merge #33 → #34 → this PR, in that order, after the owner tests it.

## What changes
- **Step 1, «Aberta»:** the rule line «Sua regra: breakeven com +8 pts, em 7.920,50.», or «Sua regra: breakeven com +8 pts.» before a side and a price are chosen.
- **Step 1, «Já fechada»:**
  - «+ Outra saída» splits an exit into 2 to 20 rows that must add up to the entry. Each row gets its own errors.
  - New lines: the sum «Saídas: 2 de 2 ct.», the result «Resultado: +6,00 pts em média · +US$ 120,00», «Corrigir» on the total, «Custos» for the whole trade, and «Venceu sem valor» on the last row.
  - The pill «Movi o stop para o breakeven» with «Preço quando moveu» and its status «com +12,00 pts a favor · Sua regra: com +5 pts.». The rule shown is the version in force at the typed entry.
  - The draft moves to v3. Drafts saved as v1 and v2 still load.
- **Step 2, «Operação aberta»** (price markets only; Ebinex is unchanged):
  - «O que registrar agora?» offers Saída · Parcial · Mover stop.
  - «Parcial» uses chips, a field, or «Metade», depending on the market.
  - «Mover stop» offers «Breakeven» or «Outro preço», with «Preço agora».
  - The «Agora» block and the «Linha do tempo».
  - «Desfazer» undoes the newest partial or stop move for 15 minutes, after a confirmation.
  - The breakeven suggestion after a partial that reaches the rule.
  - The limit banners after a partial, and the line that brings the limit back after an undo.
  - The exit after partials («Sai com os 2 ct…», «· no total …»).
  - «Desfazer entrada» names the partials and moves the trade has.
- **Step 3, «Operação fechada»:**
  - The average exit («→ 7.924,17 em média»).
  - The R line «com o stop inicial de 10 pts».
  - The timeline, with «Nª saída» numbering on «Já fechada» trades and file exits.
  - The breakeven line, in five forms, shown only when the rule covers the asset.
- **Lists:**
  - «Operações abertas» shows «· 2 ct em aberto».
  - «Operações do dia» gets a second line: «1 parcial, +US$ 40,00 · stop no breakeven» on an open trade, «em 2 saídas» on a closed one.
- **Import:**
  - New lines for the rows of a Top One position: grouped into one trade, or attached to a trade already there.
  - Trade counts read the import's new trade keys.
  - The primary button reads «Juntar N saídas» for a file that only adds exits.
- **Personalizar › Suas regras:**
  - The new group «Durante a operação» › «Mover para o breakeven», on «Padrão Futuros» and on each futures account.
  - Per-asset lines, «Adicionar ativo», «Remover», «Voltar ao padrão», the tags and «não salvo».
  - The version note «breakeven com +8 pts no MES …».
- **New code:** `lib/hub/registrarParciais.ts`, `registrarSaidas.ts` and `personalizarBreakeven.ts` (pure models); the components `AcoesAberta`, `FormParcial`, `FormMoverStop`, `BlocoAgora`, `LinhaDoTempo`, `SugestaoBreakeven`, `SaidasJaFechada`, `MoviBreakeven` and `RegraBreakeven`; a trade-events read (`useTradeEvents`); the stylesheet `hub-registrar-parciais.css`.
- **Data:** every read and write goes through the domain PR's data layer, in the browser, with the user's session. Nothing private is rendered on the server.

## Where the app differs from the approved boards (for the owner)
1. **Save bar in Personalizar.** On the board, «Adicionar ativo» with no value yet, or invalid text in a field, also brings up the bar «Alterações não salvas». Here the row shows «não salvo», but the bar follows only what can actually be saved, so it does not appear in that state. Nothing saved is different. Changing this needs a later change to the page's provider.
2. **A typo in «Preço agora» or «Preço quando moveu» on Forex.** A price 10^10 pips or more from the entry (for example 2.000.000 on EUR/USD) is refused with «Confira o preço de agora.» or «Confira o preço quando moveu.», because the database refuses it. The board's prototype would accept it and show its points. Realistic prices behave as on the board.
3. **Import file card.** When two or more rows of a file belong to one position, the file card reads «N linhas» instead of «N operações». The board does not cover this; please confirm.
4. **Focus after a refused undo.** After a refused «Sim, desfazer», the focus returns to the «Desfazer» link if it is still there (offline or network error). Otherwise it goes to the sheet's alert. «Desfazer entrada» now does the same; before, the focus was lost.
5. **First switch-on in Personalizar.** The first asset lines come from each futures account's last 200 trades: up to 3 roots, MES when there is no history. The board always shows MES, MNQ and MGC.
6. **Smaller points:**
   - The note «voltou ao valor anterior» shows the value formatted.
   - An asset added on «Padrão Futuros» but not filled in yet shows only on «Padrão Futuros». The board also shows it on the accounts that inherit.
   - In a single exit (no rows), «Venceu sem valor» still refills «0» after you clear it, as before 3c. The rows keep a cleared field empty, as on the board.
7. **Words the boards do not draw:**
   - the import lines and counts (examples below);
   - «Nª saída» for file exits on app trades;
   - «Confira o preço…» (item 2);
   - «Só o último registro pode ser desfeito.»
8. **The import's trade counts follow the import's new keys.**
   - For a file with partial exits, «Importar {n} operações», the end screen and the toast count trades, not rows. For example, 17 rows that make 16 trades read «Importar 16 operações» and «1 saída parcial juntada à sua operação.».
   - A file that only adds exits to trades already in the account reads «Juntar 2 saídas» and «2 saídas a mais entraram em operações que já estavam.». It is never «Nada novo».
   - Files with one row per trade (every file before 3c) read exactly as before.

## Tests
- **Jest:** 114 suites pass and 8 are skipped; 4,234 tests pass and 118 are skipped. That is 13 suites and 263 tests more than the domain PR.
  - Step 2 and step 3: `hubRegistrarParciais` (the models against the board's strings in all six markets), `RegistrarParciais` (scenario 14 end to end), `RegistrarMoverStop`, `RegistrarLimiteParcial` (scenario 16), `hubRegistrarEventos`, and `RegistrarParciaisCss` (scoping, 44 px targets, contrast in both themes).
  - Step 1 and Personalizar: `hubRegistrarSaidas`, `RegistrarJaFechadaSaidas` (scenarios 15 and 12), `RegistrarRegraEntrada`, `PersonalizarBreakeven` and `hubPersonalizarBreakeven`.
  - Additions to `useRegistrar`, `RegistrarFechada`, `ImportSheet`, `OperacoesDoDia`, `hubRegistrarForm` (draft v3) and `hubComoFicaHoje`.
  - Fixtures are the domain PR's recorded answers from the real SQL. Data is invented.
- **Type check and lint:** `tsc --noEmit` is clean. `next lint` shows no errors; its 9 warnings are all in files this PR does not touch.
- **Database-backed suites:** all 8 pass against a local throwaway cluster with every migration (hubMercados 4, hubParciais 12, hubRegistrar 36, hubRegistrarFluxos 8, hubRegistrarMercados 15, hubRegistrarTelas 9, hubRegras 24 + 2 skipped, hubRegrasBreakeven 8).
- **End-to-end flow on that cluster, through the real UI code:**
  - Personalizar turns on the rule and saves it through `save_rules`.
  - Register the entry, see the rule line.
  - «Parcial», then the suggestion.
  - «Mover para o breakeven» → «Registrar stop».
  - «Desfazer» the move.
  - «Saída» → step 3.
  - «Já fechada» with two exits and the pill → step 3.
  - «Operações do dia» updates after each write.
  - Every write was checked in the tables.
- **Reviews:** each lane was reviewed twice, against the boards and ag

author: jotaele44
body:
## Purpose

Close release-audit finding F-8 on current canonical main `f36b77ffb5b9baf61cb27cee0faaf755b614fb12`.

The source-checkout launcher and the packaged release artifact previously shared the visible filename `Mucaro AI.app` despite having different authority and bundle identifiers.

## Authority split

- **Source setup:** `Mucaro AI Setup.app`
  - display/name: `Mucaro AI Setup`
  - bundle ID: `ai.mucaro.source-launcher`
  - tracked beside `pyproject.toml`
  - relocatable only with the checkout
- **Packaged release:** `Mucaro AI.app`
  - bundle ID: `ai.mucaro.app`
  - release lane only

## Current-main implementation

- binary-safe tracked app rename with icon blobs preserved and launcher executable bit preserved
- generated source-wrapper builder emits only `Mucaro AI Setup.app`
- verifier rejects:
  - release filename used by a source wrapper
  - release bundle ID used by a source wrapper
  - partial source display-name drift
  - receipt path/name/scope drift
- one-click workflow, launchers, docs, and tests use the source setup name only where applicable
- portable app build excludes every tracked `.app` tree, case-insensitively
- portable manifest records excluded tracked app bundles
- verifier rejects manifest-declared nested app members while remaining compatible with historical v1 manifests lacking the new exclusion receipt

## Fail-closed boundary

This PR does **not** rename the packaged release lane. `Mucaro AI.app` remains canonical for `ai.mucaro.app`.

## Evidence required before merge

Fresh exact-head:
- CI PASS
- One-click setup PASS
- Rendered UI QA PASS
- macOS app PASS

No merge or F-8 closure claim until those executed gates pass.
